info.description:
This API is used for the classic integration. If you are just starting your implementation, refer to our [new integration guide](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms) instead.

The Fund API provides endpoints for managing the funds in the accounts on your platform. These management operations include, for example, the transfer of funds from one account to another, the payout of funds to an account holder, and the retrieval of balances in an account.

For more information, refer to our [documentation](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/classic/).
## Authentication
Your Adyen contact will provide your API credential and an API key. To connect to the API, add an `X-API-Key` header with the API key as the value, for example:

 ```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
...
```

Alternatively, you can use the username and password to connect to the API using basic authentication. For example:

```
curl
-U "ws@MarketPlace.YOUR_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT":"YOUR_WS_PASSWORD" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
...
```
When going live, you need to generate new web service user credentials to access the [live endpoints](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/live-endpoints).

## Versioning
The Fund API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://cal-test.adyen.com/cal/services/Fund/v6/accountHolderBalance
```

transactionStatuses.description:
A list of statuses to include in the transaction list. If left blank, all transactions will be included.
>Permitted values:
>* `PendingCredit` - a pending balance credit.
>* `CreditFailed` - a pending credit failure; the balance will not be credited.
>* `Credited` - a credited balance.
>* `PendingDebit` - a pending balance debit (e.g., a refund).
>* `CreditClosed` - a pending credit closed; the balance will not be credited.
>* `CreditSuspended` - a pending credit closed; the balance will not be credited.
>* `DebitFailed` - a pending debit failure; the balance will not be debited.
>* `Debited` - a debited balance (e.g., a refund).
>* `DebitReversedReceived` - a pending refund reversal.
>* `DebitedReversed` - a reversed refund.
>* `ChargebackReceived` - a received chargeback request.
>* `Chargeback` - a processed chargeback.
>* `ChargebackReversedReceived` - a pending chargeback reversal.
>* `ChargebackReversed` - a reversed chargeback.
>* `Converted` - converted.
>* `ManualCorrected` - manual booking/adjustment by Adyen.
>* `Payout` - a payout.
>* `PayoutReversed` - a reversed payout.
>* `PendingFundTransfer` - a pending transfer of funds from one account to another.
>* `FundTransfer` - a transfer of funds from one account to another.

info.description:
This API is used for the classic integration. If you are just starting your implementation, refer to our [new integration guide](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms) instead.

The Fund API provides endpoints for managing the funds in the accounts on your platform. These management operations include, for example, the transfer of funds from one account to another, the payout of funds to an account holder, and the retrieval of balances in an account.

For more information, refer to our [documentation](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/classic/).
## Authentication
Your Adyen contact will provide your API credential and an API key. To connect to the API, add an `X-API-Key` header with the API key as the value, for example:

 ```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
...
```

Alternatively, you can use the username and password to connect to the API using basic authentication. For example:

```
curl
-U "ws@MarketPlace.YOUR_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT":"YOUR_WS_PASSWORD" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
...
```
When going live, you need to generate new web service user credentials to access the [live endpoints](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/live-endpoints).

## Versioning
The Fund API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://cal-test.adyen.com/cal/services/Fund/v3/accountHolderBalance
```

>* `Payout` - a payout.
>* `PayoutReversed` - a reversed payout.
>* `PendingFundTransfer` - a pending transfer of funds from one account to another.

info.description:
>Versions 1 and 2 of the Transfers API are deprecated. If you are just starting your implementation, use the latest version.

This API provides endpoints that you can use to transfer funds, whether when [paying out to a transfer instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/payout-to-users/on-demand-payouts), [sending funds to third parties](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/business-accounts/send-receive-funds) for users with business bank accounts, or to [request a payout for a grant offer](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/capital). The API also supports use cases for [getting transactions for business bank accounts](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/business-accounts/transactions-api) and getting [grants and its outstanding balances](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/capital#get-balances). .

## Authentication
Your Adyen contact will provide your API credential and an API key. To connect to the API, add an `X-API-Key` header with the API key as the value, for example:

 ```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
...
```

Alternatively, you can use the username and password to connect to the API using basic authentication. For example:

```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-U "ws@BalancePlatform.YOUR_BALANCE_PLATFORM":"YOUR_WS_PASSWORD" \
...
```
## Roles and permissions
To use the Transfers API, you need an additional role for your API credential. Transfers must also be enabled for the source balance account. Your Adyen contact will set up the roles and permissions for you.
## Versioning
The Transfers API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://balanceplatform-api-test.adyen.com/btl/v2/transfers
```
## Going live
When going live, your Adyen contact will provide your API credential for the live environment. You can then use the username and password to send requests to `https://balanceplatform-api-live.adyen.com/btl/v2`.

info.description:
>Versions 1 and 2 of the Transfers API are deprecated. If you are just starting your implementation, use the latest version.

This API provides endpoints that you can use to transfer funds, whether when [paying out to a transfer instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/payout-to-users/on-demand-payouts), [sending funds to third parties](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/business-accounts/send-receive-funds) for users with business bank accounts, or to [request a payout for a grant offer](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/capital). The API also supports use cases for [getting transactions for business bank accounts](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/business-accounts/transactions-api) and getting [grants and its outstanding balances](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/capital#get-balances). .

## Authentication
Your Adyen contact will provide your API credential and an API key. To connect to the API, add an `X-API-Key` header with the API key as the value, for example:

 ```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
...
```

Alternatively, you can use the username and password to connect to the API using basic authentication. For example:

```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-U "ws@BalancePlatform.YOUR_BALANCE_PLATFORM":"YOUR_WS_PASSWORD" \
...
```
## Roles and permissions
To use the Transfers API, you need an additional role for your API credential. Transfers must also be enabled for the source balance account. Your Adyen contact will set up the roles and permissions for you.
## Versioning
The Transfers API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://balanceplatform-api-test.adyen.com/btl/v3/transfers
```
## Going live
When going live, your Adyen contact will provide your API credential for the live environment. You can then use the username and password to send requests to `https://balanceplatform-api-live.adyen.com/btl/v3`.

get.description:
>Versions 1 and 2 of the Transfers API are deprecated. If you are just starting your implementation, use the latest version.

Returns all the transactions related to a balance account, account holder, or balance platform.

When making this request, you must include at least one of the following:
- `balanceAccountId`
- `accountHolderId`
- `balancePlatform`.

This endpoint supports cursor-based pagination. The response returns the first page of results, and returns links to the next and previous pages when applicable. You can use the links to page through the results.

The unique identifier of the [balance platform](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/balanceplatform/latest/get/balancePlatforms/{id}__queryParam_id).

Required if you don't provide a `balanceAccountId` or `accountHolderId`.

To use this parameter, you must also provide a `balanceAccountId`, `accountHolderId`, or `balancePlatform`.

The `paymentInstrumentId` must be related to the `balanceAccountId` or `accountHolderId` that you provide.

If you provide a `balanceAccountId`, the `accountHolderId` must be related to the `balanceAccountId`.

If you provide an `accountHolderId`, the `balanceAccountId` must be related to the `accountHolderId`.

info.description:
Adyen Data Protection API provides a way for you to process [Subject Erasure Requests](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-17-gdpr/) as mandated in GDPR.

Use our API to submit a request to delete shopper's data, including payment details and other related information (for example, delivery address or shopper email).## Authentication
Each request to the Data Protection API must be signed with an API key. Get your API Key from your Customer Area, as described in [How to get the API key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#generate-api-key). Then set this key to the `X-API-Key` header value, for example:

```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: Your_API_key" \
...
```
Note that when going live, you need to generate a new API Key to access the [live endpoints](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/live-endpoints).

## Versioning
Data Protection Service API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://ca-test.adyen.com/ca/services/DataProtectionService/v1/requestSubjectErasure
```

info.description:
This API is used for the classic integration. If you are just starting your implementation, refer to our [new integration guide](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms) instead.

The Notification Configuration API provides endpoints for setting up and testing notifications that inform you of events on your platform, for example when a verification check or a payout has been completed.

For more information, refer to our [documentation](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/classic/notifications).
## Authentication
Your Adyen contact will provide your API credential and an API key. To connect to the API, add an `X-API-Key` header with the API key as the value, for example:

 ```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
...
```

Alternatively, you can use the username and password to connect to the API using basic authentication. For example:

```
curl
-U "ws@MarketPlace.YOUR_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT":"YOUR_WS_PASSWORD" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
...
```
When going live, you need to generate new web service user credentials to access the [live endpoints](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/live-endpoints).

## Versioning
The Notification Configuration API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://cal-test.adyen.com/cal/services/Notification/v2/createNotificationConfiguration
```

post.description: Creates a subscription to notifications informing you of events on your platform. After the subscription is created, the events specified in the configuration will be sent to the URL specified in the configuration. Subscriptions must be configured on a per-event basis (as opposed to, for example, a per-account holder basis), so all event notifications of a marketplace and of a given type will be sent to the same endpoint(s). A marketplace may have multiple endpoints if desired; an event notification may be sent to as many or as few different endpoints as configured.

A string with which to salt the notification(s) before hashing. If this field is provided, a hash value will be included under the notification header `HmacSignature` and the hash protocol will be included under the notification header `Protocol`. >Must be a 32-byte hex-encoded string (i.e. a string containing 64 hexadecimal characters; e.g. "b0ea55c2fe60d4d1d605e9c385e0e7f7e6cafbb939ce07010f31a327a0871f27").

info.description:
This API is used for the classic integration. If you are just starting your implementation, refer to our [new integration guide](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms) instead.

The Notification Configuration API provides endpoints for setting up and testing notifications that inform you of events on your platform, for example when a verification check or a payout has been completed.

For more information, refer to our [documentation](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/classic/notifications).
## Authentication
Your Adyen contact will provide your API credential and an API key. To connect to the API, add an `X-API-Key` header with the API key as the value, for example:

 ```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
...
```

Alternatively, you can use the username and password to connect to the API using basic authentication. For example:

```
curl
-U "ws@MarketPlace.YOUR_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT":"YOUR_WS_PASSWORD" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
...
```
When going live, you need to generate new web service user credentials to access the [live endpoints](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/live-endpoints).

## Versioning
The Notification Configuration API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://cal-test.adyen.com/cal/services/Notification/v4/createNotificationConfiguration
```

post.description: Creates a subscription to notifications informing you of events on your platform. After the subscription is created, the events specified in the configuration will be sent to the URL specified in the configuration. Subscriptions must be configured on a per-event basis (as opposed to, for example, a per-account holder basis), so all event notifications of a marketplace and of a given type will be sent to the same endpoint(s). A marketplace may have multiple endpoints if desired; an event notification may be sent to as many or as few different endpoints as configured.

This API is used for the classic integration. If you are just starting your implementation, refer to our [new integration guide](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms) instead.

The Notification Configuration API provides endpoints for setting up and testing notifications that inform you of events on your platform, for example when a verification check or a payout has been completed.

For more information, refer to our [documentation](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/classic/notifications).
## Authentication
Your Adyen contact will provide your API credential and an API key. To connect to the API, add an `X-API-Key` header with the API key as the value, for example:

 ```
curl
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
...
```

Alternatively, you can use the username and password to connect to the API using basic authentication. For example:

```
curl
-U "ws@MarketPlace.YOUR_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT":"YOUR_WS_PASSWORD" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
...
```
When going live, you need to generate new web service user credentials to access the [live endpoints](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/live-endpoints).

## Versioning
The Notification Configuration API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:
```
https://cal-test.adyen.com/cal/services/Notification/v6/createNotificationConfiguration
```

post.description: Creates a subscription to notifications informing you of events on your platform. After the subscription is created, the events specified in the configuration will be sent to the URL specified in the configuration. Subscriptions must be configured on a per-event basis (as opposed to, for example, a per-account holder basis), so all event notifications of a marketplace and of a given type will be sent to the same endpoint(s). A marketplace may have multiple endpoints if desired; an event notification may be sent to as many or as few different endpoints as configured.

A string with which to salt the notification(s) before hashing. If this field is provided, a hash value will be included under the notification header `HmacSignature` and the hash protocol will be included under the notification header `Protocol`. A notification body along with its `hmacSignatureKey` and `Protocol` can be used to calculate a hash value; matching this hash value with the `HmacSignature` will ensure that the notification body has not been tampered with or corrupted.

info.description:
The Balance Control API lets you transfer funds between merchant accounts that belong to the same legal entity and are under the same company account.

## Authentication
To connect to the Balance Control API, you must authenticate your requests with an [API key or basic auth username and password](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-authentication). To learn how you can generate these, see [API credentials](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials).Here is an example of authenticating a request with an API key:

```
curl
-H "X-API-Key: Your_API_key" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
...
```
Note that when going live, you need to generate API credentials to access the [live endpoints](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/live-endpoints).

## Versioning
The Balance Control API supports [versioning](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/versioning) using a version suffix in the endpoint URL. This suffix has the following format: "vXX", where XX is the version number.

For example:

```
https://pal-test.adyen.com/pal/servlet/BalanceControl/v1/balanceTransfer
```
info.title: Adyen Balance Control API

post.description:
Starts a balance transfer request between merchant accounts. The following conditions must be met before you can successfully transfer balances:

* The source and destination merchant accounts must be under the same company account and legal entity.

* The source merchant account must have sufficient funds.

* The source and destination merchant accounts must have at least one common processing currency.

When sending multiple API requests with the same source and destination merchant accounts, send the requests sequentially and *not* in parallel. Some requests may not be processed if the requests are sent in parallel.

info.description:
Adyen sends webhooks to inform your system about events that occur in your platform. These events include, for example, when an account holder's capabilities are updated, or when a sweep configuration is created or updated. 
When an event occurs, Adyen makes an HTTP POST request to a URL on your server and includes the details of the event in the request body.

You can use these webhooks to build your implementation. For example, you can use this information to update internal statuses when the status of a capability is changed.

counterparty.description:
The destination or the source of the funds, depending on the sweep `type`.

Either a `balanceAccountId`, `transferInstrumentId`, or `merchantAccount` is required.

currency.description:
The three-character [ISO currency code](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/currency-codes) in uppercase. For example, **EUR**.

The sweep currency must match any of the [balances currencies](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/balanceplatform/latest/get/balanceAccounts/{id}__resParam_balances).

description.description:
The message that will be used in the sweep transfer's description body with a maximum length of 140 characters.

If the message is longer after replacing placeholders, the message will be cut off at 140 characters.

id.description: The unique identifier of the sweep.

reason.description: The reason for disabling the sweep.

schedule.description: The schedule when the `triggerAmount` is evaluated. If the balance meets the threshold, funds are pushed out of or pulled in to the balance account.

status.description:
The status of the sweep. If not provided, by default, this is set to **active**.

Possible values: 

 * **active**:  the sweep is enabled and funds will be pulled in or pushed out based on the defined configuration. 

 * **inactive**: the sweep is disabled and cannot be triggered.

sweepAmount.description: The amount that must be pushed out or pulled in. You can configure either `sweepAmount` or `targetAmount`, not both.

targetAmount.description: The amount that must be available in the balance account after the sweep. You can configure either `sweepAmount` or `targetAmount`, not both.

triggerAmount.description:
The threshold amount that triggers the sweep. If not provided, by default, the amount is set to zero. The `triggerAmount` is evaluated according to the specified `schedule.type`.

* For `type` **pull**, if the balance is less than or equal to the `triggerAmount`, funds are pulled in to the balance account.

* For `type` **push**, if the balance is more than or equal to the `triggerAmount`, funds are pushed out of the balance account.

type.description:
The direction of sweep, whether pushing out or pulling in funds to the balance account. If not provided, by default, this is set to **push**.

Possible values:

 * **push**: _push out funds_ to a destination balance account or transfer instrument.

 * **pull**: _pull in funds_ from a source merchant account, transfer instrument, or balance account.

balanceAccountId.description:
The unique identifier of the destination or source [balance account](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/balanceplatform/latest/post/balanceAccounts__resParam_id).

 You can only use this for periodic sweep schedules such as `schedule.type` **daily** or **monthly**.

merchantAccount.description:
The merchant account that will be the source of funds.

You can only use this parameter with sweeps of `type` **pull** and `schedule.type` **balance**, and if you are processing payments with Adyen.

transferInstrumentId.description:
The unique identifier of the destination or source [transfer instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/legalentity/latest/post/transferInstruments#responses-200-id) depending on the sweep `type`

. To [set up automated top-up sweeps to balance accounts](https://docs.adyen.com/marketplaces-and-platforms/top-up-balance-account/#before-you-begin), use this parameter in combination with a `merchantAccount` and a sweep `type` of **pull**. Top-up sweeps start a direct debit request from the source transfer instrument. Contact Adyen Support to enable this feature.

cronExpression.description:
A [cron expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cron#CRON_expression) that is used to set the sweep schedule. The schedule uses the time zone of the balance account. 
For example, **30 17 * * MON** schedules a sweep every Monday at 17:30.

The expression must have five values separated by a single space in the following order:

* Minute: **0-59**

* Hour: **0-23**

* Day of the month: **1-31**

* Month: **1-12** or **JAN-DEC**

* Day of the week: **0-7** (0 and 7 are Sunday) or **MON-SUN**.

The following non-standard characters are supported: *****, **L**, **#**, **W** and **/**. See [crontab guru](https://crontab.guru/) for more examples.

Required when `type` is **cron**.

type.description:
The schedule type.

Possible values:

* **cron**: push out funds based on a `cronExpression`.

* **daily**: push out funds daily at 07:00 AM CET.

* **weekly**: push out funds every Monday at 07:00 AM CET.

* **monthly**: push out funds every first of the month at 07:00 AM CET.

* **balance**: pull in funds instantly if the balance is less than or equal to the `triggerAmount`.
You can only use this for sweeps of `type` **pull** and when the source is a `merchantAccount` or `transferInstrument`.
If the source is transferInstrument, merchant account identifier is still required, with which you want to process the transaction.

Adyen sends this webhook when you successfully [update an account holder](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/patch/accountHolders/_id_).
Adyen sends this webhook when you successfully [create a balance account](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/post/balanceAccounts).
Adyen sends this webhook when you successfully [update a balance account](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/patch/balanceAccounts/_id_).
Adyen sends this webhook when you successfully [create a sweep](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/post/balanceAccounts/_balanceAccountId_/sweeps).
Adyen sends this webhook when you successfully [delete a sweep](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/delete/balanceAccounts/_balanceAccountId_/sweeps/_sweepId_).

Adyen sends this webhook to indicate a successful creation of a card order after you create a [payment instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/post/paymentInstruments) of `type` **card** and `formFactor` **physical**.
Adyen sends this webhook when there is an update in card order status.

Adyen sends this webhook when you successfully [create a payment instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/post/paymentInstruments). 
>The webhook does not include the card number when creating virtual cards. You can only get the card number in the response of the POST [/paymentInstruments](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/post/paymentInstruments#responses-200-card-number) request.
Adyen sends this webhook when you successfully [update a payment instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/balanceplatform/latest/patch/paymentInstruments/_id_).

info.title: Opndoor Partner API
info.description: Create guarantee applications from your own system and receive webhooks as they progress. Organisations must already exist: create them in the opndoor portal, then send names or ids. The API key prefix decides the mode: opnd_test_ creates sandbox applications, opnd_live_ creates real ones.

get.description: Call once, store the ids against your own records, and send them from then on if you want precision. You can also send names on POST /applications instead.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed per window for this key.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp when the window resets.

X-Request-Id.description: Quote this to support.

400.description: malformed_request: Not valid JSON, or a missing idempotency key

401.description: unauthorized: Any authentication failure. Always identical

403.description: insufficient_scope: The key lacks the required scope; partner_inactive: The account is not active

404.description: not_found: Unknown, or not yours; unsupported_version: No API version in the path, or one not supported

info.title: gen-img — rerun-and-reuse
info.description: Re-run a saved generation and reuse its output images as inputs, with one-level lineage (spec §1). Delta over the shipped contracts (text-to-image-openrouter, image-inputs-openrouter, vercel-ai-gateway, curate-gallery): the start-generation request gains `source` and an ordered `inputs` list that may name stored images (ADR-0017); Generation gains `source` and `derived` (ADR-0018). No new paths. Every route passes the request guard (ADR-0007) → 403 FORBIDDEN for foreign pages. Errors use `{ error: { code, message, details? } }` with the repo's UPPER_SNAKE codes (src/server/lib/errors.ts).

get.description:
Returns events visible in the calendar. Optional query parameters filter
the results in the database (scoped to the calendar, so no full table
scan). Text filters are case-insensitive substring matches; all supplied
filters are combined with AND. Results are ordered by start time when any
filter is applied. Pagination (limit/offset) is applied after per-event
access checks.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Include events ending at or after this instant (RFC3339, or
YYYY-MM-DD for midnight UTC of that day), judged by the end the
server stores for indexing: for a recurring object the end of its
recurrence set, and otherwise the event's `dtend`. A timed event
without a `DTEND` ends at its `DTSTART`, so one that starts before
this instant is left out; an all-day one ends with its day. A
non-recurring event whose end a `DURATION` gives has no stored end
and is always included, as is any object with no stored end at
all, such as a non-recurring `VTODO`.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description:
Include events whose earliest instance starts at or before this
instant (RFC3339, or YYYY-MM-DD for midnight UTC of that day, so
events later that day are left out). Any object with no stored
start, such as a non-recurring `VTODO`, is always included.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the event summary.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the event description.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the event location.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match across summary, description, and location.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return. Values above 1000 are capped.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of events to skip, for pagination.

post.description:
The request is answered at the first of these steps that refuses it:

1. The body is decoded, before any privilege check. A `text/calendar`,
   `application/ical` or `application/ics` body gets `400` here only
   when it is over 10 MiB. Any other body is read as an
   `EventWriteRequest` and gets `400` when it is empty, over 10 MiB
   (the limit applies to the whole JSON document), not valid JSON,
   names an unknown field, or lacks the input its `inputMode` needs,
   such as a blank `rawIcal`.
2. `404` when the caller holds no grant on the calendar or on any of
   its events, as when the calendar does not exist.
3. `403` when the caller lacks `DAV:bind` on the calendar, whatever
   the body holds, the UID it names, or the conditional headers.
4. The event is built from the body and validated: `400` or `409`.
   An empty or blank `text/calendar` body gets `400` here. `rawIcal`
   under `inputMode` `raw_ical` is validated and stored by the same
   rules as a `text/calendar` body. The UID is learned here, so a
   body refused here is answered before any lock is looked at.
5. When the request carries `If-Match` or `If-None-Match`: `423` when
   a WebDAV lock covers the new event's name or the calendar. The API
   submits no lock token, so it cannot write under a lock; its holder
   writes over CalDAV. A lock that has expired refuses nothing.
6. The conditional headers are evaluated: `412`.
7. `409` when the calendar already holds an event with the UID. A
   create never updates an existing event: one that another request
   stores while this one runs is refused too, with `409`, or `412`
   under `If-None-Match: *`.
8. The event is stored once the store has checked it again under its
   locks. A request that carried no conditional header meets a WebDAV
   lock here, with `423`, after steps 4 and 7: a body refused, or an
   event that already exists, is answered `400` or `409` before
   the lock.

A create that keeps losing to concurrent changes of the calendar's
events or ACL gives up with `409`. A grant withdrawn while the create
runs fails it with `403`.

200.description: Event details and raw iCalendar data.

put.description:
The request is answered at the first of these steps that refuses it:

1. The body is decoded, before any privilege check. A `text/calendar`,
   `application/ical` or `application/ics` body gets `400` here only
   when it is over 10 MiB. Any other body is read as an
   `EventWriteRequest` and gets `400` when it is empty, over 10 MiB
   (the limit applies to the whole JSON document), not valid JSON,
   names an unknown field, or lacks the input its `inputMode` needs,
   such as a blank `rawIcal`.
2. `DAV:write-content` is checked on the event, or on the calendar
   when it holds no event with the UID. A caller who can neither read
   the event nor hold the privilege on it is answered as though the
   calendar held no event with the UID, so the answer does not reveal
   that it exists. Without the privilege on the calendar, such a UID
   gets `403` when the caller can read the calendar and `404`
   otherwise; with it, the steps below go on.
3. `404` when the calendar holds no event with the UID, whatever the
   conditional headers say (RFC 9110 §13.2.1).
4. When the request carries `If-Match` or `If-None-Match`: `423` when
   a WebDAV lock covers the event, or a depth-infinity lock covers
   the calendar. The API submits no lock token, so it cannot write
   under a lock; its holder writes over CalDAV. A lock that has
   expired refuses nothing. This precedes the checks below, a body
   refused with `400` included.
5. The conditional headers are evaluated: `412`.
6. The event is built from the body and validated: `400` or `409`.
   An empty or blank `text/calendar` body gets `400` here. `rawIcal`
   under `inputMode` `raw_ical` is validated and stored by the same
   rules as a `text/calendar` body.
7. The event is stored only if it is still the version steps 2 to 5
   decided on, which the store checks under the event's row lock. A
   request that carried no conditional header meets a WebDAV lock
   here, with `423`, after steps 3 and 6: a missing event or a body
   refused is answered `404` or `400` or `409` before the lock. An
   event another request removes meanwhile is not stored again: the
   request is decided again and answered `404`. One another request
   replaces meanwhile is read again and the conditional headers
   evaluated against it, so `If-Match` of the replaced version gets
   `412`, and a request with no `If-Match` replaces the new version.
   A grant withdrawn meanwhile fails the request with `403`, or
   `404` when it leaves the caller unable to see the event. A request
   that keeps losing to concurrent changes gives up with `409`.

delete.description:
The request is answered at the first of these steps that refuses it:

1. The caller needs `DAV:unbind` on the calendar, a privilege of the
   collection an event leaves (RFC 3744 §3.10), and some privilege on
   the event. A caller holding no privilege on the event, an
   event-level deny of every privilege included, is answered as
   though the calendar held no event with the UID, so the answer does
   not reveal that it exists. For such a UID, a caller holding no
   privilege on the calendar gets `404`, and one holding some but not
   `DAV:unbind` gets `403`. A caller holding privilege on the event
   but not `DAV:unbind` on the calendar gets `403`, whatever they hold
   on the event. DAV DELETE decides the same way but for one case: a
   caller whose ACEs on the calendar grant none of its privileges, or
   deny every one, gets `403` from DAV, which confirms the calendar
   exists, and `404` here, as `GET` answers them.
2. `404` when the calendar holds no event with the UID, whatever the
   conditional headers say (RFC 9110 §13.2.1).
3. When the request carries `If-Match` or `If-None-Match`: `423` when
   a WebDAV lock covers the event or the calendar. The API submits no
   lock token, so it cannot delete under a lock; its holder deletes
   over CalDAV. A lock that has expired refuses nothing.
4. The conditional headers are evaluated: `412`.
5. The event is removed only if it is still the version steps 1 to 4
   decided on, which the store checks under the event's row lock. A
   request that carried no conditional header meets a WebDAV lock
   here, with `423`. If the event has changed, the request is decided
   again on the new version: `404` when it is gone, `412` when the
   request's `If-Match` or `If-None-Match` no longer holds, and a
   request with no conditional header removes the new version. A
   grant withdrawn meanwhile fails the request as step 1 would. A
   request that keeps losing to concurrent changes gives up with
   `409`.

200.description: Address books owned by the authenticated user.

get.summary: List the users an address book is shared with
get.description:
Owner only. A caller who does not own the address book, or when it does
not exist, gets `404`.

200.description: The users that can read the address book, by user ID.

post.summary: Share an address book with a user
post.description:
Owner only. Grants the user read-only or editor access to the address
book and its contacts, or changes the role of a user it is already
shared with. The request is answered at the first of these steps that
refuses it:

1. `400` when the address book ID is not a number, or the body is
   over 64 KiB, not valid JSON, or names an unknown field. This
   precedes the ownership check.
2. `404` when the caller does not own the address book, as when it
   does not exist.
3. `400` when `userId` is missing, zero, the caller's own, or names no
   user.
4. `423` when a WebDAV lock covers the address book, as it refuses an
   `ACL` request that changes who can access it without the lock
   token. The API submits no lock token. A lock that has expired
   refuses nothing. Removing a share is not refused for a lock: see
   the `DELETE` operation.

204.description: The address book is shared with the user in that role.

delete.summary: Remove a share of an address book
delete.description:
The owner may remove the share of any user. Any other caller may
remove only their own share, which leaves the address book, and only if
they have one. Every grant the user holds on the address book and its
contacts is removed; denies stay. A caller who may not remove the
share of `userId`, and one who has no share to remove, gets `404`, as
when the address book does not exist.

A WebDAV lock on the address book does not refuse this operation.

get.summary: List contacts in an address book
get.description:
Returns contacts in the address book. Optional query parameters filter
the results in the database (scoped to the address book, so no full table
scan). Text filters are case-insensitive substring matches and are
combined with AND. Results are ordered by display name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the display name.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the primary email.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match across display name and email.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of contacts to return. Values above 1000 are capped.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of contacts to skip, for pagination.

post.description:
The caller needs `DAV:bind` on the address book. A caller who may not
see the address book gets `404`, and one who may see it but lacks
`DAV:bind` gets `403`. A contact the address book already holds under
the UID is never replaced: `409`, or `412` under `If-None-Match: *`.
A create that keeps losing to concurrent changes of the address book's
contacts or ACL gives up with `409`. A WebDAV lock on the address book,
or on the contact's name, refuses it with `423`, ahead of the
conditional headers.

get.description:
The caller needs `DAV:read` on the contact, which the contact's own
ACL decides ahead of the address book's. A contact the caller may not
read is answered `404`, as a contact the address book does not hold
is, so the answer does not reveal that it exists; CardDAV `GET`
answers it the same way.

200.description: Contact details and raw vCard data.

put.description:
The caller needs `DAV:write-content` on the contact, which the
contact's own ACL decides ahead of the address book's. A caller
refused it who may read the contact gets `403`. One who may not read
it either is answered as for a UID the address book does not hold, so
the answer does not reveal that the contact exists: `403` when the
address book refuses them `DAV:write-content`, `404` otherwise. The
conditional headers are checked against the contact as each attempt
reads it, so `412` means the contact itself changed; an update that
keeps losing to concurrent changes gives up with `409`. A WebDAV lock
on the contact, or on the address book to its members, refuses it with
`423`, ahead of the conditional headers.

delete.description:
Decided and answered as CardDAV `DELETE` of the contact is. The
request is answered at the first of these steps that refuses it:

1. The caller needs `DAV:unbind` on the address book, a privilege of
   the collection a contact leaves (RFC 3744 §3.10), and some
   privilege on the contact, which the contact's own ACL decides ahead
   of the address book's. The owner holds both. A grant on the
   contact alone does not reach the address book.
   - A caller holding some privilege on the contact but not
     `DAV:unbind` gets `403`.
   - A caller holding no privilege on the contact, and denied none,
     gets `404`.
   - A caller denied every privilege on the contact cannot read it,
     and is answered as though the address book held no contact with
     the UID, so the answer does not reveal that it exists.
   - For such a UID, and for one the address book does not hold: a
     caller denied every privilege by the address book's own ACL, or
     holding some there but not `DAV:unbind`, gets `403`; one holding
     none there and denied none gets `404`.
2. `404` when the address book holds no contact with the UID, whatever
   the conditional headers say (RFC 9110 §13.2.1).
3. `423` when a WebDAV lock covers the contact or its address book.
4. The conditional headers are evaluated: `412`.
5. The contact is removed if neither it nor its ACL has changed since
   step 1. Otherwise the steps run again against the new state, up to
   three times in all, and the request gives up with `409`.

basicAuth.description:
HTTP Basic with the user's primary email address and an app password.
Accepted over HTTPS only: the request must reach CalCard over TLS, or
through a proxy listed in `APP_TRUSTED_PROXIES` that sends
`X-Forwarded-Proto: https`. Basic credentials sent over plain HTTP are
refused with `401`, unless the deployment sets
`APP_DAV_INSECURE_BASIC_ENABLED` (off by default; RFC 4791 Section 11
forbids Basic without TLS, and the credentials and all data then cross
the network in cleartext), which accepts Basic on every transport.

digestAuth.description:
HTTP Digest (SHA-256 or MD5) with the user's primary email address and
an app password, accepted when `APP_DAV_DIGEST_ENABLED` is true. An app
password can answer Digest only once it is Digest ready: one issued
while Digest is enabled, or one that has since authenticated over Basic.
A client that prefers Digest picks it from the challenge and may not
fall back to Basic, so it may be unable to use an app password that is
not yet Digest ready; reissue the app password, or authenticate with it
once over Basic, before pointing such a client at it.

ShareUserID.name: userId
ShareUserID.description: Numeric identifier of the user the address book is shared with.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
Only apply the write if the current ETag matches (RFC 9110 §13.1.1): a
comma-separated list matches when any of its tags does, `*` matches a
resource that exists, and a weak tag (`W/"..."`) never matches.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description:
Only apply the write if the current ETag does not match (RFC 9110
§13.1.2): a comma-separated list fails when any of its tags matches,
weak tags included, and `*` fails when the resource exists.

ETag.description: Current entity tag for the event.

BadRequest.description: Invalid path parameter, request body, calendar data, or structured event data.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing or invalid credentials, or Basic credentials sent over plain
HTTP while `APP_DAV_INSECURE_BASIC_ENABLED` is off.

WWW-Authenticate.description:
A challenge for each scheme the request could use: `Basic` over
HTTPS (or over any transport when `APP_DAV_INSECURE_BASIC_ENABLED`
is set), and `Digest` with SHA-256 and with MD5 when Digest is
enabled. Over plain HTTP with Digest disabled and
`APP_DAV_INSECURE_BASIC_ENABLED` unset, the response carries no
challenge.

Forbidden.description: The authenticated user cannot perform the requested operation.

NotFound.description: Calendar or event was not found, or is not visible to the authenticated user.

Conflict.description:
The request conflicts with the resource it writes: the calendar data is
a scheduling message (`METHOD`) or names more than one UID, its UID
belongs to another resource in the collection, or a contact's UID or
resource name is taken, or the write kept losing to concurrent changes
of the resource or of the access that decided it. Calendar data refused
for any other reason is a `400`.

PreconditionFailed.description: Conditional request headers were not satisfied.

Locked.description:
A WebDAV lock covers the resource or the collection it is written to or
removed from, and a REST request cannot submit the lock token that
would let the write through, whoever holds the lock. The write is
refused as a CalDAV or CardDAV `PUT` or `DELETE` without the token is:
by a lock on the contact or event itself, by a depth-infinity lock on
its address book or calendar, or, for a create or a delete, by any lock
on the address book or calendar or on the name the item is created at.
A lock that has expired refuses nothing.

TooManyRequests.description:
The client has used up the rate limit that covers every `/api` request
from its address. Retry later.

resourceName.description:
Stored resource name for the calendar object. CalDAV serves the
object at this name with `.ics` added. An event this API creates is
stored under its UID, so a create whose UID contains `/` is refused
with 400.

description.description: Event description, parsed from the iCalendar DESCRIPTION property.

location.description: Event location, parsed from the iCalendar LOCATION property.

dtstart.description:
The start of the event's master `VEVENT` (the first without a
`RECURRENCE-ID`, else the first `VEVENT`) as stored for indexing,
in UTC (RFC 3339 with `Z`). An all-day event's start is midnight
UTC of its first day. Absent when the object has no `VEVENT`, or
its `DTSTART` cannot be read.

dtend.description:
The end of the event's master `VEVENT` as stored for indexing, in
UTC (RFC 3339 with `Z`). An all-day event's end is midnight UTC of
the day after its last day, the exclusive iCalendar `DTEND`. An
event without a `DTEND`, or with one that cannot end it, ends at its
`DTSTART`, or for an all-day event at midnight UTC after its one day
(RFC 5545 §3.6.1), and `dtend` is returned for it. Absent when a
`DURATION` gives the event's end instead, and when the object has
no `VEVENT`. An object stored without a readable `DTSTART` returns
its `DTEND`, if it has one. A row a 1.1.x release stored without a
`DTEND` has no `dtend` when any `DURATION` appears in it, an
alarm's included, and the `start` filter always includes it.

rawIcal.description: Raw iCalendar data for the event.

Required when `inputMode` is `raw_ical`. An iCalendar object,
validated and stored by the same rules as a `text/calendar` request
body.

uid.description: Optional event UID. On path-based updates, it must match the path UID when supplied.

dtstart.description:
Event start. For a timed event (`allDay` false or omitted) a local
date-time, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, read as a
wall clock in `timezone`. A value carrying a UTC offset or `Z` is
refused with `400`; to give a UTC time, send the UTC wall clock and
omit `timezone`. For an all-day event a date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, the
event's first day. A value of the other shape than `allDay` calls
for is refused with `400`.

dtend.description:
Event end, in the same format as `dtstart` and read the same way. A
timed end may equal the start but not precede it, compared as the
instants both name in `timezone`; otherwise the request is refused
with `400`. For an all-day event it is the event's last day,
inclusive: `dtstart` and `dtend` both `2026-03-20` is a one-day
event, stored with the exclusive iCalendar `DTEND` of 2026-03-21.

allDay.description:
Whether the event is all-day, its times being dates with no time of
day or zone (`VALUE=DATE`). Defaults to false.

timezone.description:
The time zone a timed event's `dtstart`, `dtend` and recurrence
`until` are wall clocks in, as an IANA name from the server's time
zone database, such as `America/Chicago`. The event is stored with
`DTSTART;TZID=<timezone>:<wall clock>` exactly as given, and the
server adds the `VTIMEZONE` defining the zone from its database.

When `timezone` is omitted, empty or `UTC`, the values are read as
UTC wall clocks and stored as UTC (`DTSTART:20260320T100000Z`).
Before 1.2.0 they were read in the time zone of the server process,
so a client of a server not running in UTC that omits `timezone` now
gets times that many hours from where it did. Any other name the
server's database does not define is refused with `400`, all-day
events included. A structured update replaces the whole event, so a
zone a stored event defines only by its own `VTIMEZONE`, such as
Outlook's `Eastern Standard Time`, is refused here as well; send
`rawIcal` to keep it.

A wall clock a daylight-saving change skips (02:30 on the morning
New York springs forward) is stored as given and names the instant
RFC 5545 §3.3.5 gives it, read with the offset before the change
(02:30 EST, which is 03:30 EDT); a wall clock a change repeats names
its first occurrence. An all-day event's dates are not read in it.

status.description: iCalendar status value.

items.description: Reminder offset in minutes.

until.description:
The last day of the series, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive: an occurrence
on that day is part of it. For an all-day series it is stored as
the date `UNTIL`; for a timed one as the last second of that day
(23:59:59) in the event's `timezone`, or in UTC under the same rules
`timezone` describes, written as a UTC `UNTIL`. Ignored when
`count` is greater than zero. A value that is not a `YYYY-MM-DD`
calendar date is refused with `400`, whatever `count` or
`frequency` is.

RawICalendar.example:
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
VERSION:2.0
BEGIN:VEVENT
UID:example-event
DTSTAMP:20260320T150000Z
DTSTART:20260320T150000Z
DTEND:20260320T160000Z
SUMMARY:Example event
END:VEVENT
END:VCALENDAR

email.description: Primary email address of the user, empty when it cannot be read.

userId.description: The user to share with. It cannot be the caller.

role.description:
`editor` (also `write`, `read-write` or `readwrite`, in any case)
grants read and write access. Any other value, and an absent one,
grants read-only access.

resourceName.description: Stored resource name for the contact object.

email.description: Primary email address parsed from the vCard.

rawVcard.description: Raw vCard data for the contact.

StructuredContactInput.description: Structured contact fields assembled into a vCard server-side.

uid.description: Optional. Generated when omitted; on update must match the path UID.

RawVCard.example:
BEGIN:VCARD
VERSION:3.0
UID:example-contact
FN:Example Person
EMAIL;TYPE=INTERNET:person@example.com
END:VCARD

info.description:
maimail is complete e-mailing solution with advanced antispam, antivirus, nice UI and API.

In order to use this API you have to create a API key and add your IP address to the whitelist of allowed IPs this can be done by logging into the MaiMaiL UI using your admin account, then go to Configuration > Access > Edit administrator details > API. There you will find a collapsed API menu.

There are two types of API keys
  - The read only key can only be used for all get endpoints
  - The read write key can be used for all endpoints
info.title: maimail API

info.title: ForteBank video analysis API
info.description: Contract only; handlers are not implemented. Default job view satisfies the jury's required full JPEG/base64 result. view=ui supplies local-LLM overview and backend-defined progress; events are paginated and frames fetched separately. Both views are projections of the same immutable result, not separate analyses. Examples are synthetic. Cross-field invariants documented in api-contract.md must also be implemented by the server; Zod refinements are not represented in JSON Schema.

get.description: Authenticated aggregate readiness check, not job progress. backend=ok means the API can accept and persist jobs; gpu_server=ok requires a responsive GPU worker, usable GPU and loaded analysis/LLM models. Probe both independently with a 2-second budget; do not run inference. UI polls every 10 seconds through the same-origin proxy, which times out after 3 seconds. If the backend is unreachable, the proxy returns 503 HealthResponse with backend=error and gpu_server=unknown; it must not assert GPU failure. Health 503 uses the health body, not ApiErrorResponse. No query parameters. No cached success.

Cache-Control.description: Do not cache video analysis responses or frames.

gpu_server.message: GPU и модели готовы к анализу.

503.description: At least one service is not ready. A valid health report, not a transport error. status=degraded when backend is ready but GPU is not; unavailable when backend is not ready.

Cache-Control.description: Do not cache video analysis responses or frames.

post.summary: Upload one MOV and create a job
post.description: Authenticate before reading the upload. Return 202 after persisting it, without waiting for inference. Repeated POST creates another job; do not retry automatically. Processing, local LLM overview and result publication share the five-minute deadline, measured from upload receipt start.

requestBody.description: One nonempty .mov file, at most 104857600 bytes. Verify container and video stream. Accept generic or absent part MIME for a valid MOV.

202.description: Accepted and persisted; no verdict yet.

Cache-Control.description: Do not cache video analysis responses or frames.

Location.description: Job resource; UI clients append view=ui.

get.summary: Get state and result in jury or UI representation
get.description: view=jury (default) returns JuryJobResponse, including all events with JPEG/base64 on done. view=ui returns JobResponse: progress for every state, overview and violations_count only on done, never inline events or frames. Stage IDs, display labels, descriptions, ordered plan and percentages are determined by the backend. done and failed are terminal. Both views have the same job_id, status and verdict. A failed job is HTTP 200. Unknown/repeated view, or page/page_size on this endpoint, return 400; paginate via /violations.

info.title: DeenBridge Backend API
info.description:
REST API for DeenBridge: authentication and sessions, courses, the book library,
community spaces, reels, search, Stellar USDC payments, scholarship escrow,
refunds and disputes,
educator payouts, media upload signing and the SEP-1 metadata document.

Provenance of this document:
  - Paths, methods and auth requirements are derived from app.js and src/routes/**,
    which are the authoritative mounting and middleware sources.
  - Component schemas are derived from the Mongoose schemas in src/models/**.
  - Per-endpoint request bodies are described from route middleware and the model
    fields they write. Where a controller accepts more than the model exposes, the
    body is intentionally permissive rather than invented.

Known response inconsistencies (see issue about response standardization):
  - Most handlers return an envelope of the form { success, message, data }.
  - Some list handlers return a bare array with no envelope.
  - POST /api/email returns { success, otp, message } on success but a bare
    { message } on validation failure.
  - GET /admin/jobs returns HTML when the Accept header prefers HTML, otherwise
    { success, jobs }.
  - GET /metrics returns Prometheus text, and the SEP-1 document returns text/toml.
Endpoints whose envelope was not verified against the controller are marked with
x-envelope-unverified so maintainers can confirm them incrementally.

AccessRecordRequest.description:
Who read what, for which purpose — the ledgered access event.

Two ways to name the reader, one preferred (D-AG7):

* ``actor_did`` — the structured identity of the component that performed the
  read (a holder's or app's service DID today; an agent's DID once agent
  identities exist). Preferred, because a DID can be authenticated and
  aggregated: "what did this actor do this week" is answerable from it.
* ``accessor`` — the legacy free-text label (``"node0:agent:weekly-synthesis"``).
  Still accepted and still recorded, so existing callers keep working; free text
  can be neither verified nor grouped, which is why it is the one being replaced.

At least one must be present. During the transition both are recorded when both
are sent.

``consent_id`` names the grant the read was made under, when the reader knows
it: a data source has it from introspection (``consent_id`` on an active
access token). Optional, so every existing caller keeps working; when it is
present the ledger entry carries it, so an access can be read back to the
grant that allowed it (sandbox partner finding, 2026-10-04). It is checked for
shape only, against the form this service mints; whether such a grant exists
is not checked, because the ledger records what the caller asserted.

consent_id.description: The grant the read was made under (`urn:lifecare:consent:<32 hex>`), when the reader knows it.
consent_id.title: Consent Id

AgentManifest.description:
**Defined, not yet registrable.** What an AI client declares about itself
(healthspannode `docs/personal-agent-and-multiparty-ledger-design.md` §5.1
D-AG6a; `docs/provider-ehr-context-and-portability-design.md` §6.2, D-PE5).

A manifest is a *declaration*, not a measurement: nothing here is attested by
the network, which is exactly why `trust` and the grant sit above it. The
ladder is the ceiling (D-AG6b: T0 resolvable → T1 vouched → T2 attested,
carried as `trust`, the same three values
:class:`DelegatedTokenIntrospection` already publishes, so there is one
spelling of an agent's tier in the contract and not two), the person's grant
is the floor, and a client can never receive more than the smaller of them.

The two fields the provider-EHR design adds are `hosting` and `egress_class`,
and the rule binding them (§13a, the tightening of D-PE5) is the hard
constraint written as a validator: **outside the box the node sends
categorical envelopes only, and no grant lifts that.** Values leave in one
way: through the write fence into the EHR, where a clinician relied on them.
From the chart they travel under the provider's own legal basis, with the
network not in that path.

There is no registration route. This is published so a holder, a practice
node and a client vendor agree on the shape and the refusals before the first
manifest exists, exactly as the delegated token shape was published ahead of
its issuance.

post.description:
Create a grant on the server-to-server channel.

Two gates, each with its own flag and each fail-open only in its default
position (F1/F2):

* **who is calling, and for whom**: a holder signature, confidential-
  client credentials or the member's own session, verified whenever
  presented, required when ``require_caller_auth`` is on; with it on, the
  caller must be the member or a first-party client;
* **who approved it**: the subject's device proof over the canonical
  grant digest, verified whenever presented, required when
  ``require_grant_proof`` is on, except for the narrowed first-party
  exemption (``caller_auth.may_grant_without_proof``).

And one rule with no flag of its own: a grant naming a grantee in
``member_only_grantees`` is accepted from the member alone
(``caller_auth.require_member_for_grantee``), checked first.

post.description:
Grant a partner access to scopes for a purpose, as the session user.

**Named exemption (F1), narrowed 2026-09-28 (W0-5).** When
``require_grant_proof`` is on, a grant with **no device proof** is accepted
here only when its grantee is first party: an id in
``Settings.first_party_grantees`` or the member's own DID. The session
behind it was minted by a passkey ceremony, so the person is present, and
the panel client has no proof plumbing yet. A grant to anyone else needs
the device proof, because a session is not held by the member alone: every
relying party that signs the member in receives one (security review
P2-2), and before the narrowing any of them could grant any party through
this route. A proof the panel *does* send is verified exactly as anywhere
else, and the remaining gap is written down in ``docs/security-audit.md``.

post.description:
A holder registers / versions / tiers / moves / shreds a resource.

Who may write (security audit F11, operator ruling of 2026-10-04):

* **the member's own node**, a client in
  ``LIFECAREID_FIRST_PARTY_CLIENTS`` presenting its client credential
  (HTTP Basic): its own entries (``holder.id`` is its client id) in any
  ``holder.role`` but ``user_device``, and source entries
  (``holder.role: source``, a provider id as ``holder.id``), for any
  member;
* **a signed holder** (``X-LifeCare-Signature``): only entries whose
  ``holder.id`` is the DID that signed, in any ``holder.role`` but
  ``home_node`` and ``user_device``, and only for a member who has an
  active grant naming that DID as grantee;
* **the member's own device** (their session, ``Bearer lcs_...``, or a
  signature by their own DID): only their own ``user_device`` entries,
  ``holder.id`` their DID;
* **anyone else** writes nothing: no credential is ``401``, any other
  caller ``403``, both before the subject DID is looked up and before
  anything is written or ledgered.

So ``home_node`` ("Your home node" in the member's ledger) is written
only by the member's own node, and ``user_device`` ("Your device") only
by the member's own device.

This holds in every deployment: it does not depend on
``LIFECAREID_REQUIRE_HOLDER_SIGNATURE`` or
``LIFECAREID_REQUIRE_CALLER_AUTH``. A credential that is presented is
verified (a bad signature or client secret is ``401``). An admitted
write for a subject lifecare.id does not know is ``404``.

schema.title: Response Record V1 Registry Record Post

401.description: No credential was presented, or a presented one failed (a bad signature, a wrong client secret). Checked before the subject DID is looked up.

403.description: The caller may not write this entry: a client that is not first party, a first-party client writing an entry that names neither itself nor a provider source, or a user_device entry; a holder writing an entry that names another holder, a home_node or user_device entry, or for a member with no active grant naming it; or a session writing for another member or anything but its own user_device entries. Checked before the subject DID is looked up.

404.description: An admitted caller wrote for a subject DID lifecare.id does not know.

get.description:
The chained resource history for a DID, newest first, keyset-paginated
on ``entry_hash``.

Who reads what (security audit F11, operator ruling of 2026-10-04):

* **the member**, with their own session (``Bearer lcs_...``) or a
  signature by their own DID: every entry (``read_as: "subject"``);
* **a signed holder** (``X-LifeCare-Signature``): only the entries whose
  ``holder_id`` is the DID that signed (``read_as: "holder"``). A holder
  with no entries for this DID gets an empty page, whether or not the DID
  is registered. ``before`` must be one of the holder's own entries.
  ``chain_valid`` checks each entry shown against its real predecessor in
  the member's chain, so it means the same as in the member's view;
* **anyone else** reads nothing: no credential is ``401``, any other
  caller (a client, another member's session) is ``403``, both before the
  DID is looked up.

This holds in every deployment: it does not depend on
``LIFECAREID_REQUIRE_HOLDER_SIGNATURE`` or
``LIFECAREID_REQUIRE_CALLER_AUTH``. A credential that is presented is
verified (a bad signature or client secret is ``401``).

post.description:
Validate a token for a resource server.

**Client authentication is required** (RFC 7662 section 2.1): present
your own client credentials, as HTTP Basic or as `client_id` and
`client_secret` in the body. Any registered client may introspect: a
service client, the operator's app client, a sandbox-registered developer
client. No credential is `401`; a member's session or a holder signature
is `403`. Both are answered before the token is looked up, whatever the
token, in every deployment.

parameters.description: `Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`: the calling resource server's own client credentials (RFC 7662 section 2.1). `client_id` and `client_secret` in the JSON body are accepted too.
parameters.name: authorization

schema.description: `Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`: the calling resource server's own client credentials (RFC 7662 section 2.1). `client_id` and `client_secret` in the JSON body are accepted too.
schema.title: Authorization

requestBody.description: The token to check. RFC 7662 section 2.1: a form body with `token` (and optionally `client_id` and `client_secret`, client_secret_post); a JSON body with the same fields is accepted too.

oneOf.description: The session token (`lcs_`) of a signed-in user: the caller IS this user.
oneOf.title: UserTokenIntrospection

oneOf.description:
A data-access token (`lc_`) issued to a requester against a grant.

Names whose data it unlocks (`resource_owner`) and never carries a
`subject_did`: the holder is an app, not the user.

aud.description: The resource (RFC 8707 `resource`, RFC 7662 `aud`) the token was issued for, present only on a token the OAuth authorization code flow issued. A resource server must refuse a token whose `aud` names another resource.
aud.title: Aud

oneOf.title: AccessTokenIntrospection

oneOf.description:
**Defined, not yet issued.** An actor exercising a subset of a subject's
authority (D-AG4b; RFC 8693 actor-claim semantics).

Semantics a resource server must implement before the first one is ever
minted:

* The actor acts **for** the subject, never **as** the subject. A delegated
  token can no more satisfy a "the caller is the user" check than an access
  token can; `subject_did` here names on whose behalf the actor acts, not who
  the caller is.
* Scope, purpose and expiry are bounded by `parent_grant` and can never
  exceed it. No token of any type can create, widen or extend a grant; only
  the person can, through the passkey ceremony.
* Revoking the delegation kills the token and leaves the parent grant intact.

No issuance path exists, so introspection cannot return this shape today. It
is published so resource servers branch on `token_type` now.

parent_grant.description: consent_id of the grant that bounds this delegation
parent_grant.title: Parent Grant

scope.description: a single scope, as an access token carries
scope.title: Scope

subject_did.description: on whose behalf the actor acts
subject_did.title: Subject Did

trust.description: the actor's trust tier; see the agent-trust developer doc
trust.title: Trust

oneOf.title: DelegatedTokenIntrospection

oneOf.description: Expired, token-revoked, consent-revoked, or simply unknown.
oneOf.title: InactiveIntrospection

schema.title: Response Introspect V1 Token Introspect Post

200.description: Token status. `token_type` distinguishes the shapes: `user` (the caller is this user), `access` (an app may read this scope), and `delegated` (an actor acting for a subject inside a grant — defined here, never issued today). A resource server must fail closed on any `token_type` it does not implement.

401.description: No client credential was presented, or a presented one failed (a wrong or unknown client secret, a malformed Basic value, a bad holder signature). Answered before the token is looked up, so the answer is the same for every token.

403.description: The caller authenticated, but not as a client: a member's session or a holder signature. Answered before the token is looked up.

429.description: Too many requests for this route from this client (or, on the routes that send mail, for this mailbox) inside the window. Sent only while the deployment's rate limits are on (`LIFECAREID_RATE_LIMITS=enforce`); carries `Retry-After` in seconds. See docs/developers/security-and-compliance.md, Rate limits.
