post.summary: Authenticates a user and issues an access token plus a refresh token.
post.description:
Open to anonymous callers and rate limited to 10 requests per minute (fixed window,
shared by all callers of the auth endpoints). Token lifetimes come from configuration:
`Jwt:AccessTokenExpirationMinutes` (15) and `Jwt:RefreshTokenExpirationDays` (7).
Only a SHA-256 hash of the refresh token is persisted, so the raw value is returned here once.

200.description: Access token, refresh token, the access token's UTC expiry and the username.

post.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token.
post.description:
Open to anonymous callers (the refresh token itself is the credential) and rate limited
like login. Refresh tokens rotate: the presented token is revoked and its replacement
stored in the same save, so a token can only be redeemed once. Presenting an already
rotated token is treated as theft and revokes every refresh token of that user.

200.description: A new access token, a new refresh token and the access token's UTC expiry.

post.summary: Revokes the supplied refresh token, ending that one session.
post.description:
Other sessions of the same user keep working. Access tokens are validated by signature
and lifetime only, so an already issued access token stays usable until it expires.

post.summary: Revokes every refresh token of the calling user, ending all their sessions.
post.description:
The user is taken from the access token's subject claim. As with a single logout,
access tokens already handed out remain valid until they expire.

get.summary: Reports whether this instance still has no user account and needs the initial setup.

200.description: `needsSetup` — true while not a single user exists.

post.summary: Creates the first user account and signs it in.
post.description:
Open to anonymous callers, but only while the instance has no user at all — once one
exists the call is rejected. The password must be at least 8 characters long.

200.description: The same token set as a login: access token, refresh token, expiry and username.

get.summary: All saved selections, ordered by name.

put.summary: Saves a selection under a name; an existing one with that name is overwritten.
put.description:
The name is trimmed and matched case-insensitively, so saving "pumpe" updates "Pumpe" (and
adopts the new spelling). Addresses are trimmed and de-duplicated, keeping their order.
Validation: the name must be 1 to 100 characters, and there must be 1 to 8 addresses of at most
20 characters each, otherwise 400 and nothing is stored.

get.summary: Recent log entries from the in-memory buffer, optionally filtered.
Availability of the recording: when did the monitor run, and was the bus link up.
get.description:
Answers the question a hole in the telegram history cannot: a stretch reported as
`Up` was genuinely quiet on the bus, `BusDown` means the link was gone, and
`MonitorDown` means the process was not running (restart, standby, crash). Derived from
the one-per-minute heartbeats, so boundaries are accurate to about one minute. Stretches the
record does not cover — before the first beat was ever written, or past its retention —
report as `Unknown` and are deliberately not counted as outages.
The range is clamped to now, because the future is neither up nor down.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start (UTC). Defaults to seven days before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End (UTC). Defaults to now; a later value is clamped to now.

get.summary: Downloads a diagnostics zip: recent log files + a system-info.json.
Current state of the KNX bus link.
get.description:
Read-only — nothing is sent to the bus. Configuration is the configuration the live link
was established with and is null while disconnected; it is not necessarily the stored
configuration flagged active. ManualDisconnect is latched by a manual disconnect and keeps
the auto-connect worker from reconnecting until the next connect clears it.

200.description:
Connection flag, link state (Disconnected / Connecting / Connected), the
    manual-disconnect latch, the configuration currently in use, and recording health
    (link timestamps plus drop counters, both reset on restart).

post.summary: Opens the KNX bus link using the stored configuration with the given id.
post.description:
Touches the installation: an IP tunnel is opened (or the routing multicast group joined),
and received telegrams start flowing into the live view and the history again. An existing
link is torn down first. Clears the manual-disconnect latch, so the auto-connect worker may
keep the link up from here on. The request body is the bare configuration id (a JSON number).
Unknown id yields 404, a failed connect 400.

Ends telegram recording until the next connect. Latches manual-disconnect so the
auto-connect worker does not reconnect on its own; the next connect (or enabling
auto-connect) clears the latch. Succeeds even when no link is currently up.

post.summary:
Probes whether a stored configuration can reach the bus. Sends no group telegram and
changes nothing in the stored configuration.
post.description:
The probe uses a throwaway connection. If a live link is currently up it is paused for the
duration of the probe (freeing the gateway's tunnel slot) and restored afterwards, so
recording has a short gap — the frontend warns before triggering this while live.
For routing configurations the probe additionally listens up to five seconds for real bus
traffic: joining a multicast group succeeds locally even when no telegram can ever arrive.
That case is reported as JoinedWithoutTraffic and counts as a warning, not a failure
(Success stays true). Unknown id yields 404.

200.description: Success flag (false only for Failed), the outcome and a human-readable message.

get.summary:
Auto-connect state for the effective configuration (active one, else the first).
The active project is coupled to the bus link, so this governs whether it auto-connects.
get.description:
Read-only. When no configuration is stored at all, Enabled is reported as true (the default
for a configuration that has yet to be created).

200.description: The auto-connect flag and whether a bus link is currently up.

put.summary: Enables or disables auto-connect for the effective configuration.
put.description:
Applied immediately, not merely stored: enabling opens the bus link right away when none is
up (which clears the manual-disconnect latch), disabling closes an existing link. A failed
immediate connect is not reported as an error — the auto-connect worker retries on its next
tick (roughly every ten seconds). 404 when no configuration is stored.

200.description: The stored flag and whether a bus link is up afterwards.

post.summary:
Sends a GroupValueWrite to the bus. ⚠ Writes to the real KNX installation — the frontend
gates this behind an explicit confirmation dialog.
post.description:
This has a physical effect: the addressed actuators act on the value. The value is encoded
with the given datapoint type; without a DatapointType only a raw hex string ("0x01",
"01 02") is accepted, anything else is rejected. Answers 400 with Success=false when the
address is missing or unparsable, when no bus link is up, or when the value could not be
encoded for the given DPT.

post.summary: Sends a GroupValueRead; the response shows up as a normal telegram.
post.description:
Puts a telegram on the real installation, but changes no value — the addressed device
answers with its current one. The answering GroupValueResponse arrives through the normal
receive path and appears in the live view and the history; this endpoint itself only
confirms that the request was sent, it does not return the value. Answers 400 with
Success=false when the address is missing or unparsable, or when no bus link is up.

post.summary: Stores a new KNX interface configuration.
post.description:
Storing alone does not touch the bus: the entry is created inactive and no connection is
opened here. Connect explicitly, or leave AutoConnect on — the auto-connect worker picks a
configuration only while no link is up, preferring the active one, else the first with
AutoConnect enabled. Tunneling accepts a host name as well as an IP address; routing needs a
multicast IP. The tunnel options (protocol, requested address, IP Secure) are ignored for routing.

200.description: The stored configuration including its assigned id.

get.summary: Lists all stored KNX interface configurations.
Returns a single stored KNX interface configuration.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the stored configuration; 404 when it does not exist.

put.summary: Updates a stored KNX interface configuration; may re-establish the live bus link.
put.description:
When the connection actually changes (address, port, connection type or one of the tunnel
options), the configuration has AutoConnect enabled and a link is currently up, the running
connection is re-opened with the new settings — that briefly interrupts recording. Changing
only the physical address or the auto-connect flag does not trigger a reconnect. A failed
reconnect is not an error: the response reports Reconnected=false and the auto-connect
worker retries.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the stored configuration; 404 when it does not exist.

requestBody.description: The new values — same payload shape as when creating a configuration.

200.description: The stored configuration and whether the live link was re-established.

post.summary: Uploads an ETS project file and starts the import as a background job.
post.description:
Returns as soon as the job exists — the parse itself runs in the background, so poll
`GET imports/{id}` for progress. Only files ending in `.knxproj` are accepted,
and the request body is capped at 200 MB.

If the archive is password protected the job stops in `WaitingForInput` and lists what
it needs; feed those inputs to `POST imports/{id}/provide-input`, then the job continues
on its own. Re-uploading a project that was imported before is recognised by its ETS project
id and updates the existing project in place, so recorded telegrams keep their group-address
link. A genuinely new project is auto-activated when no other project is active yet.

200.description: The created import job: id, status, the step list and (once finished) the project id and counts.

get.summary: Returns the current state of an import job.
get.description:
Jobs are held in memory only. A job that has completed, failed or been cancelled is swept
an hour after it terminated (the cleanup worker runs every five minutes) and is reported as
not found from then on.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id returned by the upload call.

200.description: Status, overall progress, per-step detail and the outstanding requirements.

delete.summary: Marks an import job as cancelled.
delete.description:
This flips the job state only. A parse already running in the background is not interrupted
and a project it has written stays. Unknown job ids are accepted without effect.

post.summary: Supplies one requested input — project password, keyring file or keyring password — to a waiting import job.
post.description:
Each call fulfils exactly the requirement named in `type`; the keyring file is passed
Base64-encoded. The call is only accepted while the job is in `WaitingForInput` and
rejected otherwise.

Supplying the project password triggers a second look inside the now decryptable archive:
if KNX Secure devices turn up, an optional keyring file and keyring password requirement are
added and the job stays in `WaitingForInput`. As soon as every listed requirement is
marked fulfilled, the import resumes in the background — poll `GET imports/{id}` from
there. The password is not verified at this point; a wrong one surfaces as a failed job.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id of the waiting import.

requestBody.description: The values for the requirements the job is waiting on.

200.description: Per project: name, source file name, import date, active flag and the group-address and device counts.

get.summary: Returns one project together with its group addresses and devices.
get.description: Both lists come back complete and unpaged, so the response grows with the size of the project.

delete.summary: Deletes a project and everything parsed from it.
delete.description:
Removes the project's group addresses, devices, locations, communication objects, group
ranges and stored keyring material in one transaction. Recorded telegrams are kept but lose
their group-address link and are shown undecoded from then on. Deleting the active project
leaves no project active; the bus link stays up.

put.summary: Makes this project the active one.
put.description:
Activation is exclusive: any other active project is deactivated in the same transaction,
so at most one project is ever active. Afterwards the group-address cache is refreshed and
incoming telegrams resolve to this project's names and DPTs. The bus connection is
deliberately left untouched — activating decodes, it does not connect.

put.summary: Deactivates the project, leaving no project active.
put.description:
The group-address cache is cleared, so telegrams are shown undecoded — raw hex, without name
or DPT. Monitoring keeps running: the bus link stays up. Deactivating a project that is
already inactive succeeds and changes nothing.

get.summary: Reports what deleting this project would affect, for the confirmation dialog.

200.description:
The project's group-address and device counts plus the number of recorded telegrams mapped
to it. Those telegrams survive the deletion — they only lose their group-address mapping.

get.summary: Returns the project's locations (buildings, floors, rooms, …).
get.description:
A flat list, not a tree — the hierarchy is expressed through each entry's parent id. Every
entry also carries the device and group addresses assigned to that location.

get.summary: Returns the project's communication objects, optionally only those linked to one group address.
get.description:
Each entry is enriched with the name, manufacturer and product name of the device behind its
physical address, as far as that device is part of the project. Sorted by device address,
then by object number.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Project id.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Group address (`m/m/s`). When set, only objects whose group-address link matches it exactly are returned.

get.summary: Returns the project's group ranges — the named main and middle groups — ordered by range start.
Resolves a single device of the project by its physical address.
get.description:
The address is matched exactly, and an unknown project id is reported the same way as an
unknown device.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Project id.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Physical address (`a.l.d`) to look up. Required.

post.summary: Attaches a keyring (`.knxkeys`) to an already imported project.
post.description:
Multipart upload of the file plus its password; both are required and only files ending in
`.knxkeys` are accepted. Any keyring material previously stored for the project is
replaced — both the decrypted per-key rows and the raw keyring bytes, which KNX Data Secure
needs when it loads the keyring at connect time. Because of that the keyring password is
stored with the project. A wrong password or an unreadable file is reported as a client error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Project the keyring belongs to.

requestBody.description: Password of the keyring file. Required.

200.description: How many keys were read, split into group-address and tool keys, and whether a backbone key is present.

get.summary: Current recording settings: hot-buffer size and cold-archive options.
get.description:
Served from the cached snapshot that the recording services themselves read, so this needs
no database round-trip.

put.summary: Updates the recording settings; they take effect on the running recording.
put.description:
The values are persisted and swapped into the snapshot the recording workers read, so no
restart is needed. What the fields do:
HotBufferMaxCount is the number of telegrams kept in the database — a retention pass
periodically deletes everything older than the newest HotBufferMaxCount rows, so lowering
the value discards the oldest telegrams. Deletion happens chunked on the following passes,
not the instant the value is saved.
ArchiveEnabled toggles the additional NDJSON+gzip day-files; switching it off stops new
writes but leaves existing archive files untouched.
ArchiveRetentionDays deletes archive day-files older than that many days, null keeps them
forever. The sweep runs at startup and at the daily file rollover, so a shortened retention
only takes effect at the next sweep.
HistoryWriteIntervalSeconds collects telegrams for that long and writes them to the history
in one transaction (0 = right away). It spares SD cards and eMMC; a power cut loses what is
still buffered, the live view is not delayed. The NDJSON archive syncs on the same rhythm.
Validation: HotBufferMaxCount must be greater than 0, ArchiveRetentionDays must be null or
greater than 0, HistoryWriteIntervalSeconds 0 to 600 — otherwise 400 and nothing is changed.

200.description: The settings as they are now in effect.

get.summary:
Numeric time-series per destination group address. Each telegram's decoded value is
projected to a number (leading numeric token, else On/Off-style boolean → 1/0); telegrams
that yield no number are skipped. The result is down-sampled to at most maxPoints per address.
get.description:
A number is taken from the decoded value as the first numeric token (leading minus and
    decimal point or comma allowed), so "21.5 °C" becomes 21.5; failing that, a known
    boolean-ish word (On/Off, True/False, Open/Closed, Up/Down, …) becomes 1 or 0. Anything
    else is dropped, and an address whose telegrams yield no number at all is omitted from the
    response instead of appearing empty. `unit` is whatever remains of the first chartable
    sample once the number is stripped — "°C" for "21.5 °C"; for a boolean sample, which holds
    no number to strip, the word itself remains.
    Down-sampling keeps the minimum and the maximum of each bucket rather than every n-th
point, so spikes survive a wide range. maxPoints is the budget per address, not the
exact count — the result may be shorter, and downSampled plus totalPoints
(the numeric points before down-sampling) report what happened.
    At most 200 000 rows are read per request. When the range holds more, the newest
rows win, the older end is missing and truncated is true — a chart is easier to
distrust when it starts late than when it ends early.
    carry is the last chartable value before from (with its original
timestamp), so a client can draw the curve from the left edge instead of starting it at
the first telegram inside the range, since a KNX value holds until the next telegram. It is null
when there is no earlier value, and always null when truncated is true, since the
missing older end would sit between it and the first point. An address with a carry value
but no telegram inside the range is returned with an empty points list.
    A timestamp without a zone designator (from=2026-07-30T00:00:00) is interpreted as
server local time, not UTC. Send ISO-8601 with a trailing Z to be unambiguous.
Returned point timestamps are always UTC with a trailing Z.

parameters.name: addresses
parameters.description:
Comma-separated destination group addresses (e.g. `1/2/3,1/2/4`). Duplicates are
dropped and at most the first 8 are used; the rest are silently ignored. Missing or empty
yields an empty series list rather than an error.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the range (inclusive). Defaults to 24 hours before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the range (inclusive). Defaults to now. A reversed range is swapped, not rejected.

parameters.name: maxPoints
parameters.description: Maximum points returned per address after down-sampling. Default 2000, clamped to 1..10000.

200.description:
One entry per requested address that has chartable data, in the order the addresses were
requested, plus a `truncated` flag for the whole request.

get.summary:
Telegram volume histogram over [from,to] split into buckets equal buckets,
plus the total count. Backs the statistics "telegrams over time" / msg-per-second view.
get.description:
Counts all telegrams in the range — there is no address, source or type filter here. Every
    bucket is returned, including empty ones, so the buckets always tile the range gap-free.
    `bucketMs` is the bucket width in milliseconds and is fractional: the range is divided
    into equal parts rather than snapped to a round interval, and each bucket's `t` is its
    start. Divide a count by `bucketMs` to get a rate.
    A timestamp without a zone designator is interpreted as server local time, not UTC. Send
ISO-8601 with a trailing Z to be unambiguous.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the range (inclusive). Defaults to 24 hours before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the range (inclusive). Defaults to now. A reversed range is swapped, not rejected.

parameters.name: buckets
parameters.description: Number of equal-width buckets. Default 60, clamped to 1..500.

get.summary:
Activity heatmap: telegram counts bucketed by (weekday, hour-of-day) over [from,to].
Binning is done in the caller's local time via tz (minutes the local
zone is behind UTC, i.e. JS getTimezoneOffset()), so "18:00 Monday" means the user's 18:00.
get.description:
The grid is always 7 × 24 (weekday 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday, then hour 0..23) and is
    filled with counts, not averages: a 30-day range puts roughly four Mondays into the same
    cell. Counts all telegrams in the range — there is no address, source or type filter.
    A timestamp without a zone designator is interpreted as server local time, not UTC. Send
ISO-8601 with a trailing Z to be unambiguous. Note that tz shifts only the
binning, not the range boundaries.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the range (inclusive). Defaults to 24 hours before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the range (inclusive). Defaults to now. A reversed range is swapped, not rejected.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description:
Minutes the display zone is behind UTC, exactly as JavaScript's
`Date.getTimezoneOffset()` reports it (CEST = -120). Default 0 bins in UTC. A fixed
offset is applied to the whole range, so a range spanning a DST change is binned with one
offset throughout.

get.summary:
The busiest destination group addresses and the busiest senders over [from,to], for the
bus-load breakdown in the statistics view.
get.description:
Both lists are ranked by telegram count, highest first, ties broken by address, and hold
    at most limit entries each. `share` is the percentage of all
    telegrams in the range (`total`), `perHour` the count divided by the length of
    the range in hours (`rangeHours`), so a short range is not mistaken for a quiet one.
    Names and DPTs come from the currently active project: an address that is not part
of it, or a range recorded under an older project, shows whatever today's project says,
or null. Counts all telegrams in the range, every message type included.
    A timestamp without a zone designator is interpreted as server local time, not UTC. Send
ISO-8601 with a trailing Z to be unambiguous.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the range (inclusive). Defaults to 24 hours before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the range (inclusive). Defaults to now. A reversed range is swapped, not rejected.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per list. Default 20, clamped to 1..100.

get.description:
Reads the database hot tier only — the day archive on disk is served by the
    `archive/*` endpoints. Filters: `from`/`to`, `address` (destination
    group address), `source` (individual address), `type` or `types`
    (comma-separated, OR-combined and taking precedence over `type`) and `q`
    (free-text LIKE across source, destination, decoded value, GA name and DPT).
    Paging is keyset-based over (Timestamp, Id), not offset-based: pass the nextCursor
of the previous response as cursor to get the following page. The cursor is opaque;
a malformed one yields 400. pageSize defaults to 100 and is clamped to 1..1000.
order=asc sorts oldest first, any other value newest first — the sort direction must
stay the same while paging, because the cursor is interpreted relative to it.
    from/to are compared against the stored UTC timestamps without any conversion
(unlike the chart endpoints), so pass UTC values.

200.description:
One page of telegrams plus `hasMore` and `nextCursor`; `nextCursor` is null
on the last page.

delete.summary: Permanently deletes the entire telegram history (the DB hot-tier). Irreversible.
delete.description:
Deletes every row in one statement — the request carries no filter, so there is no way to
clear only part of the history. The SQLite WAL is checkpointed afterwards so the file
shrinks. Archive files on disk are not touched and stay downloadable.

200.description: An object with a single `deleted` property: the number of rows removed.

get.summary: Number of telegrams matching a filter.
get.description:
Takes the same query parameters as `GET /api/telegrams`, but only the filtering ones
have an effect — `cursor`, `pageSize` and `order` are ignored. Counts the
database hot tier only.

200.description: An object with a single `count` property.

get.summary: Server-streamed CSV export over the full filtered DB range.
get.description:
Accepts the same filters as `GET /api/telegrams`, but exports every matching row:
    `cursor` and `pageSize` are ignored and there is no row limit. Rows are always
    written chronologically (oldest first), regardless of `order`.
    The response is streamed while the query is still running, so the body starts arriving
before the row count is known and no Content-Length is sent. The header line is
always written, even when nothing matches. Encoding is UTF-8 without BOM; fields that
contain a comma, quote or line break are quoted with doubled inner quotes. The filename is
knx-telegrams-{UTC timestamp}.csv.
    Columns: Timestamp, SourceAddress, SourceName, SourceLocation, DestinationAddress, GroupAddressName,
Functions, DatapointType, MessageType, Value, ValueDecoded. SourceLocation is the sender's full
building path ("Building › Floor › Room"), Functions the ETS functions of the destination
joined by "; "; both resolve against the active project like SourceName. Value is the raw payload as uppercase hex without
separators. Timestamp is the UTC value in ISO-8601 round-trip format but carries no
zone designator — unlike the JSON responses, which end in Z. GroupAddressName and
DatapointType are empty when the telegram has no linked group address; SourceName is empty
when the sender is not a device of the active project.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Only `csv` is supported; any other value yields 400.

get.summary: Lists the days available in the cold-tier archive, newest first.
get.description:
The archive holds one NDJSON file per UTC day, written independently of the database hot
tier and unaffected by its retention or by `DELETE /api/telegrams`. Finished days are
gzipped (`compressed: true`), the current day stays plain and is still being appended
to, so its size grows between calls. `sizeBytes` is the size on disk, i.e. the
compressed size for gzipped days. Archiving is opt-in via the recording settings, so the
list is empty as long as nothing has been archived.

200.description: One entry per day with `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `fileName`, `sizeBytes` and `compressed`.

get.summary: Downloads the raw archive file of one UTC day.
get.description:
Serves the gzipped file (`application/gzip`) when it exists and falls back to the
plain, still-open file of the current day (`application/x-ndjson`); 404 when neither
is present for that day. The payload is NDJSON — one JSON object per line with the keys
`t` (UTC timestamp), `s` (source address), `d` (destination address),
`mt` (message type), `r` (raw value) and `v` (decoded value, omitted when
there is none). The current day is served while the writer still holds it open, so it can
be missing the last few seconds — the writer flushes on an interval.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Archive day as `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC). Any other shape yields 400.

info.title: Radiation Tracking Backend
info.description:
Backend service for the TUHH Big Data radiation tracking project (Topic C).

Consumes the processed Kafka streams (`radiation.clean`, `radiation.alerts`,
`radiation.aggregated`), serves them to the map frontend, and publishes the
global pipeline thresholds back to Flink via the `config.updates` topic.
Area/timespan filtering is **per client** on the read path (ADR-017): `/recent`
query params and the `/ws/stream` subscribe message below — one client's
filters never affect another client or the pipeline.

## WebSocket: `/ws/stream`

Live push of processed events (not part of the OpenAPI paths below — WebSockets
are outside the spec):

* **Origin policy** — auth-less but origin-checked: a browser `Origin` header
  must be in the `CORS_ORIGINS` allowlist (`*` allows all; a missing header —
  curl, tests — is allowed). Disallowed origins are closed with code `1008`
  before the upgrade.
* **On connect** the client receives a catch-up snapshot of recent
  `radiation.clean` events, then the live stream.
* **Message envelope** — every frame is
  `{"type": "clean" | "alert" | "aggregated", "data": {...}}`; for `clean`,
  `data` is a `RadiationEvent`. One socket multiplexes all three streams.
* **Per-client view filter (ADR-017)** — the client may send
  `{"type": "subscribe", "area": {"min_lat", "max_lat", "min_lon", "max_lon"},
  "timespan": {"start", "end"}}` at any time; both parts optional, nulls widen
  the view back. Only this connection's live stream is narrowed (the catch-up
  snapshot is unfiltered — clients filter it locally). Malformed subscribe
  frames are ignored and the previous filter kept.
* **Backpressure** — per client, `clean`/`aggregated` state coalesces
  latest-wins per key; `alert` frames are FIFO and never coalesced, and each
  flush delivers alerts first.

get.description: Always HTTP 200 while the app is serving (the image HEALTHCHECK and the compose `service_healthy` gate depend on it); a Kafka component that could not reach the broker is reported as `degraded` in the body.

post.summary: Update filter settings and publish them to Flink
post.description: Merges the partial payload onto the active config, validates the merged state, and publishes the **full merged** settings to the `config.updates` Kafka topic (Flink broadcast state). The change is visible on the map within seconds. Publish-before-commit: on broker failure nothing changes. On the droplet this write is gated by an `X-Config-Token` header when `CONFIG_WRITE_TOKEN` is set (no-op locally).

202.description: Successful Response

403.description: `X-Config-Token` did not match the configured write token.

422.description: Validation failed — thresholds must satisfy warn < danger (also re-checked on the merged state), lat/lon ranges need min < max, and a timespan needs start < end.

503.description: `config.updates` topic unavailable — the settings were NOT committed; backend and Flink still agree on the previous state.

get.summary: Newest buffered clean events (cursor-paginated, per-client filters)
get.description: Returns the newest `radiation.clean` events from the in-memory ring buffer for seeding the map. Paging walks backwards through the buffered window via the opaque `next_cursor`; events evicted from the buffer before a client pages back to them are gone (best-effort by design). `limit` is clamped, never rejected, so the map always gets a usable response. The optional bounding-box (`min_lat`/`max_lat`/`min_lon`/`max_lon`, all-or-none) and time-range (`start`/`end`, both-or-none) parameters are **per-client view filters** (ADR-017): they narrow only this response, never the pipeline or other clients.

info.title: Zung Member API
info.summary: Read a SACCO/MFI member's own loans, savings and wallets, and submit loan applications.
info.description:
The Zung Member API is the API behind the Zung mobile app. It lets you build
**member-facing** channels on top of a Zung-powered SACCO or MFI: a branded
mobile app, a WhatsApp/USSD bot, a member portal.

## Who a token belongs to

Every token is issued to **one member** (a client with portal access) and
can only ever see that member's own data. It is not a back-office API: it
cannot list other members, post transactions, or read the institution's
books.

## Authentication

1. `POST /login` with the institution's Zung subdomain (`business`), the
   member's username or email (`login`) and password.
2. Send the returned `token` on every other request as
   `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
3. `POST /logout` revokes it. Tokens do not expire on their own, so revoke
   them when the member signs out.

Always send `Accept: application/json`; without it, authentication errors
may come back as redirects instead of JSON.

## Prerequisites on the institution's side

Login only succeeds if the institution has the client portal (CRM module)
in its Zung subscription, and the member has a portal login that is
active, allowed to log in, and linked to their client profile.

## Errors

Every error body has the same shape: `{"message": "..."}`. Validation
errors (`422`) report the first failing field only.

## Rate limits

Limits are counted per client IP address:

- `POST /login`: 10 requests per minute.
- Everything else: 60 requests per minute.

Exceeding a limit returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds).
Call the API from the member's own device where you can; a server that
proxies many members' traffic shares one IP's allowance.

## Lists

List endpoints return the member's **50 most recent** records, newest
first. There is no pagination.

## Numbers and dates

Money amounts are JSON numbers (not strings). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`
strings in the institution's local calendar; `submitted_at` on loan
applications is a full ISO 8601 timestamp.

AtriumDocument.title: ATRIUM document record
AtriumDocument.description: Per-document record built by accretion across the ATRIUM pipeline, schema 2.0 (doc-schema-v2, atrium-project#84). It holds content only: the identity of the original, its text in a form the enrichment steps work on, and what they add. No run data and no licence (D1, D2): which run wrote which blocks and fields is named by that run's paradata `result` (RO-Crate 1.2 / Process Run Crate 0.5 CreateAction). No copy of the layout (D26): blocks, tables, reading-order roles and page verdicts stay in the document's stored `atr/docproc-json`, and each line names its docproc block. The positional blocks (pages, content, lines) have one writer, the record builder (ocr-postprocess, D20). Keys removed in 2.0 are refused by name; any other unknown key passes, so a newer 2.x minor's additions survive a tool that vendored an older 2.x schema (rule 6). Produced by atrium_document.py; a 1.x record is migrated on load (migrate_document).
AtriumDocument.$comment: A record carries evidence that something was written into it: the source (the seed's identity) or at least one content block. A stage that ran and wrote nothing is refused (the #54 floor, without stamps since 2.0).

schema_version.description: Record schema version, MAJOR 2. A newer MAJOR than the reading tool supports must be refused; an older one is migrated (atrium_document.migrate_document).

record_type.description: 'atrium-document' for the normal linear accretion; '-merged' when parallel partial records were folded.

doc_id.description: Stable document identifier, carried unchanged by every tool. In the AMČR pilot it is the AMČR file id, written by the seed before the first stage (atrium-project#71); a tool keeps the baseline's value and never re-derives it from a file name.

source.description: The ORIGINAL input, named by the archive's SHA-512 (contract §5, H1). Intake (the AMČR seed, whose profile requires sha512, filename and media_type) writes the identity fields, first-writer-wins; the record builder adds language, page_count and origin. No path, no other digest. Absent on a standalone run that had no seed (rule 3).

sha512.description: SHA-512 of the original's bytes as the archive computed it (AMČR: the Fedora digest), lower-case hex. Written by the seed and carried unchanged by every tool (atrium-project#71).

language.description: Languages of the text, ISO 639-1 codes, dominant first.

origin.description: How the text was obtained, descriptive only (#84 §1): `digital` the text layer of a born-digital file, `atr` the ATR step, `legacy` converted PCSS (ABBYY) ALTO. It selects no writer: the positional blocks have one.

sha256.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — the original is named by its sha512 only (§6).

page_categories.description: Owner: page-classification. Predicted category per page label, for the pages that needed ATR (H3). Values come from the `page-category` scheme in the hub-canonical atrium_vocab.py -- 11 concepts, `atrium_vocab.labels_for('page-category')` -- and each has a stable URI via `atrium_vocab.concept_uri('page-category', value)`. Deliberately NOT constrained by `enum`: page-classification derives its label list from the filesystem at runtime (utils.py collect_images), so an enum here would turn a naming slip into a hard pipeline failure instead of the advisory NOTE the registry raises. See docs/skos_strategy.md 4.

pages.description: Owner of the rows: the record builder (ocr-postprocess), one row for every page of the original, empty pages included (D29). page-classification adds category fields to the pages that needed ATR; nlp-enrich adds teitok_surface. Field-level ownership — never co-mutated. The page's text-layer verdict and needs_atr live in docproc's routing (D27).

page.description: The printed page label as a string, so 'iv' or 'A-1' survive; written by the record builder, and what lines[].page and entities[].page name. Consumers must NOT derive ordering from it — use page_index.

page_index.description: The physical page number, 1-based: the row's key, the join key with docproc `pageNumber` (H2) and the ordering key. Every writer of a page row passes it.

content_status.description: `text`: the page has text; `empty`: it has none — no lines, no page score, counted apart in quality_summary (D29; D18 rule 7).

category.description: page-classification, on the pages that needed ATR (H3).

teitok_surface.description: Logical TEITOK <surface> id — an identifier, never an image path.

text_layer.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — the page verdict lives in the stored docproc's routing (D27).

needs_ocr.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — became `needs_atr` in docproc's routing (D27).

needs_ocr_reason.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — its reason is docproc's, with needs_atr (D27).

ocr.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — the engine is the producer's paradata (D9).

allOf.$comment: An empty page carries no page score (D18 rule 7).

content.description: Owner: the record builder. The text of the document, rebuilt in docproc's reading order, so the record never holds partial text (H8).

reading_order.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — reading order is docproc's (D26).

lines.description: Owner of the rows: the record builder (ocr-postprocess): text, box, docproc block, text source and box precision, and — as the line-quality model's owner (D18) — categ, quality_score and lang for every line. nlp-enrich adds lemma, upos, feats and teitok_ref. Field-level ownership. NOTE for validators: only page+line are required, so a row stripped of its text by a field-ownership filter still validates here — the round-trip assertion belongs in the writing tool.

page.description: Page LABEL, matching a pages[].page. A string for the same reason as there — 'iv' and 'A-1' must survive — so a writer must not pass an integer here: merge_block() keys rows on it, and a consumer sorting on int(page) needs pages[].page_index to order non-numeric labels.

line.description: 1-based, in reading order within the page; with `page`, the row's key.

bbox.description: The line's box in the one coordinate space ($defs/bbox); how it was obtained is bbox_precision.

block.description: The id of the docproc block this line belongs to (D26), e.g. `p3-b7`; on a mixed document, the ATR block that contains a kept text-layer line (H6).

text_source.description: Where the line's text came from (D25): the born-digital text layer, the ATR, or converted PCSS ALTO.

bbox_precision.description: How the box was obtained (D16, D25): measured for the line by its producer, derived from its docproc block, or none.

unit.description: Written by the record builder only: `block` marks a row that holds a whole docproc block scored as one unit, because the block came without lines and with no line break in its text (D18 rule 5). The row keeps its categ and quality_score (rule 1) but stays out of the calibrated statistics: pages[].quality_score and quality_summary.lines.by_categ (counted as quality_summary.lines.block_units). Absent: a visual line. The name is proposed by this implementation (atrium-project#84).

categ.description: Line category, the five values of the `line-category` scheme only (D18 rule 2). Written by the record builder for every line, whatever its text source. digital-convert's decode verdict (Garbage, Inverted) is a flag on docproc lines, never a category here.

quality_score.description: From the text alone: one model, one set of constants, one band scheme for every source (D18 rule 3).

lemma.description: nlp-enrich: UD lemma of the line's dominant token/lead form.

group_id.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — layout grouping is docproc's (D26).

style.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — layout cues are docproc's (D26).

entities.description: Owner: nlp-enrich; keyword-extract writes pid. `translation_en` is RESERVED, not in the pilot (contract §5). Carries all three tagsets so no mapping is lost. `page` and `line` are the record's line key; `bbox` is in the one coordinate space.

type_onto.description: OntoNotes v5 — the default configured NameTag tagset.

translation_en.description: RESERVED, written by no tool. Declared for the translator, which runs before nlp-enrich creates entities[]; English is produced only for free-text metadata in the AMČR pilot (atrium-project#70).

pid.description: FAIR ontology cross-references — the ARIADNE/GoTriple hook. Null until resolved.

translations.description: RESERVED, not in the pilot (contract §5): the translator's metadata-en is a record-level job and writes nothing into this record.

enrichment.description: Owner: keyword-extract (llm-enrich before 2026-10-01). Superset of the LLM document schema, plus the explicit page citation.

locator.description: Short verbatim snippet copied from the document.

page.description: Page label from the nearest PAGE_BREAK / '## Page N' marker.

teater_category.description: Single most relevant TEATER/AMCR vocabulary category: the source label as the vocabulary spells it (e.g. `kostel`), not an ATRIUM theme.

teater_category_ids.description: The AMCR and TEATER records `teater_category` stands for, by id: its own and those of the same label the vocabulary build merged into it. Written by keyword-extract; the RO-Crate names them by their source URIs (`https://api.aiscr.cz/id/<id>`, `https://teater.aiscr.cz/id/<id>`).

source.description: `amcr` or `teater`.

id.description: The record's id in its source (`HES-…` for AMCR).

keywords.description: Owner: keyword-extract (atrium-project#73). The STATISTICAL keywords of the document and of each page: KeyBERT by default, YAKE or KER (`legacy`) when a run asks for them; one run writes one method's lists. The controlled-vocabulary keywords are `enrichment`'s and never appear here, and the two kinds are never merged into one list. A score means something different per method (KeyBERT: a cosine in [0, 1]; YAKE: normalised per document to [0, 1]; KER: an occurrence count), so compare scores only within one list; `rank` orders every list from 1.

pages.description: The same per page, in page order; empty when the run asked for document keywords only.

quality_summary.description: Owner: the record builder, ocr-postprocess (atrium-project#73). A deterministic read-out of the stored quality fields, recomputed by atrium_document.quality_summary() whenever ocr-postprocess writes or scores pages and lines: statistics of `pages[].quality_score` and line counts per `lines[].categ`. Numbers only: no band, no threshold, and no tool reads it to route or refuse a document. `pages[].quality_score` stays the authoritative signal; a consumer that needs bands computes them from these numbers with its own thresholds.

pages.description: `total`: rows in pages[]; `empty`: those with content_status empty; `scored`: those with a quality_score; mean, median, min and max of those scores, absent when none is scored.

empty.description: Pages with content_status empty, counted apart (D18 rule 7).

lines.description: `total`: rows in lines[]; `by_categ`: visual lines per `categ` value (the `line-category` scheme); `block_units`: rows marked `unit: block`, kept out of `by_categ` (D18 rule 5). Visual lines without a category are `total` minus `block_units` minus the sum of `by_categ`.

provenance.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — run data and the calculated licence leave the record (D1, D2); the run's paradata describe it.

assembled.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — no stamps (D1): the run's paradata `result` names the blocks and fields it wrote.

derived_from.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — inputs are named in the run's paradata `object`, by distribution name and SHA-512 (D1, D23).

regenerable.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — a regeneration recipe is run data (D1).

tables.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — a table is docproc's `cellGrid`; its text stays in the record as lines (D26).

file.title: File
file.description: The XML to translate, its name ending in `.xml`: an ALTO page, or a metadata record such as AMČR's. Its root element decides which, unless `is_alto` is sent.

document_json.title: Document Json
document_json.description: Optional ATRIUM document record, or an AMČR seed (`doc_id`, `source`): its `doc_id` names the outputs. Since record schema 2.0 (atrium-project#84) the translator writes nothing into it: it comes back unchanged, as the second part of the multipart/mixed response, or as `document_json` with `response_format=json`. One that cannot be opened is refused (422 `invalid_record`). An empty part counts as none.

xpaths.title: Xpaths
xpaths.description: For a metadata record, required: the fields to translate, one XPath per line (AMČR's list, aiscr-webamcr#3570). The service has no default list; a metadata record without one is refused (422). Ignored for ALTO.

source_lang.title: Source Lang
source_lang.description: The source language, or `auto` (the default) to detect it. Also read from the query.

target_lang.title: Target Lang
target_lang.description: The target language; `en` by default. Also read from the query.

is_alto.title: Is Alto
is_alto.description: `true`: ALTO XML; `false`: AMČR metadata XML. Unset (since v1.6.0-beta): the upload's root element decides, `alto` or any other. Until then unset meant `true`, so a metadata record sent without it came back untranslated. Also read from the query.

fast_align.title: Fast Align
fast_align.description: ALTO only: distribute a block's translation over its lines by word counts instead of translating each line as an anchor (the command line's --fast-align): far fewer calls, coarser line splits. Default false. Also read from the query.

xsd_strict.title: Xsd Strict
xsd_strict.description: With `XSD_PATH` set, for a metadata record: `true` refuses a translation that does not validate (422), `false` returns it with `xsd_valid: false`. Default: the `XSD_STRICT` setting. Also read from the query.

include_log.title: Include Log
include_log.description: `true`: also return the translation log, the command line's `<doc>_log.csv` (`log_csv` with `response_format=json`, else a part of the multipart/mixed answer). Default false. Also read from the query.

include_record.title: Include Record
include_record.description: Kept for compatibility. Since record schema 2.0 the translator writes no record, so a record comes back only when `document_json` was sent. Also read from the query.

output_mode.title: Output Mode
output_mode.description: `replace` (the default, or the OUTPUT_MODE setting) or `append` — see issue #46. Also read from the query.

response_format.title: Response Format
response_format.description: `xml` (the default): the translated XML, or multipart/mixed when a record was sent or `include_record` or `include_log` is true. `json`: one `TranslateResponse` object with the XML as text, the record as `document_json` and the log as `log_csv`. Also read from the query.

@context.title: @Context
@context.description: The JSON-LD context: RO-Crate 1.2, plus the terms ATRIUM adds.

@type.title: @Type
@type.description: `CreateAction`.

name.title: Name
name.description: A human-readable name of the run.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the action describes.

instrument.title: Instrument
instrument.description: The tool: a `SoftwareApplication` with `version`, its release page as `@id`, its repository as `url` and its authors as `creator`.

containerImage.title: Containerimage
containerImage.description: The image the service ran as (`ATRIUM_RUNNER_IMAGE`): `registry`, `name`, `tag`.

object.title: Object
object.description: The inputs, each by AMČR distribution name (`name`) and SHA-512 (`sha512`): the uploaded file and the record version sent with it. An input that is not stored carries `stored: false` (D23).

result.title: Result
result.description: The outputs, by distribution name and SHA-512. The record's (`atrium/document-json`) names the blocks and fields the call wrote in `recordFields`; an output that is not stored carries `stored: false`.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: The organisation operating the service (`ATRIUM_RUN_AGENT`); absent when it is not set.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why the run failed, with `FailedActionStatus`.

paradataRecord.title: Paradatarecord
paradataRecord.description: The run's atrium_paradata record (schema 3.0: no calculated licence), as the tool wrote it.

CreateAction.title: CreateAction
CreateAction.description:
The RO-Crate `CreateAction` of this call: its provenance (atrium-project#71 R2).

One Process Run Crate 0.5 action per call, as nested JSON-LD, built by
`atrium_rocrate.create_action()`; the same document an archive stores as the run's paradata
file. It names the tool as its `instrument` (with `version`, its release page as `@id` and its
authors as `creator`), the image as `containerImage`, the inputs as `object`, what the call
wrote as `result`, the `agent`, `startTime`/`endTime` and `actionStatus`, and the run's whole
paradata record as `paradataRecord`. Every service returns it with a successful response; its
`@id` is the run's `run_uuid`. Since doc-schema-v2 (atrium-project#84) the record carries no
stamps: the `result` names the record blocks AND fields the call wrote, and every input and output
is named by its AMČR distribution name and SHA-512.

status.title: Status
status.description: The HTTP status, as an integer.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: A registered reason code, listed with its statuses in the spec's `x-atrium-reason-codes`, or null when no code is registered for the cause. An open string: a release may add a code, but never renames or removes one.

limit.description: Only with `limit_exceeded`: the limit and the input's size.

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: The request-validation problems, or a structured detail.

accepted.title: Accepted
accepted.description: Only with `unsupported_media_type`: the file extensions or media types the endpoint reads.

cause.title: Cause
cause.description: A finer, unregistered cause (for example a reader's code). Informational; it may change.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: The body of every error a service returns (§4.4).

status.title: Status
status.description: `ok`, or `degraded` (HTTP 503) when the deep check fails or the replica drains.

in_flight.title: In Flight
in_flight.description: Deep check only: requests being served.

draining.title: Draining
draining.description: Deep check only: the replica is shutting down.

HealthBody.title: HealthBody
HealthBody.description: `GET /health`: liveness, and with `?deep=true` a check of the backends.

env.title: Env
env.description: The environment variable that sets it; null for a derived limit.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the current value came from: `env`, `config`, `default` or `derived`.

default.title: Default
default.description: The built-in default (not for a derived limit).

derived_from.title: Derived From
derived_from.description: For a derived limit: the settings it is computed from.

zero_means_unlimited.title: Zero Means Unlimited
zero_means_unlimited.description: True when 0 switches the limit off.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The `/info` `limits` key.

value.title: Value
value.description: The limit's value when it applied.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: What it did: `sampled` or `split`. (`trimmed`, `skipped` and `stopped` fail the request since doc-schema-v2, D13; they appear only in notes written before it.)

count.title: Count
count.description: How many times it applied.

LimitNote.title: LimitNote
LimitNote.description:
One limit that shaped a result without refusing it (the paradata `limits`, §4.5).

Since doc-schema-v2 (D13) only sampling and splitting are recorded: a limit that trims, skips
or stops content fails the request instead.

key.title: Key
key.description: The `/info` `limits` key of the limit.

env.title: Env
env.description: The environment variable that sets it; null for a derived limit.

value.title: Value
value.description: The limit's effective value.

observed.title: Observed
observed.description: What the input measured; null when it is not known exactly.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: Only when a limit trimmed, skipped or stopped content during processing (D13): that effect. The step failed; `observed` is the number of units affected.

LimitRef.title: LimitRef
LimitRef.description: Which limit a `limit_exceeded` refusal is about, and by how much.

status.title: Status
status.description: `ready`; or `starting` or `draining`, both with HTTP 503.

type.title: Type
type.description: What the upload was translated as: `alto` (ALTO XML) or `metadata` (AMČR XML).

content.title: Content
content.description: The translated XML document, as UTF-8 text.

limits_applied.title: Limits Applied
limits_applied.description: Every limit that shaped the translation without refusing it (also the response header).

document_json.description: When a record was sent as `document_json`: that record, unchanged. The translator writes nothing into the record (record schema 2.0, atrium-project#84).

document_json_schema_error.title: Document Json Schema Error
document_json_schema_error.description: Only when the returned record does not validate: the schema error (the sent record's).

log_filename.title: Log Filename
log_filename.description: With `include_log=true`: the log's file name, as the command line writes it.

log_csv.title: Log Csv
log_csv.description: With `include_log=true`: the translation log (`file, page_num, line_num, text_<src>, text_<tgt>, status`), the `<doc>_log.csv` of the command line, as CSV text.

xsd_valid.title: Xsd Valid
xsd_valid.description: Only for a metadata record when the deployment sets `XSD_PATH`: whether the translation validates.

xsd_errors.title: Xsd Errors
xsd_errors.description: When `xsd_valid` is false: the validator's messages.

paradata.description: The call's paradata: its Process Run Crate `CreateAction` (paradata 3.0, atrium-project#84). For a metadata record, `object` is `metadata` and `result` is `metadata-en`, each by SHA-512; the field list and the language pair are parameters.

TranslateResponse.title: TranslateResponse
TranslateResponse.description: `/translate` with `response_format=json`: the translated XML and the record in one object.

service.title: Service
service.description: The tool id, which is the repository name.

version.title: Version

Pages converted from PCSS ALTO whose original cannot be matched may be in px (canvas.unit).

AtriumDocument_canvas.description: The displayed page's size and the unit of every box on it (D28).

AtriumDocument_line_ref.description: A reference to one lines[] row by its natural key — the same key BLOCK_KEY_FIELDS['lines'] merges on. Survives merge_document_records(), which an array index does not.

AtriumDocument_statistical_keyword.description: One statistical keyword (`keywords`): the phrase, the method that found it, the method's own score (higher is more relevant) and its place in its list.

limit_exceeded.description: The input is over one of the service's limits. The body's `limit` member names it (`key`, the environment variable `env` that sets it, `value`, `observed`, `unit`). HTTP 413 when the request content is too large, 422 when a parameter or a per-input processing budget is exceeded, 504 when a time limit that depends on an upstream service expired. Split the input, or raise the limit.

busy.description: Every processing slot or queue place is taken (HTTP 429). Retry after the `Retry-After` header's number of seconds.

unsupported_media_type.description: The upload is not a type this endpoint reads (HTTP 415). `detail` says what was sent; the body's `accepted` member lists the file extensions or media types the endpoint accepts, and `cause` may name a finer, unregistered reason. Convert the input or send it to the tool that reads it; do not retry it unchanged.

invalid_record.description: The document record sent with the request cannot be opened (HTTP 422): it is not UTF-8 JSON, not a JSON object, or its `schema_version` has a newer major than this tool reads. Also sent when a block the tool adds rows to (`pages`, `lines`, `entities`) is not a list of objects. A record that opens but does not validate against the schema is otherwise accepted and reported in `document_json_schema_error`. Fix the record; do not retry it unchanged.

ocr_text_layer.description: DEPRECATED since doc-schema-v2 (atrium-project#84, H12): no service sends it. It meant: the PDF's text layer is an earlier OCR run's invisible text over page images (HTTP 422). Such pages are now marked `needs_atr` in docproc's routing, and the document goes through the ATR.

source_digest_mismatch.description: The record sent with the request names the original by its `source.sha512`, and the uploaded file is not that file (HTTP 422): the record would describe one file under another file's identity. Send the original the seed was made for, or a seed made for this file; do not retry unchanged.

upstream_unavailable.description: A backing service the tool calls (named at the start of `detail`, e.g. LINDAT UDPipe) did not answer after the tool's own retries (HTTP 502): it returned a server error, or refused or dropped the connection. The input is not at fault. Retry later with backoff. A backing service that timed out is a 504 `limit_exceeded` instead.

info.title: SiteProof API
info.description:
REST API for SiteProof - a mobile-first T&M (Time & Materials) and variation 
capture system for construction subcontractors.

## Authentication

Most endpoints require a valid JWT access token passed in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

Access tokens expire after 15 minutes. Use the refresh token endpoint to obtain new tokens.

## Multi-tenancy

All data is scoped to the authenticated user's company. Users can only access 
resources belonging to their company.

## Error Handling

All errors follow a consistent format:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ERROR_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable message",
    "details": {}
  }
}
```
See `components/schemas/ErrorCode` for the current list of error codes.

## Idempotency

For POST operations, include an `Idempotency-Key` header with a unique client-generated 
UUID to prevent duplicate submissions on flaky mobile connections.

post.description:
Request a signature from the GC superintendent. 

This will:
1. Generate a unique signing link
2. Send SMS and email to the GC with the link
3. Generate a 6-digit verification code for same-device fallback

The GC can sign on their own device (recommended) or use SMS verification
to sign on the foreman's device.

info.description:
A clean, read-only API over the legacy Urja Meter Ops portal.

All data comes from the portal (see PROTOCOL.md). Meters and transformers are loaded once into memory from the
portal's bulk export; energy readings are fetched on demand and cached. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in IST (+05:30),
numbers are numbers, enums are lower_snake_case, and every row the service had to discard is reported, not hidden.

get.summary:
Finality-bearing directory envelope for trusted consumers such as Cortex. The legacy
`/v1/agents` array remains unchanged for compatibility; sync workers must use this route
and refuse snapshots whose operator-controlled finality bit is false.

Merges three real event streams into one time-ordered feed -- the genuine
"everything logged" table a manual-debugging view needs, not just policy
decisions: `audit_log` (BCC intercept decisions -- the only source with an
explicit allow/deny verdict), `telemetry_events` (SDK-submitted telemetry,
surfaced as "flagged"/"recorded" so a compliance operator sees
signature-verified-but-suspicious submissions alongside policy denials),
and `otel_spans` (every real span, flat, `decision` repurposed as the
span's own real status_code). Merged in Rust rather than a single SQL
UNION because the three source tables don't share a column shape and
coercing them into one query would obscure more than it saves — see each
table's own migration for why they're separate to begin with. The
telemetry_events and otel_spans sides only mix in when `agent_id` is
given: neither table has an existing "recent across all agents" query
(both underlying db:: functions are always agent-scoped), so the global
feed (no agent_id) is audit_log only rather than paying for a new
unscoped scan just for this one aggregate view.

parameters.description: Filter to one agent's DID; omit for the global feed

parameters.description: Max entries per source table before merging (default 100)
