finalized_block_number.description:
Canonical execution-client finalized head observed while creating this
response. `None` means the configured RPC did not expose the tag.

handle.description: Primary handle registered for this agent's SovereignAgent, or null if none.

did_document.description:
§4.1 DID Document, as supplied on `POST /v1/agent/register`. `None` for agents that
registered before this field existed, or that were only ever seen via a chain
backfill (see the "chain-backfill"/"unavailable" `primitives_source` cases below,
which synthesize a response with no local `agents` row at all).

handle.description:
This agent's Oracle-local XNS handle, if any -- see migration 0022. Independent
of `oracle_registered`/on-chain state: a chain-only agent can still hold one.

oracle_registered.description:
True only when this DID has a real row in this oracle's own `agents` table (a real
`POST /v1/agent/register` call against THIS oracle, at some point in its history).
**Not** the same question as "does this DID exist" — a DID that resolves live on-chain
(see `primitives_source: "chain-backfill"` below) but was never registered against
this specific oracle instance still returns `200` here with `oracle_registered: false`,
a synthesized `id`/`primitives` and no other real fields. Added because that
distinction was previously only inferable by checking `primitives_source != "cache"`
AND `has_ed25519_key`/`has_eth_address`, which every caller had to reverse-engineer —
`GET /v1/telemetry/ingest` and `GET /v1/agent/{id}/ais` both fail closed
(`AgentNotFound`) on exactly this same local-row check (`db::get_agent`), so a caller
deciding "is it safe/worthwhile to send telemetry for this agent" needs this exact
boolean, not "does the DID exist anywhere."

primitives_source.description:
True when this response's `primitives` came from a live chain read performed just
now (cache miss / no local `agents` row), rather than the Postgres cache.

verification_tier.description:
Effective server-verified tier: registration floor unioned with active, unexpired,
unrevoked DNS/GitHub/Nitro evidence. Scoring-core uses it as the identity ceiling,
and BCC policy additionally requires minimum tiers for sensitive intent types.

controller.description:
Lowercase EVM controller resolved from the on-chain registry cache.
Consumers must compare this exact address; it is not a user-editable label.

erc8004_binding_status.description:
`"verified"` / `"stale"` / `"transfer_conflict"`, or `None` if this agent has no
ERC-8004 binding on record. A directory filtering on this must never treat `None`
as untrustworthy — most agents simply haven't linked a public listing.

handle.description:
The agent's primary XNS handle (e.g. `"xibalba.integrity"`), read live from
`XibalbaNameService.primaryHandle(sovereignAgent)`. This is the protocol's own
naming authority — self-service and on-chain (see XibalbaNameService.sol's NatSpec
on why there is deliberately no privileged off-chain registrar) — so consumers
should prefer it over `name` when displaying an agent.

`None` is a normal, expected outcome, never an error: the agent hasn't claimed a
handle, XNS isn't deployed on this chain, or the on-chain read failed. See
`list_agents` on why a chain hiccup must not take the whole fleet list down.

name.description:
Legacy secondary display name, if the agent's DID document carries an `alsoKnownAs`
entry. Kept as a last-resort fallback below `handle` — most agents have none, and
nothing in this system can write it (`register_agent` is an insert with no update
path), so new naming should go through XNS.

AgentUsageDto.description:
Default lookback window when `since` isn't given: 7 days, distinct from
`compute_ais_for_agent`'s 30-day (`AIS_REPORTING_PERIOD_DAYS`) scoring window — the
two are read for different purposes (a chart's default view vs. the score itself)
and don't need to share a constant.
Token and cost rollup for an agent, from the OTLP metrics receiver (`otel_metrics`).

`tokens` is keyed by the emitter's token `type` attribute, so Claude Code yields
`input` / `output` / `cacheRead` / `cacheCreation` — the breakdown the signed telemetry
path cannot supply, since providers report cache and reasoning tokens only in their own
usage objects.

cost_usd_by_model.description: model -> summed reported cost in USD.

evidence_tier.description:
Always `"unsigned_vendor"`. This data arrives over the UNAUTHENTICATED OTLP port and
carries no agent signature, so it is deliberately NOT an AIS input — it is reported
here for observability and for cross-checking what an agent signs against what its
runtime reports. Surfaced in the response so a consumer cannot mistake it for
agent-attested evidence.

tokens.description: token type -> summed count over the window.

compliance.description:
`null` when the window has no evidence-backed compliance verdict
(`compliance_observed == false`): there is no axis value to report.
`null` for a bucket with no evidence-backed compliance verdict.

anchor_coverage.description:
Whether this agent's on-chain `StateAnchor` shows anchoring activity at or after
`period_start`, given it had telemetry activity in that same window.
Informational only (see `anchor_coverage.rs`) — never fed into `ais` itself.

compliance_observed.description:
False when the window has events but none carried an evidence-backed compliance
verdict. `weights` then shows the compliance weight as 0 with the other three
renormalized, and `components.compliance` does not enter the score.

constraint_score.description:
spec/integrity-protocol-v3.2.md §3.1.1 eq. 4b's `r(ι)`: the normalised, pre-boost,
tier-ceilinged constraint input in `[0,1]`. Distinct from `ais` above (post-boost,
unclamped, display-only) — any integration reading a reputation-parameterised bound
off this response MUST use this field, never `ais`. See `AisBreakdown`'s doc comment.

onchain_assurance_tier.description:
On-chain assurance state for migrated factory clones. Legacy clones that
predate the tier-authority initializer return `null` here.

onchain_base_score.description:
Exact pre-boost value to synchronize into ReputationRegistry after
every Oracle-side post-score adjustment (including anchor coverage).
Consumers must not reconstruct this from component fields.

onchain_zk_boost_consistent.description:
Present only when a cached on-chain ReputationRegistry address is known for this
agent — a nice-to-have cross-check (per the task's "not required" note) that the
oracle's off-chain `zk_verified_event_ratio` telemetry flag agrees with the
contract's own independently-earned `isZkBoosted` state. A mismatch here doesn't
fail the request (the two are allowed to be transiently out of sync — e.g. a proof
submitted directly to the contract that hasn't shown up in telemetry yet) but is
worth surfacing to an operator.

sacrifice_observed.description:
False when the window has events but none carried attested compute (validator or
TEE). `weights` then shows the sacrifice weight as 0 with the others renormalized,
and `components.sacrifice` does not enter the score. No attestation path exists
yet, so this is false for every agent with events.

shadow_gate.description:
**Shadow-mode only** (spec §3.1.4 row 5, `PRODUCTION_GAPS.md` §27) — reports what
the proposed per-component floor + conjunctive gate would decide, using this
oracle's currently-configured `AisFloors` (provisional defaults unless an operator
has overridden them). Purely observational: does not affect `ais` or
`constraint_score`, does not gate anything, and is not consumed by
`bcc_middleware`'s chain-push or dispute logic.

zk_verified_event_ratio.description: Fraction of events in this exact reporting window with their own verified proof.

AisWeightsSchema.description:
Schema-only mirror of `scoring_core::AisWeights` for OpenAPI generation.
`scoring-core` is deliberately dependency-free beyond `serde` (see its Cargo.toml —
it's the single source of truth for the AIS formula and must stay trivially
auditable), so it doesn't derive `utoipa::ToSchema` itself. This struct's fields
must stay in sync with `scoring_core::AisWeights` by hand; a `scoring_core` unit
test pinning its `Serialize` output's field names is the backstop against drift
(see scoring-core's existing `default_weights_sum_to_one` test module).

last_anchored_at.description:
`None` if the on-chain read failed (RPC unreachable, bad address) or the
`StateAnchor` has never anchored anything (`latestEpoch == 0`) — indistinguishable
from each other at this layer, both surfaced as "we don't know," never coerced
into a false `Stale` or `Current`.

leaves.description: 0x-prefixed keccak256 Merkle leaves that were committed in this anchor tx.

recorded.description: Rows inserted (leaves already recorded are skipped idempotently).

AuditEffectJoinRow.description:
BCC intent-vs-effect join (~/.claude/plans/velvet-giggling-quill.md): both the original
ALLOW row (written with `intended_state_hash` in its metadata, see /v1/audit/ingest) and
any `posttool_effect` row(s) reporting an actual effect hash against it (see
`submit_audit_effect`) share the same `intended_state_hash` value inside their JSONB
`metadata` -- there's no dedicated column for it (see this session's own earlier
investigation: it lives only in the blob), so this queries the JSONB field directly
(`metadata->>'intended_state_hash' = $1`) rather than requiring a migration. `AuditLogRow`
doesn't carry `metadata` (it's a read DTO shaped for the dashboard's audit panel), so this
returns a lighter-weight row that does, since inspecting the metadata IS the point here.

status.description: SmartBAA.Status: Proposed | Active | Disputed | Terminated.

BenchmarkDto.description: Network-wide model/provider stability benchmark (aggregated telemetry per model).

simulated_ais.description: Simulated AIS on the 0-1000 scale from this model's stability + grounding.

stability_metric.description: Behavioral stability in [0,1] = exp(-1.5 * avg_variance^2) (mirrors the entropy score).

agent_id.description:
The agent claiming this handle. Need not exist in `agents` -- see migration
0022's header note: an agent may hold a handle without ever registering on-chain.

zone_green_threshold.description: At or above this AIS the agent is green.

zone_policy.description: Which rule chose the zone thresholds: `per_tier` (default), `relative` or `absolute`.

zone_recovery_threshold.description: The AIS an agent that was yellow or red must reach to become green again.

zone_yellow_threshold.description: Below this AIS the agent is red.

oneOf.description:
Optional provider-reported cost. This is absent when the provider did not
report a price; the oracle never derives one from token counts.

compliance.description:
Whether the BCC/OPA pipeline (bcc_middleware) flagged this specific event's intent.
This oracle treats it as a straightforward boolean-ish signal (>0.5 => flagged);
see the field's doc in `aggregate_for_ais`/scoring-core for how per-event flags
become the period's `penalty_ratio`.

entropy.description:
Maps to `telemetry_events.performance_variance` (S_entropy's raw input, §4.3) —
higher means less stable/more erratic behavior for this event.

JudgeEvaluationDto.description:
A judge (LLM-as-judge) evaluation, optionally carried alongside a telemetry
ingestion — storage + ingestion plumbing only (task write-up item 6). No judge/
rubric implementation exists in this codebase; this is purely "if some other
component produces one of these, the oracle can persist it." Deliberately NOT part
of `ingest_telemetry`'s signed payload (see that handler's `signable` JSON
construction below, which does not reference this field) — adding it there would
retroactively invalidate every telemetry signature a client produced before this
field existed. It rides along as an unauthenticated sidecar on an otherwise-
authenticated request (the rest of the payload still requires a valid agent
signature); this is an accepted, documented scope limit for now.

provider.description: Lowercase provider id configured in `KYC_PROVIDER_KEYS`.

nonce.description: Fresh nonce returned by the Oracle's KYC challenge endpoint.

opaque_subject_reference.description:
Provider-local random reference. Must not contain a name, email, document number,
or other directly identifying value.

provider.description: Identifier matching a key in `KYC_PROVIDER_KEYS`.

signature.description: Hex Ed25519 signature over `receipt_message`.

effective_score.description:
Real `ReputationRegistry.effectiveScore` read (decimal string — see
migrations/0002's header note on uint256 serialization), NOT the off-chain
`scoring-core` AIS float `GET /v1/agent/{id}/ais` returns — the two are related
but distinct numbers (the on-chain value is the last score this oracle itself
pushed via `ReputationRegistry.updateScore`, possibly zk-boosted).

realized_pnl.description:
Realized P&L is NOT computed. It would require indexing `IntegrityMarket`
`PositionEntered`/`MarketResolved`/`PayoutClaimed` events across every market —
out of scope for this pass. `null`, always — never a fabricated number. See
`docs/wiki/entities/integrity-oracle.md` for the documented follow-up.

ed25519_pubkey_hex.description: The agent's Ed25519 public key, 32 bytes of hex (`0x` prefix and case tolerated).

handle.description: Optional XNS handle to claim in the same transaction.

signature.description:
Hex Ed25519 signature over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of
`{did, domain: "integrity.agent.register.offchain.v1", ed25519_pubkey_hex, timestamp}`.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds the proof was signed; accepted within +/-300 s of server time.

handle.description: The handle claimed by this request, if one was supplied.

PrimitiveSetDto.description:
Wire shape for the 7-address PrimitiveSet (§6.1), matching
`integrity-dashboard/src/lib/api/types.ts`'s `PrimitiveSet` field-for-field (camelCase)
so the dashboard can deserialize this oracle's responses without a translation layer.

decision.description: The policy decision that produced the leaf (allow / shadow_deny / …), if joined.

intent_type.description:
The committed intent type (the "action"), when the anchored leaf joins to
an audit_log decision row.

leaf.description: 0x keccak Merkle leaf of the committed intent (the provenance input hash).

root.description: 0x per-agent StateAnchor root the leaf was committed under.

did.description:
`did:integrity:<fingerprint>` — the agent's canonical off-chain identifier and
the primary key of the `agents` table.

did_document.description:
§4.1 DID Document. Stored verbatim in the response for now (no dedicated column —
see README/gaps note); its `verificationMethod` is where `ed25519_pubkey_hex`
below is expected to have come from, but this handler trusts the explicit field,
not a parse of the document, to avoid a second, redundant multibase-decode path.

handle.description:
Mandatory unique username for this agent, chosen by the human operator the same
way one picks a chat-app handle -- checked for availability against Oracle's own
`xns_handles` directory (see migration 0022), independent of on-chain state.
Every agent that completes this registration holds exactly one.

primitives.description:
The 7 on-chain primitive addresses the client claims it registered via
`AgentPrimitivesFactory`. Independently re-verified against
`XibalbaAgentRegistry.resolveDID` below — never trusted as-is (see chain.rs's
module doc comment for why).

verification_tier.description:
ADVISORY ONLY — never trusted. A previous version of this handler stored this
client-supplied value directly, which meant any client could self-assert
`verification_tier: 3` at registration with nothing server-side checking the
claim, defeating the entire point of a verification ladder (see
docs/wiki/concepts/identity-ceiling.md). `register_agent` now always computes
the real, server-verified tier itself (see that function) and ignores this
field; it's kept on the wire only for backward request-shape compatibility.

RegistrationOutcome.description: What an off-chain registration call did to the `agents` row.

compliance_pass.description: `null` when compliance is unobserved: it neither passes nor fails the gate.

would_pass.description: Conjunction over the observed axes only.

children.description:
`no_recursion`: `SpanTreeNode` is self-referential (a node's children are more
nodes) — without this, utoipa's schema builder recurses into its own field
type with no cycle-breaking and stack-overflows at `gen_openapi` runtime. This
only affects generated OpenAPI *documentation* depth, not actual serialization
(`Vec<SpanTreeNode>` still holds real, arbitrarily-nested data at runtime) or
the `MAX_TREE_DEPTH` recursion guard in `build_tree`, which is unrelated and
still fully enforced.

duration_ms.description:
Always >= 0: `end_time` before `start_time` (a malformed/adversarial span) is
clamped to 0 rather than surfacing a negative duration to callers.

merkle_root_id.description:
Always `null` today — see `db::fetch_pending_leaves`'s doc comment. Real Merkle
anchoring for this event's leaf happens out-of-band, per-agent, in
`bcc_middleware/app/anchor.py`, not via a root assigned back onto this row.

evidence_tier.description:
Explicit provenance tier for the signed-agent ingestion path. Version 1
payloads may omit this field and are treated as the historical signed tier.

oneOf.description:
See `JudgeEvaluationDto`'s doc comment: optional, unauthenticated sidecar, not part
of the signed envelope.

observed_at.description:
Agent-observed wall-clock time for this signed batch. Required for
schema_version 2+; it is optional only for historical pre-versioning and
schema-version-1 envelopes. It is deliberately inside the signed envelope
so delayed submissions cannot move an event into a different AIS window.

schema_version.description:
Version of the signed envelope. Inside the signed object, so it cannot be rewritten
in transit to make this handler reinterpret a payload under different rules.

`None` means the pre-versioning shape, which stays valid forever — signed payloads
are evidence and old evidence must remain verifiable. Critically, the signable bytes
are rebuilt WITHOUT the key when this is `None`: serializing it as `null` would
change the canonical JSON and break every historical signature.

signature.description:
Hex signature over the canonical JSON (see `crypto::canonical_json_bytes`) of every
field above EXCEPT this one and `judge_evaluation` — i.e. the client constructs the
object without `signature`, canonicalizes+signs that, then adds this field before
POSTing. This mirrors the §4.2 BCC Commitment convention (sign the payload minus the
signature field itself) rather than inventing a different scheme for telemetry.

truncated.description:
True if the deepest branch was cut off (see `trace_tree::MAX_TREE_DEPTH`) —
an honest signal that this isn't the complete tree, never silently dropped.

UnregisteredAgentDto.description:
Real "shadow AI" discovery (Shield vertical): DIDs the oracle has telemetry/policy
evidence for (`otel_spans`, `audit_log`) but that never registered via
`POST /v1/agent/register`. See `db::list_unregistered_agents`'s doc comment for why
this is the correctly-scoped, zero-new-infra version of this feature rather than
literal network/process scanning (out of scope for a web app regardless).

source.description: "otel" | "audit_log" — which table this DID was first observed in.

transaction_history.description:
Transfer/stake/payout history requires indexing on-chain events (`Transfer`,
`PositionEntered`, `PayoutClaimed`, ...), which this pass does not build. `null`,
never a fabricated transaction list. See `docs/wiki/entities/integrity-oracle.md`.

suggestions.description:
Populated only when `available` is false: a handful of close, currently-free
variations on the requested handle, so a search UI can offer them immediately
instead of making the user guess-and-check one at a time.

XnsHandleResolveDto.description:
Oracle-local handle resolution (distinct from the pre-existing, on-chain
`GET /v1/xns/resolve?handle=` / `XnsResolveDto` pair below, which resolves against the
deployed XibalbaNameService contract instead).

did.description: DID (did:integrity:<sovereign_agent>) when a reverse mapping exists in the oracle DB.

sovereign_agent.description: SovereignAgent address the handle points at, or null if unregistered.

proof.description: Base64-encoded raw bytes of `bb prove`'s `proof` output file.

public_inputs.description: Base64-encoded raw bytes of `bb prove`'s `public_inputs` output file.

get.description:
Returns a time-limited SIWE-style EIP-191 message for the given wallet address. Sign the exact challenge string and submit it to /verify.

Agent policy: Step 1 of owner auth. Call with the owner wallet address to receive a time-limited SIWE-style message. Sign the exact challenge with ECDSA (EIP-191) and pass it to POST /auth/verify.

Submit wallet-signed proof to update account name, notification preferences, and email binding intent. New or changed email addresses are staged as pendingEmail until a verification code is confirmed. post.description:
Confirms the 6-digit code sent to a pending email address. Only after this succeeds does Gateway bind the email to the wallet account.

Agent policy: Step 3 of email binding. Submit the code from the verification email. Codes expire after 10 minutes and lock after 5 bad attempts.

info.title: PokéAPI
info.description:
All the Pokémon data you'll ever need in one place, easily accessible through a modern free open-source RESTful API.

## What is this?

This is a full RESTful API linked to an extensive database detailing everything about the Pokémon main game series.

We've covered everything from Pokémon to Berry Flavors.

## Where do I start?

We have awesome [documentation](https://pokeapi.co/docs/v2) on how to use this API. It takes minutes to get started.

This API will always be publicly available and will never require any extensive setup process to consume.

Created by [**Paul Hallett**(]https://github.com/phalt) and other [**PokéAPI contributors***](https://github.com/PokeAPI/pokeapi#contributing) around the world. Pokémon and Pokémon character names are trademarks of Nintendo.

info.title: FluxMQ Admin API
info.description:
Admin-facing HTTP endpoints for FluxMQ broker monitoring and management.

FluxMQ exposes two HTTP servers with distinct responsibilities:

- **API Server** (`admin_api_addr`): Admin endpoints for stats, cluster info, session
  management, and a combined overview. Also serves the Queue Service gRPC/Connect API.
- **Health Server** (`health_addr`): Lightweight k8s probes for liveness, readiness,
  and basic cluster status.

Both servers are internal/trusted — no authentication is required.

Pending entry list size. Only classic queues maintain one; a stream
consumer group tracks a cursor instead.

QueueStats.description:
Queue manager counters. Queues are shared by every protocol, so this
section sits beside `by_protocol` rather than inside it. Omitted when
the node runs no queue manager.

capture_failures.description:
Matching queues a captured publish failed to reach, because the
append failed or the queue's configuration could not be read. The
unit is the queue, so a publish missing two of its matching queues
counts twice. A resolution failure, where the matching set is
unknown, counts once.

capture_dropped.description:
Capture jobs discarded before any append was attempted, because the
capture backlog was full or shutdown drained past its deadline.
Distinct from `capture_failures`, where the append was tried and did
not succeed: a rising `capture_dropped` means capture cannot keep up
with the publish rate. Capture runs off the publish path and never
fails the publish, so these two counters are its only signal.

StatsResponse.description:
Top-level fields are aggregated totals across all protocols.
The `by_protocol` section contains per-protocol breakdowns with
protocol-specific fields (e.g. MQTT subscriptions, AMQP channels).
The `queues` section is cross-protocol and is present only when the
node runs a queue manager.

info.title: ScholarMarket API
info.description:
REST API for the ScholarMarket educational content marketplace.
Provides endpoints for managing materials, purchases, creator analytics,
marketplace discovery, and checkout flows.

## Authentication
All write endpoints require a valid `token` cookie issued by the
`/api/auth` login flow (HS256 JWT signed with `JWT_SECRET`).

## Rate Limits
Most endpoints are rate-limited. Limits vary by route and are applied
per-user. Check response headers for `X-RateLimit-*` fields.

info.title: PokéAPI
info.description:
All the Pokémon data you'll ever need in one place, easily accessible through a modern free open-source RESTful API.

## What is this?

This is a full RESTful API linked to an extensive database detailing everything about the Pokémon main game series.

We've covered everything from Pokémon to Berry Flavors.

## Where do I start?

We have awesome [documentation](https://pokeapi.co/docs/v2) on how to use this API. It takes minutes to get started.

This API will always be publicly available and will never require any extensive setup process to consume.

Created by [**Paul Hallett**](https://github.com/phalt) and other [**PokéAPI contributors**](https://github.com/PokeAPI/pokeapi#contributing) around the world. Pokémon and Pokémon character names are trademarks of Nintendo.

tags.name: pokemon
tags.description: Pokémon are the creatures that inhabit the world of the Pokémon games. They can be caught using Pokéballs and trained by battling with other Pokémon. Each Pokémon belongs to a specific species but may take on a variant which makes it differ from other Pokémon of the same species, such as base stats, available abilities and typings. See [Bulbapedia](http://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species)) for greater detail.

tags.name: evolution
tags.description: Evolution is a process in which a Pokémon changes into a different species of Pokémon.

tags.name: berries
tags.description: Berries can be soft or hard. Check out [Bulbapedia](http://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Category:Berries_by_firmness) for greater detail.

tags.name: items
tags.description: An item is an object in the games which the player can pick up, keep in their bag, and use in some manner. They have various uses, including healing, powering up, helping catch Pokémon, or to access a new area.

tags.name: machines
tags.description: Machines are the representation of items that teach moves to Pokémon. They vary from version to version, so it is not certain that one specific TM or HM corresponds to a single Machine.

tags.name: location
tags.description: Locations that can be visited within the games. Locations make up sizable portions of regions, like cities or routes.

tags.name: contest
tags.description: Pokémon Contests are a type of competition often contrasted with Pokémon battles and held in Contest Halls

tags.name: moves
tags.description: Moves are the skills of Pokémon in battle. In battle, a Pokémon uses one move each turn. Some moves (including those learned by Hidden Machine) can be used outside of battle as well, usually for the purpose of removing obstacles or exploring new areas.

tags.name: games
tags.description: The Pokémon games are all video games in the Pokémon franchise.

info.title: Saral Privacy API
info.summary: Consent capture, signed receipts, and the audit log.
info.description:
Authentication: send an API key, or a staff session token from `/v1/auth/mfa/verify`, as `Authorization: Bearer <...>`. A publishable key (`pk_...`, scope `sdk`) is safe
to ship in a browser and may be restricted to origins. A secret key (`sk_...`) carries one or more of the scopes
`tenant_admin`, `dpo` and `auditor` and must stay on a server. Every request is limited to the key's tenant.

Failures to authenticate all return the same 401 body. A request for another tenant's data returns 404, never 403.

Browsers may call the API: CORS reflects the caller's origin and never allows cookies. This is not authorisation;
the key, its scopes and its origin list are checked on every request.

Rate limits (counted per minute, in each running instance): 600 requests from one address, 10 sign-in steps from one
address (`/v1/auth/login`, `/v1/auth/mfa/enroll` and `/v1/auth/mfa/verify` share this), and 1200 requests with one secret key
or one staff session from anywhere. A publishable key is public, so it is not limited as a whole, only by the address limit. Past a limit the answer is 429 with `Retry-After` (seconds) and
`{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "Too many requests. Try again in N seconds." }`. `Retry-After` is exposed to
browser scripts. `/healthz` is never limited. An address is its IPv4 address or its IPv6 /64. The caller's address is the
connection's own unless the deployment states how many proxies to believe (`TRUST_PROXY`); `X-Forwarded-For` is ignored
otherwise.

200.description: The process is up. This does not check the database.

get.summary: Public keys that verify consent receipts

200.description: A JSON Web Key Set with public members only. May be cached for 5 minutes.

post.summary: Publish a new version of the organisation's privacy notice
post.description: The text is made from the reviewed template for the language, filled with the values given here. It is never taken from the caller, and it is marked `pending-human-review`. Every publication is a new version of its language (the first is version 1, and each language is numbered on its own). A published notice never changes, so an edit is a new notice, and receipts keep pointing to the text the person saw. Each purpose carries both its notice wording (`name`, `description`, `dataItems`, `retention`) and what receipts say about it (`key`, `retentionDays`, categories, third-party disclosure). A purpose that discloses to a third party must name an organisation that is listed in `notice.thirdParties`. Fields that are not part of the request are refused, so a misspelt field is not silently ignored. Publishing is an audit event (`notice.published`). The response has no text; read it at `GET /v1/notices/{id}`.

400.description: Invalid. `field` names the first problem by its place in the request, for example `notice.withdrawalUrl` or `purposes[1].retentionDays`. When there are several problems with the notice text, `errors` lists them all. Nothing submitted is echoed back.

422.description: `receipt_too_large`: a receipt that grants every purpose would be over the 16384-character limit of a receipt (the estimate counts the organisation's receipt profile and leaves room for the signature), so every consent that grants all of it would fail. Use fewer or shorter purposes and categories. Not checked until the organisation has a receipt profile.

get.summary: The organisation's published notices, newest first
get.description: Without the text, which is public at `GET /v1/notices/{id}`. Use it to find the id of a notice to give the SDK.
Public by design. The URL is what a receipt points to.

200.description: The notice text exactly as hashed.

post.summary: Record a consent and get a signed receipt
post.description:
Retention and receipt details come from the notice's purpose definitions, never from the request. At least one
purpose must be granted. The person is identified by a phone number or email address that is turned into a
keyed HMAC and then discarded; it is never stored or logged.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A random, unguessable token (8 to 128 letters, digits, dashes or underscores) that the caller keeps for this request. Without it every request is a new consent, and the API never recognises a person by identifier alone, because that would hand a stored receipt to anyone who knows the identifier.

200.description: A retry: the request carries an `Idempotency-Key` that was already used for this same request, and the first result is returned unchanged. Nothing is recorded again, so a lost response is safe to retry.

201.description: Recorded. `receipt` is a Kantara KI-CR-v1.1.0 receipt as an RS256 JWT. Its `policyUrl` is the public notice URL (when the server has a public base URL), and the extension claims `saralConsentId`, `saralNoticeId` and `saralNoticeSha256` say which consent and which exact notice text it covers.

409.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different request, or its consent is no longer granted. Use a new key.

post.summary: Withdraw every consent a person has, by identifier alone (secret keys only)
post.description: For a tenant's server, after it has verified the person itself (a signed-in user, a support request). The identifier alone proves nothing about who is calling, and a publishable key is visible in a web page, so **a publishable key gets 403**. Withdraws every granted consent of the person in the tenant, optionally only for one notice. Each withdrawal is audited and queued as an event. A wrong identifier, another tenant's person, and nothing left to withdraw are all the same 404. The browser SDK withdraws by consent id and identifier instead (`/v1/consents/{id}/withdraw`).
The caller proves who they are with the same identifier. A wrong identifier looks the same as an unknown consent (404).

409.description: The consent is already withdrawn or expired.

post.summary: Find a person's consents by identifier
post.description: For the data protection officer (scope `dpo`), who needs to answer a person who writes in. The identifier (a phone number in E.164 form or an email address) is in the body, not in the address, is turned into the person's pseudonym, and is never stored, logged or answered back. The consents come newest first, at most 100 (`truncated` says there were more). Someone with no consent has none: they are not created by being searched for. A search that finds a person is an audit event (`consent.searched`) naming who looked and the person's internal id, never the identifier.

get.description: Counts only, for the data protection officer (scope `dpo`). `totals` and `purposes` cover every consent ever recorded (a purpose counts the consents that agreed to it). `days` covers the last `days` UTC days up to and including today, oldest first, one line for every day, with the consents given and withdrawn that day.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days, from 1 to 366. The default is 30.

200.description: The receipt issued when the consent was recorded.

post.description: The URL must be https on the standard port, with no credentials, and every address its host name resolves to must be public (private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses are refused, and checked again at every delivery). A tenant may have at most 10 active endpoints (disable one to free a place). The signing secret is shown only in this response; `rotate-secret` issues a new one. Creating an endpoint is an audit event.

409.description: The tenant already has 10 active endpoints.

delete.description: Nothing more is sent to it and its place in the cap of 10 is free again. Events still waiting for it are marked failed. Disabling is an audit event. An endpoint cannot be enabled again; register a new one. Saral also disables an endpoint whose last ten finished deliveries have all failed for good (none delivered among them): the endpoint then reads `disabledReason: failures`, and the event `webhook.endpoint_auto_disabled` is in the audit log.

post.description: The new secret is shown only in this response. By default the old one stops working at once: later deliveries are signed with the new secret only, which is the right choice if the old one may have leaked. With `overlap: true` the old secret keeps signing for 24 hours after the rotation, alongside the new one: every delivery then carries two `v1=` signatures in `X-Saral-Signature`, the new secret's first, so a receiver can be switched over without missing a delivery. Only the secret just before the current one is kept: a second rotation ends the overlap of the first, and a rotation without `overlap` ends any overlap at once. Rotating is an audit event. A disabled endpoint cannot be rotated.

overlap.description: Keep the old secret working for 24 hours.

previousSecretValidUntil.description: When the old secret stops signing deliveries; null when it stopped at once.

post.summary: Switch a disabled endpoint on again
post.description: For an endpoint that the administrator disabled or that Saral switched off after repeated failures. It keeps the secret it had (rotate as well if the secret may have leaked). The address is checked again as for a new endpoint (422 `invalid_url` if it no longer passes), and the cap of 10 active endpoints applies (409 `too_many_endpoints`). An endpoint that is already on is 409 `already_enabled`. It is an audit event.

409.description: `already_enabled` or `too_many_endpoints`.

422.description: The address no longer passes the checks (`invalid_url`).

get.summary: The delivery log of an endpoint
get.description: The most recent deliveries of one endpoint, newest first, with their state and what happened on the last try. It works for a disabled endpoint too. The payload that was sent is not included.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to show, from 1 to 100. The default is 50.

post.description: Puts a failed delivery back in the queue with its attempts unused. The worker then sends it with the same `Idempotency-Key` (the delivery id), so a receiver that already acted on it can tell. Only a delivery that has failed (`409 not_failed` otherwise) and only to an endpoint that is still enabled (`409 endpoint_disabled`). It is an audit event (`webhook.delivery_redelivered`). The database lets the application role do exactly this to a delivery and nothing else.

409.description: `not_failed` (the delivery has not failed) or `endpoint_disabled`.

post.description: For the officer or the administrator. The record starts as `reported`. The Board has to be told within 72 hours of the time the breach was found (`boardDeadline`); that period is the figure the plan cites for Rule 7 and has not been confirmed against the Rules, which the lawyer advisor must do before it is shown to customers as advice. The free text can mention people, so audit entries hold a hash of the content and never the words. The record is never deleted.

get.description: Newest discovery first, at most 100.

patch.description: Any of the report's fields, at least one; `null` clears the time it happened or the number of people. Only while the incident is `reported`: after sign-off it answers 409 `locked`. It is an audit event.

409.description: `locked`: the incident has been signed off.

get.summary: The drafts for the Board and for the affected people
get.description: Plain text written from the incident and the organisation's profile, each starting with a warning that it is a draft nobody has reviewed. Saral sends nothing to the Board or to anyone. 422 `incomplete_setup` when the profile does not say who the controller is.

post.summary: The officer signs off the drafts
post.description: The officer's word, given for exactly the drafts they read: the body carries the two hashes that came with the drafts, and if the drafts are now different (the report was corrected after they were opened) the answer is 409 `drafts_changed` and nothing is signed. Otherwise it records who and when, and the hash of the two drafts (so it can be shown later what was signed), and the incident can no longer be changed. Officer only. An audit event. Once: 409 `illegal_transition` otherwise.

409.description: `illegal_transition`, or `drafts_changed`.

post.summary: Record that the Board was told
post.description: After sign-off. The time it was told (not before the breach was found, not in the future) and the reference the Board gave. `boardNotifiedLate` says whether it was after the deadline. Officer only. An audit event.

409.description: `illegal_transition`: not signed off, or already recorded.

post.summary: Record that the affected people were told
post.description: Once, after sign-off, before or after the Board. How they were told and how many (zero if nobody was affected). Officer only. An audit event.

409.description: `illegal_transition` or `already_recorded`.

post.description: After the Board was told and the affected people were told (409 `principals_not_notified` otherwise), with a closing note. Final. Officer only. An audit event.

409.description: `illegal_transition` or `principals_not_notified`.

post.summary: Save the next version of the record of processing
post.description: For the officer or the administrator. The record is stored as its canonical JSON text with the SHA-256 of that text, as the next version (1, 2, 3, ...), and a version is never changed or deleted. A save that would change nothing (the same record as the latest version) is refused with 409 `unchanged`, so the history is a list of changes, and an organisation can keep at most 200 versions (409 `version_limit`). A save may say which version it started from (`basedOn`, 0 when nothing had been saved); if another version has been saved since, it is refused with 409 `stale` and the number of the newest version, so nobody overwrites a change they have not seen. The record can be at most 90 KiB. It is an audit event (`ropa.version_created`) that holds the hash and never the words.

409.description: `unchanged`, `version_limit`, or `stale` (with `latest`, the number of the newest version).

get.summary: The versions of the record, newest first
get.description: At most 100, without the records themselves.

get.summary: The newest version, with its record

post.summary: A person asks for access, correction, erasure, nomination, or to complain
post.description: The answer is the same whether or not the person is already known, so it cannot be used to find out who is a customer. The person's phone number or email address is kept only sealed (AES-256-GCM) so the data protection officer can answer; it is never in audit entries or webhooks. The request is due 30 days after it is submitted (a working default, not yet confirmed against the Rules). Submitting is an audit event and queues `dsr.submitted`.

get.description: Soonest due first, with the details the person wrote. `overdue` lists open requests past their due date.

post.summary: Move a request to its next state
post.description: Legal moves: submitted to identity_pending, in_review or rejected; identity_pending to in_review or rejected; in_review to fulfilled or rejected; fulfilled or rejected to closed. A rejection needs a reason. Fulfilling an **erasure** request, in the same transaction, withdraws the person's consents, deletes the sealed contact, and replaces their pseudonym so their identifier no longer leads to them; the audit chain stays intact. Every move is an audit event and queues `dsr.transitioned`. Whether this erasure design satisfies the Act is a question for the lawyer advisor.

409.description: That move is not allowed from the current state. `allowed` lists the moves that are.

post.summary: Show the person's phone number or email address to the data protection officer
post.description: Every read is an audit event (`dsr.contact_revealed`) that names the key that read it. 410 after the contact was erased.

410.description: The contact was erased or was never captured.

post.summary: Step one of signing in: the password
post.description: Returns a short-lived (5 minute) **challenge**, never a session. `mfa` says whether the person must set up an authenticator (`enroll`) or has one (`verify`). An unknown organisation, an unknown email, a wrong password, a disabled person and a locked account all give exactly the same 401, and take about the same time. Five wrong passwords or codes lock the account for 15 minutes (and that is an audit event). Staff accounts are created by operators.

post.summary: First time only: a new authenticator secret to scan
post.description: The secret is not trusted until a code from it is accepted by `mfa/verify`. 409 if an authenticator is already set up.

200.description: The secret, and the link an authenticator app scans as a QR code.

409.description: An authenticator is already set up.

post.summary: Step two of signing in: the authenticator code or a recovery code
post.description: A six-digit authenticator code (one step of clock drift allowed; a code works once), or a recovery code such as `abcde-fghij` (once). The first successful code confirms the authenticator and returns eight **recovery codes, shown only this once**. The session lasts 15 minutes and can be refreshed until eight hours after this sign-in.

409.description: The authenticator has not been set up yet.

post.summary: A new session for a still-valid one
post.description: Sessions only (an API key gets 403). Refuses once eight hours have passed since the person last signed in with a password and a code. A session whose password must still be changed may renew itself.

Sessions only (an API key, even a tenant admin's, gets 403). The current password must be right. Wrong ones are counted and lock the account for 15 minutes after five, as at sign-in, so a stolen session cannot be used to guess it. A wrong current password is a 422 and never a 401, because a 401 means the session has ended. The new password is judged first (12 to 128 characters, not the email address, not one character repeated, not the current password), and a refusal for that reason counts no failure. On success every other session of the person ends, including the one used, and the answer is a new session that keeps the time of the real sign-in, so the eight-hour limit does not start again, and a session already more than eight hours past the real sign-in is refused with 401, as renewing it is (otherwise changing the password would be a way to keep a session alive). The authenticator and the recovery codes are not changed. It is an audit event (`staff.password_changed`). No password is echoed in any answer.

403.description: Not a signed-in person (an API key), or the account is locked after five wrong passwords (`error` is `locked`).

422.description: `wrong_password`: the current password is not right.

get.summary: Who is signed in and what they may do
Recompute the tenant's audit hash chain
get.description: Verifies the whole chain, or one UTC day when `date` is given. When the chain does not verify the result has `ok` set to false and names the first failing entry. A chain that does not verify is not an HTTP error.

get.summary: One UTC day of audit entries
get.description: The day's entries in order, as stored: hashes, ids, times, the actor and the action, and no personal data. With that day's anchor (the file the nightly job writes, or `/v1/audit/merkle-root`) an outside auditor can check them with the standalone `saral-audit-verify` command: without any key it proves they are exactly the anchored entries; with the audit key, also that each says what its hash was made from. A day with no entries is an empty list. A day over 100,000 entries is refused (422).

get.summary: The anchor for one UTC day

200.description: Count, head hash and Merkle root of the day's entries.

409.description: The day's chain does not verify, so no anchor is given.

post.summary: An event Saral sends to a registered endpoint
post.description:
Delivery is at least once. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds; anything else (including a redirect, which is
not followed) is retried with exponential backoff and jitter, from about 10 seconds up to 6 hours between tries,
15 attempts in all. De-duplicate with the `Idempotency-Key` header, which is the delivery id.

Verify `X-Saral-Signature` (`t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`): the value is the HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the endpoint's
signing secret (the bytes after `whsec_`, base64url), of the string `<t>.<raw request body>`. Reject the request if
`t` is more than 5 minutes from your clock. The header may carry several `v1` values during a secret rotation;
accept the request if any one matches. Payloads hold ids and states only, never a phone number or email.

apiKey.description: A publishable (`pk_...`) or secret (`sk_...`) API key.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed. `field` names the problem.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, unknown, wrong or revoked key. Always the same body.

Forbidden.description: The key is valid but lacks the scope, or is used from an origin it is not allowed from. A staff session whose password must still be changed gets `error` `password_change_required` on every route except `/v1/auth/me`, `/v1/auth/refresh` and `/v1/auth/password`.

NotFound.description: Not found, or belongs to another tenant.

TooLarge.description: The request would read more than the limit (100,000 entries). Verify one UTC day at a time with `date`.

Unprocessable.description: The notice does not define a purpose, nothing was granted, or the tenant profile is incomplete.

errors.description: Every problem, when there are several (publishing a notice).

WebhookEvent.description: The first four are events that happen. The last four are reminders sent by a job (`pnpm --filter @saral/api reminders`, run at least once an hour): `breach.deadline_soon` (the Board has not been told of an incident and its deadline is within 24 hours), `breach.deadline_passed` (the deadline has passed), `ropa.review_soon` (the next review of the record of processing is within 14 days) and `ropa.review_overdue` (the review date has passed). Each reminder is sent once for each incident or version of the record.

disabledReason.description: Null while the endpoint is active. `failures` when Saral disabled it; `admin` otherwise, including endpoints disabled before reasons were kept.

previousSecretUntil.description: While a rotation's old secret still signs deliveries alongside the new one

id.description: Also the `Idempotency-Key` the receiver sees.

lastStatus.description: The HTTP status of the last try

lastError.description: Short words about why the last try failed.

data.description: For consent.granted: consentId, receiptId, noticeId, principalId (pseudonymous), collectionMethod, status and purposes (key and granted). For consent.withdrawn: consentId, noticeId, principalId, status, withdrawnAt. For dsr.submitted: requestId, type, state, dueAt, principalId. For dsr.transitioned: requestId, type, from, state, dueAt. For breach.deadline_soon and breach.deadline_passed: breachId and boardDeadline. For ropa.review_soon and ropa.review_overdue: ropaVersionId, version and nextReviewDue (a date). Never the person's text or contact, and never the words of an incident or of the record.

BreachReport.description: The fields of the incident form. All but `occurredAt` and `approxPrincipalsAffected` are required to report; a correction sends any of them.

discoveredAt.description: When the organisation found out. Not in the future

boardSha256.description: The `boardSha256` that came with the drafts the officer read.

principalSha256.description: The `principalSha256` that came with the drafts the officer read.

boardSha256.description: SHA-256 of `boardNotification`. A sign-off must carry it.

principalSha256.description: SHA-256 of `principalNotice`. A sign-off must carry it.

boardDeadline.description: 72 hours after `discoveredAt`. A working default that has not been confirmed against the Rules.

boardOverdue.description: The Board has not been told and the deadline has passed.

boardNotifiedLate.description: The Board was told after the deadline. Null until it has been told.

note.description: Why this version was saved. It is not part of the record

basedOn.description: The version the change started from

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored text of the record.

RopaDocument.description: The record of processing. About thirty questions in all (ten about the organisation and its review, fifteen for each activity).

website.description: An https address without a user name or password.

name.description: Unique among the activities

securityMeasures.description: At least one, unless `otherMeasures` says what is done.

token.description: A signed session token (starts with st_v1.). Send it as a bearer token.

mustChangePassword.description: True while the person is still using a password an operator gave them (accounts made or reset with the operator tool). Such a session can only call `/v1/auth/me`, `/v1/auth/refresh` and `/v1/auth/password`; every other route answers 403 with `error` `password_change_required`. Changing the password makes it false.

recoveryCodes.description: Only on the first sign-in, shown once.

Identifier.description: An E.164 phone number (+919876543210) or an email address.

withdrawalUrl.description: https. Every receipt names it as the way to withdraw.

key.description: What the SDK sends. Unique in the notice.

retention.description: How long, in words, as the notice says it.

retentionDays.description: How long, in days, as receipts say it.

thirdPartyName.description: Required, and listed in notice.thirdParties, when thirdPartyDisclosure is true. Not allowed otherwise.

DividendEvent.description:
One discrete cash dividend.

Time is a year fraction on the same basis as `time_to_expiry_years`, not a
calendar date. The contract carries no calendar, day-count convention or
timezone, and introducing one here to express a dividend date would add a
basis the rest of the contract does not have and cannot validate. The
engine's own `DividendEvent` is `ex_time_years` for the same reason.

FusedAnalyticsRequest.description:
A request for price and Greeks, optionally at a volatility solved from an
observed premium first.

With `market_price`, volatility is solved and the Greeks are evaluated at
the solved value — one admission, one solve, and the solved point passed
inward as verified evidence rather than re-derived. Without it, the
supplied `volatility` is used and the result is the all-ten-Greeks
operation under another name.

market_price.description: The observed premium to invert before evaluating the Greeks.

GreeksAllTen.description:
Available Greeks on the contract's stated bases; absent values are explained by `unavailable`.

Time derivatives are **per year**. The engine reports them per calendar
day, which embeds a 365-day calendar; the contract carries no calendar,
so the service scales by the engine's own day count at this boundary and
the caller applies whichever convention it holds. Vega is raw `dV/dσ` per
unit volatility, not per point. Nothing else is rescaled.

unavailable.description:
Each omitted Greek has a reason. A resolved zero is present as 0.0.
Codes distinguish unsupported quantities, model domain/validity,
accuracy refusals and unresolved numerical derivatives.

RegimeRequest.description:
At least 512 comparable positive prices, ordered oldest to newest.
No sampling interval is supplied, inferred or assumed.
Longer arrays are cropped to the latest 512; inference uses that window's
latest 507 prices. Every supplied price must be finite and positive.
The encoded request body is limited to 32 KiB (policy may narrow this).
Corporate-action adjustment is the caller's responsibility; the V1 model
was trained on split-adjusted closes, without cash-dividend total-return adjustment.

from the server clock. RFC 3339 with an explicit UTC offset.

RegimeScoreContract.description:
Applies separately to every available decision, direction and state head;
never multiply heads or interpret their scores as a joint probability.
Identifies score semantics, not calibration. The volatility head has no scores,
and the crisis score has its own crisis_score_contract.

sum_tolerance.description:
For each available prediction, using serialized values:
abs(sum(prediction.scores[*].value) - 1) <= sum_tolerance.

value.description: Finite score in [0,1]; not a calibrated probability.

label.description:
Volatility relative to the other state in the reference Markov model, not
historical norms. Fixed Student-t degrees of freedom make scale ordering
identical to standard-deviation ordering. Neither label indicates direction.

value.description: Finite score in [0,1]; not a calibrated probability.

RegimeStateLabel.description:
Volatility relative to the other state in the reference Markov model, not
historical norms. Fixed Student-t degrees of freedom make scale ordering
identical to standard-deviation ordering. Neither label indicates direction.

RegimeVolatilityBasis.description: What the label states; neither component fits a model on this request.

RegimeVolatilityHead.description:
Same envelope as the other heads. Available has a prediction and no
reason_code. not_applicable (predicted_not_eligible) occurs exactly when the
detector is not in crisis and the decision is not_eligible; it does not
assert not-crisis, which result.crisis states separately.

RegimeVolatilityLabel.description:
Served current-volatility label under `three-label-v1`. Not a probability,
forecast or historical-norm level.

RegimeVolatilityLabelProvenance.description:
Identity of the served volatility label: its combination rule and both
pinned inputs. A different student, detector or rule has a different method.

ResidualBasis.description:
The basis a solved residual is expressed in.

The residual is not one quantity. European and Black paths report a
forward-normalised price residual comparable against the engine's
convergence threshold; American models report a
raw option-price residual. Publishing the number without its basis would
invite exactly the cross-model comparison it does not support, so the basis
travels with it and a client that ignores this field cannot silently get it
wrong.

Submits ownership proof + a certification image for the listing; drives the listing through the verification state machine (SUBMITTED -> AI_REVIEW -> AI_SUGGESTED) and returns the created review.

post.description: Validates the email/password, hashes the password with Argon2id, persists the account with the default role, and returns the created account.

post.description: Revokes the refresh token presented in the HttpOnly cookie so it can no longer be used to obtain a fresh access token, and clears the cookie. Idempotent: always succeeds regardless of whether the token was ever valid.

Verifies the email/password against the stored Argon2id hash and returns a short-lived access token (RS256 JWT with the account's RBAC role) in the body; the rotating refresh token is set as an HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax cookie scoped to the auth routes and is never returned in JSON.

info.title: Bindu Agent API
info.summary: A2A-protocol agent over JSON-RPC 2.0, with DID identity, OAuth2 authentication, and optional x402 payments.
info.description:
# Bindu Agent — canonical OpenAPI

This specification describes the HTTP surface every Bindu-built agent
exposes. Agents built with [`bindufy()`](https://docs.getbindu.com/bindu/reference/bindufy)
answer to these endpoints out of the box; no per-agent route code is
written by the handler author.

The spec is **generic** — it intentionally avoids any one domain
(stock analysis, weather, etc.). Use it as the source of truth for
clients calling *any* Bindu agent; domain-specific overlays belong
in a per-agent OpenAPI that `$ref`s the schemas here.

---

## Mental model: one endpoint, many methods

Every call goes to `POST /`. The `jsonrpc.method` field in the body
selects what you want to do:

| Method | What you're doing |
|---|---|
| `message/send` | Kick off work. Returns a `Task` object. |
| `tasks/get` | Poll that task by id until it terminates. |
| `tasks/list` | See the caller's task history. |
| `tasks/cancel` | Stop a running task. |
| `tasks/feedback` | Rate a completed task. |
| `contexts/list` | See active conversation contexts. |
| `contexts/clear` | Reset a context. |
| `message/stream` | *(Experimental)* SSE stream of task deltas. |

Auxiliary endpoints (skills, DID resolution, negotiation, payment)
use conventional REST paths — see the *Paths* section.

---

## Task-first architecture

Every interaction creates a trackable **Task** with a unique
`id`. This matters even for "quick" agents because:

- **Tasks are pollable** — long-running work (5–10 minutes of
  multi-agent analysis, say) doesn't block your HTTP connection.
- **Tasks chain** — pass `referenceTaskIds` to build Task B on
  top of Task A's results. The server orchestrates the ordering
  automatically.
- **Tasks share context** — pass the same `contextId` to keep
  conversation history across calls.
- **Tasks have states** — you always know where the work is.

### State machine

Non-terminal (work still possible):
- `submitted` — queued, not yet picked up
- `working` — agent is actively processing
- `input-required` — paused, waiting for user clarification
- `auth-required` — paused, waiting for an auth flow

Terminal (task frozen, cannot be resumed):
- `completed` — success, artifacts available
- `failed` — processing error (check `status.message`)
- `canceled` — user terminated via `tasks/cancel`
- `rejected` — invalid input / agent declined (check `status.message`)

**Terminal tasks are immutable.** To refine a completed answer,
submit a new `message/send` with `referenceTaskIds: [<old-task-id>]`
— the new task can read the old task's artifacts and build from
there.

---

## Authentication

### Layer 1 — bearer token (required on writable methods)

```
Authorization: Bearer <hydra-issued access token>
```

The server introspects the token against Ory Hydra. Scopes map to
methods:

| Scope | Unlocks |
|---|---|
| `agent:read` | `tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `contexts/list`, all `GET`s |
| `agent:write` | `message/send`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/feedback`, `contexts/clear` |

`agent:execute` (legacy) implies both.

### Layer 2 — DID request signing (optional, recommended for agent-to-agent)

When you're an agent calling another agent, sign each request:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-DID` | Your full DID string |
| `X-DID-Timestamp` | Unix seconds (must be within ±300s of server clock) |
| `X-DID-Signature` | base58(Ed25519 signature over the payload) |

The payload is Python's `json.dumps({"body":body,"did":did,"timestamp":ts}, sort_keys=True)`
— note default separators include spaces after `:` and `,`. The
body is the exact UTF-8 bytes you send — any re-serialization by
middleware breaks the signature and the server responds
`reason: "crypto_mismatch"`.

Signature verification is:
1. Gate 1 — introspect bearer → `client_id` must start with `did:`
2. Gate 2 — `X-DID` header must equal the token's `client_id`
3. Gate 3 — Hydra metadata for that client must have `public_key` set
4. Gate 4 — Ed25519 verify + timestamp within window

See [`docs/DID.md`](./DID.md) for the full walk-through and common
failure modes.

### Layer 3 — x402 payment (optional, on paid endpoints only)

Send a base64-encoded x402 payload as `X-PAYMENT` on
`message/send`, or obtain a session-based grant via
`POST /api/start-payment-session` first.

---

## Error catalog

Errors come back in the JSON-RPC envelope as
`{ jsonrpc, id, error: { code, message, data? } }`.

### Standard JSON-RPC (per RFC)

| Code | Name | HTTP | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-32700` | Parse error | 400 | Body isn't valid JSON |
| `-32600` | Invalid Request | 400 | Body is JSON but not a valid JSON-RPC request |
| `-32601` | Method not found | 404 | `method` isn't one this agent supports |
| `-32602` | Invalid params | 400 | `params` fails schema validation |
| `-32603` | Internal error | 500 | Server-side bug; file a GH issue |

### A2A protocol

| Code | Name | HTTP | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-32001` | TaskNotFound | 404 | `taskId` doesn't exist or isn't yours |
| `-32002` | TaskNotCancelable | 400 | Task already in a terminal state |
| `-32003` | PushNotificationNotSupported | 400 | Agent doesn't do push |
| `-32004` | UnsupportedOperation | 400 | e.g. `message/stream` on a non-streaming agent |
| `-32005` | ContentTypeNotSupported | 400 | `acceptedOutputModes` doesn't overlap agent capabilities |
| `-32006` | InvalidAgentResponse | 500 | Agent produced a malformed result (bug in agent) |
| `-32007` | AuthenticatedExtendedCardNotConfigured | 400 | Extended card requested but agent didn't publish one |

### Bindu extensions

| Code | Name | HTTP | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-32008` | TaskImmutable | 400 | Attempted to modify a terminal task |
| `-32009` | AuthenticationRequired | 401 | No bearer token on a protected method |
| `-32010` | InvalidToken | 401 | Token introspection returned `active: false` |
| `-32011` | TokenExpired | 401 | `exp` in the past |
| `-32012` | InvalidTokenSignature | 403 | X-DID-Signature failed verification |
| `-32013` | InsufficientPermissions | 403 | Token valid but scope doesn't cover this method |
| `-32020` | ContextNotFound | 404 | `contextId` doesn't exist |
| `-32021` | ContextNotCancelable | 400 | Tried to clear a context still in use |
| `-32030` | SkillNotFound | 404 | `skillId` in the URL doesn't exist |

---

## Versioning

- Path shape is stable. New methods may be added under `POST /`
  but existing methods don't break compatibility.
- Schema fields may be added (backward-compatible). Renames or
  removals go through a deprecation window announced in the
  [changelog](https://docs.getbindu.com/changelog).
- Error code numeric values are permanent once assigned.

servers.description: Default local-development server (first `bindufy()` agent on a host)
Local agent on a custom port (set via `BINDU_PORT`)

agent.description: Agent subdomain (matches the agent's `name` in config)

tags.name: JSON-RPC
tags.description:
The central endpoint (`POST /`). Every task, message, and context
operation goes here, differentiated by the `method` field inside
the body.

tags.name: Agent Discovery
tags.description:
How clients learn what an agent can do. The agent card
(`/.well-known/agent.json`) is the canonical A2A discovery
surface. Skills endpoints expose per-capability metadata.

tags.name: DID Resolution
tags.description:
Turn a `did:bindu:...` identifier into a DID Document (the
public key + verification method + controller). Used by peers
that want to verify signatures without hitting Hydra directly.

tags.name: Skills
tags.description:
Each agent has zero or more `Skill`s. A skill is one specific
thing the agent can do — with structured input/output types,
description, and documentation.

tags.name: Negotiation
tags.description:
Capability-matching endpoint for orchestrators. Given a task
summary and constraints, the agent scores whether it can
handle the task and returns a confidence.

tags.name: Payment (x402)
tags.description:
For paid agents. Implements the x402 payment protocol over
USDC on Base. Session-based so clients don't have to sign
every request.

tags.name: Health & Monitoring

get.description:
A convenience: `GET /` returns `302 Found` pointing at the
agent card. Useful for humans browsing to the agent's base
URL — they end up at something meaningful instead of a 404.

302.description: Redirect to `/.well-known/agent.json`

post.summary: JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint (all agent operations dispatch here)
post.description:
Every write or read operation on tasks, messages, and contexts
uses this endpoint. The `method` field in the body selects the
operation. See the *Error catalog* in the top-level description
for every possible `error.code`.

**Accepted methods:** `message/send`, `message/stream`
*(experimental)*, `tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `tasks/cancel`,
`tasks/feedback`, `contexts/list`, `contexts/clear`.

**Casing tolerance:** the server accepts both camelCase
(`taskId`) and snake_case (`task_id`) in `params` — pick one
and stick with it per-call. Responses are always snake_case
for legacy consistency (see
[`bugs/known-issues.md#wire-field-casing-is-mixed`](../bugs/known-issues.md)).

**Size limit:** request bodies over 10 MB return `413
Payload Too Large` at the ASGI layer (does not use the
JSON-RPC error envelope).

**Idempotency:** `message/send` is NOT idempotent — a repeat
call creates a new task. If you need idempotency, have your
client generate a stable `messageId` and use `contexts/list`
+ `tasks/list` to check whether you've already sent it.

parts.text: What is the capital of France?

messageSendChained.summary: Continue from an earlier task (Task A → Task B)
messageSendChained.description:
Pass `referenceTaskIds` to make this task depend on
a previous one. The server propagates the earlier
task's artifacts into this task's context.

parts.text: Summarize the previous analysis in three bullets.

messageSendWithPayment.summary: Paid agent (x402 payload inline in metadata)
messageSendWithPayment.description:
When the agent requires payment and you've already
executed the x402 flow, embed the payload in
`message.metadata.x402.payment` with
`status: "payment-submitted"`. The server's
middleware auto-injects the verified context into
`message.metadata._payment_context` before the
handler sees the message — don't set
`_payment_context` yourself.

tasksGetWithHistory.summary: Poll and trim history to the last N turns
tasksGetWithHistory.description:
`historyLength` caps the returned `history` array
to the most recent N messages. Useful for polling
loops where you only want the newest updates.

tasksList.description:
Returns tasks scoped to the caller's DID (when
auth is on). `history_length` caps the `history`
array inside each returned task — it does NOT
cap the number of tasks returned. *Spec bug we've
flagged — see below.*

tasksFeedback.description:
Feedback is advisory — stored against the task row
for later analytics. Does NOT modify the task's
state (it's already terminal).

contextsList.description:
`history_length` caps tasks-per-context in the
returned view. Does not cap number of contexts.

contextsClear.summary: Clear a context (all non-running tasks purged)
contextsClear.description:
Running tasks inside the context are NOT affected.
The agent may refuse with `-32021 ContextNotCancelable`
if any task is still `working`.

200.description:
Successful JSON-RPC response. `result` contains the typed
output per method — see `components/schemas/*Result`.

messageSendSubmitted.description: Task created and queued. Poll `tasks/get` for progress.

parts.text: What is the capital of France?

tasksGetInputRequired.description:
The agent paused and needs clarification. Look at
`status.message` for the question; send a new
`message/send` on the same context to continue.

parts.text: Which period should I analyze — last 30 days or year-to-date?

tasksGetCompleted.description:
Work finished. The answer is in `artifacts[]`.
`metadata.did.message.signature` (when present)
is the agent's Ed25519 signature over the artifact
text — clients can verify authenticity via DID
resolution.

parts.text: What is the capital of France?

tasksGetFailed.description:
Processing error. `status.message` carries the
human-readable cause. Task is terminal — can't
be resumed; submit a fresh message if you want
to retry.

parts.text: Upstream data source unavailable; tried 3 times.

tasksGetRejected.description:
Agent declined to process the input (e.g., outside
its capability scope, invalid format). Check
`status.message` for the decline reason.

parts.text: Request is outside this agent's declared capabilities.

errorTaskNotCancelable.description: Cannot cancel a task that's already terminal.

error.message: Task is already in terminal state 'completed' and cannot be canceled

errorInvalidParams.description: params didn't match the method's schema

errorInsufficientPermissions.description: Valid token but scope doesn't cover the method.

error.message: Scope 'agent:read' does not permit method 'message/send'; requires 'agent:write'

403.description: Token valid but DID signature failed (when DID signing is required)

413.description: Request body exceeded the 10 MB limit

500.description: Internal error

get.description:
The A2A standard discovery document. Any client that knows the
agent's base URL can `GET` this to learn the agent's DID,
capabilities, published skills, and where to send requests.

`OPTIONS` and `HEAD` are also accepted — useful for CORS
preflight and liveness probes respectively.

skills.name: Example Skill
skills.description: One thing the agent can do.

get.description:
Return the DID Document for a `did:bindu:...` identifier. The
document contains the agent's public key, which peers use to
verify signatures on artifacts and requests.

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: Full DID string

post.description:
Alternate form for clients that prefer POST (keeps the DID
out of URL logs). Returns the same document `GET` would.

get.summary: List all skills this agent publishes

example.name: Example Skill
example.description: One thing the agent can do.

get.description:
The authoritative user-facing doc for this skill. Returns the
frontmatter-ed Markdown file the agent shipped. Use this
instead of the short `description` when you need full usage
guidance, examples, or input schemas.

text/markdown.example:
---
name: Example Skill
version: 1.0.0
---
# Example

Usage...

post.summary: Ask whether this agent can handle a task
post.description:
Orchestrators use this to pick the best agent for a task
before sending a real `message/send`. The agent returns a
capability score (0–1) weighted across skill match, I/O
compatibility, performance, load, and cost.

A score below the caller's `min_score` is interpreted as
"decline" — the orchestrator should route the task
elsewhere. This endpoint never actually performs the task;
it's advisory.

example.task_details: Reader is a non-technical manager. Output should be plain English Markdown.

reasons: Current load at 12%, well below threshold

post.description:
Initiates a payment session for agents that charge per
request. Returns a session handle the caller uses with
`message/send` (via the `X-PAYMENT` header or session-linked
metadata) until the session is spent or expired.

Paid agents only. Unpaid agents return `404`.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description:
When `true`, the server blocks up to 60 seconds waiting
for the session to transition to a terminal state
(`completed`, `failed`, `expired`). Useful to avoid
tight-loop polling.

get.description:
HTML page users browse to in order to complete payment via a
browser wallet. Not a machine-callable endpoint — clients that
want programmatic payment should use the x402 flow directly.

Returns 200 when healthy, 503 when any mandatory dependency
(storage, scheduler, message bus, grpc) is degraded. The body
carries per-component status so orchestrators can show which
specific thing is broken.

503.description: Degraded — at least one critical component failing

get.description:
Standard Prometheus text format. Key series include:

- `http_requests_total{method, path, status}` — request counts
- `http_request_duration_seconds` — latency histogram
- `agent_tasks_active` — count by state
- `agent_tasks_completed_total{state}` — lifetime terminal counts
- `agent_llm_tokens_total{direction, model}` — token usage

text/plain.example:
# HELP http_requests_total Total HTTP requests.
# TYPE http_requests_total counter
http_requests_total{method="POST",path="/",status="200"} 42
# HELP agent_tasks_active Active tasks by state.
# TYPE agent_tasks_active gauge
agent_tasks_active{state="working"} 3

bearerAuth.description:
Ory Hydra-issued OAuth 2.0 access token
(opaque `ory_at_...`). Required on all writable JSON-RPC
methods and on paid endpoints. Scopes map to methods
(see the top-level description).

didSignature.name: X-DID
didSignature.description:
Optional DID-based request signing. When `X-DID` is sent, the
request body is signed with the DID holder's Ed25519 private
key. **Three headers** must all be present:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-DID` | Full DID string (the same as the bearer token's `client_id`) |
| `X-DID-Timestamp` | Unix seconds, ±300s of server clock |
| `X-DID-Signature` | base58(Ed25519 over payload) |

Payload is Python's `json.dumps({"body":<raw-body-bytes>,"did":<did>,"timestamp":<ts>}, sort_keys=True)`.
Default Python separators include spaces after `:` and `,` —
match exactly. Any re-serialization of the body between the
signer and the wire breaks verification.

x402Payment.name: X-PAYMENT
x402Payment.description:
Base64-encoded x402 payment payload. Required on paid
endpoints when you haven't started a session via
`POST /api/start-payment-session` first. The decoded payload is:

```json
{
  "x402Version": 1,
  "scheme": "exact",
  "network": "base-sepolia",
  "payload": {
    "signature": "0x...",
    "authorization": {
      "from": "0x...",
      "to": "0x...",
      "value": "100",
      "validAfter": "...",
      "validBefore": "...",
      "nonce": "0x..."
    }
  }
}
```

See [x402.org](https://x402.org) for the full spec.

JsonRpcRequest.description:
JSON-RPC 2.0 request envelope. One of the per-method
`params` shapes must be supplied via the `method` field.

id.description: Caller-chosen request id. The response echoes it back.

JsonRpcResponse.description:
JSON-RPC 2.0 response envelope. Exactly one of `result` or
`error` is present.

result.description: Method-specific result (see per-method result schemas)

code.description:
Error code. See the *Error catalog* in the top-level
description for the full list.

data.description: Optional structured detail — varies per error.

contextId.description:
Conversation context. New contexts are created
automatically when omitted; pass a previous
`contextId` to continue the same conversation.

taskId.description:
Caller-provided task id. The server uses this as the
outbound task's id — lets clients correlate before a
response arrives.

referenceTaskIds.description:
Earlier tasks this task depends on. The server fetches
their artifacts and makes them available to the handler
as context.

metadata.description:
Free-form. Two reserved keys:
- `x402.payment` — inline x402 payment submission (see
  the `message/send - With Payment` example).
- `_payment_context` — server-injected, read-only; the
  verified x402 context. Do not set this yourself.

acceptedOutputModes.description:
MIME types the client accepts in artifacts. Common
values: `application/json`, `text/plain`,
`text/markdown`. If the agent can't produce any of
these, it returns `-32005 ContentTypeNotSupported`.

blocking.description:
If `true`, the server holds the HTTP connection open

info.description: Design contract for Spring Boot4.1.0/JDK21 single-instance memory mode. api.md and feature spec supply normative business invariants and code precedence.
