post.summary: Register a tenant admin account and bootstrap tenant access
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
A brand-new subscriber needs a secure, first-class admin identity to operate the platform. Without this endpoint,
onboarding would require manual platform-team intervention and would break self-service SaaS adoption.

What this endpoint does:
It creates the first admin user for a tenant, ensures tenant provisioning exists, ensures a trial subscription exists,
sets access/refresh tokens as HttpOnly cookies, and returns safe user context in response body.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates uniqueness of email, provisions tenant records when necessary, enforces admin-user quota policy,
stores password hash securely, issues an engine-signed JWT access token, creates a refresh token row, and controller
writes both tokens into secure cookies before returning AuthUserResponse.

201.description: Admin account created and authenticated session returned

post.summary: Log in an existing admin and issue fresh auth cookies
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Admin operators need a secure login path to start authenticated management sessions for tenant resources.

What this endpoint does:
It authenticates the admin using email/password, revokes prior refresh tokens for session hygiene, and issues
a fresh access token plus a new refresh token as HttpOnly cookies.

How this endpoint does it:
The service verifies account status and password hash, rotates refresh-token state to avoid stale session reuse,
and controller writes cookies while returning safe user context payload.

200.description: Login successful and new auth cookies issued

post.summary: Rotate refresh cookie and issue a new admin session
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Access tokens are intentionally short-lived. A secure refresh mechanism is required to keep admins signed in
without repeatedly collecting credentials.

What this endpoint does:
It reads refresh token from HttpOnly cookie, validates it, rotates token state, and sets fresh access/refresh cookies.

How this endpoint does it:
Controller extracts refresh_token cookie, service validates persistence state (including expiry/revocation),
applies one-time-use rotation semantics, and controller rewrites secure cookies.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Sessions must support explicit and secure sign-out to prevent lingering browser-side authentication state.

What this endpoint does:
It clears access_token and refresh_token cookies.

How this endpoint does it:
Controller writes both token cookies with maxAge=0, path=/, HttpOnly/Secure attributes.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Frontend needs a lightweight session-hydration endpoint after reload to confirm authentication and tenant context.

What this endpoint does:
It returns current authenticated user's profile details (no tokens).

How this endpoint does it:
JWT filter populates security/tenant context from cookie or bearer token, and controller maps context to response DTO.

get.summary: Get CSRF token for browser cookie session mode
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Browser-based admin sessions use HttpOnly auth cookies and require CSRF token submission for state-changing requests.

What this endpoint does:
It returns the current CSRF token value and ensures CSRF cookie state is initialized for the caller.

How this endpoint does it:
Spring Security creates/loads token via cookie token repository, controller returns it as a simple JSON payload.

post.summary: Register admin in headless token mode
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Headless/API clients cannot reliably consume browser cookie flows and need explicit token payloads.

What this endpoint does:
It performs the same registration flow as cookie mode but returns access/refresh tokens directly in response body.

How this endpoint does it:
Service runs standard tenant bootstrap/registration pipeline and controller returns AuthResponse without writing cookies.

201.description: Admin registered and token payload returned

post.summary: Log in admin in headless token mode
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
API clients and external automation flows need explicit JWT credentials in response body.

What this endpoint does:
It authenticates admin credentials and returns fresh access/refresh tokens directly in payload.

How this endpoint does it:
Service validates credentials, rotates refresh-token state, and controller returns AuthResponse DTO.

200.description: Login successful and token payload returned

post.summary: Refresh session in headless token mode
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Headless integrations need refresh-token rotation without cookie transport.

What this endpoint does:
It validates provided refresh token and returns a rotated access/refresh token pair.

How this endpoint does it:
Controller accepts RefreshTokenRequest payload and delegates to refresh-token rotation service.

post.summary: Restore original super-admin cookies after impersonation
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Super-admin support sessions must safely return from tenant impersonation to original privileged context.

What this endpoint does:
It restores stashed super-admin auth cookies and clears temporary impersonation cookies.

How this endpoint does it:
Cookie utility reads stashed `sa_*` cookies, rewrites primary auth cookies, and clears impersonation artifacts.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Tenant operators must understand their active entitlement before launching campaigns or scaling usage.

What this endpoint does:
It returns the authenticated tenant's current subscription record, including plan, status, billing period,
quota limits, and latest payment reference.

How this endpoint does it:
Tenant context is extracted from admin JWT claims, then subscription and plan metadata are joined and mapped into
a SubscriptionResponse object for a single, dashboard-friendly read.

post.summary: Start or change tenant subscription plan
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
SaaS tenants need a direct API path to activate or upgrade plans without out-of-band support workflows.

What this endpoint does:
It takes the requested plan, executes the checkout flow (mock success in MVP), updates subscription status,
records payment transaction metadata, and returns updated subscription state.

How this endpoint does it:
The service uses authenticated tenant context, validates requested plan existence, executes payment gateway abstraction,
persists subscription changes and payment reference details, and returns normalized quota-aware response fields.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Tenants and platform operators both need a canonical list of active plans with limits and pricing attributes.

What this endpoint does:
It returns all active plan definitions including quota constraints such as maximum campaigns,
max responses per campaign, and max admin users.

How this endpoint does it:
The plan catalog service reads persistent plan definition rows, filters active plans, maps entities to API DTOs,
and returns a list suitable for onboarding forms and pricing pages.

put.summary: Create or update a plan definition (SUPER_ADMIN)
put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Plan governance must evolve over time as business strategy changes. A controlled mutation endpoint is needed
for super administrators to adjust commercial limits safely.

What this endpoint does:
It inserts or updates a plan definition, including display metadata, billing-cycle metadata, and quota parameters.

How this endpoint does it:
The endpoint is protected by super-admin role checks, validates request constraints,
persists the plan catalog mutation, and returns the resulting plan definition used by runtime quota enforcement.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Platform operators require fast, aggregate visibility into tenant and subscription health.

What this endpoint does:
It returns key platform counters such as total tenants, active subscriptions, and aggregate usage.

How this endpoint does it:
Super-admin service aggregates metrics from tenant/subscription/usage stores and maps them to response DTO.

get.summary: List tenants with subscription and status overview
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Super-admin workflows require tenant inventory with billing and active-state context for support and governance.

What this endpoint does:
It returns paged tenant overview data including subscription plan and activity state.

How this endpoint does it:
Tenant-admin service queries tenant/subscription aggregates and returns Spring Data paged response structure.

get.summary: Retrieve platform metrics via tenant-admin namespace
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Some super-admin UI bundles consume tenant-admin namespace for platform metrics.

What this endpoint does:
It returns the same platform metrics payload as `/api/v1/admin/superadmin/metrics`.

How this endpoint does it:
Controller delegates to the same metrics service used by primary super-admin metrics endpoint.

post.summary: Override tenant subscription plan as super admin

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
The question bank is the foundation of reusable survey content. Teams need a way to add standardized question assets
once and reuse them across many surveys.

What this endpoint does:
It creates a question with text, type, and scoring metadata and stores version context used by downstream snapshots.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates required fields and max score constraints, applies tenant scoping from auth context,
persists the question entity, and returns a QuestionResponse containing metadata and version pointers.

get.summary: List active questions for current tenant
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Authoring UIs require fast retrieval of available question inventory during survey design.

What this endpoint does:
It returns active, tenant-scoped question records currently available for composition.

How this endpoint does it:
The question service uses tenant-aware repository filtering and maps entity rows into response DTOs for list rendering.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Detailed question retrieval is required for edit forms, review pages, and diagnostics.

What this endpoint does:
It returns one question record by identifier under tenant access control.

How this endpoint does it:
The service resolves the record by ID with tenant-scoped checks and maps the result to a QuestionResponse DTO.

put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Content quality evolves over time and questions require controlled updates.

What this endpoint does:
It updates question fields and maintains version continuity used by snapshot-based references.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates payload constraints, checks tenant ownership, persists changes, and returns updated question data.

delete.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Historical integrity is important, so hard-deletes are avoided while obsolete questions must be removed from active authoring lists.

What this endpoint does:
It marks the target question as inactive.

How this endpoint does it:
The service resolves the question by tenant context, updates active status, and returns no-content on success.

post.summary: Create a category grouping for questions
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Categories group question assets into business dimensions that support structure, analytics, and scoring design.

What this endpoint does:
It creates a category with optional question mappings and stores category metadata under tenant ownership.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates category payloads, checks referenced question constraints where needed,
persists category + mappings, and returns CategoryResponse with mapping summaries.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Authoring screens need category inventory for survey composition and weighting strategy.

What this endpoint does:
It returns active categories available in the authenticated tenant workspace.

How this endpoint does it:
The category service applies tenant filters and active-state filters, then maps entity results to response DTOs.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Category detail pages and editor forms need full mapping visibility.

What this endpoint does:
It returns a single category record including mapped-question metadata.

How this endpoint does it:
The service loads category and mapping state under tenant scope and returns a DTO optimized for UI consumption.

put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Category definitions and ordering can change as survey programs mature.

What this endpoint does:
It updates category metadata and mapped-question configuration.

How this endpoint does it:
Validation and tenant checks run first, then mapping set updates are persisted and reflected in the response DTO.

delete.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Teams need to retire categories without deleting historical campaign and scoring references.

What this endpoint does:
It marks the category as inactive for future authoring while retaining historical records.

How this endpoint does it:
The service enforces tenant ownership, flips active status, and returns no content.

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Survey lifecycle begins with a draft container where structure can be assembled before publication.

What this endpoint does:
It creates a tenant-scoped survey draft with title, description, and page/question structure.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates schema, persists draft state, and returns the survey representation including lifecycle status.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Admin dashboards require an overview of reusable survey assets and lifecycle states.

What this endpoint does:
It returns active surveys under current tenant scope.

How this endpoint does it:
Survey repository filters by tenant and active state, then maps records to response DTOs.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Teams need detailed survey context for editing, publishing decisions, and audits.

What this endpoint does:
It returns one survey including pages/questions and lifecycle metadata.

How this endpoint does it:
The service resolves survey by id and tenant, then maps nested structures into SurveyResponse.

put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Draft surveys evolve before publication and require iterative edits.

What this endpoint does:
It updates survey details and structure when lifecycle rules allow modification.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates immutability/lifecycle constraints, persists updates, and returns the updated survey.

delete.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Organizations need to retire obsolete surveys without physically deleting historical references.

What this endpoint does:
It marks the survey inactive.

How this endpoint does it:
Tenant ownership is validated and active flag is disabled; endpoint returns no-content on success.

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Lifecycle transitions are a governance gate that prevents unsafe operations (for example activating campaigns from unpublished surveys).

What this endpoint does:
It applies a requested lifecycle transition (such as Draft->Published or Closed->Published with reason).

How this endpoint does it:
The service checks allowed transition matrix, validates transition requirements, updates lifecycle state,
and returns the updated survey representation.

post.summary: Create a campaign from a survey
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaigns are the executable delivery unit for collecting responses from a specific survey snapshot and runtime policy set.

What this endpoint does:
It creates a tenant-scoped campaign with name, survey binding, description, and access mode (PUBLIC/PRIVATE).

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates survey reference and tenant scope, normalizes deprecated auth mode values, persists campaign state,
and returns CampaignResponse.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaign operations teams need a dashboard view of active and manageable campaigns.

What this endpoint does:
It returns campaigns under authenticated tenant scope.

How this endpoint does it:
Campaign service executes tenant-scoped retrieval and response mapping.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaign detail retrieval is required for settings updates, monitoring, and support troubleshooting.

What this endpoint does:
It returns one campaign record with current status and metadata.

How this endpoint does it:
The service resolves campaign by tenant and id and returns mapped DTO fields.

put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaigns require controlled edits to operational metadata and associations.

What this endpoint does:
It updates campaign request fields while preserving lifecycle constraints.

How this endpoint does it:
Service validates ownership and allowed update semantics, then persists and returns updated campaign data.

delete.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Retiring campaign availability should not erase historical response evidence.

What this endpoint does:
It marks campaign inactive.

How this endpoint does it:
Tenant-scoped campaign lookup is followed by status/active-state mutation and no-content completion.

get.summary: Get admin preview payload for a campaign
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaign owners need a pre-launch visual/data validation endpoint to verify header/footer/questions and responder UX flags.

What this endpoint does:
It assembles campaign, survey, and settings into a responder-facing preview model for admin users.

How this endpoint does it:
Campaign service resolves campaign/settings/survey in tenant scope, maps each page/question with pinned version context,
and returns CampaignPreviewResponse.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Operations and UI flows require a read endpoint for persisted runtime controls before edit/save cycles.

What this endpoint does:
It returns the current campaign settings object.

How this endpoint does it:
Campaign service validates tenant-scoped campaign visibility and returns mapped CampaignSettingsResponse.

put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaign runtime behavior (quota, timeout, restrictions, UI toggles, metadata capture) must be adjustable
independently from core campaign identity.

What this endpoint does:
It stores runtime policy controls that are enforced when responders submit answers.
If closeDate is set to now/past, open responses are auto-locked immediately.

How this endpoint does it:
The service loads target campaign by tenant, merges settings payload, persists state,
and returns updated campaign context.

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Activation is a controlled launch gate. It prevents collecting responses from improperly prepared campaigns.

What this endpoint does:
It transitions a campaign into active state when preconditions pass, links latest survey snapshot,
and upserts campaign default weight profile from pinned category weights.

How this endpoint does it:
The service verifies linked survey lifecycle requirements (must be PUBLISHED), loads latest snapshot,
upserts default weight profile, updates campaign status to ACTIVE, and returns campaign response.

post.summary: Generate distribution channels for a campaign
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Operations teams need standardized distribution artifacts (links and embed formats) to launch outreach quickly.

What this endpoint does:
It generates and stores channel records such as public/private links and embed snippets.

How this endpoint does it:
Distribution service builds channel values from campaign context, persists channel rows, and returns generated list.

get.summary: List generated channels for a campaign
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Teams often need to re-fetch channel assets after initial generation for reminders and omnichannel delivery.

What this endpoint does:
It returns all persisted distribution channels for the campaign.

How this endpoint does it:
Distribution service reads campaign channel rows under tenant scope and maps to response DTOs.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Responder runtime needs a non-admin endpoint to load campaign form structure for public/private submission flows.

What this endpoint does:
It returns preview payload for campaigns currently active.

How this endpoint does it:
Service resolves campaign/settings/survey and returns CampaignPreviewResponse when campaign is active; access
mode enforcement for private campaigns happens on submit/auth endpoints.

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Private campaign authentication must be configured once per tenant so every campaign can reuse a consistent trust policy.

What this endpoint does:
It creates a tenant auth profile containing auth mode, trust metadata, claim mappings, fallback policy,
and OIDC/signing settings.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates tenant scope, enforces mapping rules (including required respondentId mapping),
applies defaults (such as OIDC scope defaults), persists profile + mappings, and writes audit events.

put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Identity provider details and claim models change over time; profile updates must be supported without rebuilding tenants.

What this endpoint does:
It updates auth profile trust settings, claim mappings, scope behavior, and fallback policies.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates tenant access and mapping constraints, applies secure defaults where required,
persists profile changes, and records before/after snapshots in auth audit.

get.summary: Get auth profile for a tenant
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Operators need an easy way to verify effective auth configuration before launching or troubleshooting private campaigns.

What this endpoint does:
It returns the tenant's auth profile and claim mapping configuration.

How this endpoint does it:
Tenant access checks are performed, then profile data is loaded and mapped to response DTO.

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Signing key version rotation is required for security hygiene and incident response readiness.

What this endpoint does:
It increments the active key version for a tenant auth profile.

How this endpoint does it:
The service updates active key version, persists change, and creates an audit record describing the rotation action.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Security-sensitive configuration changes require traceability for compliance and troubleshooting.

What this endpoint does:
It returns ordered audit entries for an auth profile including actor and before/after values.

How this endpoint does it:
The repository queries audit rows by auth_profile_id in descending timestamp order and returns serialized audit objects.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Tenant onboarding is faster and less error-prone when common IdP providers have pre-defined setup templates.

What this endpoint does:
It returns template metadata for supported providers, including default scopes, required config fields,
and default claim mapping suggestions.

How this endpoint does it:
A template service returns static curated provider definitions consumed by UI and SDK onboarding flows.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Setup forms often require provider-specific field guidance and defaults rather than a full template catalog.

What this endpoint does:
It returns one template by provider code (for example OKTA, AUTH0, AZURE_AD, KEYCLOAK).

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates provider code input, resolves the template from in-memory catalog, and returns structured metadata.

post.summary: Validate responder token against tenant auth policy
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Integrations and runtime checks require an explicit token-validation endpoint that applies tenant-specific trust policy.

What this endpoint does:
It validates responder token input according to configured auth mode and claim-mapping rules,
then returns standardized success/failure payload.

How this endpoint does it:
Service loads tenant auth profile, routes validation by mode (public/signed/OIDC external trust),
applies cryptographic and claim checks, and returns TokenValidationResult.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Private campaigns need a secure and tenant-aware way to initiate responder SSO without exposing platform-internal logic.

What this endpoint does:
It validates campaign + tenant eligibility for OIDC flow, creates one-time state/nonce context,
and returns IdP authorization URL details.

How this endpoint does it:
The OIDC service checks campaign auth mode and tenant auth profile mode, fetches OIDC metadata,
stores state with expiry, composes authorization URL with scopes/state/nonce, and returns OidcStartResponse.

get.summary: Complete OIDC callback and issue one-time responder access code
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Authorization-code OIDC requires callback handling to exchange code, verify trust, and convert external auth into
internal responder access state.

What this endpoint does:
It validates callback state/code, exchanges token at IdP, validates token claims, and issues one-time responder access code.

How this endpoint does it:
OIDC state record is checked for expiry and one-time use, token exchange is executed via configured metadata,
token validation service verifies claims/mappings, responder access code row is persisted, and either JSON response
or redirect response is returned.

200.description: Callback processed and access code returned

302.description: Redirect response emitted when returnPath was provided

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Tenant operators need visibility into operational activity for troubleshooting and governance.

What this endpoint does:
It returns paged audit logs filtered to the current tenant context.

How this endpoint does it:
Controller derives tenant id from security context and applies optional filter parameters on audit-log repository.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Super-admin operations require cross-tenant traceability for investigations and compliance.

What this endpoint does:
It returns paged audit logs across all tenants with optional filters for actor/action/entity/tenant.

How this endpoint does it:
Controller applies optional filter predicates and queries audit repository with descending timestamp ordering.

post.summary: Submit survey response (public and private campaign entry)
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
This is the central data-ingestion endpoint where responder participation is captured.

What this endpoint does:
It accepts answer payload for a campaign, enforces campaign status and runtime controls,
enforces private-auth requirements where applicable, validates against pinned snapshot versions,
auto-calculates weighted score when default profile exists, stores response and answers, then auto-locks response.

How this endpoint does it:
The service performs campaign lookup, access-mode enforcement (public or private), credential validation
(responderToken or responderAccessCode for private), settings checks (quota/restrictions/timeouts), snapshot-based
answer validation/scoring, persistence, and status transition to LOCKED before returning SurveyResponseResponse.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Support and operational teams need direct access to a specific response record for verification and exception handling.

What this endpoint does:
It returns one response and its answer details.

How this endpoint does it:
Response service resolves response by id under tenant context and maps nested answer records to DTO.

Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaign managers need a scoped list view of responses for review, quality checks, and manual workflows.

What this endpoint does:
It returns campaign-scoped response list under tenant ownership checks.

How this endpoint does it:
The service validates campaign accessibility under tenant context and fetches mapped response rows by campaign id.

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Although responses auto-lock on submit, operations teams may need explicit lock controls for exceptional workflows.

What this endpoint does:
It changes response state to locked and records lock timestamp.

How this endpoint does it:
Locking service validates current state and tenant ownership, applies status mutation, and returns updated response.

post.summary: Reopen a locked response with reason
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Real operations require a controlled exception path for corrections after lock.

What this endpoint does:
It reopens a previously locked response and captures reason/window metadata.

How this endpoint does it:
Locking service validates state transitions and reason constraints, updates response status,
and returns reopened response record. If campaign close date has passed, close-time lock enforcement may lock it again.

get.summary: Get aggregated analytics for a campaign
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaign operators need near-real-time aggregate visibility without reading raw response payloads.

What this endpoint does:
It returns aggregate counts and completion rate metrics for a campaign.

How this endpoint does it:
Analytics service runs campaign-scoped aggregate queries under tenant context and returns CampaignAnalytics DTO.

post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Score computation requires explicit category weighting definitions linked to campaign context.

What this endpoint does:
It creates a weight profile that defines how raw category scores contribute to total score.

How this endpoint does it:
Service validates campaign scope and category-weight payload, persists profile and nested weights,
and returns profile representation.

get.summary: Get one scoring profile by id
get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Teams need profile-level visibility for verification and lifecycle updates.

What this endpoint does:
It returns one weight profile including category weights.

How this endpoint does it:
Service loads profile by id under tenant context and maps to DTO.

put.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Scoring rubrics evolve and profiles require controlled updates.

What this endpoint does:
It updates profile metadata and category-weight assignments.

How this endpoint does it:
Service validates payload and tenant ownership, persists new values, and returns updated profile DTO.

delete.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Obsolete profiles must be retired while preserving historical result integrity.

What this endpoint does:
It marks profile inactive.

How this endpoint does it:
Tenant-scoped lookup followed by active-state mutation and no-content response.

post.summary: Validate category weight sum for a profile
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Invalid weighting definitions can produce misleading score outputs; explicit pre-check endpoint reduces operational mistakes.

What this endpoint does:
It validates profile constraints (including total weight sum rule).

How this endpoint does it:
Service computes profile totals and throws deterministic business error when constraints are violated.

get.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Campaign-level scoring operations need discoverability of attached profiles.

What this endpoint does:
It returns all active/in-scope profiles linked to the specified campaign.

How this endpoint does it:
Service validates campaign access by tenant and fetches profile rows filtered by campaign id.

post.summary: Calculate weighted score from raw category scores
post.description:
Why this endpoint is needed:
Consumers need deterministic score output from raw category data and configured business weighting policy.

What this endpoint does:
It computes normalized category contributions and returns a total weighted score breakdown.

How this endpoint does it:
Scoring engine loads profile weights, validates inputs, computes per-category normalized and weighted values,
and returns ScoreResult with category details.

bearerAuth.description: Engine-issued admin access token

ValidationError.description: Request validation failed or business rule validation failed

ForbiddenError.description: Authenticated but not allowed by tenant/role/security policy

NotFoundError.description: Referenced resource does not exist or is not visible in tenant scope

ConflictError.description: Requested action conflicts with current resource state

PaymentRequiredError.description: Active subscription is required for this operation

TooManyRequestsError.description: Quota or throttling rule prevented execution

CapabilityGrant.description: Handed to the authorised participant only: present it to the simulator to act.
CapabilityGrant.title: CapabilityGrant

CreateInvestigation.description: Legacy developer/evaluation input. Production creation selects a saved site instead.
CreateInvestigation.title: CreateInvestigation

DirectoryParticipant.description: A person in the site directory, ready to be added to an investigation.
DirectoryParticipant.title: DirectoryParticipant

DisagreementView.description: Two people's different answers to the same question, and how the engine reads them.
DisagreementView.title: DisagreementView

Extraction.description: Structured meaning of one participant answer. Never contains decisions.
Extraction.title: Extraction

InvestigationForecast.description:
An estimate of how this investigation will go if it carries on. Advisory only: it is
computed on a private copy of the engine and never changes the investigation.
InvestigationForecast.title: InvestigationForecast

info.title: SuperMolt API
info.description:
# SuperMolt Arena API

**AI Agent Trading Competition Platform**

Complete your agent's onboarding, compete for XP, trade on-chain, and earn USDC rewards.

## Quick Start

1. Authenticate via SIWS (Sign-In With Solana)
2. Complete onboarding tasks (300 XP)
3. Compete in token research tasks
4. Trade on-chain (Jupiter/Raydium)
5. Climb leaderboards (XP + Trading)

## Authentication

Most endpoints require JWT token:
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN
```

Get your token via `/auth/siws/challenge` → sign → `/auth/siws/verify`

## Base URL

```
https://sr-mobile-production.up.railway.app/api
```

info.title: OculOS API
info.description:
Universal UI automation API. Control any desktop app through structured JSON.
OculOS reads the OS accessibility tree and exposes every button, text field,
checkbox, and menu item as an API endpoint.

**Security.** The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default. Requests whose `Host`
header is not an IP literal, `localhost` or a name allowed with `--allow-host`,
and browser requests whose `Origin` is not the server itself or allowed with
`--allow-origin`, are rejected with 403 `forbidden`. When a token is configured
(`--token` / `OCULOS_TOKEN`, or generated automatically for non-loopback binds)
every route except `GET /health` and the dashboard requires it.

**Element ids** are 16 hex characters and stable: the same element found twice
gets the same id. They expire after 30 minutes idle or when the element
disappears (404 `not_found` → search again).

**Errors** use the envelope `{success: false, data: null, error, code}`.

get.description: Never requires a token. `auth_required` tells clients whether to send one.

get.summary: Full UI element tree for a process
Wait for elements to appear or disappear
get.description:
Polls every 250 ms until the condition holds or the timeout expires.
`until=appears` (default) returns the matching elements as soon as there is
at least one; `until=gone` returns an empty list once nothing matches
(a window that disappears counts as gone).
Implemented on Windows; other platforms return 400 `unsupported`.

Use for processes with several windows (same PID, different HWND).
Supported on Windows and macOS; on Linux `hwnd` is 0 and HWND routes
return 400 `unsupported` (use the PID routes).

get.summary: Wait for elements by window handle
get.description: Same as `GET /windows/{pid}/wait`, scoped to one window.

keys.description:
Text plus special keys in braces (case-insensitive):
`{ENTER}` `{TAB}` `{ESC}` `{SPACE}` `{BACKSPACE}` `{DELETE}` `{INSERT}`
`{HOME}` `{END}` `{PGUP}` `{PGDN}` `{UP}` `{DOWN}` `{LEFT}` `{RIGHT}`
`{F1}`–`{F24}` `{CAPSLOCK}` `{PRINTSCREEN}` `{MENU}`;
chords `{CTRL+A}`, `{CTRL+SHIFT+T}`, `{ALT+F4}`, `{WIN+D}`
(modifiers CTRL, ALT/OPTION, SHIFT, WIN/CMD/SUPER/META,
MOD = Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere); a lone modifier `{WIN}`;
repeat `{TAB 3}` (1–100); literal braces `{{` and `}}`.
`\n` presses Enter, `\t` presses Tab. The whole string is
validated first — invalid syntax → 400 and nothing is typed.

post.summary: Expand dropdown, tree item, or menu
Collapse dropdown, tree item, or menu
Select list item, radio button, or tab
Set numeric value on slider or spinner

post.description: Implemented on Windows; other platforms return 400 `unsupported`.

200.description: Success (data is the element's bounding rect)

get.description: Implemented on Windows; other platforms return 400 `unsupported`.

post.summary: Execute multiple interactions in one request
post.description:
Up to 100 actions. Every step is validated before anything runs; if one is
invalid the request fails with 400 and nothing is executed. With
`stop_on_error` (default true) execution stops at the first failing step.
The response contains one result per executed step.

get.description:
Upgrade to WebSocket to receive real-time events. When a token is
configured, pass it as `?token=<token>` (browsers cannot set headers on
WebSocket handshakes). Events:
`{"type":"action","data":{action, element_id, success, error?}}`,
`{"type":"tree_loaded","data":{pid?, hwnd?, nodes}}`,
`{"type":"windows","data":{count}}`.

TokenHeader.description: API token (`--token` / `OCULOS_TOKEN`, or the one printed at startup for non-loopback binds).

BearerAuth.description: The same API token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

info.title: Helpdesk API
info.description:
API-only, multi-tenant helpdesk for a separate frontend. All API paths are
relative to this server's root. Select a business using X-Helpdesk-Account;
sessions, resources and email-link tokens are scoped to that business.
Public operations ignore Authorization. Protected operations require an
unexpired bearer session for a verified, unsuspended user in that business.

Cancellation revokes sessions. Cancelled
businesses reject ordinary operations with 403 (public portal returns 404).
For 90 days the owner can sign in and use account
status, reactivation and sign-out. Other users cannot sign in.
Accounts still cancelled at 90 days are eligible for permanent erasure.

Request bodies use application/json. Missing required bodies, envelopes or
required envelope fields and invalid JSON return 400. Unknown attributes
and invalid values return 422; filtering all attributes out of a required
envelope returns 400. Non-object bodies and incorrectly shaped attributes
return 400 or 422. Unsupported body media types return 415.
Unknown query parameters and invalid query shapes return 400. For repeated
scalar query parameters, the last value is used.
Updates documented as PATCH also accept PUT with the same semantics.
Update envelopes may be empty; omitted fields preserve their values. Null
clears only explicitly nullable fields. Writes are atomic, and rejected
operations and no-ops preserve timestamps. Resource IDs are server-generated
UUIDv7 strings returned in canonical lowercase, hyphenated form. UUIDs in JSON
bodies, query parameters and paths must be hyphenated; either letter case is
accepted. Timestamps are UTC ISO8601
strings with fractional seconds. Resource visibility and authentication are
checked before exposing protected data. Errors contain no secrets.

CORS allows only HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL (default http://localhost:3001), with
Vary: Origin on success and errors. Preflight OPTIONS requests with
an allowed Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method return 200 without
account selection or authentication. Allowed methods are GET, POST, PATCH,
PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS; allowed headers are Authorization, Content-Type
and X-Helpdesk-Account.
Authentication uses bearer headers, not cookies.

post.summary: Register a business and its owner
post.description: Atomically creates the business and an unverified admin, sends one verification email and creates no session. Duplicate subdomain or invalid fields create nothing and send no mail. Ignores account and Authorization headers.
Owner only. Revokes all sessions and stops ordinary access. No request body. Repeating cancellation does not extend the original 90-day reactivation period.

Owner only, before 90 days have elapsed since cancellation. No request body. Preserves helpdesk data and the current owner session without restoring revoked sessions. An already active account is unchanged.

get.description: Reveals only the selected business name and subdomain.

post.summary: Sign in to the selected business
post.description: Creates an independent session expiring seven days later without sliding renewal. Wrong credentials and suspended users receive the same generic 401. Correct password for an unverified user returns 403 EmailNotVerified. Failed login creates no session; login preserves profile timestamps.

email.description: Trimmed and lowercased. Malformed or unknown email strings return the same generic 401 as a wrong password.

delete.description: Revokes only the presented session. Other sessions remain usable; reusing the revoked token returns 401.

patch.description: Only name is editable. An empty user object or unchanged normalized name succeeds without advancing updated_at.

put.summary: Change the password and revoke all sessions
put.description: Incorrect current password returns 422. A missing or empty new password returns 400. Success revokes all of this user's sessions, including the current one, and outstanding recovery links, even when the new password equals the old password. Sign in again afterwards.

post.description: Sends one link only to an existing unverified, unsuspended user. The link expires after 24 hours and replaces previous unused verification links. Unknown and ineligible users receive the same response without mail. No user creation or session changes.

202.description: Accepted

post.description: Atomically consumes the business- and purpose-bound token and marks its user verified; creates no session. Expired, consumed, revoked, wrong-purpose or wrong-business tokens return 400 InvalidToken. Missing tokens return 400; empty tokens return 422. Invalid token types return 400 or 422.

Sends one link only to an existing verified, unsuspended user. The link expires after one hour and replaces previous unused recovery links. Unknown and ineligible users receive the same response without mail. Requesting recovery does not change passwords, verify users or revoke sessions.

202.description: Accepted

post.summary: Reset a password using an emailed token
post.description: Atomically consumes the token, changes the password and revokes all of this user's sessions and remaining recovery tokens. Creates no session. Invalid tokens return 400 InvalidToken; missing tokens return 400 and empty tokens return 422. Invalid token types return 400 or 422. An invalid new password leaves a valid token usable and changes nothing. A missing or empty new password returns 400 without consuming the recovery link.

Creates an unverified customer and sends one verification email. Returns no session. An email already used in this business returns 422; another business may use the same email. Ignores Authorization. A pending, unexpired invitation reserves its email against customer registration, which returns 422 with no user or email created.

Customers only. Atomically creates an open request and its first public comment, both attributed to the authenticated customer. Subject and requester cannot subsequently change. No other creation fields are accepted.

get.description: Customers only; includes only the authenticated customer's requests. Ordered by customer-visible updated_at descending, then ID descending. Counts and pagination include only visible records. Supports only the status filter alongside pagination. Counts include only that customer's matching requests; invalid or unsupported filters return 400. Without page[size], preserves offset pagination with page=1 and per_page=25 by default. With page[size], returns only the collection, meta and links. Both directions retain normal list order. Cursors bind the business, user, endpoint (including parent), filters and sort order; another valid session for the same user and a changed page size are allowed. Query parameter order is irrelevant. Tokens survive restarts and save a position without requiring the boundary row to still exist; this is not a frozen snapshot. Malformed or cross-context cursors, mixed modes, missing size, unknown pagination keys or both directions return 400. Authentication, role and resource visibility checks precede cursor decoding.

Cursor mode, selected by page[size]; offset counts and page numbers are omitted.

get.description: Customers only. A missing, foreign, or other customer's request returns 404. The role check precedes resource lookup.

patch.summary: Reply to or solve a customer request
patch.description: Customers only, for their own requests. A reply is public and reopens a pending or solved request unless the same update explicitly sets status to solved. An empty request object is a no-op. Unknown fields, null fields, or any invalid combined update return 422 without changing the request or creating a comment. Every PATCH to a closed (merged) source returns 422, including an empty update. Neither closed status nor merged_into_id is writable. Ordinary solved tickets remain editable.

patch.summary: Update a ticket or add a staff reply
patch.description: Staff only. Explicit status may move between open, pending, and solved in any direction; a comment alone preserves status. Public comments and meaningful status changes advance both staff and customer timestamps. An empty ticket object or unchanged status is a no-op. Combined updates are atomic; rejected writes preserve timestamps. Staff cannot create tickets on a customer's behalf. Admins and agents can work on every ticket. Private notes (public:false) and assignment changes advance only the staff timestamp; public defaults to true. Customers never see assignment or private-note metadata. Priority is normal by default; changing priority advances only the staff timestamp. Null or invalid priority rejects the entire update. A public staff comment sends one email reply only when the ticket originated by email. Private notes and updates without a public comment send no mail; portal-origin tickets remain portal-only. Group routing is staff-only and does not restrict ticket visibility. Both group_id and assignee_id accept null. When both are supplied, use the exact pair; a nonnull pair requires membership. A null group allows any eligible staff assignee. With only group_id, retain the assignee only if they belong to the selected group; a null group clears the assignee. With only nonnull assignee_id, a grouped ticket requires membership; an ungrouped ticket adopts that user's default group if any. assignee_id:null alone preserves the group. Invalid combinations return 422 atomically. Missing groups or assignees, including those in another business, return 404. Group or assignee changes affect only the staff timestamp. Every PATCH to a closed (merged) source returns 422, including an empty update. Neither closed status nor merged_into_id is writable. Ordinary solved tickets remain editable.

post.summary: Receive a raw email from the trusted mail relay
post.description: Accepts a raw RFC 822 message. Routes by the unique support-domain address in To/Cc, using HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN (default support.example.test). No account header or user session is required. Mail to SUBDOMAIN@DOMAIN opens an unassigned, normal-priority ticket and its first public comment; mail to a ticket reply address appends a public requester reply. Only the original requester may reply. Accepted, duplicate and deliberately discarded deliveries all return an empty 204. Processing completes before the response in the test environment. Invalid routing, unsupported content, automated mail and ineligible senders are silently discarded. Successful Message-IDs are deduplicated within each business. Raw messages and reply tokens are not exposed by the API. Replies addressed to a merged source are discarded without reopening or forwarding and do not reserve the Message-ID.

post.summary: Add a staff member to a group
post.description: Admins only. Requires an existing group and verified, unsuspended staff member in this business. Missing groups or users, including those in another business, return 404. Duplicate memberships and ineligible staff members return 422. The first membership is always default, even if default is false or omitted. Later memberships default to false; default:true atomically demotes the previous default. User, group and existing ticket timestamps are unchanged.

group_id.description: UUID of a group in this business.

user_id.description: UUID of a staff user in this business.

get.description: Admins and agents. Missing and foreign memberships return 404.

delete.summary: Remove a staff member from a group
delete.description: Admins only; no request body. Removes the membership and promotes the user's remaining membership with the lowest ID if the default was removed. Clears that user's assignments in this group while retaining the group on those tickets; advances only affected staff ticket timestamps. Sends no mail.

put.summary: Set a staff member's default group
put.description: Admins only; no request body. Atomically promotes this membership and demotes that user's previous default, advancing only changed membership timestamps. Selecting the current default is a no-op. Changes affect future assignments, not existing tickets.

post.summary: Merge a duplicate into another ticket
post.description: Admins and agents. The source must be open or pending; the target must be open, pending or solved, in this business and have the same requester. Missing or foreign tickets return 404; self-merges, ineligible statuses and different requesters return 422. Atomically closes the source, records the direct target ID, and appends exactly one staff-authored note to each ticket. Optional note bodies replace default private notes that identify the opposite ticket. Note visibility defaults to private; no merge note sends email. Original histories, assignments and priorities stay on their original tickets. The target's status and email identity are preserved. Both source timestamps advance; the target's customer timestamp advances only for a public target note. Closed sources remain readable and listed; all direct PATCHes and repeat merges return 422. A survivor may later be merged, retaining previous direct pointers; no unmerge exists.

ResourceId.name: id
ResourceId.description: Hyphenated UUID; either letter case is accepted. Invalid or inaccessible IDs return 404.

Page.name: page
Page.description: Offset page number, encoded once as a positive decimal integer without a leading zero. Defaults to 1.

PerPage.name: per_page
PerPage.description: Offset page size, encoded once as a positive decimal integer without a leading zero. Defaults to 25.

PageSize.name: page[size]
PageSize.description: Select cursor pagination. Required when either cursor is supplied; no default. Cannot be combined with page or per_page. Decimal integer from 1 through 100.

PageAfter.description: Read strictly after this saved position. Requires page[size]; cannot be combined with page[before].

PageBefore.description: Read the nearest preceding page, in normal order. Requires page[size]; cannot be combined with page[after].

Error400.description: BadRequest: malformed body, header or query, or missing required parameters. InvalidToken: unusable email-link token.

Error401.description: Unauthorized: missing, malformed, expired, revoked, wrong-business or otherwise unusable credentials.

Error403.description: Forbidden: authenticated caller cannot perform this operation. EmailNotVerified: correct login password for an unverified user.

Error404.description: NotFound: unknown business, route, invalid path ID or inaccessible resource.

Error409.description: Conflict: the operation conflicts with the resource's current state.

Error415.description: UnsupportedMediaType: request body must use application/json.

Error422.description: ValidationError: invalid, unknown, forbidden or incorrectly typed attributes, including missing nested attributes. No changes are committed.

Id.description: Server-generated UUIDv7, returned in canonical lowercase, hyphenated form. Input IDs must be hyphenated; either letter case is accepted.

Name.description: Trimmed before validation and storage; must contain 1–100 Unicode characters after trimming.

Email.description: Trimmed and lowercased. At most 254 characters after normalization, exactly one @, a nonempty local part, a domain containing a dot, and no internal whitespace. Unique within a business; no DNS lookup.

Subdomain.description: Trimmed and lowercased; normalized identifier is 3–40 characters matching [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]* across the entire string. Globally unique.

Password.description: At least 12 characters and at most 72 UTF-8 bytes. Passwords are not trimmed.

PasswordAttempt.description: Password used to authenticate an existing user. Whitespace is significant; the new-password minimum length does not apply to login attempts.

Token.description: Opaque, unguessable bearer secret. Never log or persist in recoverable form.

enum: If the account is eligible, an email will be sent.

Subject.description: Trimmed on input; the normalized subject must be nonblank and at most 200 Unicode characters. Immutable after creation.

CommentBody.description: Nonblank plain text. Original whitespace and line breaks are preserved.

Request.description: Customer-visible ticket representation. updated_at tracks public conversation and status changes. Only the requester can access it.

Ticket.description: Staff representation of a ticket in the selected business. Embedded user details reflect current profiles.

Comment.description: Immutable comment; the embedded author contains only the user's current ID and name.

assignee_id.description: Null clears assignment. Otherwise use the UUID of verified, unsuspended staff in this business. Ineligible users return 422; missing users or users in another business return 404. Assignment does not limit ticket visibility.

group_id.description: UUID of a group in this business; null clears the group.

Invitation.description: Contains no token or secret URL. Pending invitations appear expired once expires_at is reached, without changing stored timestamps; accepted and revoked invitations retain their state.

target_id.description: UUID of the target ticket in this business.

Cursor.description: Opaque, tamper-resistant saved position. Treat as uninterpreted and URL-encode when constructing requests.

CursorMeta.description: has_more describes the requested direction (earlier for page[before], later otherwise). Nonempty pages include both boundary cursors even at an edge. Empty pages have false has_more and null cursors.

CursorLinks.description: Navigation links preserve the endpoint, active filters and page size; they contain only the appropriate cursor direction. Links are API-relative or same-origin absolute URLs. Missing neighbors have null links; both links are null for an empty page. Continue sending account and bearer headers.

info.title: Wikipedia Knowledge Explorer API
info.description:
Clean, cited context from Wikipedia for LLMs and people. A dossier is
built once per (page_id, rev_id, pipeline_version) and rendered per
request for a token budget (2000 | 8000 | 32000) as JSON or Markdown.
Building is asynchronous: POST /api/v1/dossiers answers 202 with a job
to poll. GET never builds. Every 4xx/5xx body is
application/problem+json (RFC 9457). Every response carries
X-Request-ID. Quoted text is Wikipedia content under CC BY-SA 4.0;
summaries are model output and labelled as such.
The wke-ml wire protocol is included under the "internal" tag with its
own server; the public server does not route it, and the frontend client
generator excludes that tag.

servers.description: Local development backend; the Vite dev and preview servers proxy the API paths to it

get.description: One Action API `list=search` call on cache miss (cached 1 h), zero on hit. When no result matches the query as typed, one more fuzzy `list=search` call (also cached 1 h) looks for a nearby spelling; `did_you_mean` carries the API's own suggestion or that title, and is null when a result already is the query. Rate limit 30/min per client IP.

did_you_mean.description: Suggested title for a misspelt query; null when none.

get.description: Pure read over the `built` ZSET (page_id scored by built_at), newest build first; covers today's prebuilt list plus every dossier built in the last 7 days. One row per page, its latest pin. Rate limit 120/min per IP (GET reads). The scan is cached in-process for 10 s; ETag/304, Cache-Control public max-age=10.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the title

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous page

post.summary: Get or build a dossier for a title
post.description: Resolves the title (redirects followed, 1 Action API call, cached 10 min). If a dossier for the current revision exists, returns it (200). Otherwise enqueues a build (202) with Location and Retry-After; concurrent requests for the same page share one job. Cold build costs exactly 3 Wikimedia calls. Rate limit 6/min per IP, 2 in-flight jobs per IP, 60 builds per IP per day.

refresh.description: Force a rebuild of the current revision (2/h per IP).

200.description: Dossier already built for the current revision. The body equals GET /api/v1/dossiers/{page_id} for the same parts at the default budget (8000) and summaries off.

WKE-Dossier-Tokens.description: Budget.used_est_tokens, the counted dossier part (chars/4 of the content with its [cN] markers, never above the requested budget)

WKE-Total-Tokens.description: chars/4 of the whole body as delivered, whatever parts were selected

202.description: Build enqueued or already running

409.description: Disambiguation page; pick a candidate

get.summary: Latest built dossier for a page, packed to a token budget
get.description: Pure read: never triggers a build. 404 not_built if nothing is built yet. ETag "{rev_id}-{pv}-{budget}-{format}-{state}-{done}-{s0|s1}-{l0|l1}-{parts}" (build state, summaries done, summaries on or off, parts as p plus d, m, s), Cache-Control public max-age=60. post.summary: Embed chunks, cluster, compute relevance and related edges (wke-ml)
post.description: Vectors never leave wke-ml. One inference at a time; queue 4, then 503 + Retry-After. Two callers -- the dossier pipeline (lead + chunks + up to 8 related leads, edges capped at 20) and the trending job (lead = top topic, chunks empty, the other topics as related_leads, max_edges 80). Empty chunks skip clustering and relevance. Graph node ids are page ids; page_id names the seed node.

page_id.description: Seed node id (the article or the top topic).

Links.name: links
Links.description: Markdown only. Writes the link spans of each passage as inline Markdown links to the Wikipedia page. Off by default: passages are plain verbatim text and links are never charged to the budget. With links=true the Markdown can exceed the budget and the budget line says so. The JSON keeps the spans (`Chunk.links`) either way.

Parts.name: parts
Parts.description: Comma list over dossier, metadata, sources; it must contain dossier (422 validation_error otherwise, and for an unknown part). Order and duplicates do not matter. Default `dossier`: the sections and passages alone, with no [cN] markers, no revision pin, no budget line and no truncation signal. `metadata` adds them (Markdown: the title, pin line, budget line, notices and "Left out:" line; JSON: id, topic, build, freshness, budget, links). `sources` adds the [cN] markers and the Sources list (JSON: citations). `dossier,metadata,sources` is the full document. The budget counts the dossier part only, markers included; the passage selection never depends on parts. The licence notice is always present and never counted.

RateLimited.description: Client rate limit hit; Retry-After set

Upstream.description: Wikimedia budget exhausted (upstream_budget), Wikimedia throttled us (upstream_rate_limited, Retry-After passed through), Wikimedia unavailable (upstream_unavailable) or queue full (queue_full).

anchor.description: The id attribute of the section's heading element in the Parsoid HTML of the pinned revision, never a slug built from the label. Absent for the revision-level citation (the lead, c1) and for related-article citations.

url.description: The exact place cited: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=<rev>#<anchor>` for a section, the plain revision permalink when there is no anchor.

kind.description: prose is a run of whole sentences (it starts at a sentence start and ends at a sentence end, and has no "see X" pointer sentences). facts is the infobox as up to 12 "Label: value" lines, placed right after the lead. table is one table as a caption line, a header row and rows of compact Markdown table text; a cell that a rowspan covers repeats its text in each row it covers. list is one outermost list of a section that has little prose of its own, as one "- item" line per item (a nested item is a further line indented by two spaces). A table or list that does not fit the budget is cut at a row or item boundary: its first rows or items, the first "Total" row of a table when it lies past them, and a last line "(N rows; M shown)" or "(N items; M shown)" (the same line marks a parse-time cut at 200 rows or items). Cell and item text is verbatim; est_tokens counts the stored text and the chunk's text in a response is the shortened text when budget.shortened_chunk_ids names the chunk.

citation_id.description: The citation of the chunk's own section.

relevance.description: Cosine similarity to the article lead

links.description: Links from the passage to other Wikipedia articles, live and not citations (they carry no revision pin). Prose chunks only. start and end are code-point offsets into text (end exclusive); a JavaScript client indexes UTF-16, so use Array.from(text) when text holds astral characters. Spans lie inside the text the response carries: a passage cut at a sentence end keeps only the spans that remain.

formulas.description: Stretches of text that are TeX formula source, with the same offsets as links. The text keeps the TeX verbatim; the Markdown rendering shows each stretch as inline code.

citation_id.description: Citation of the section the summary summarises.

Section.description: One section of the article. The JSON keeps every section, including those with summary_state no_prose (machine contract, flagged). The Markdown rendering (the .md endpoints and the MCP get_dossier markdown format) leaves out a no_prose section unless a section nested under it has prose, and names the left-out titles in one header line.

heading_path.description: Ancestor headings plus the section's own heading, outermost first (the same shape every chunk of the section carries). Empty for the lead. Its length is the heading depth: one for a top-level section, two for its subsections.

citation_id.description: Citation of the section's heading in the pinned revision. Its passages, tables and summary all cite it.

dropped_non_prose.description: True when the section's own text held a list or a table that no chunk carries (after the infobox and the wikitables with a header row were extracted). A client may say the source text is complete only when this is false.

dropped_lists.description: Content lists of the section that no chunk carries (the section has prose of its own

dropped_tables.description: Content tables of the section that no chunk carries (a table that cannot be read as header and rows

summary_state.description: no_prose means the section kept no chunk of its own (heading only parent, or only lists). A section holding only a table has its table chunk and is skipped. It is never selected for a summary and is distinct from skipped, which means text exists but the model was not asked to summarise it. withheld means the model produced a summary that failed the source check (cut off, not ending at a sentence end, pointing to another page, or naming a capitalised name or number that is not in the passages it read, a number without its context, dense novel phrases, swapped roles, a quotation stated as fact, a sentence cut inside, or a repeated sentence); the text is not kept and withheld_reason says why.

withheld_reason.description: Why the summary was withheld; set only with summary_state withheld.

importance.description: How much the section matters to the article, 0 to 1: similarity to the lead, size, a U-shaped position prior (first and last sections high) and a bonus for outcome headings (arrest, trial, death, legacy, aftermath, result, reception, outcome). The packer ranks sections by it, and the build summarises the top ones. 0 on the lead and on dossiers stored before the field existed.

checked_at.description: When the watcher last observed an edit to this page. Null, with source "none", while the watcher has no data for the page; never the time of the request.

counts.description: What requested and used_est_tokens cover, the dossier part only.

used_est_tokens.description: Measured est_tokens (chars/4) of the dossier part rendered as Markdown with its [cN] markers: headings, passages, markers and summaries. The metadata head, the Sources list, the licence footer and inline links are not counted. Never above requested.

shortened_chunk_ids.description: Chunks cut back to fit the budget: the lead's first passage at a sentence end (only when it alone does not fit), and tables and lists at a row or item boundary (a table or list takes at most 15 percent of a ladder step's budget).

id.description: {page_id}@{rev_id}:{build_hash[:12]}

DossierResponse.description: The JSON body of a dossier read (schema 2; the flat schema 1 is no longer served, a break for JSON clients). Parts that were not selected are left out, never null. With the default parts (`dossier`) the body has no revision pin, no budget line and no sign that the article was cut: `parts=dossier,metadata` adds them (metadata.budget.complete, omitted_chunks, build, freshness) and `parts=dossier,metadata,sources` adds the citations.

freshness_state.description: Same rule as Freshness.state, computed at read time

edits_since_pin.description: 0 means current; from the watcher's latest_rev pointer, also 0 when freshness_state is unknown (no watcher data)

largest_budget_filled.description: Smallest budget at which Budget.complete is true, or 32000 if none

queue_position.description: Place in the build queue; present only while status is queued.

started_at.description: When a worker picked the job up; absent while queued.

finished_at.description: When the job reached done or failed; absent before that.

date.description: Yesterday UTC (pageviews day)

  types.<type>     — per event-type buckets (a partition of types.all)

`event_type` (the active category) narrows ONLY the CHANNEL buckets — the
source rail partitions the feed, so its counts move with the category —
and never the TYPE buckets, because each category badge counts its own
type under the other filters regardless of which category is selected.

AgentTokenIn.title: AgentTokenIn
AgentTokenIn.description: New shared agent credential for the collector fleet.

AlertPatchIn.title: AlertPatchIn
AlertPatchIn.description:
The extended PATCH contract: the triage transition plus the P0 finding
verdicts (disposition / confidence) and the optional investigation link.
All of them optional — a status-only PATCH behaves exactly as before.

AnalysisJobCreateIn.title: AnalysisJobCreateIn
AnalysisJobCreateIn.description:
Start an analysis job. `backend` selects the execution backend;
`sample_id` (vault sample) or `sample_name` identifies the artifact. For
`static` the analysis runs synchronously; `watched-host` and
`external-provider` persist queued state (their executors arrive in later
phases); `isolated-outpost` is reserved and returns 501 — OutPost has no
isolated execution backend yet.

AnalysisJobDTO.title: AnalysisJobDTO
AnalysisJobDTO.description:
One persisted analysis job — `run_id` doubles as the job id (the run
lifecycle/report/export machinery stays the single source of truth).

FindingDTO.title: FindingDTO
FindingDTO.description:
The semantic finding resource — a compatible superset of Alert (the
physical table stays `alerts`; this is the API-level abstraction).

FindingIn.title: FindingIn
FindingIn.description:
Create an analyst-authored finding. `source` is forced to 'analyst'
server-side — the detection engine owns the 'detection' provenance.

HostTimelineDTO.title: HostTimelineDTO
HostTimelineDTO.description:
The host timeline envelope — host metadata plus the merged, filtered,
paginated feed. `total` is the honest count across ALL kinds after the
active filters (not just this page); `limit`/`offset` echo the request.

HostTimelineEntry.title: HostTimelineEntry
HostTimelineEntry.description:
One row of the host aggregate timeline. `kind` discriminates the
resource; `timestamp` is the unified sort key (event time, alert trigger,
session start, IOC first-seen, investigation created); `title`/`subtitle`
carry the display text; `payload` carries the deep-link fields per kind.

IntelImportIn.title: IntelImportIn
IntelImportIn.description:
A threat-intel feed to pull into the watchlist + IOC layer.

`content` is either a raw STIX 2.1 bundle (source=stix / auto-detect) or
a plain one-IOC-per-line text list; `url` fetches a STIX feed instead of
pasting it. Imported values are upserted into the watchlist labeled
`intel:<source>` so they read honestly as feed-derived, and every
existing run that touches an imported value is reported back so the UI
can flag it immediately.

InvestigationDTO.title: InvestigationDTO
InvestigationDTO.description:
One investigation — the case header with derived counts. `severity` is
DERIVED from the attached findings (max of the canonical suspicious /
malicious vocabulary), NULL when no findings are attached.

InvestigationDetailDTO.title: InvestigationDetailDTO
InvestigationDetailDTO.description:
The investigation workspace payload: the header, its tags, the attached
findings (from the canonical alerts model — never duplicated), the
evidence refs (pointers, not copies), and the analyst notes.

InvestigationPatchIn.title: InvestigationPatchIn
InvestigationPatchIn.description:
Fields justified by the P0 contract: title / tags / status / conclusion.
Only fields actually present are written (Pydantic v2 model_fields_set).

IocDetailDTO.title: IocDetailDTO
IocDetailDTO.description:
The IOC workspace payload: the row plus everything OutPost knows about
the indicator — where it was observed, the findings it links to, the runs
and hosts it appeared in. Runs/hosts are DERIVED from provenance refs
(event/finding → run → host); nothing is fabricated.

choice.title: Choice
choice.description: demo = seed the labeled demo campaign; empty = start clean

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: demo = keep real host sessions; all = complete wipe

purge_samples.title: Purge Samples
purge_samples.description: Whether to also wipe samples in vault

SandboxDetonateIn.title: SandboxDetonateIn
SandboxDetonateIn.description:
Push a vault sample to an external sandbox for dynamic detonation.

`provider` is one of anyrun/triage/joe/demo (or auto = the configured
provider, falling back to the labeled demo when none is configured).
`platform` overrides the sample's sniffed OS for the detonation VM;
default is the sample's detected platform.

SandboxTaskOut.title: SandboxTaskOut
SandboxTaskOut.description:
One sandbox detonation task — the shape both the POST response and the
status poll return, so the webapp can render the same card.

SearchGroupResult.title: SearchGroupResult
SearchGroupResult.description:
A group's slice of the envelope: the page total (honest count across
all matches in the group, not just this page) and the page hits.

SearchHit.title: SearchHit

SearchResponseDTO.title: SearchResponseDTO
SearchResponseDTO.description:
The GET /search envelope — `q` echoes the normalized free text (after
qualifiers were stripped), `qualifiers` echoes the parsed filters, and
`groups` holds one SearchGroupResult per resource group searched.

text.description: The text content to be converted to speech. For English, German, Dutch, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish, the server normalizes the text (numbers, dates, abbreviations) before synthesis; the other languages are in Early Access without text normalization, so write numbers and dates out in words. May contain inline pause controls (`\{pause:500ms\}`, 500-3000 ms in 100 ms steps, at most 8 per request) and inline pronunciation controls (`\{"word": "...", "pronounce": "<IPA>"\}`, Early Access). Pronunciation cannot be combined with pause or with a `speed` other than `1.0`, and `speed` is capped at `1.15` when a pause is present. See [Speed, Pause, Pronunciation](/docs/tts-voice-controls).

parameters.description:
Key term prompting improves recognition of specialized terminology and brands. Only compatible with Nova-3.

`keyterm` accepts plain terms only. Unlike the legacy `keywords` feature, it does not support weights or intensifiers. Appending one (for example, `keyterm=term:0.15`) is not rejected—the weight is silently ignored and the entire value is treated as a literal keyterm.

To boost multiple separate keyterms, repeat the `keyterm` parameter (for example, `keyterm=term1&keyterm=term2`). To boost one multi-word phrase as a single keyterm, join the words with `%20` or `+` (for example, `keyterm=customer%20service`). Do not separate keyterms with commas, semicolons, or line breaks.
parameters.name: keyterm

parameters.description: Keywords can boost or suppress specialized terminology and brands. `keywords` is not supported with Nova-3 models; use `keyterm` instead.

A code that is not in the [Nova-3 multilingual list](/docs/models-languages-overview#nova-3) fails the request with HTTP 400. See [Nova-3 Language Prompting](/docs/nova-3-language-prompting).

Accepted values: `-2`, `-1`, `0`, `1`, `2`. `0` (the default) is the voice's tuned delivery and the production-validated setting, with `-2` the calm end of the range and `2` the animated end. Supported on all Flux voices; applies to the whole request. Beta: behavior may change in future model versions, and non-default values increase the risk of hallucinations and pronunciation errors; audition before shipping. An invalid value is rejected with a `400` — `EXPRESSIVITY_OUT_OF_RANGE` for a value outside the range, `EXPRESSIVITY_INCREMENT_INVALID` for a fractional value. See [Expressivity](/docs/tts-expressivity).

parameters.name: sample_rate

Not yet supported in all languages. When the text contains an inline pause marker, speed is capped at `1.15` (`PAUSE_SPEED_CAP_EXCEEDED` above that). A value other than `1.0` cannot be combined with inline pronunciation controls (`CONTROL_COMBINATION_INVALID`).
parameters.name: speed

parameters.description: Processing priority for asynchronous (callback) requests. The only supported value is low.
parameters.name: priority

200.description: Returns the synthesized audio in the requested encoding as a binary stream. When a `callback` URL is supplied, the request is processed asynchronously and the response body is instead a JSON acknowledgement (Content-Type `application/json`) of the form {"request_id": "..."}, with the audio delivered to the callback URL. Because this endpoint is typed as a binary audio stream, SDK callers that set `callback` receive this JSON acknowledgement through the audio byte iterator as raw bytes and must join the chunks and parse `request_id` themselves.

400.description: Invalid Request. Inline control violations return a structured error whose `err_code` names the rule: `CONTROL_COMBINATION_INVALID` (pronunciation combined with speed or pause, or all three together), `PAUSE_SPEED_CAP_EXCEEDED` (a pause marker with `speed` above `1.15`), `BREAK_OUT_OF_RANGE` (a pause outside 500-3000 ms), `BREAK_INCREMENT_INVALID` (a pause off the 100 ms grid), `BREAKS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (more than 8 pause markers, or two pauses with no text between them), `BREAK_SYNTAX_INVALID` (a malformed pause marker, such as a simple marker without backslashes or an escaped structured marker), plus the existing pronunciation and speed codes. A `speed` of `1.0` does not count as a speed control for the combination rules. See [Speed, Pause, Pronunciation](/docs/tts-voice-controls).
