info.title: Email API
info.description:
API contract for the web mail system of the semester project.

## Scope and assumptions

* The contract is designed from the client's perspective. Database tables, storage folders, and
  framework classes are implementation details and are not visible here.
* The current user is already identified (JWT bearer token). Registration, login, user
  administration, and receiving external email are out of scope of this contract.
* A user can only see and change their own emails and attachments. A resource that belongs to
  another user is reported exactly like a resource that does not exist (`404 Not Found`), so the
  API never reveals whether a foreign resource exists.

## Conventions

* **Identifiers** are UUIDs generated by the server.
* **Date-times** are RFC 3339 date-times with an explicit UTC offset of the server's local time
  zone, for example `2026-11-06T09:15:00+01:00`. An unset `sentAt` is represented by an explicit
  `null`.
* **Request and response bodies** are JSON (`application/json`), errors are
  `application/problem+json`, attachment content is binary.
* **Writable and server-controlled data:** Clients can only write `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`,
  `replyTo`, `subject`, and `content`. `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `sentAt`, `status`,
  `source`, and `attachments` are controlled by the server. A request that contains any of them
  (or any other unknown property) is rejected with `400 Bad Request`, because the body cannot
  be read into the request schema; it is never silently ignored.
* **Omitted, empty, and null values:** Optional recipient lists that are omitted are treated as
  empty lists. Empty lists are allowed as long as at least one of `to`, `cc`, `bcc` is not
  empty. Explicit `null` is never accepted in requests (`400`).
* **Updates** use `PUT` with the complete writable representation. Properties that are omitted
  are reset to their empty value. `PATCH` is not supported (`405`).
* **Unsupported HTTP methods** on an existing path are answered with `405 Method Not Allowed`
  and an `Allow` header that lists the supported methods.

## Error policy

| Status | Meaning in this API |
|---|---|
| 400 | The request cannot be read: malformed JSON, wrong types, missing required properties, explicit `null`, unknown or server-controlled properties, or an invalid query parameter (pagination or filter). |
| 401 | Missing or invalid token. |
| 404 | Unknown resource, or a resource of another user. |
| 405 | HTTP method not supported for the path. |
| 409 | The request is valid but conflicts with the current state, for example the email is already sent. |
| 413 | An uploaded file or the attachments of an email exceed the size limit. |
| 415 | Unsupported request media type. |
| 422 | The request body was read, but its values violate a rule: no recipient, blank subject or content, invalid address, too many entries, values too long. |
| 500 | Unexpected error in the server. The response never exposes internal details such as stack traces. |

## Processing model of sending

Sending is **synchronous**. `POST /emails/{emailId}/transmissions` performs one transmission
attempt and answers when the attempt is finished. A rejected request (for example, an already
sent email) never starts an attempt. An accepted attempt that fails is still a successful HTTP
exchange (`201 Created`) whose transmission has the outcome `failed`.

Filters are combined with AND and are applied before pagination, so `totalElements` and
`totalPages` describe the filtered result. A page that is beyond the last page, or a
filter without matches, returns `200` with an empty `data` array.

representation. The representation must satisfy the same rules as an email creation, so an
update can never produce an email without recipients. Attachments are managed through their
own resources. The server sets `updatedAt` to the time of the update.

An email with the status `sent` is read-only (`409`). An email with the status `error` can
be edited. Repeating the same request leaves the email in the same state (idempotent).

post.description:
Performs one synchronous transmission attempt for an email with the status `draft` or
`error`. The request has no body.

**Effects**

| Outcome | `status` | `sentAt` | `updatedAt` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `succeeded` | `sent` | time of the attempt | time of the attempt |
| `failed` | `error` | stays unset | time of the attempt |

**Rejected requests** do not start an attempt and change nothing: an email with the status
`sent`, or a received email (`source` is `extern`), answers `409`. An email with the status
`error` can be edited and sent again.

**Retry policy:** `POST` is not idempotent by definition, but this operation protects
itself: after a successful attempt the email is `sent`, so a repeated request is rejected
with `409` and cannot send the email twice. If a request times out, the client first reads
`GET /emails/{emailId}/transmissions` (or the email) to learn the outcome and only repeats
the request if the email is still `draft` or `error`. The server processes transmissions of
one email one after another.

post.description:
Uploads **one** file as `multipart/form-data` in the part named `file`. To attach several
files the client repeats the request, once per file.

The server reads the file name from the `Content-Disposition` header of the part, the MIME
type from the `Content-Type` header of the part, and counts the bytes while it receives
the file; the client does not send these values in a separate field.

**Limits:** one file has at least 1 byte and at most 10 MB (10485760 bytes), all
attachments of one email together at most 25 MB, and one email has at most 10
attachments. Attachments can only be added to emails with the status `draft` or `error`.

info.title: FX Conversion & Cross-Currency Transfer API
info.description:
Extension to the Fund Transfer Service API adding live exchange rate retrieval,
currency conversion preview, enhanced cross-currency transfer support (split fees,
state lifecycle), and in-app notifications.

**Fee model**: Transfers incur a *sending fee* (charged to sender on top of source amount)
and a *receiving fee* (deducted from the converted amount before crediting the recipient).

**Rate staleness**: If exchange rates are older than the configured maximum age,
transfer initiation is blocked. Rate viewing remains available.

**Transfer lifecycle**: `PENDING → PROCESSING → COMPLETED / FAILED`

TransferStatus.description:
Transfer lifecycle state:
- `pending`: record created, rate locked
- `processing`: debit/credit in progress

- `failed`: rolled back, no funds moved

and net amount to be credited to the recipient. Uses the current (latest non-stale)

post.description:
Creates a cross-currency transfer with PENDING status, re-validates the rate from
the supplied snapshot, applies split fees, executes the atomic debit/credit
(pessimistic lock), and returns the final transfer record.

**Rate deviation**: If the current rate deviates from the snapshot rate by more than
the configured threshold (default 1%), a 409 is returned with the updated rate.
The client must call `POST /fx/convert` again and resubmit with the new snapshot_id.

**Idempotency**: The `X-Idempotency-Key` header is required. Duplicate submissions
with the same key return the original response without re-executing.

get.description:
Public liveness signal: this process is up and serving.

Runs **no dependency probes**.  Liveness and readiness are different
questions and this endpoint answers only the first, for three reasons:

- ``db/engine.py`` builds the engine with ``pool_pre_ping=True`` and no
  connect timeout, so a database host that stops answering SYN blocks the
  probe on OS TCP retries (~130s on Linux).  The Dockerfile healthcheck is
  ``--timeout=5s --retries=3``, so probing here would turn a slow
  dependency into a container restart loop.
- This is a sync ``def``, so it runs on the anyio threadpool.  A probe that
  blocks lets unauthenticated callers park every thread in that pool and
  stall every other sync route in the app.  ``db/engine.py`` now bounds the
  connect at ``CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS``, but a bounded probe on an
  anonymous endpoint is still a lever an attacker can pull for free.
- A per-component rollup readable by anonymous callers is a disclosure
  oracle in its own right ("one of their backends is erroring right now").

Nothing consumes the rollup: Railway ``healthcheckPath``, Render
``healthCheckPath`` and the Dockerfile ``HEALTHCHECK`` all assert on the
status code alone.  Readiness lives on ``/health/detail``.

Full health payload - build identity plus per-component status.

Authenticated-only: the git commit identifies the exact deployed revision
of an open-source codebase, which is exactly the disclosure ASVS V14.3.3
warns about.

This is a sync ``def`` and it does probe, so the threadpool argument in
``health_check`` applies here too - authentication changes who can pull the
lever, not that it exists.  What bounds it is ``db/engine.py``'s
``CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS``: the Redis client already carries its own
socket timeouts and the Stripe probe makes no network call, so with the
database connect bounded, no probe here can hold a worker indefinitely.

SEP-2127 Server Card - pre-connect registry/client discovery.

Lets agents preview the server before opening a transport: identity
(``name``/``title``/``description``/``version``/``icons``), where to connect
(``serverUrl`` + ``remotes``), and the tool surface (``tools[]``).

No ``$schema`` is emitted: the draft SEP-2127 server-card schema is not yet
published (the URL 404s), so advertising it would only break validators.

A2A Agent Card (spec v0.3.0) - pre-connect agent discovery document.

Discovery/branding only: it advertises this agent's identity and skills so
A2A registries/clients can find it. We intentionally do not declare a
``preferredTransport`` because the template implements no A2A wire transport;
advertising one would point clients at an endpoint that can't speak it.

RFC 9727 API catalog - points agents/crawlers at the OpenAPI description.

Returns an RFC 9264 linkset whose ``service-desc`` link references this
server's OpenAPI document, so function-calling agents can discover the
machine-readable API contract from one well-known URL. Absolute URLs are
emitted when ``API_PUBLIC_URL`` is configured (matching the OpenAPI
``servers`` block); otherwise relative hrefs let the client resolve them
against the request origin.

Web Bot Auth key directory - the agent's Ed25519 public signing keys.

Public discovery: any origin verifying this agent's HTTP Message Signatures
reads it cross-origin, so it is served with ``Access-Control-Allow-Origin:
*`` and the directory-specific JWKS media type.

info.title: Unified Care Model API
info.description:
Complete UCM model including Core, Participation, and Domain semantic layers.

Reference API generated from the Unified Care Model ontology <https://www.w3.org/ns/ucm#> and its SHACL shapes. Payloads are JSON-LD: every schema maps to an ontology class, every property to an ontology property (x-semantic-uri). Shapes constraints are reflected as required/cardinality where JSON Schema can express them and listed in x-ucm-constraints where it cannot.

tags.name: ActivityFocus
tags.description: The matter, condition, or situation toward which a coordinated activity is orchestrated and which the activity seeks to jointly maintain, update, resolve, or bring about.

tags.name: CareCommitment
tags.description: A continuing agreement among participants to coordinate care toward a joint purpose, according to terms or conditions that may evolve.

tags.name: CareCoverageGap
tags.description: A condition in which a care coverage requirement is in force but is not satisfied by any applicable in-force care commitment during a specified interval.

tags.name: CareCoverageRequirement
tags.description: A requirement that some participation in care coordination concerns an activity focus, in a given role, over a defined context or interval.

tags.name: CareTrajectoryContext
tags.description: A position or extent defined relative to the progression of a care process, state trajectory, or coordinated activity, which does not require anchoring to clock or calendar time.

tags.name: DefinitionArtifact
tags.description: A ruleset, policy definition, constraint, or governance artifact.

tags.name: Entity
tags.description: A stable independently identifiable semantic thing.

tags.name: Membership
tags.description: Contextual membership relationship between an Entity and a SocialGroupEntity.

tags.name: MembershipCriteria
tags.description: Rules or conditions defining membership within a SocialGroupEntity.

tags.name: Participation
tags.description: Contextual involvement of an Entity within a Process and Semantic Context.

tags.name: Process
tags.description: A bounded interaction or activity occurring over time.

tags.name: Role
tags.description: A contextual, anti-rigid classification assumed through participation.

tags.name: SemanticContext
tags.description: An interpretive environment, governance scope, or applicability boundary.

tags.name: Statement
tags.description: An informational assertion, finding, determination, or conclusion.

Ineligible.definition: The person does not meet the receiving program's eligibility criteria.

MissingVerification.label: Missing verification
MissingVerification.definition: Documentation or verification the receiving party requires was not provided.

OtherClosureReason.label: Other reason
OtherClosureReason.definition: Not connected for a reason not listed here.

OutOfArea.label: Out of area
OutOfArea.definition: The person is outside the receiving party's service area.

ProgramCapacity.label: Program at capacity
ProgramCapacity.definition: The receiving program had no capacity for the person.

CommitmentStatus.description: Commitment Status. Is a care commitment binding on its participants? Open vocabulary: known concepts are listed; other concept IRIs are accepted when SKOS-mapped into the scheme.

CommitmentInForce.label: In force
CommitmentInForce.definition: The commitment is agreed and binding on its participants.

CommitmentLapsed.label: Lapsed
CommitmentLapsed.definition: The commitment ended without being released, for example by expiry or abandonment.

CommitmentProposed.label: Proposed
CommitmentProposed.definition: The commitment has been offered but not yet agreed.

CommitmentReleased.label: Released
CommitmentReleased.definition: The commitment ended deliberately: completed, handed over or ended by agreement.

CommitmentSuspended.label: Suspended
CommitmentSuspended.definition: The commitment is agreed but temporarily not binding.

HandoffStatus.description: Handoff Status. Where does responsibility for the agreed services stand between the sending and receiving parties? Open vocabulary: known concepts are listed; other concept IRIs are accepted when SKOS-mapped into the scheme.

HandoffAcknowledged.label: Acknowledged
HandoffAcknowledged.definition: The receiving party has acknowledged the handoff but has not yet assumed responsibility.

HandoffAssumed.label: Assumed
HandoffAssumed.definition: The receiving party has assumed responsibility for the agreed services, and the sending party has released it.

HandoffDropped.label: Dropped
HandoffDropped.definition: The sending party released responsibility before the receiving party assumed it, leaving no one responsible for the agreed services.

HandoffOffered.label: Offered
HandoffOffered.definition: The sending party has offered responsibility for the agreed services; the receiving party has not acknowledged it.

HandoffReturned.label: Returned
HandoffReturned.definition: The receiving party handed responsibility back to the sending party.

HandoffShared.label: Shared
HandoffShared.definition: The sending and receiving parties hold responsibility for the agreed services jointly.

HandshakeFulfillment.description: Handshake Fulfillment. How much of the service negotiated in a handshake has been delivered? Open vocabulary: known concepts are listed; other concept IRIs are accepted when SKOS-mapped into the scheme.

FulfillmentConfirmed.label: Confirmed delivered
FulfillmentConfirmed.definition: The requesting party has confirmed that the negotiated services were delivered.

FulfillmentNotStarted.label: Not started
FulfillmentNotStarted.definition: None of the negotiated services has been delivered yet.

FulfillmentPartial.label: Partially delivered
FulfillmentPartial.definition: Some, but not all, of the negotiated services have been delivered.

FulfillmentReported.label: Reported delivered
FulfillmentReported.definition: The delivering party reports the negotiated services delivered; the requesting party has not confirmed it.

LifecycleState.description: Lifecycle State. A state associated with a process during a portion of its lifecycle. Open vocabulary: known concepts are listed; other concept IRIs are accepted when SKOS-mapped into the scheme.

Accepted.label: Accepted Care Coordination Lifecycle
Accepted.definition: A care coordination request that has been accepted for ongoing care.

ReferralDisposition.description: Referral Disposition. What has the receiving party decided about a care coordination request? Open vocabulary: known concepts are listed; other concept IRIs are accepted when SKOS-mapped into the scheme.

ReferralAccepted.label: Accepted
ReferralAccepted.definition: The receiving party agreed to take part in the requested coordination.

ReferralDeclined.label: Declined
ReferralDeclined.definition: The receiving party declined the request. The reason is recorded with a ucm:ClosureReason concept.

ReferralExpired.label: Expired
ReferralExpired.definition: The receiving party made no decision within the time allowed for a response.

ReferralPending.label: Pending
ReferralPending.definition: The request has been sent and the receiving party has not yet decided.

ReferralWithdrawn.label: Withdrawn
ReferralWithdrawn.definition: The requesting party withdrew the request before the receiving party decided.

get.summary: Get nfts for an account info
get.description:
Returns information for all non-fungible tokens for an account.

## Ordering
When considering NFTs, their order is governed by a combination of their numerical **token.Id** and **serialnumber** values, with **token.id** being the parent column.
A serialnumbers value governs its order within the given token.id

In that regard, if a user acquired a set of NFTs in the order (2-2, 2-4 1-5, 1-1, 1-3, 3-3, 3-4), the following layouts illustrate the ordering expectations for ownership listing
1. **All NFTs in ASC order**: 1-1, 1-3, 1-5, 2-2, 2-4, 3-3, 3-4
2. **All NFTs in DESC order**: 3-4, 3-3, 2-4, 2-2, 1-5, 1-3, 1-1
3. **NFTs above 1-1 in ASC order**: 1-3, 1-5, 2-2, 2-4, 3-3, 3-4
4. **NFTs below 3-3 in ASC order**: 1-1, 1-3, 1-5, 2-2, 2-4
5. **NFTs between 1-3 and 3-3 inclusive in DESC order**: 3-4, 3-3, 2-4, 2-2, 1-5, 1-3

Note: The default order for this API is currently DESC

## Filtering
When filtering there are some restrictions enforced to ensure correctness and scalability.

**The table below defines the restrictions and support for the NFT ownership endpoint**

| Query Param   | Comparison Operator | Support | Description           | Example |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ------- |
| token.id      | eq                  | Y       | Single occurrence only. | ?token.id=X |
|               | ne                  | N       | | |
|               | lt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. | ?token.id=lte:X |
|               | gt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. | ?token.id=gte:X |
| serialnumber  | eq                  | Y       | Single occurrence only. Requires the presence of a **token.id** query | ?serialnumber=Y |
|               | ne                  | N       | | |
|               | lt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. Requires the presence of an **lte** or **eq** **token.id** query | ?token.id=lte:X&serialnumber=lt:Y |
|               | gt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. Requires the presence of an **gte** or **eq** **token.id** query | ?token.id=gte:X&serialnumber=gt:Y |
| spender.id    | eq                  | Y       | | ?spender.id=Z |
|               | ne                  | N       | | |
|               | lt(e)               | Y       | | ?spender.id=lt:Z |
|               | gt(e)               | Y       | | ?spender.id=gt:Z |

Note: When searching across a range for individual NFTs a **serialnumber** with an additional **token.id** query filter must be provided.
Both filters must be a single occurrence of **gt(e)** or **lt(e)** which provide a lower and or upper boundary for search.

get.summary: Get the account traces for a historical transaction on the network with the given transaction ID or hash
get.description:
Inspects contract result related data for a transaction and returns a response containing detailed information
for the accounts needed for the transaction execution with some basic fields about them.

The `Accept-Encoding` request header must include `gzip`. Responses can be large (especially with `code` or
`storage`), and compression is required to keep the payload size bounded.

When `diff=true`, each `post` entry always includes `address` and only the fields that changed relative to the
matching `pre` entry. Unchanged storage keys are omitted; slots cleared during the transaction are reported as
a 32-byte zero word.

get.summary: List contract logs from a contract on the network
get.description:
Search the logs of a specific contract across multiple contract calls. Chained logs are not
included but can be found by calling `/api/v1/contracts/{contractId}/results/{timestamp}`
or `/api/v1/contracts/results/{transactionId}`. When searching by topic a timestamp parameter must be supplied
and span a time range of at most seven days.

The order is governed by the combination of timestamp and index values. If the index param is omitted, the order is determined by the timestamp only.

Note: The default order for this API is currently DESC

## Filtering
When filtering there are some restrictions enforced to ensure correctness and scalability.

**The table below defines the restrictions and support for the endpoint**

| Query Param   | Comparison Operator | Support | Description           | Example |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ------- |
| index         | eq                  | Y       | Single occurrence only. Requires the presence of timestamp | ?index=X |
|               | ne                  | N       | | |
|               | lt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. Requires the presence of timestamp | ?index=lte:X |
|               | gt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. Requires the presence of timestamp | ?index=gte:X |
| timestamp     | eq                  | Y       | Single occurrence only. | ?timestamp=Y
|               | ne                  | N       | | |
|               | lt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. Optional second timestamp **gt(e)** | ?timestamp=lte:Y
|               | gt(e)               | Y       | Single occurrence only. Optional second timestamp **lt(e)** | ?timestamp=gte:Y


Both filters must be a single occurrence of **gt(e)** or **lt(e)** which provide a lower and or upper boundary for search.

info.title: FantasyWiki API
info.summary: The HTTP contract of the FantasyWiki Worker.
info.description:
A fantasy league played with Wikipedia articles. Players found leagues, buy
contracts on articles out of a Top Read Snapshot, field a formation, and are
scored on how much those articles were read.

Three authentication regimes sit side by side, and which one applies is
decided by the path prefix rather than by the operation:

| Prefix | Who calls it | How |
|---|---|---|
| `/auth/*` | A browser being signed in | Nothing yet — this is where a session is minted |
| `/api/v1/*` | The frontend, as a signed-in player | The `session_token` cookie, HTTP-only |
| `/internal/v1/*` | The scoring engine | A bearer service token |

The major version lives in the path segment (`v1`), not in a header or a
query parameter, so a future `v2` can be mounted beside `v1` while clients
migrate; `version` above is the contract version, and its major component
must always equal that segment.

Identity is always resolved server-side, from the session or the token. No
endpoint takes a `playerId` from the client, which is why the self-scoped
reads are spelled `/api/v1/me` and `my-…` rather than carrying an id in the
path.

Every failure answers the same shape, a single `error` field carrying a
constant the frontend matches on. The constant is never parsed for meaning;
the status code is what says whose fault it was.

servers.description: Production — the Worker the live app talks to
QA — deployed from the dev branch

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Minting a session. Both operations end in a redirect back to the frontend with the session cookie set, so neither is callable from a documentation page.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: Who the caller is, and signing them out.

tags.name: Leagues
tags.description: Founding, finding and closing leagues. A league is never deleted — closing one records its closure and leaves everything in it readable.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: Joining a league with a team, and leaving one.

tags.name: Market
tags.description: The Article Availability shelf a league offers, and the contracts a player holds against it.

tags.name: Line-ups
tags.description: The formation a team fields, and the days it has been scored on.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: What happened to a player's contracts while they were away.

tags.name: Article Genie
tags.description: The conversational article finder. Present only where the deployment has the Workers AI binding; GET /api/v1/session reports whether it does.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Filing a problem report as a GitHub issue.

tags.name: Reference data
tags.description: Answers that are the same for every player.

tags.name: Internal
tags.description: The scoring engine's two endpoints. Outside /api/v1/* because the caller is a service rather than a person, and authenticated with a shared bearer secret instead of a session.

get.summary: What frontend URL this deployment resolved
get.description: A deployment probe, not part of the game. It answers with the configured FRONTEND_URL and the absolute URL the Worker derived from it, which is the value every OAuth redirect and cookie decision is made against — the one piece of environment that silently breaks sign-in when it is wrong.

FRONTEND_URL.description: As configured, which may carry no scheme.

get.description:
Both halves of the OAuth exchange. Called without a code it redirects to
Google; called with one it exchanges it, finds or creates the player,
signs a seven-day JWT and sets it as the HTTP-only `session_token`
cookie before redirecting to the frontend callback.

A first sign-in redirects to `/auth/callback?new=1`, which is what the
frontend uses to start the onboarding tour.

302.description: To Google, or back to the frontend. A failed exchange redirects to /home?error=auth_failed rather than answering an error status — the caller is a browser mid-navigation, not a client reading JSON.

Set-Cookie.description: session_token, HTTP-only, SameSite=Lax, seven days. Secure whenever the frontend URL is HTTPS.

500.description: The Worker is missing GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET or JWT_SECRET.

get.description:
The Google flow with the identity provider removed, so the app can be
run by someone who has no share of the project's OAuth client. It
produces the identical session — same claims, same secret, same cookie —
so no feature downstream has to know this route exists.

Outside a machine running `wrangler dev` it answers 404 rather than 403:
saying "forbidden" would advertise that the route exists somewhere.

302.description: To the frontend callback, with the session cookie set.

404.description: ENVIRONMENT is not "local", so this route does not exist here.

500.description: The Worker is missing JWT_SECRET.

post.summary: Create a username/password account (MongoDB build only)
post.description:
Creates the credential and the player it belongs to as one write, then
signs the same seven-day session the Google flow does — same claims,
same secret, same `session_token` cookie — so nothing downstream knows
this route exists.

**Absent from the deployed Worker.** Not refused there, not 404 there:
the Cloudflare build's entry point (`src/index.ts`) does not import this
router, so the handler, the password hashing and the credential store
are not in that bundle at all. Only `src/indexPassword.ts`, named by
`wrangler.mongo.jsonc`, mounts it. See
`docs/architecture/auth-modes.md`.

201.description: The account was created and the session cookie set.

Set-Cookie.description: session_token, HTTP-only, SameSite=Lax, seven days. Secure whenever the frontend URL is HTTPS.

400.description: USERNAME_INVALID for a username that is not a legal one, or PASSWORD_TOO_LONG for a password past 200 characters. Named on purpose, unlike the credential failures: neither says anything about who has an account. There is no minimum length and no composition rule — the ceiling is there to bound the key derivation's work, not to judge the password.

403.description: The request's Origin is not the frontend's.

413.description: The body is past the 4KB limit. Plain text, not the usual error shape — this is the body-limit middleware answering before any handler runs.

409.description: The username is already taken — by another credential or by a Google player, the two sharing one username space.

500.description: The Worker is missing JWT_SECRET, or the credential store failed.

post.summary: Sign in with a username and password (MongoDB build only)
post.description:
Verifies the password against the stored PBKDF2 record and signs the
same session the Google flow does.

An unknown username and a wrong password are the same answer, and cost
the same time — telling them apart is how a login form becomes a way to
find out who has an account.

**Absent from the deployed Worker**, in the same sense as
`/auth/password/register` above.

200.description: Signed in, with the session cookie set.

400.description: USERNAME_INVALID for a username that is not a legal one, or PASSWORD_TOO_LONG for a password past 200 characters. Named on purpose, unlike the credential failures: neither says anything about who has an account. There is no minimum length and no composition rule — the ceiling is there to bound the key derivation's work, not to judge the password.

401.description: No such username, or the wrong password. Indistinguishable by design.

403.description: The request's Origin is not the frontend's.

413.description: The body is past the 4KB limit. Plain text, not the usual error shape — this is the body-limit middleware answering before any handler runs.

500.description: The Worker is missing JWT_SECRET, or the credential store failed.

get.description: Every team with a line-up to score on the given day, flattened into the shape the scoring engine consumes: the articles it fielded and the Chemistry Link topology of its schema.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The day to score. An impossible date is rejected rather than rolled over.

200.description: One entry per scorable team. Empty when nothing was fielded.

400.description: The date parameter is missing or not a real date.

post.summary: Write back the day's computed performances
post.description: Idempotent and chunkable: the engine may send a day in several calls and may resend one it already sent, which is what lets a failed run be retried without reconciling first.

200.description: How many rows the call wrote.

400.description: Malformed JSON, a missing or impossible date, or a result the service refused.

get.description: Read straight off the JWT rather than out of the database — these are the claims the cookie carries, not a player record. `features` is read off the Worker's own bindings, so a deployment that was never given the Workers AI model reports the Genie as absent whatever any config says.

delete.description: Expires the session cookie. Nothing server-side is revoked — the JWT is stateless, and a copy taken before this call stays valid until it expires.

get.summary: The leagues the caller plays in

200.description: Every league the caller fields a team in, the Global League included.

post.description: The founder is the caller, resolved from the session and never taken from the body, and is written into the league as both its admin and its first team in one transaction. The response carries no invitation code — a private league's founder reads theirs from the invite-code endpoint, which they now pass by being a member.

400.description: A field the caller sent and can fix: an unknown icon, domain, duration, visibility or invite policy, a name or team name outside its length bounds, or an edition below the acceptance floor.

503.description: Wikimedia was unreachable, so the edition's Language Scale Factor could not be measured. The request was well-formed and the same payload retried in a minute may found the league.

200.description: The league every player belongs to.

404.description: The Global League has not been seeded in this deployment.

get.description: The shelf offered to a player looking for somewhere else to play. Not caller-scoped: the leagues they already play are dropped client-side, where the list of those already lives.

get.summary: The league an invitation code opens
get.description: The preview that lets a player see what they have been invited to before naming a team in it. Rate limited, and this is the endpoint that most needs it: it is the cheapest possible probe of the code space — one GET, no body, no write. It shares its bucket with the join path, so alternating between the two buys no extra attempts. A malformed code, an unused code and a missing league are one answer.

404.description: No league answers to this code.

429.description: The caller has spent their code attempts. Not a leak — they learn about their own quota, never about the code they sent.

get.description: Readable by anyone holding the id, private leagues included: visibility governs joining, not reading. Nothing caller-specific is on this shape — that is the my-role endpoint.

200.description: Every team in the league, ranked. `rankDelta` is null on the first scored day, when there is no previous position to have moved from.

get.summary: What the caller is in this league
get.description: It exists so the page can offer the right two actions, not to authorize either: both are settled again inside their own write.

For a caller its invite policy lets hand it out. Not `my-`: the code is the league's datum, not the caller's — the caller only decides whether they may see it. A caller the policy does not trust is answered 404 rather than 403, so the endpoint never confirms that a code exists.

404.description: No such league, no code on it, or the caller may not see it.

post.description: A noun, and POST rather than DELETE on the league, because nothing is removed: this creates the league's closure and leaves the league itself — teams, contracts, standings — entirely readable. There is no endpoint that deletes a league, and there should not be one.

200.description: The league, now carrying its closedAt.

403.description: The caller is not the league's admin. 403 rather than 404: a league's page, dates and standings are readable by anyone holding its id, so there is nothing here to conceal.

409.description: The league is already closed.

get.summary: The caller's team in this league

404.description: The caller fields no team in this league.

post.summary: Join a league with a team
post.description: Only a request that presents a code spends from the rate-limit bucket, which keeps the limiter off signup and off the public-league shelf — neither carries one, and neither is a guessing surface. A request without a code learns only "this league is private", which is the same sentence for every private league in the database.

name.description: The team's name, unique within the league.

invitationCode.description: Only consulted for a private league; a public one ignores it.

201.description: The team as created, with its starting credits.

400.description: A missing name, a name outside its length bounds or already taken, or the caller already has a team here.

403.description: The league is private and no valid code was presented.

409.description: The season has ended or the league was closed. 409 rather than 403: the refusal is about the state of the league, not about who is asking — a valid code and the admin themselves are turned away too.

429.description: The caller has spent their code attempts.

post.description: A departure rather than a deletion, because the team stays: it keeps its contracts and its place in the final table. The last member leaving is the one case where the league itself goes, which the response reports.

200.description: Whether the departure emptied the league.

403.description: Nobody may leave the Global League.

404.description: The caller fields no team in this league.

409.description: The season has ended, or the departure is already on the record.

get.description: Unscoped, and readable by anyone holding the league id: who owns what is already visible from the market shelf and the standings.

get.summary: The caller's contracts in this league

404.description: The caller fields no team in this league.

post.summary: Buy a contract on an article
post.description: The price is the league's, computed at purchase and frozen for the term — a contract is bought at a price, not at a rate. The tier decides how long the term runs.

articleId.description: The canonical page title, underscored — the article's identity.

400.description: An unknown tier, an article already under contract to someone else or already owned by the caller, a full team, or not enough credits.

404.description: The caller fields no team in this league.

post.summary: Sell a contract before it expires
post.description: An Early Sell settles at the article's current value prorated over the part of the term already served, which is what stops a sale from being a free exit from a bad buy.

400.description: Not the caller's contract, already sold, already settled, or expired.

404.description: No such contract, or the caller fields no team in this league.

post.summary: Elect to renew a contract at expiry
post.description: An intent, not a purchase: the settlement sweep is what acts on it, at the price the article commands then plus the renewal premium. Only electable inside the renewal window.

200.description: The contract, now carrying the election.

400.description: Not the caller's contract, the renewal window is closed, or the contract is already gone.

404.description: No such contract, or the caller fields no team in this league.

delete.description: DELETE on the same path because the election is the resource being removed. The intent can be withdrawn any time before the settlement sweep acts on it.

200.description: The contract, with the election withdrawn.

400.description: Not the caller's contract, or no election to withdraw.

404.description: No such contract, or the caller fields no team in this league.

get.summary: The caller's line-up in this league

404.description: The caller fields no team in this league.

put.description: PUT because the line-up is replaced wholesale rather than amended. The schema must be a known formation and every occupied position must belong to it, which is what the read side relies on when it indexes the Chemistry Link topology by schema.

400.description: An unknown schema, a position outside it, or a contract the caller does not hold.

get.description: Read-only, and the team is named in the path because the viewer does not own it. That id is not a security control: the standings already name every team in the league to every member. A team id from another league is not found rather than readable.

404.description: No such team in this league.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many days back, most recent first. Floored at 1.

404.description: The caller fields no team in this league.

get.summary: The caller's notifications in this league

200.description: Notifications, each carrying the contract it is about.

403.description: The notification belongs to another player.

get.description: The row behind the session, as distinct from the claims the cookie carries: this id is what every contract and team in the database is keyed by.

get.summary: The caller's notifications across every league

200.description: Notifications, newest first, each naming the league it belongs to.

post.summary: Read an opening request into searches
post.description: Separate from a turn only because of ordering: a turn is defined over a candidate list, and there is no list until the query has been read. The Worker answers with the searches, and the browser runs them.

query.example: Portuguese footballers who played in England

200.description: The keywords and anchors to search on.

400.description: A malformed body, or a query that is missing or too long. None of these should ever reach a player — they mean the frontend built a payload it should not have, and a 400 says so instead of burning a model call.

429.description: GENIE_RATE_LIMITED — the caller's budget for this window is spent.

503.description: GENIE_ASLEEP where the deployment has no Workers AI binding, or the model refused. 503 rather than 502: the day's neuron allocation coming back is a matter of waiting.

post.summary: One turn of the Article Genie
post.description: The Worker does exactly one thing here — call the model — because every other part of the feature is cheaper in the browser: the Wikimedia search and link fetches run against the client's own cache, where neither the subrequest nor the CPU limit applies.

200.description: The Genie's utterance, its next question, and which candidates survive it.

400.description: A malformed body, too many candidates, none at all, an over-long history, or an unknown bucket.

post.description: Opens a labelled GitHub issue as the FantasyWiki app rather than under a maintainer's own account. The reporter is the session, never the body. Rate limited per player, which is really there to protect the shared GitHub credential from its secondary limits.

400.description: A malformed body, an unknown category, or a missing or over-long title or body.

429.description: REPORT_RATE_LIMITED — a double submit, or a script.

502.description: GitHub was unreachable. The frontend answers this by offering the pre-filled issue link, so the reporter never loses what they typed.

get.summary: The Wikipedia editions a league can be founded on
get.description: Unscoped: the answer is the same for every player, which is what lets the client hold it for the session. Every live edition, unfiltered — the acceptance floor is applied at league creation instead of here.

503.description: Wikimedia was unreachable. The request was well-formed and will work later.

sessionCookie.name: session_token
sessionCookie.description: A seven-day HS256 JWT, set by the sign-in redirect and HTTP-only, so no script — the frontend's own included — can read it. The frontend simply sends every request with credentials included. Identity is the `sub` claim; nothing about who is asking is ever taken from a URL or a body.

serviceToken.description: The shared secret the scoring engine presents on /internal/v1/*. Compared in constant time, and an unset secret fails closed rather than open.

InvitationCode.name: code
InvitationCode.description: Five characters from an alphabet with no look-alikes, so a code read off a screen and typed back in cannot be mistyped into a different valid one. In the path rather than a query string because it is the resource being addressed.

Unauthorized.description: No session cookie, or one that has expired or does not verify.

NoSuchPlayer.description: The session verifies but names a player this deployment has no record of — a cookie outliving the database it was minted against.

NoSuchLeague.description: No league answers to this id.

ServerError.description: Something nobody named — a D1 outage, an upstream failure. Never a refusal the caller could act on: those are 4xx and carry a constant.

Error.description: Every failure, in one shape. `error` carries a constant the frontend matches on exactly; its wording is not part of the contract and must never be parsed for meaning.

PasswordCredentials.description: A username/password pair, for the MongoDB build's sign-in. The username is 3–30 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. The password has no minimum and no composition rules — any string up to 200 characters is accepted, empty included. That ceiling bounds the work one request can ask of the key derivation, which is fed the whole string.

PasswordSession.description: The session itself arrives as the `session_token` cookie, as it does from the Google flow; this only says where to go next.

isNew.description: True when the account was just created, so the SPA starts onboarding.

sub.description: The Google account id the session was minted for.

picture.description: Avatar URL. Empty for the demo player.

features.description: What this deployment can offer, read off its own bindings.

credits.description: Derived, not stored: the starting budget less what the team's live contracts cost. Stated once, in a database view.

id.description: The canonical page title, underscored. This is the article's identity.

Domain.description: A Wikipedia language edition code, as Wikimedia writes them — lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. What an edition may actually host a league on is decided against live data at league creation, not by this shape.

ContractTier.description: How long a contract's term runs.

Contract.description: A contract as it travels. Dates and durations are ISO-8601 strings on the wire; the frontend deserialises them into Temporal values in its service layer rather than trusting the shape it received.

startDate.description: When the term began, as an instant.

duration.description: The term, as an ISO-8601 duration.

purchasePrice.description: What was paid, frozen at purchase. A contract is bought at a price, not at a rate, which is what makes a settlement a gain or a loss.

renewalCount.description: Consecutive renewals so far, which drive the renewal premium.

renewalElected.description: Whether the owner has elected to renew at expiry.

languageScale.description: The Language Scale Factor every price and every score in this league is computed at, measured when it was founded and frozen there. A league that read a live registry would silently re-price every contract in it the day the registry was recalibrated.

icon.description: One emoji from the league icon set.

closedAt.description: When the admin closed the league early, or null while it is still open. Never unset once written, and never accompanied by a delete.

LeagueVisibility.description: Whether a league can be joined by anyone or only with its invitation code. The rule governs joining, not reading — a private league's page and standings stay visible.

LeagueInvitePolicy.description: Who may hand out the league's invitation code.

LeagueDuration.description: How long a season runs, as the choices a player is offered. Floored at two weeks because a shorter season could not hold a LONG contract to expiry, and capped at six months because past that a Top Read Snapshot's article mix has turned over enough that the market a player joined is not the one they end in.

icon.description: One emoji from the league icon set.

teamName.description: The founder's own team, created in the same transaction.

rankDelta.description: Places gained since the previous scored day, or null on the first one — there is no earlier position to have moved from, and zero would claim there was.

Position.description: A slot on the pitch. Which of these a line-up may occupy is decided by its schema.

ChemistryLevel.description: How strongly two adjacent articles link to each other. Mutual links are excellent, one-way good, neither weak; empty is an unfilled slot.

ChemistryLink.description: One edge of the schema's fixed topology. The set of edges is decided by the schema, not by the client — a saved line-up whose links do not match its schema is normalised back to the schema's own.

formation.description: The occupied slots, keyed by position. Every key must belong to the schema; a position the schema does not have is refused rather than ignored.

Performance.description:
One team's score for one day.

**The formation it was scored on is not sent.** It is held in the
database as the opaque snapshot the scoring engine relayed, under a
column `PerformanceService` does not read, so the field is `undefined`
by the time the response is serialised and is dropped. `PerformanceDTO`
declares it as present and required; this document describes what
actually arrives, and the two disagree until the service resolves the
snapshot or the DTO stops promising it.

Notification.description: What happened to one of the player's contracts while they were away.

autonym.description: What the edition calls its own language.

GenieBucket.description: How many candidates are still standing, as flavour rather than a count. The Genie speaks in character and never reads the number out.

candidates.description: Ids must be distinct — a duplicate is refused rather than deduplicated.

utterance.description: What the Genie says before it asks.

keep.description: The candidate ids that survive this turn.

kind.description: Whether the question narrows the field or only ranks it. A filter may discard candidates; a preference may not.

contactConsent.description: Whether the reporter is willing to be followed up on the issue.

diagnostics.description: What the client can say about where the problem happened.

ScoringInput.description: One scorable team, flattened into what the scoring engine needs and nothing else.

articles.description: The canonical titles fielded that day.

chemistryLinks.description: The schema's topology as article pairs, already resolved from positions.

formationSnapshot.description: The position-to-article map, pre-serialised. Opaque to the backend, which stores it verbatim and hands it back untouched.
Echoed back from the scoring input it was computed from.

info.title: Kremeing
info.summary: Hot-light tracking for every Krispy Kreme location in the US.
info.description:
Public read API for the Krispy Kreme hot-light status of every US store.

Backed by a poller that hits Krispy Kreme's official store API every five
minutes and records *flip events* — the moments a store's hot light goes
on or off. Clients get both the live snapshot and a historical view they
can render as uptime graphs or trend heatmaps.

The API only stores changes plus a "last polled at" sentinel, so each
store's footprint stays tiny while the staleness of the data remains
observable.

servers.description: Local dev (in-memory or Postgres-backed depending on KREMEING_DATABASE_URL)

tags.name: live
tags.description: Live status sourced directly from Krispy Kreme.

tags.name: history
tags.description: Flip events and uptime aggregations from our local store.

stores.description:
Number of stores in the current discovery registry.
A value stuck at 0 indicates discovery failed and the
poller has nothing to poll — alert on it.

lastDiscoveryRefresh.description:
When the registry was last (re)published by discovery.
Stale relative to the configured refresh interval means
refreshes are failing.

get.description:
Proxies Krispy Kreme's `/shops` endpoint and enriches each entry
with our cached temporal context (`lastFlippedAt`, `firstObservedAt`).
Upstream caps the result at 12 — `limit` only narrows further.

Responses are cached for ~30s, keyed on coordinates quantized to
~1 km resolution. Rate-limited at 60 req/min per client IP
(token bucket, shared with `/hot-light`).

200.description: Nearby stores with current hot-light status.

get.summary: List every store visible in a map viewport
get.description:
Reads the complete local discovery registry and returns every store
inside the supplied bounds, including its last-known hot-light status.
Unlike `/stores/nearby`, this endpoint is not capped by the upstream
search API.

Keep `includeHistory=false` for wide map views. That performs one bulk
status read without loading temporal columns. Set it to `true` after
zooming in to add `lastFlippedAt` and `firstObservedAt`.

parameters.name: includeHistory
parameters.description: Include temporal status context for detail views.

200.description: Every registry store within the viewport.

get.summary: Find stores by zip or "City, ST"
get.description:
Free-text proxy over Krispy Kreme's `/shops/search?cityStateZip=`.
Accepts a 5-digit ZIP (`98109`) or a `"City, ST"` (`"Seattle, WA"`)
— both shapes are normalized upstream.

Responses are cached for ~30s, keyed on the lowercased,
whitespace-trimmed query (so `"Seattle, WA"` and `"seattle, wa"`
share an entry). Same 60 req/min/IP token bucket as `/nearby`
and `/hot-light`.

get.summary: Current hot-light status for one store
get.description:
Live read backed by a 60-second in-process cache, so a hot link
getting passed around won't translate into hundreds of requests
per second against `api.krispykreme.com`. Use this for "is the
light on right now" UIs; for graphs and trends, use `/uptime`.

Rate-limited at 60 req/min per client IP (token bucket, shared
with `/nearby`).

get.summary: Flip events for one store within a time range
get.description:
Returns every status flip we observed for the store inside the range,
oldest first. The first entry per store is a `FirstObservation`
anchor (when we started tracking), not a real flip — pair entries
sequentially to reconstruct intervals.

Defaults to the last 7 days if `since`/`until` are omitted.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound (ISO-8601 with offset).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound (ISO-8601 with offset).

get.summary: Basemap tile URL for the map clients
get.description:
Returns the raster tile URL template each client should hand to
its map library (Leaflet / osmdroid), including that client's
tile-server key as `?key=`. Served from the backend so the URL and
keys can change without a client release. If the operator hasn't
configured a key for the client, the template comes back without
`?key=` (tiles will then 403). Cached for an hour.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Which client is asking. Missing or unknown values get the web key.

Cache-Control.description: `public, max-age=3600`

tileUrlTemplate.description:
Leaflet-style template. `{r}` is empty for 256 px tiles
or `@2x` for 512 px retina tiles.

get.summary: VAPID public key for the web-push subscription flow
get.description:
Returns the URL-safe-base64 public key the browser must include
in `pushManager.subscribe({ applicationServerKey: ... })`. The
matching private key never leaves the server. Returns 503
`push_disabled` when the operator hasn't configured push
(no Postgres + VAPID env vars).

publicKey.description: URL-safe base64 of the 65-byte uncompressed P-256 public key.

get.summary: Stores this browser is currently subscribed to
get.description:
Pass the browser's `pushManager.getSubscription().endpoint`. The
server returns every storeId this endpoint has an active row
for. Used by the web client on app load to restore per-store
bell state.

post.summary: Subscribe a browser push endpoint to a store's hot-light flips
post.description:
Body matches the JSON shape of the browser's
`PushSubscription.toJSON()`. Idempotent on
`(storeId, subscription.endpoint)`; re-posting refreshes the
keys (handles browser key rotation).

delete.description:
Removes the row matching `(storeId, endpoint)`. Idempotent —
no row matching the criteria is treated as a successful
no-op. Use this when the user toggles "Notify me" off in the
UI; let 410-Gone bounce cleanup handle dead subscriptions.

post.summary: Register a native device (FCM) for nearby hot-light alerts
post.description:
Used by the Android Auto companion app. The device asks to be
notified whenever a store within `radiusMiles` of its
(`latitude`, `longitude`) flips its hot light on. Idempotent on
the FCM `token`: re-posting refreshes the stored location/radius
(handles the device moving or rotating its token).

delete.description:
Removes the row matching the FCM `token`. Idempotent — a missing
token is treated as a successful no-op.

get.description:
Aggregates the flip log into time-series buckets. `observedSeconds`
may be less than `totalSeconds` when poll gaps exist — clients
should render those gaps as unknown rather than as 0% uptime.

Defaults: bucket=hour, range=last 24h (or last 30d when bucket=day).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description:
Exclusive upper bound. The total span (`until - since`)
must be ≤ 90 days; wider ranges return `range_too_wide`.

BadRequest.description:
Malformed request — query param missing/wrong type, invalid path
id, out-of-range coordinates, invalid viewport ordering
(`invalid_bounds`), or `until - since > 90 days`.

StoreNotFound.description: No store exists with that `shopId` (live), or we've never observed it (history).

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests from this client IP. The proxy endpoints
(`/stores/nearby`, `/stores/{id}/hot-light`) share a token bucket
of 60 req/min per IP. Honor the `Retry-After` header (seconds).

UpstreamUnavailable.description: The Krispy Kreme upstream API failed.

PushDisabled.description:
Push notifications are not configured on this server (no
Postgres + VAPID env). Clients can fall back to in-page
polling when they see this.

HotLightStatusValue.description: Wire encoding of the live status. Always lowercase ASCII.

observedAt.description: When the response was generated, not necessarily when the light flipped.

lastFlippedAt.description:
Null until a flip is observed, or when viewport history was not
requested; `firstObservedAt` is set first.

firstObservedAt.description:
Null when the store has never been observed by us, or when viewport
history was not requested.

endpoint.description:
Push service URL the browser hands us when calling
`pushManager.subscribe()`. Different per browser
(FCM, Mozilla autopush, Apple web-push, etc.).

token.description: FCM registration token identifying this device install.

radiusMiles.description: Notify about hot-light flips within this many miles of the point.

fractionOn.description:
On-seconds divided by *observed* seconds (not total). Use
`observedSeconds / totalSeconds` to detect partial coverage.

error.description: Stable machine-readable error code.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. May change between releases.

info.title: Search
info.description:
# Introduction
The Searoutes web services APIs allow you to programmatically access tools and services from the Searoutes ecosystem. You can use these APIs to retrieve informations about vessel positions, vessel routes, GHG emissions, weather and other core data points. Searoutes services are divided in five categories:

- Our [Geocoding service](#tag/geocoding) searchs points of interests, like ports or airports, and provides you with their geolocations.

- Our [Search service](#tag/search) searchs entities used in other endpoints such as carriers or services.

- Our [Vessel service](#tag/vessel) gives you up to date positions of vessels and estimated travel times to their next destination.

Note that this is the documentation page for most recent stable version of Searoutes API. For the previous stable versions, [visit this documentation page](http://developer.searoutes.com/api/v1). 

If you have a `valid API key`, you may try the API by copying the code samples in your shell, your favorite editor, or API development platform. Please be aware that some endpoints may not work with your API key depending on your service plan. If you would like a trial key or you want to add additional endpoints to your plan, please [get in touch with us](https://searoutes.typeform.com/to/ZRAoy5).

tags.name: geocoding
tags.description: The Searoutes search service is currently composed of a reverse geocoding functionality. Reverse geocoding returns a place, in the general sense, for a coordinate pair `longitude,latitude`.

get.summary: Find airport by name, locode or IATA
get.description:
This endpoint does forward geocoding: given a name, a locode or IATA code, it returns airports matching the request with their name, locode, IATA code, country, subdivision and coordinates.

This endpoint can be used for exact matching using `locode` or `iataCode` parameter or for partial matching using `query` parameter. Only one of these fields must be used in a request.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A partial string used for search. For instance, part of an airport name or part of a locode

parameters.name: iataCode
parameters.description: A string representing the iata code of the searched airport.

parameters.name: locode
parameters.description: A string representing the locode of the searched airport.

parameters.name: sizes
parameters.description: A list of strings used to filter the location by size. Permitted values are `large`, `medium`, `small`. If not passed, all the sizes will be taken into account.

parameters.name: countryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to filter the location by country.

parameters.name: excludeCountryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to exclude location of some countries.

404.description: Location not found for type airport.

messages: Location 'ZZZZ' not found for type airport.
Geocoding service unavailable.

get.description: This endpoint does forward geocoding: given a partial string, for instance `panam`, it returns a given number of routing areas which name contains `panam`. It also returns the `id`, `name` and `geolocation`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A partial string, with at least 3 characters

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: An integer to limit the number of results

messages: Area name can only contain letters and spaces
Area 'test' not found.

get.summary: Find port by name or locode
get.description:
This endpoint does forward geocoding: given a name or a locode, it returns ports matching the request with their name, locode, country, size, coordinates and whether the port is in an eca zone or not.

Use either `locode` or `query`, not both in the same query.

parameters.name: locode
parameters.description: A string representing the locode of the searched airport.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A partial string used for search. For instance, part of an port name or part of a locode.

parameters.name: sizes
parameters.description: A list of strings used to filter the locations by size. Permitted values are `large`, `medium`, `small`, `tiny`. If not passed, all the sizes will be taken into account.

parameters.name: countryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to filter the locations by country.

parameters.name: excludeCountryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to exclude locations of some countries.

404.description: Location not found for type port.

messages: Location 'Bobigny' not found for type port.
Geocoding service unavailable.

get.summary: Find closest sea point at location
get.description:
Given a point as a coordinates pair, this endpoint checks if it is on sea or not. If on sea, it returns the coordinate pair `{longitude},{latitude}` as GeoJSON. If on land, it returns the closest coordinate pair on sea.

The field 'valid' tells whether the given point is on sea or not.

The response also contains information about the point : `isSeca` if the point is in an ECA zone and `isCoastal` if the point is close to the coast.

parameters.name: coordinates
parameters.description: A pair `longitude,latitude`. Longitude should be between -180 and 180 degrees, and latitude between -90 and 90 degrees.

schema.description:
GeoJSon object
The coordinate reference system for all GeoJSON coordinates is a geographic coordinate reference system, using the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84) datum, with longitude and latitude units of decimal degrees. This is equivalent to the coordinate reference system identified by the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) URN An OPTIONAL third-position element SHALL be the height in meters above or below the WGS 84 reference ellipsoid. In the absence of elevation values, applications sensitive to height or depth SHOULD interpret positions as being at local ground or sea level.

bbox.description: A GeoJSON object MAY have a member named "bbox" to include information on the coordinate range for its Geometries, Features, or FeatureCollections. The value of the bbox member MUST be an array of length 2*n where n is the number of dimensions represented in the contained geometries, with all axes of the most southwesterly point followed by all axes of the more northeasterly point. The axes order of a bbox follows the axes order of geometries.

messages: Longitude must be between -180 and 180.

get.summary: Find the geocoordinates of a zipcode
get.description: This endpoint does forward geocoding: given a postal code and a list of countries, it returns both coordinates and information about that particular location.

parameters.name: countryCodes
parameters.description: A two letter string denoting the country.

parameters.name: postalCode
parameters.description: A string denoting the postal code. Either `query` or `postalCode` must be given.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A partial string used for search. For instance, part of the city name. Either `query` or `postalCode` must be given.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Deprecated, use `countryCodes`

parameters.name: postal
parameters.description: Deprecated, use `postalCode`.

messages: Location with postal code 13001123 in country FR not found.
Geocoding service unavailable.

get.description:
This endpoint can be used to retrieve the closest locations from a point ordered by distance or the locations around a point (inside a geographical circle with a given radius (in meters)). You can also choose the number of results. By default, the endpoint only returns the closest location.

The `coordinates` of the point (or center of the circle) must be passed as path parameter as coordinates pair `longitude,latitude`.

The query parameter `locationTypes` allows to filter the types returned. A list of values can be passed among `port,airport,zipcode,railTerminal, roadTerminal`. 
If this parameter is not passed in the query, all the types will be searched.

The query parameter `sizes` allows to filter the sizes of the locations returned for ports and airports.

For each location found, geometry (coordinates) is returned as well as a `properties` field that contains different information according to the type of the location.

For ports : `name`, `locode`, `country`, `countryName`, `size` and `distance` (in meters) from the point passed in the query.

For airports : `name`, `locode`, `size`, `iataCode`, `countryName`, `countryCode` (as a two letters code), `subdivisionName`, `city`.

For zipcodes : `name`, `countryCode`, `countryName`, `postalCode` and `distance` (in meters) from the point passed in the query.

For rail terminals and road terminals : `name`, `locode`, `countryCode`, `countryName` and `distance` (in meters) from the point passed in the query.

parameters.name: coordinates
parameters.description: coordinates pair of the point as `longitude,latitude`. Longitude should be between -180 and 180 degrees, and latitude between -90 and 90 degrees.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: the radius of the geographical circle used to search closest locations (in meters). If not passed, the closest locations are retrieved.

parameters.name: locationTypes
parameters.description: A list of strings used to filter the location types. Permitted values are `port, airport, zipcode, railTerminal, roadTerminal`. If not passed, all the types will be taken into account.

parameters.name: sizes
parameters.description: A list of strings used to filter the location by size. Permitted values are `large`, `medium`, `small` and `tiny`. Note that this parameter is available for ports and airports search only. If not passed, all the sizes will be taken into account.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results (between 0 and 50). If not passed, the default limit is 1.

parameters.name: countryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to filter the location by country.

parameters.name: excludeCountryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to exclude location of some countries.

messages: Value 'test' is of invalid type for parameter 'locationTypes'.
Geocoding service unavailable.

get.description:
This endpoint returns the locations that match a partial string passed as query parameter (`query`) or matches exactly a specific field (`locode`, `iataCode` or `postalCode`). Only one of these fields must be used in a request.
Locations returned can be either `airport`, `port`, `zipcode`, `railTerminal` or `roadTerminal`. 

The query parameter `locationTypes` allows to filter the types returned. A list of values can be passed among `port,airport,zipcode,railTerminal, roadTerminal`. 
If this parameter is not passed in the query, all the types will be searched.

The query parameter `sizes` allows to filter the sizes of the locations returned for ports and airports.

The results are returned with this priority order : `port` > `airport` > `railTerminal` > `zipcode` > `roadTerminal`.

For each location, geometry (coordinates) is returned as well as `properties` fields. These fields differ according to the type of the location.

For airports : `name`, `locode`, `size`, `iataCode`, `countryName`, `countryCode` (as a two letters code). 

For zipcodes : `name`, `country`, `countryName`, `postalCode`, `stateCode`, `stateName`, `countyCode`, `countyName`.

For ports : `name`, `locode`, `size`, `country`, `countryName`, `subdivisionCode`, `subdivisionName`.

For ports, rail terminals and road terminals : `name`, `locode`, `country`, `countryName`, `subdivisionCode`, `subdivisionName`.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A partial string used for search. For instance, part of an airport name or part of a locode

parameters.name: postalCode
parameters.description: A string denoting the postal code.

parameters.name: locode
parameters.description: A string representing the locode of the searched airport.

parameters.name: iataCode
parameters.description: A string representing the iata code of the searched airport.

parameters.name: locationTypes
parameters.description: A list of strings used to filter the location types. Permitted values are `port`, `airport`, `zipcode`, `railTerminal`, `roadTerminal`. If not passed, all the types will be taken into account.

parameters.name: sizes
parameters.description: A list of strings used to filter the location by size. Permitted values are `large`, `medium`, `small`. Note that this parameter is available for airports search only. If not passed, all the sizes will be taken into account.

parameters.name: countryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to filter the location by country.

parameters.name: excludeCountryCodes
parameters.description: A list of country codes (2 characters ISO) used to exclude location of some countries.

messages: Value 'test' is of invalid type for parameter 'locationTypes'.
Geocoding service unavailable.

get.description: This endpoint allows to get carrier information by id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the carrier

messages: Carrier with id '37' not found.

get.summary: Find a carrier by name or SCAC
get.description: This endpoint allows to get carrier information by name or SCAC. The API returns a list of carriers matching the request.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name or partial name to search.

parameters.name: scac
parameters.description: The SCAC of the searched carrier.

messages: Either parameter 'scac' or 'name' must be given to search for a carrier.
No carrier found for value CMZ.

get.description:
This endpoint allows to get service information by id including the name, the ids of the carriers which operate the service, the designation of the service per carrier, the intermediate port calls and the IMOs of the vessels operating these services.

Note that `carrierIds`, `portLocodes` and `vesselImos` in the response are deprecated.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the service

messages: Service with id '2' not found.

get.description:
This endpoint allows to search for services by name or partial name and retrieve the matching services and their information including the name, the ids of the carriers that operate the service, the designation of the service per carrier, the intermediate port calls and the IMOs of the vessels operating these services.
You can also pass a carrier SCAC to filter on the services operated by this carrier.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The id of the service

parameters.name: carrierScac
parameters.description: The SCAC of a carrier that operates the wanted service

messages: Parameter 'name' must be given to search for a service.
No service found for name FAL11.

get.description: This endpoint returns basic vessel information (imo, width (in m), length (in m), maximum draft (in m)). You can search vessels by name. If several vessels match the given string, up to 5 vessels can be returned.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name or a part of the name of the searched vessel.

api_key.description: Use your `x-api-key` to authenticate with our APIs. Note that your key is tied with a usage plan. You are therefore rate limited depending on your subscription. If you wish you increase your request calls, please [get in touch with us](/contact/).

GeoJsonObject.description:
GeoJSon object
The coordinate reference system for all GeoJSON coordinates is a geographic coordinate reference system, using the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84) datum, with longitude and latitude units of decimal degrees. This is equivalent to the coordinate reference system identified by the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) URN An OPTIONAL third-position element SHALL be the height in meters above or below the WGS 84 reference ellipsoid. In the absence of elevation values, applications sensitive to height or depth SHOULD interpret positions as being at local ground or sea level.

bbox.description: A GeoJSON object MAY have a member named "bbox" to include information on the coordinate range for its Geometries, Features, or FeatureCollections. The value of the bbox member MUST be an array of length 2*n where n is the number of dimensions represented in the contained geometries, with all axes of the most southwesterly point followed by all axes of the more northeasterly point. The axes order of a bbox follows the axes order of geometries.

Position.description:
GeoJSon fundamental geometry construct.
A position is an array of numbers. There MUST be two or more elements. The first two elements are longitude and latitude, or easting and northing, precisely in that order and using decimal numbers. Altitude or elevation MAY be included as an optional third element.
Implementations SHOULD NOT extend positions beyond three elements because the semantics of extra elements are unspecified and ambiguous. Historically, some implementations have used a fourth element to carry a linear referencing measure (sometimes denoted as "M") or a numerical timestamp, but in most situations a parser will not be able to properly interpret these values. The interpretation and meaning of additional elements is beyond the scope of this specification, and additional elements MAY be ignored by parsers.

LinearRing.description:
A linear ring is a closed LineString with four or more positions.
The first and last positions are equivalent, and they MUST contain identical values; their representation SHOULD also be identical.
A linear ring is the boundary of a surface or the boundary of a hole in a surface.
A linear ring MUST follow the right-hand rule with respect to the area it bounds, i.e., exterior rings are counterclockwise, and holes are clockwise.

info.title: Scalar Galaxy
info.description:
The Scalar Galaxy is an example OpenAPI document to test OpenAPI tools and libraries. It's a fictional universe with fictional planets and fictional data. ## Resources * https://github.com/scalar/scalar * https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification * https://scalar.com ## Markdown Support All descriptions *can* contain ~~tons of text~~ **Markdown**. [If GitHub supports the syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax), chances are we're supporting it, too.
Examples **Blockquotes** > I love OpenAPI. <3 **Tables** | Feature | Availability | | ---------------- | ------------ | | Markdown Support | ✓ | **Accordion** ```html

message.content:
Generative AI is a subfield of artificial intelligence that focuses on generating new, original content, such as images, music, text, or videos. These models are trained on large datasets and learn to recognize patterns, relationships, and structures within the data, allowing them to generate new content that is similar in style, tone, or characteristics to the training data. 
 
 Generative AI models can be categorized into two main types: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). GANs consist of two neural networks: a generator and a discriminator. The generator creates new content, while the discriminator evaluates the generated content and tells the generator whether it's realistic or not. VAEs are neural networks that learn to compress and reconstruct data. 
 
 Generative AI has numerous applications across various industries, including art and design, content generation, data augmentation, and recommendation systems. Some examples of Generative AI in action include Deep Dream Generator, Amper Music, and DALL-E. 
 
 In summary, Generative AI is a powerful technology that enables the creation of new, original content using machine learning models. It has the potential to revolutionize various industries and create new opportunities for artists, designers, and content creators.
