info.title: Ardent control-plane API used by the CLI
info.description:
Review draft describing the current control-plane handlers used by the Ardent CLI, plus the frontend approval endpoint needed for browser login. This is a subset of the customer API, not an inventory of all routes. The document version is not a server API version.

The server implementation is authoritative. This file does not generate handlers or CLI types, and the routes-package TestCLIOpenAPIParity checks documented route registrations and selected struct schema shapes. Handler validation, authentication, status codes, and deployed behavior remain outside that partial gate. Descriptions were checked against source, not against a deployed service. API authentication uses Authorization: Bearer <token>; the CLI uses an organization-scoped API key. Browser approval uses a user JWT.

Typical token flow: GET /organizations, GET /projects?organization_id=..., then GET /connectors?organization_id=...&project_id=..., then GET /branches?connector_id=.... Create a branch with POST /branches and poll GET /workflows/{workflowID} using operation.workflow_id. All example identifiers and credentials are placeholders.

HTTP 202 means accepted, not completed. HTTP 503 with error workflow_result_timeout means durable work is still running. Authenticated resource clients inspect workflow_id and Location before retrying; an unauthenticated login exchange instead retries the same code and verifier after five seconds. Not all errors are JSON. Local CLI status, logout, project switch, and branch switch have no dedicated API endpoints; logout does not revoke the key. Internal workload routes, other customer endpoints, and database connection/credential delivery are outside this document's scope.

get.description: Opens the frontend approval flow. code_challenge is the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the verifier. The CLI holds the verifier and listens on its loopback callback.

302.description: Redirect to the frontend approval page.

post.description: Called by the frontend with a registered user JWT, not an API key. Requires api_keys.create in the organization. The frontend follows redirect_uri to deliver code and state to the CLI loopback callback.

Exchange the approved code with its original verifier. On workflow_result_timeout the CLI retries this exchange after five seconds with the same code and verifier. The returned key is a credential: store it securely.

201.description: API key for the approved organization.

key.description: Sensitive API key. Store securely; never log it.

503.description: Credential creation is still running. Retry POST /auth/cli/exchange after five seconds with the same code and original verifier. The client has not received its API key; it cannot use the authenticated workflow endpoint to poll this result.

Location.description: Relative workflow status URL emitted by the server. This endpoint requires authentication; an unauthenticated exchange client retries the exchange instead.

get.description: The CLI validates its API key with this endpoint and requires exactly one organization. API keys require organizations.read and are scoped to their own organization.
Requires projects.read in organization_id. An optional project_id filters the returned array; an absent match then returns 404.

post.description: Requires projects.create. A duplicate name returns 409 project_already_exists. A 503 workflow_result_timeout does not mean the project was not created.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required. Trimmed, non-empty, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes. Keep the same key and request fields when retrying the same mutation.

delete.description: Requires projects.delete. The resource and organization must match. A project with retained dependent records, including deleted branches, returns 409 project_has_dependents.

get.description: Requires organization_memberships.read.

delete.description: Requires organization_memberships.update. Removing the last owner returns 409. Handler errors are plain text, except the JSON workflow timeout response.

get.description: Requires organization_invitations.read. The CLI omits invitations from member listing when this returns 403 permission_denied.

post.description: Requires organization_invitations.create and every requested scope. role_display_name is a label; permissions come from scopes. A 502 delivery error means the invitation was created but email delivery failed.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required. Trimmed, non-empty, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes. Keep the same key and request fields when retrying the same mutation.

502.description: Invitation created but email delivery failed. Inspect invitation_id before retrying.

delete.description: Requires organization_invitations.delete. The invitation must belong to the named organization.

get.description: Requires connectors.read. Both organization_id and project_id are required. Source credentials are not included in the response.

200.description: Connector metadata and optional onboarding failure details.

post.description: Requires connectors.create. Omitting environment_id requests Ardent Cloud placement. A reused request_id with conflicting fields returns 409 request_id_conflict. Poll GET /connectors/{connectorID}; registered means metadata-workflow completion, not source replication readiness.

202.description: Registration accepted.

get.description: Requires any of connectors.create, connectors.read, or connectors.delete in the owning organization. Missing or unauthorized connectors return 404. Handler errors are plain text. Registration completion does not establish replication readiness.
Requires environments.read in the connector organization. Deleted branches are omitted. Missing or unauthorized connectors return 404.

post.description: Requires environments.update in the connector organization. Uses the newest published snapshot and refuses an unavailable newest snapshot with 409 snapshot_unavailable. Caller-selected snapshots and other unknown fields are rejected. Names are unique within a connector while the branch is not deleted. One JSON object, at most 16 KiB. Poll operation.workflow_id; acceptance is not completion.

202.description: Branch reservation and accepted workflow.

delete.description: Requires environments.update in the connector organization. Resolves connector_id and name server-side. One JSON object, at most 16 KiB. Poll operation.workflow_id; the branch in this response is the record read before erasure, not proof of deletion.

202.description: Branch record and accepted erasure workflow.

get.description: The CLI polls this endpoint for branch operations. SUCCESS means the workflow completed; ERROR, CANCELLED, and MAX_RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED are terminal failures. The getWorkflow handler in api/routes/workflows.go selects actor-identity checks or organization authorization through auth.CheckOrganizationPermissions; the latter uses the recorded authorization scope for organization-owned workflows. Missing and unauthorized workflows return 404. A client timeout does not cancel server work.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Progress stream offset. Continue from next_offset.

UserBearer.description: Authenticated user JWT used by the browser approval endpoint.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked authentication.

JSONError.description: Request rejected; inspect error and message.

TextError.description: Request rejected; the response body is plain text.

InternalError.description: Internal failure. Authentication middleware can return plain text even when the handler returns JSON.

WorkflowPending.description: The durable mutation is still running, not confirmed failed. Poll the Location URL before retrying. Authorization for polling remains subject to the workflow owner and scope.

ConnectorStatus.description: Registration workflow completion is not replication readiness. Deletion status can also be returned by this endpoint. halted means a source runtime component reported a standing halt; failure is then <component>:<classification>.

ProjectCreate.description: The handler trims both fields and requires non-empty values.

email.description: Parsed as a mail address; the address is lowercased.

role_display_name.description: Display label, not an authorization role enum. Send the desired scopes explicitly.

scopes.description: Every scope must be a valid organization scope held by the caller. Omitted or null scopes become an empty list.

environment_id.description: Optional. An omitted or empty value selects Ardent Cloud through server-side placement.

info.title: AI Requirements Intelligence API
info.description:
Agent-driven API for requirements discovery, clarification, feature definition,
and implementation planning. Supports the early phase of the software development
lifecycle — from raw project materials to structured tickets.

## Streaming

All agent-triggered endpoints (`/ingest`, `/generate`, `/rebuild`) return a
Server-Sent Events stream (`text/event-stream`). Each event is a JSON object
on a `data:` line. The stream closes when the agent emits a `result` or `error` event.

Example stream:
```
data: {"type":"status","message":"Starting ingestion"}
data: {"type":"progress","message":"Processing document 2 of 4","progress":50}
data: {"type":"result","data":{...}}
```

info.title: TryggHverdag API
info.description: The server that watches journeys home. Every route lives under /v1; a breaking change gets a new version rather than changing this one, because phones keep running old app versions (AR-08).

deviceCredential.description: The device’s own credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. The server keeps only its hash.

get.description: Returns 200 whenever the API is up. Read `status` in the body to tell whether the worker is still running, because an API with no worker raises no alerts.

status.description: ok when the worker has checked in recently; degraded when it has not, which means nothing is watching the journeys.

checkedAt.description: When the server answered, from the database clock (REL-01), as RFC 3339.

lastBeatAt.description: The worker’s last check-in, or null if it has never checked in.

silentForMs.description: How long the worker has been silent, or null if it has never checked in.

worker.description: What the API can see of the worker.

schema.description: Whether the safety system as a whole is working, not just this process.

post.description: Needs a device credential: the walker is the user whose device sends it. A walker can have only one unended journey, so a second start is refused with 409 and the ID of the journey already running.

responderIds.description: The users who should follow this journey. Each must be a member of the walker's group other than the walker; a repeated ID counts once. An empty list is accepted here and refused as NO_RESPONDER.

schema.description: A start request. The walker is the user whose device sends it; no field names one.

state.description: A journey starts ACTIVE.

startedAt.description: When the journey started, from the database clock (REL-01), as RFC 3339.

schema.description: The journey that started.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
The walker already has a journey that has not ended.
A responder named is the walker, or is not a member of the walker's group.
A journey needs at least one responder to start.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Answers only for the device user’s own journeys, and only from the device that started the journey. A 200, RECORDED or DUPLICATE, means the server has the event, so the phone may drop it. A 409 means the journey has ended: stop sending.

journeyId.description: The journey this heartbeat belongs to.

eventId.description: The heartbeat’s own ID, unique within its journey. Sent again, it changes nothing and is answered DUPLICATE (SM-08).

batteryLevel.description: The battery level from 0 to 1, or null when the phone does not know it.

accuracyMeters.description: The position’s accuracy in metres, 0 or more.

recordedAt.description: When the phone recorded the position, by the phone’s clock, as RFC 3339 with an offset, whose instant in UTC falls in the years 0001 to 9999. Within those years, any time is accepted, however far from the server’s clock: it labels the position and decides nothing (REL-01).

anyOf.description: Where the phone was, as the phone recorded it.

position.description: The position, or null when the phone has none (SM-03).

schema.description: A heartbeat. The walker is the user whose device sends it, and the device must be the one that started the journey; no field names either.

200.description: The server has the heartbeat, so the phone may drop it.

outcome.description: RECORDED when the heartbeat was stored now; DUPLICATE when its journey already had its event ID, so nothing changed.

schema.description: The server has the heartbeat, so the phone may drop it.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
Only the device that started this journey can send its heartbeats.
The walker has no journey with this ID.
The journey has ended, so the heartbeat was not stored. Stop sending them.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Ends the journey named in the path; only the device that started the journey may end it. The body is empty, or absent. A 200, ENDED, and a 409, JOURNEY_ENDED, both mean the journey is over: stop tracking it and drop anything queued for it.

schema.description: The journey to end.
Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.
The journey is over, so the phone may stop tracking it.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
Only the device that started this journey can end it.
The walker has no journey with this ID.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Says "I’m on it" for the alert named in the path; only a responder of the alert’s journey may acknowledge it. The body is empty, or absent. A 200, ACKNOWLEDGED, means the caller is the one on it, recorded now or already. A 409, ALREADY_ACKNOWLEDGED, means another responder is on it; a 409, ALERT_RESOLVED, means the alert is over.

schema.description: The alert to acknowledge.
Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.

outcome.description: The caller is the one on this alert.

schema.description: The caller is on it: recorded now, or already theirs.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
The caller follows no alert with this ID.
Another responder is already on this alert.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Closes the alert named in the path once the walker is known to be safe; only the responder on the alert may close it. The body is empty, or absent. A 200, CLOSED, means the alert is resolved and the journey has ended, and the other responders are told. A 403, NOT_THE_ACKNOWLEDGER, means the caller is not the one on it; a 409, ALERT_RESOLVED, means the alert is over.

schema.description: The alert to close.
Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.

outcome.description: The alert is closed, and its journey has ended.

schema.description: Closed now: the walker is safe, and the other responders are told.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
Only the responder on this alert can close it.
The caller follows no alert with this ID.

post.summary: Join the group with an invitation
post.description: Public: needs no device credential. Joins the group with an invitation code, or, while no group exists, as its first admin with the bootstrap code. The answer carries the device credential once, and is not cached. The same code sent again with the same join key, while the invitation has not expired and its member has not been removed, is the same join retried: the same member, and a new credential that replaces the first. A 404, INVITATION_NOT_VALID, is the one answer for every code that lets nobody in.

invitationCode.description: The invitation code as typed: 20 base32 characters, in any case, with spaces or hyphens between, O read as 0 and I or L as 1. The first admin types the bootstrap code here.

joinKey.description: A key the phone makes once, 32 random bytes as base64url, and sends again with a retried join, so a join whose answer was lost can be retried.

displayName.description: The name the person typed for themself: 1 to 40 characters once the spaces around it are trimmed; no control character; no bidirectional control or other format character but ZWNJ (U+200C) and ZWJ (U+200D); and at least one visible character.

schema.description: A join: the code, the phone’s join key, and the name the person typed.

credential.description: This phone’s device credential, shown once: keep it in secure storage, and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`.

userId.description: The member this phone is signed in as.

role.description: ADMIN for the one admin; MEMBER for everyone else.

schema.description: Joined: a member of the group, signed in on this phone.

message.default: The invitation is not valid. Ask the admin for a new one.

get.description: Needs the admin’s device credential. Lists every member: their ID, the name they typed and their role.

userId.description: The member.

displayName.description: The name the member typed when they joined.

role.description: ADMIN for the one admin; MEMBER for everyone else.

items.description: A member of the group.

schema.description: The members of the group.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
Only the admin can do this.

get.summary: Who this phone is signed in as
get.description: Needs a device credential. Answers the member the device belongs to: their ID, the name they typed and their role. A 401 means this phone is no longer signed in to the group.

200.description: The member this phone is signed in as.

userId.description: The member.

displayName.description: The name the member typed when they joined.

role.description: ADMIN for the one admin; MEMBER for everyone else.

schema.description: A member of the group.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
This device belongs to no member of the group.

post.description: Needs the admin’s device credential. Makes an invitation that brings one person in, once, within seven days. Only its hash is kept, so the code is shown once.

schema.description: Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.

invitationCode.description: The code, shown once: 20 base32 characters in four groups of five.

expiresAt.description: When it expires: seven days after it was made, by the database clock (REL-01), as RFC 3339.

schema.description: A new invitation: it brings one person in, once, before it expires.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
Only the admin can do this.

delete.summary: Remove a member from the group
delete.description: Needs the admin’s device credential. Removes the member at once, in one step: their phones are signed out, they are taken off every journey they follow that has not ended, and nothing more is sent to them. A journey of their own that has not ended runs to its end. A 404, MEMBER_NOT_FOUND, after a removal whose answer was lost means it is done.

schema.description: The member to remove.
Removed, all of it, now.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
Only the admin can do this.
The group has no member with this ID.

delete.summary: Remove a responder from a journey
delete.description: Needs the walker’s device credential. Removes the responder named in the path from the walker’s journey named in the path: anything not yet sent to them about it is withdrawn, an alert they were on goes back to unacknowledged, and when none is left the walker is warned. A 409, NOT_A_RESPONDER, after a removal whose answer was lost means it is done.

schema.description: The walker’s journey.
The responder to remove from it.
Removed: they follow the journey no more, and nothing more is sent to them about it.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
The walker has no journey with this ID.
The user named is not a responder of this journey.

get.summary: The caller's tournament bonus picks and lock state
get.description: Returns the authenticated user's seven-category tournament bonus picks plus the server-authoritative lock state. `lock_at` is the configured `BONUS_LOCK_AT` (RFC3339); `locked` is true once `now >= lock_at`. Each pick's `ref_type` is `team` (winner/runner_up/fair_play) or `player` (golden_ball/golden_boot/golden_glove/young_player); `label` is the resolved team/player name; `points` is present only once scored. Categories with no pick are omitted.

200.description: The caller's picks and lock state

put.summary: Upsert the caller's tournament bonus picks
put.description: Upserts any subset of the seven bonus picks. Each `ref_id` is validated against the correct table for the category's ref-type (team vs player). The server is authoritative for the bonus lock and rejects all writes once `now >= BONUS_LOCK_AT`. Returns the same shape as `GET /api/bonus`.

400.description: Bad request (invalid category, missing/wrong-type ref, or invalid JSON body)

403.description: Bonus predictions are locked (now >= BONUS_LOCK_AT)

get.description: Returns all seven award categories in canonical order (winner, runner_up, golden_ball, golden_boot, golden_glove, young_player, fair_play) so the admin Bonus Outcomes screen renders every row, set or not. Each row carries the category's points, its ref_type (team or player), and — for a set category — the stored `ref_id` plus its resolved `label`. Unset categories return `ref_id: 0`, `label: ""`, `set: false`; a stale ref resolves to an empty label. A standard admin route (`RequireAdmin`) registered in all environments.

200.description: All seven categories with their current outcomes

403.description: Not an admin

put.description: Upserts one or more bonus-award outcomes (the actual winner, golden ball, etc.), each validated like a pick (known category, `ref_id` exists in the correct table). A standard admin route (`RequireAdmin`) registered in all environments. After the validate-all-then-upsert, the handler immediately materializes `bonus_predictions.points` from the new outcomes (idempotent recompute, never increment), so the overall leaderboard reflects the winners at once. Outcomes are persisted before scoring: a scoring failure returns 500 but never loses the saved outcomes (re-run via `POST /api/admin/recompute`). The response is `{ saved }` only.

info.title: PACT — Programmable Agent Commerce Trust
info.summary: Contract-aware, fulfillment-gated PayPal settlement for agent-to-agent commerce.
info.description:
A buyer agent and a seller agent negotiate; PACT compiles a hashed contract, checks a deterministic spending policy, places a PayPal authorization, verifies the delivery and captures only if the contract is satisfied.

Rules that hold for every endpoint:

- The browser never supplies an amount, a status, a seller or a contract. Amounts come from the signed contract on the server.
- Identity is an anonymous session in a signed, http-only cookie. Only the session that created a deal may change it; showcase deals are read-only.
- State-changing requests must be same-origin and, where they have a body, JSON.
- Money is integer minor units (US cents). Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC.
- Every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and an `x-request-id`.
- PACT runs against PayPal Sandbox only. Without credentials a simulator stands in and every payment is labelled `simulated`.

tags.name: Deals
tags.description: Create a deal, drive it one step at a time, decide at human gates.

tags.name: Operations
tags.description: The operations ledger and reconciliation against the payment provider.

tags.name: Policy
tags.description: The deterministic spending policy of a session.

tags.name: PayPal
tags.description: Redirect targets and webhooks called by PayPal.

tags.name: Simulator
tags.description: Stand-in for PayPal's approval page when no credentials are configured.

post.summary: Create a deal from a request in words
post.description: Derives the mandate, matches a seller agent and starts the negotiation. A request whose budget is stated only in a currency other than US dollars is refused (400): PACT settles in USD and does not guess a conversion. Creates the anonymous session if there is none. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 8 per session per 10 minutes, 40 per network address per hour.

get.description: Newest first. An empty list without a session; never creates one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Deal id.

get.description: Readable by anyone holding the id (ids are unguessable; showcase deals are public). The buyer's private mandate is included only for the owning session.

200.description: The deal as the caller may see it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Deal id.

post.summary: Execute at most one automatic step
post.description: Owner only. The deal's stored status decides which step runs; the caller cannot choose it. Runs under a per-deal lease: a concurrent call answers 200 with `busy: true`. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

schema.description: An empty JSON object.

200.description: The deal after the step, or unchanged when nothing ran.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Deal id.

post.summary: Record a human decision at a gate
post.description: Owner only. The decision must be one the deal's current gate offers (`next.options`), otherwise 409. The body never carries an amount or a status; a release still has to pass the settlement guard before any money moves. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Deal id.

get.description: Seller-supplied content, served as an attachment under a sandboxing content security policy with MIME sniffing off.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Deal id.

post.summary: Compare PACT's ledger with the provider's record of the deal
post.description: Re-reads the order and authorization from the payment provider and compares them field by field with PACT's ledger. The verdict is deterministic. With PayPal Sandbox and AI enabled, a read-only auditor agent (PayPal Agent Toolkit, `get_order` only) adds a short statement; if it fails, the facts are returned alone. Changes no payment and no status. Anyone who can read the deal may call it; only the owner's call is written to the audit trail (`payment.reconciled`). State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 12 per session (or network address) per 10 minutes and, for callers with a session, 36 per network address per 10 minutes. The agent's statement is additionally budgeted for the whole deployment (120 per hour); beyond it the facts are returned alone.

schema.description: An empty JSON object.

200.description: The comparison. A provider failure is reported as `status: unavailable`, not as an error.

get.description: The calling session's deals plus the seeded showcase deals (newest first, at most 300), their payment events, verification checks and totals. Without a session only the showcase is returned. Read-only.
The default policy until one is saved. Never creates a session.

200.description: The policy and today's committed spend.

put.description: Applies to this session only and only to what happens next: a signed contract keeps the thresholds it was signed with. Creates the session if there is none. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 30 per session per 10 minutes, 120 per network address per hour.

get.description: Whether the session's wallet and the shared demo wallet are connected, and how the next in-policy deal will be approved. Never creates a session.

delete.description: Scope `session` forgets the caller's wallet (a no-op without a session). Scope `demo` forgets the shared wallet and requires the operator token. Existing authorizations are unaffected. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

parameters.name: x-admin-token
parameters.description: Operator token. Required for scope `demo`.

post.description: Asks the provider for a vault setup token, stores it server-side as a pending connection and returns where the payer gives consent. Creates the session if there is none. Scope `demo` requires the operator token and binds the connection to the calling session. A connected wallet must be disconnected before another is connected (409). State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 10 per session per 10 minutes and 30 per network address per hour; 20 attempts on scope `demo` per network address per 10 minutes.

parameters.name: x-admin-token
parameters.description: Operator token. Required for scope `demo`.

get.summary: What is configured in this deployment
get.description: Reports that integrations are configured, never their values. Answers 200 even when the database is unreachable; the affected components are then listed under `degraded`.

post.description: Called by PayPal, cross-origin and without a session. The signature is verified over the exact bytes of the body; an event that does not verify changes nothing. Verified events are de-duplicated on PayPal's event id and may only confirm or advance a payment along its state machine.

schema.description: A PayPal webhook event, at most 256 KiB.

200.description: Verified and applied, or needing no action.

400.description: Not verified, not a usable event, or too large. Empty body.

503.description: The deal is in the middle of a step; PayPal redelivers. Empty body.

get.summary: Return from the PayPal approval page
get.description: Browser redirect target. Nothing in the URL is trusted: the order authorized is the one stored for the deal, re-read from PayPal (status, amount, contract hash) before authorizing.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: PayPal's order id. Must equal the deal's stored order id.

Location.description: `/deals/{id}?paypal=approved|pending|error`, or `/workspace?paypal=error` for a malformed deal id.

get.summary: Return from a cancelled PayPal approval
get.description: Browser redirect target. Changes nothing: the deal keeps waiting for payment until its owner cancels it.

Browser redirect target. Exchanges the setup token stored for the pending connection — never a token from the URL — for the vault token and marks the wallet connected. For scope `demo` the returning browser must be the operator session that started the connection.

post.summary: Approve a simulated order as the payer
post.description: The simulated payer approves; PACT then authorizes exactly as after a real PayPal return. Exists only while the simulator stands in for PayPal: with PayPal Sandbox credentials configured it answers 404. Owner only. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

post.summary: Cancel a simulated order as the payer
post.description: The simulator voids the order and the deal is cancelled with it, recorded as the owner's decision. Exists only while the simulator stands in for PayPal: with PayPal Sandbox credentials configured it answers 404. Owner only. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

get.description: For a scheduler, not for browsers. Runs the next automatic step of deals that hold money (authorized, revision required, submitted, verified, rejecting) and have not changed for two minutes: verification and capture, or the release of a rejected delivery's hold, do not depend on the payer's browser staying open. One step per deal, a few deals per call, through the same lease and idempotency keys as `POST /api/deals/{id}/advance`. Never touches a deal before authorization or at a human gate.

examined.description: Stalled deals found for this run.

advanced.description: The deals a step was attempted for.

executed.description: The step that ran to completion, or null when it stalled (the deal's `lastError` says why).

get.summary: Whether the dashboard agents can run here
get.description: Reports whether the Operations dashboard's AI agents are available on this deployment and which models they may use. Starts no session and calls no model.

message.description: One sentence for the visitor when `available` is false.

post.summary: Model proxy for the dashboard agents
post.description: Accepts an OpenAI Responses-format request from the Operations dashboard, rebuilds it from an allow-list of fields and forwards it to the AI Gateway with PACT's own credentials. Only the allowed models are ever called, output is capped, and the caller is rate-limited per session and per network address. The provider's answer (JSON, or a server-sent event stream when `stream` is true) is passed straight back. May start a session.

schema.description: An OpenAI Responses-format request. Fields outside the allow-list are dropped.

session.name: pact_sid
session.description: Anonymous session: `<id>.<HMAC-SHA256>`; http-only, SameSite=Lax. Set by the endpoints that may start a session.

adminToken.name: x-admin-token
adminToken.description: Operator token for the shared demo wallet. Compared in constant time; rejected when none is configured.

cronSecret.description: The deployment's CRON_SECRET, sent by the scheduler as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` (what Vercel Cron does). Compared in constant time; the endpoint answers 404 while no secret is configured.

InvalidRequest.description: The request is malformed: not JSON, too large, or failing validation (`invalid_request`).

Forbidden.description: Cross-site request, missing session, not the deal's owner, or missing operator token (`forbidden`).

Conflict.description: The action is not possible in the current state (`conflict`).

RateLimited.description: Too many requests (`rate_limited`); `details.resetAt` says when the window ends and `Retry-After` how many seconds that is from now.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate-limit window reopens.

PaymentError.description: The payment provider could not complete the step (`payment_error`); `details` carries the provider's issue code and debug id.

Internal.description: Unexpected failure (`internal`). Details are logged under the request id, never returned.

Unavailable.description: A dependency this request needs is switched off or did not answer (`unavailable`).

Minor.description: Money in integer minor units (US cents). Never a float.

Category.description: Kind of work. `other` has no seller; `restricted` is always blocked by policy.

DealStatus.description: Deal lifecycle state. Transitions are table-driven; the last eight values are terminal.

PaymentStatus.description: Payment lifecycle state: none → created → approved → authorized → captured | voided | expired | failed.

ProviderKind.description: `simulated` is the labelled stand-in used only when no PayPal Sandbox credentials are configured.

ApprovalMode.description: How the payer consented: in PayPal for this order, or once through a delegated (vaulted) agent wallet.

StepKind.description: An automatic step of the engine. One call to /advance executes at most one.

Mandate.description: The buyer's private instruction derived from the request. Only returned to the session that owns the deal.

GuardrailNote.description: A correction the deterministic rules engine made to an agent's proposal.

Contract.description: The immutable contract compiled from the agreed terms.

termsHash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `contract`. Written to the PayPal order as custom_id `pact:v1:<hash>`.

Policy.description: Deterministic spending policy. autonomousLimitMinor ≤ maxTransactionMinor and humanReviewMinConfidence ≤ autoCaptureMinConfidence.

aspectRatio.description: Aspect ratio the seller claims; the verifier recomputes it.

degraded.description: True when the AI evaluator was unavailable and AI rules were marked uncertain.

hash.description: sha256(prevHash + canonical JSON of the event).

AuditEvent.description: One entry of the hash-chained audit trail.

demoFault.description: Set only for sellers with a controlled demo fault.

approveUrl.description: Where the payer approves the order. A path for the simulator.

PaymentRecord.description: The deal's payment as PACT records it. All ids are the provider's. Never contains a vault id.

NextStep.description: What happens next: an automatic step, a human gate, or nothing.

isOwner.description: True when the calling session created this deal and may act on it.

contract.description: The hashed contract plus the live payment state (the state is not part of the hash).

auditChainValid.description: Result of re-verifying the audit hash chain on read.

intent.description: The request in plain words, 10–600 characters after cleaning. May be empty when scenarioId is given.

scenarioId.description: Optional demo scenario: pre-fills the request and pins the seller agent — as long as the request still asks for the kind of work that seller offers; otherwise the request is matched like a free-form one.

tzOffsetMinutes.description: The browser's Date#getTimezoneOffset(), so "tomorrow at 6 PM" resolves in local time.

CreateDealRequest.description: No amount, status, seller or contract can be supplied: they are derived on the server.

busy.description: True when another request holds the step lease; poll again.

percent.description: Required for release_partial: percentage of the contract price to capture.

origin.description: `mine` = created by the calling session, `showcase` = seeded reference deals.

heldMinor.description: Authorized and neither captured nor released.

hoursToDeadline.description: One decimal; negative once the deadline has passed.

day.description: UTC day the deal was created.

OpsRow.description: One row of the operations ledger.

type.description: The audit event type without its `payment.` prefix.

amountMinor.description: The amount the event itself states; 0 when it states none.

reference.description: The most specific provider id the event is about.

releasedMinor.description: Voided or expired authorizations plus the uncaptured remainder of partial captures.

pendingHumanReview.description: Deals waiting for a spend approval or a delivery review.

verificationFailureRate.description: Share of first deliveries that were not capture-eligible. 0 when nothing was verified.

firstPassRate.description: Share of first deliveries that were capture-eligible. 0 when nothing was verified.

webhooks.description: A webhook id for signature verification is configured.

delegatedWallet.description: The shared demo wallet is connected, so in-policy deals authorize without a PayPal login.

degraded.description: Present only when a component could not be checked or is misconfigured.

SystemStatus.description: What is configured, never the values.

WalletScope.description: `session` = the caller's own wallet; `demo` = the shared wallet of the public demo (operator only).

WalletStatus.description: Delegated agent wallet status. The vault id is never part of any response.

approveUrl.description: Absolute URL where the payer gives consent.

field.description: e.g. "Order status", "Authorized amount", "Contract binding (custom_id)".

pact.description: PACT's ledger value. For statuses it includes what PACT expects the provider to report.

status.description: Computed deterministically from `facts`. `unavailable`: there was nothing to compare or the provider could not be read.

narrative.description: Plain-language statement by the read-only auditor agent. Null when the agent did not run.

toolCalls.description: PayPal Agent Toolkit tools the agent called, in order. Only `get_order` is ever available to it.

details.description: Present for some errors: validation issues, `{ resetAt }` for rate limits, `{ issue, debugId, retryable }` for payment errors.

ApiErrorBody.description: Every error response has this shape. Internal details are logged with the request id, never returned.

Ack.title: Ack
Ack.description:
What an action changed. The page shows the result where it was taken; `message` is set
only for what it cannot show (DESIGN.md, acknowledgement): a thumb that gives or takes back
the owner's word on a Focus topic, and a reported miss.

Acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement
Acknowledgement.description:
Items of Needs you, each as shown: stopped steps, full-text passes, failed digests (by
id) and Deep cards with process notes. The owner's Acknowledge names them; the answer names
those it marked.

AmongRow.title: AmongRow
AmongRow.description:
A paper a Deep card places this one among: one of the collection's, by its arXiv id, with
how the two relate and its rarity now (null outside the collection).

Answer.title: Answer
Answer.description:
One paper's answers. Fit for the topic it was drawn or taken for (central, related,
adjacent, none or unsure) is required on the first answer; an edit after it may leave it
out, and the recorded answer stands. A Fit sent is a label; one left out writes none, so
editing the appraisal alone recreates no label the owner has since taken back.

Awaiting.title: Awaiting
Awaiting.description:
What every action on a paper awaiting classification names: the paper revision the
owner saw on Quality. The action applies only to that text.

Badge.title: Badge
Badge.description:
A followed topic as a badge shows it: its class's slug and name, its depth (the badge's
shape), monogram and colour.

Brief.title: Brief
Brief.description:
The paper's Brief: its current revision's, or the newest from an older revision
(`revision` says which) until the current one is written. `overstatement`, when the full
text does not support the abstract, opens it.

CardPass.title: CardPass
CardPass.description:
The paper's Deep card in the full-text queue: the owner's request or automatic (a Focus
must read, or an Area pick), and where it is (awaiting the paper's text, ready, being
written, or failed this run and to be tried again; `failed_runs` says how often).

CardSeen.title: CardSeen
CardSeen.description:
A Deep card's process notes as Needs you showed them: the paper, and when its card was
written, which names the card.

Changes.title: Changes
Changes.description: A page of the changes feed, and the position to read on from.

CitedIn.title: CitedIn
CitedIn.description: A paper outside the collection, as a search hit gives it: enough for an arXiv entry.

Classification.title: Classification
Classification.description:
The newest classification and the current memberships, classes of the current tree only
(a retired class leads nowhere).

Contribution.title: Contribution
Contribution.description: What kind of contribution a paper makes. Facts, not scores.

CurrentVerdict.title: CurrentVerdict
CurrentVerdict.description:
A topic's current verdict: the Fit that stands, each grader's answer by role, and the
paper revision it was made from. `one_lab`: one Focus grader refused throughout and the
other's Fit stands.

Day.title: Day
Day.description:
A day's daily digests in the fixed topic order. `released` is false on a day arXiv listed
nothing; `previous` and `next` are the nearest days with digests; on a Monday, `weekly` is
the Monday of the week whose weekly digests came out that day. `run` is today's nightly run,
on today only (in the schedule's zone) and only while the schedule is on.

DeepCard.title: DeepCard
DeepCard.description:
A Deep card: the reading card the deep service wrote, as it wrote it, and what it was
written from (the paper revision and arXiv version, null where unknown, and the text's
source). `among` is its "among the collection" section as rows.

Depth.title: Depth
Depth.description: How closely the owner follows a topic: the research question, the area, the wider field.

Digest.title: Digest
Digest.description:
A digest in full: its text, which marks each paper it names as [the name](its arXiv
id), and every paper by role; why it failed, when it did. `job` is its newest job writing it
again, on /api (Write again; DESIGN.md, Jobs).

DigestCard.title: DigestCard
DigestCard.description:
A digest at Gist level (a Day or a Week): its Gist and up to three of its papers (its
picks, else its central papers); `more` are the rest.

DigestCounts.title: DigestCounts
DigestCounts.description:
What a digest's Mark counts: the papers it covered, its picks, and of them those central,
related, and graded must read; apart from them, its updated papers.

DigestMark.title: DigestMark
DigestMark.description: A digest at Mark level (History): its topic, how many papers, its best rarity.

DigestPaper.title: DigestPaper
DigestPaper.description:
A paper as a digest showed it, frozen then; `set_aside` and `withdrawn_at` are live: the
owner has since set it below relevant where it was graded, arXiv has since withdrawn it. An
updated paper has the arXiv `version` it came back with; its `announced` is when it first
came out.

DigestRole.title: DigestRole
DigestRole.description: How a digest shows one of its papers.

DigestState.title: DigestState
DigestState.description:
A digest is published once written, or once it says "Nothing new"; a failed one is
written again by the next run, over the papers due then.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: A fact written to the outbox in the same transaction as the data it describes.

Facets.title: Facets
Facets.description: Facts about the paper, never combined into anything.

Failing.title: Failing
Failing.description: The event an integration is stuck on; its later events wait behind it.

Fit.title: Fit
Fit.description: How close a paper is to one topic, most inclusive first.

Grade.title: Grade
Grade.description: A paper's standing on one topic, from its Fit there and its Weight, most inclusive first.

GradeCounts.title: GradeCounts
GradeCounts.description: Papers per grade on a topic's page; `ungraded` have none there.

GradedBadge.title: GradedBadge
GradedBadge.description:
A badge on a paper, one per followed topic whose page holds it: the grade and rarity
that page shows (`core.page_standing`); grade null where neither the topic nor a followed
descendant graded it, the rarity then its Weight's floor.

GradedOut.title: GradedOut
GradedOut.description: What grading now found: the Fit that stands, or why there is no verdict.

Grader.title: Grader
Grader.description:
One grader's answer in the verdict: its role, and its Fit, or for `area_check` whether
the judge's Fit holds.

Hand.title: Hand
Hand.description: The owner's newest use of the Save toggle.

History.title: History
History.description:
Days from `until` back to `since`, newest first, and the weeks they touch; `start` is the
day of the oldest digest, where History stops.

HistoryItem.title: HistoryItem
HistoryItem.description:
Something said about the paper, oldest first: every verdict (`value` its Fit), the
owner's label (its value) and thumb (its value and reason) as they stand, misses, and each
classification (`topic` is its primary class). `followed`: the topic is followed now.

Job.title: Job
Job.description:
One row of the Jobs page (DESIGN.md, Jobs): a job (`id`), or a Deep card the owner asked
for (`pass_id`), read from its pass with the pass's state as a job's (awaiting text or ready
is queued). `papers` and `done` say how far it got (a re-run's `graded` how many it graded);
`cost` is what its runs spent so far, None before any and for a card, which runs on the
subscription. `at` is when it last changed state. A re-run has its topic, `scopes`, the
`estimate` it was offered with and its `ceiling`, a replay its estimate and ceiling;
stopped by the ceiling, `error` says where. A digest written again has its `digest` and
topic.
`actions` are those its state allows: Run now, With tonight's run and Discard while it is
not run; Try again once it failed, for a card only once it waits for the owner (a card that
failed fewer runs is tried again by the next nightly run).

JobDigest.title: JobDigest
JobDigest.description: The digest a job writes again.

JobRef.title: JobRef
JobRef.description: A job as the thing it works on names it: where it stands, and why it failed or stopped.

JobRun.title: JobRun
JobRun.description:
Run now or With tonight's run: a re-run's new ceiling in USD, which a stopped one needs
above what it spent.

JobTopic.title: JobTopic
JobTopic.description: A re-run's topic, and the revision of it the re-run was offered for.

Jobs.title: Jobs
Jobs.description: The Jobs page's four groups: Not run, Running and queued, Failed, and the newest Done.

LabelValue.title: LabelValue
LabelValue.description: A label's answer: a Fit (`core.grading.Fit`), or unsure.

MissTrace.title: MissTrace
MissTrace.description:
What each stage concluded for the owner's topic when the reported paper went through the
pipeline (feedback.md, misses), on the paper's current text. `classified`: classification
has run; then `probability` is the classifier's for the topic's class against the class's
`threshold`, and `classifier`, `uncertain` and `keyword` say which way in admitted it;
`below` says the classifier admitted it to a class under the topic's only, not to the
topic's own class.
`graded`: a verdict exists; then `fit` is the Fit that stands by the rule of the depth it
was graded at (core.grading), and `graders` the answers it stands on, in the order the
topic's current depth asks its graders (the roles a verdict from another depth holds
after). The page reads where the paper was let go from `fit`, not from the graders.

OpenState.title: OpenState
OpenState.description:
What waits on the owner for this paper, as Needs you lists it, with the paper revision
the action endpoints take: `awaiting_classification` (dismiss, classify by hand, fix the
text), `analysis_stopped` (try again), a topic's `split`, `escalated`, `one_lab` (label it)
or `ungraded` (grade it now), and a full-text pass (`pass_id`) `fulltext_failed`, a Deep
card's `card_failed`, or either `awaiting_text` over a week (run it now). `refused`: every
model refused, rather than the last error.

Opinion.title: Opinion
Opinion.description:
One grader's answer: a Fit with one sentence why, or, from `area_check`, whether the
judge's Fit holds and the probability that it does.

OutsideRow.title: OutsideRow
OutsideRow.description: A paper a search provider found that the collection lacks.

Paper.title: Paper
Paper.description:
A paper's page: its header, its ladder (Gist, Brief or abstract, deep card, the paper)
and the rail, its open states and its history. Outside the collection (never classified)
it has no rarity; an archive paper litwatch has not fetched is not `stored` either, and has
only the archive's metadata.

PaperClass.title: PaperClass
PaperClass.description:
A class the paper has a membership of, by source. `member`: one stands that puts the
paper in the class (the uncertain band and the keyword check are for grading only). `path`
is its classes' names from the top down to it.

sort.description: Omitted: `best` (search rank) while `q` is given, else `rarest`.

PaperQuery.title: PaperQuery
PaperQuery.description:
Papers' filters: also the pages of one or more topics (each with its subtree), or of
every topic at a depth, and one band of a search.

PaperTopic.title: PaperTopic
PaperTopic.description:
A followed topic the paper is in, graded for, or has the owner's word or a thumb on: its
own effective Fit, how its page shows the paper (grade, rarity, `via`: as the topic page),
its current verdict, the owner's word that stands (from the label, a thumb or a miss), the
label and thumb themselves, and its open state.

Papers.title: Papers
Papers.description:
A page of Papers, the whole filter's total, and the papers per rarity under every filter
but the levels. A search also brings what search providers found that the collection lacks,
as a band of its own on the first page; a provider that failed or was too slow is named in
`left_out`.

PassSeen.title: PassSeen
PassSeen.description:
A full-text pass as Needs you showed it, and since when it waited, which names this
failure.

ProcessJob.title: ProcessJob
ProcessJob.description:
A paper's Process job (DESIGN.md, the paper page): its button reads "Processing" while
the job is queued or running. `again`: failed, and Process would put it back in the queue,
since no step of its paper waits on the owner (then the owner's action there settles it).

Publication.title: Publication
Publication.description: The published record of a paper: what a BibTeX entry needs, as DBLP has it.

PublicationIn.title: PublicationIn
PublicationIn.description: The owner's correction: a DBLP key, a DOI, or that there is no published version.

Rarity.title: Rarity
Rarity.description: What a paper's colour shows, low to high.

RarityCounts.title: RarityCounts
RarityCounts.description: Papers per rarity level; `unrated` have none yet (not classified).

ReactionReason.title: ReactionReason
ReactionReason.description:
What a thumb says went wrong or right, each pointing at the stage that would have made the
mistake (feedback.md, reactions).

ReplayIn.title: ReplayIn
ReplayIn.description: Run replay under a ceiling, in USD; a stopped replay goes on only above what it spent.

ReplayOffer.title: ReplayOffer
ReplayOffer.description:
Overview's Run replay (DESIGN.md, Overview): what Run would do. `running`: a replay
queued or running already, which Run only answers with. Else `continues`, a replay its
ceiling stopped that Run goes on with, having spent `spent`; else a new replay of every
cohort's labels. `labels` counts its labels by cohort, `papers` and `pairs` what is left to
classify and to grade (paper and topic), `left_out` the labelled papers the database lacks;
`estimate` what is left would cost, `unpriced` the models (`role: model`) with no price
bound, whose calls a replay does not send, and `ceiling` the one offered, in USD.

RerunIn.title: RerunIn
RerunIn.description:
A re-run to start (`run`) or to keep under Not run: its topic, its scopes (the date
range's days in the schedule's zone, both included) and its ceiling in USD.

RerunOffer.title: RerunOffer
RerunOffer.description:
The re-run offer after a topic edit (DESIGN.md, the re-run offer): each scope with its
paper count and estimate; `papers` and `estimate` for the scopes chosen, a paper in two of
them counted once. `missing` are the roles with no calls to estimate by; `unpriced` the
models (`role: model`) with no price bound, whose calls a re-run does not send. `ceiling`
is the one offered, in USD.

RerunScopeRow.title: RerunScopeRow
RerunScopeRow.description:
One scope of the re-run offer: its papers and what grading them is estimated to cost
(None when a role has no calls to estimate by).

Row.title: Row
Row.description:
One paper in a list. `rarity` is the list's: the mixed list's on Papers, the topic page's
on a topic. No Gist, Weight or facets until analysis succeeds; no rarity until classified.

RunStatus.title: RunStatus
RunStatus.description:
The latest nightly run: none yet, running, failed, or finished without an error, with
papers waiting for the owner (`attention`) or not (`quiet`).

ScheduleOut.title: ScheduleOut
ScheduleOut.description:
The schedule as the Runs page shows it: whether it is on, the zone the cron times are
read in, and when each job next fires (or would, if it were on).

SearchScope.title: SearchScope
SearchScope.description:
What the search box reaches beyond the collection: the papers the archive's search index
holds, None without an archive or when it does not answer in time.

SearchStats.title: SearchStats
SearchStats.description: How a search provider has answered since the service started.

SettingsHints.title: SettingsHints
SettingsHints.description:
What the Settings sidebar says beside each page: how many things wait on the owner, the
last Calibrate session, the misses reported, the topics followed and the classes, the
month's spend against its budget (the budgeted providers' spend, or every provider's when
none has a budget), and the integrations failing.

SetupFailing.title: SetupFailing
SetupFailing.description: The integration's setup is failing: no event is handed to it until it succeeds.

Status.title: Status
Status.description: Whether a topic is in use.

StepSeen.title: StepSeen
StepSeen.description:
A stopped step as Needs you showed it: the paper, its revision then, a grading's topic,
and when it last failed, which names this failure.

StripDigest.title: StripDigest
StripDigest.description:
One square of a topic's digest strip: a digest, coloured by its best rarity (none for
nothing new), red when it failed.

Summary.title: Summary
Summary.description:
What the shell shows on every page (the status line, the sidebar's topics, the Settings
hints), read by one poll and never through a page's own reads: counts only.

Taxonomy.title: Taxonomy
Taxonomy.description:
The tree, parents before children and siblings in the owner's order, and the followed
topics in the owner's order. Construction fails with every problem found.

TaxonomyClass.title: TaxonomyClass
TaxonomyClass.description: One node of the tree. `parent` is the parent's slug, None at the top.

TaxonomyStats.title: TaxonomyStats
TaxonomyStats.description:
What the Taxonomy and Topics pages show beside the tree: papers standing in each class or
under it, the threshold each class is admitted at (its own, or the configured default for
its depth), and the current revision of each followed topic.

TextPass.title: TextPass
TextPass.description:
The full-text pass queued last for the paper's current text: a Brief (Focus) or a Weight
re-check with a Brief (Area pick candidate), and where it is. A paper without one shows its
abstract in the Brief's place.

TodayRun.title: TodayRun
TodayRun.description:
Where today's nightly run stands: `waiting` until it is due, `late` once it is overdue
and has not started, `running` (`overrun` past the night's deadline) with the papers read
of `total`, `failed` with its error, or `done`. `due` and `deadline` are tonight's.

Topic.title: Topic
Topic.description:
A class the owner follows, keyed by the class's slug (`class` in YAML and JSON). The
graders read its subject (the Fit definition) and, for a Focus topic, its rubric (what each
Fit level means for it).

TopicCard.title: TopicCard
TopicCard.description:
A topic on the Topics tab: its page's papers, how many are saved, how many at each of
the page's rarity levels, and its newest must read.

TopicPage.title: TopicPage
TopicPage.description:
A page of a topic's papers, its total, and the papers per rarity and per grade under
every filter but the levels.

TopicRow.title: TopicRow
TopicRow.description:
A paper on a topic's page: the topic's own grade, else the highest of the followed topics
under it (`via`), else none (ungraded there, coloured by its Weight).

Week.title: Week
Week.description: A week's weekly digests in the fixed topic order, keyed by its Monday.

Weight.title: Weight
Weight.description: How much a paper matters in its own area, whatever topic it is graded for.

Withdrawn.title: Withdrawn
Withdrawn.description:
arXiv withdrew the paper: its newest version is a withdrawal, submitted `at`; `reason` is
the comments arXiv gives with it, when known. litwatch no longer processes it.

info.title: EHPS API
info.description: Equipment Health & Performance System — semiconductor fab equipment maintenance. Covers fab-coordinator machine/technician management, routine checkups, alert escalation and approval, repair assignment/completion, and the equipment health dashboard. All endpoints (except /api/auth/**) require a bearer JWT obtained from POST /api/auth/login, and are scoped by role: FAB_COORDINATOR, MANAGER, or TECHNICIAN. See docs/API-CONTRACT.md for the full endpoint contract.

info.title: Zato Pub/Sub REST API
info.description:
REST API for Zato's publish/subscribe messaging system.
All operations require HTTP Basic Authentication.

post.summary: Publish a message to a topic
post.description:
Publish a message to the specified topic. The user must have publish permissions for the topic.
Topic names are validated and must meet specific requirements.
A request with a msg_id that is already stored with the same content returns the stored message
without storing it again, which makes a repeated request idempotent. A msg_id that is stored with
different content is rejected with 409.

parameters.name: topic_name
parameters.description: Name of the topic to publish to

data.description: The message content

priority.description: Message priority (0=lowest, 9=highest)

in_reply_to.description: ID of message this is replying to

pub_time.description: Custom publication time (ISO format with timezone)

msg_id.description:
Message ID supplied by the client. A new ID is generated if this element is absent.
The msg_id is deduplicated for as long as its message is retained, which ends when the message
expires or when the retention of fully delivered messages removes it.

idempotent_message.summary: Message with a message ID supplied by the client

400.description: Bad request (invalid topic name, missing data, invalid msg_id, malformed JSON)

schema.description: HTML error page for malformed requests
HTML error page for malformed requests

409.description: The msg_id is already stored with different content

schema.description: HTML error page for malformed requests

post.description:
Subscribe to receive messages from the specified topic. The user must have subscribe permissions for the topic.
Topics are automatically created if they don't exist.

parameters.name: topic_name
parameters.description: Name of the topic to subscribe to

schema.description: HTML error page for malformed requests
HTML error page for malformed requests

schema.description: HTML error page for malformed requests

post.description:
Get messages from all topics the user is subscribed to. Messages are delivered in priority order
(highest priority first), then by publish time (oldest first) within the same priority level.
Retrieved messages are reserved for this client and remain in the queue until the client acknowledges them
through /pubsub/messages/ack. A message that is not acknowledged within the reservation period, 30 seconds
by default, is retrieved again by the next call.

max_messages.description: Maximum number of messages to retrieve

max_len.description: Maximum total length of message data in bytes

400.description: Bad request (malformed JSON, no subscription found for user)

schema.description: HTML error page for malformed requests
HTML error page for malformed requests

500.description: Internal server error

schema.description: HTML error page for malformed requests

post.description:
Removes messages retrieved through /pubsub/messages/get from the queue of the user.

A request with msg_ids removes the messages that are still in the queue. Messages that were already
acknowledged, or that are no longer in the queue, are not counted.

A request with consumed names the delivery_attempt with which each message was retrieved, and it may
publish messages in the same transaction through publish. The acknowledgement and the publications are
committed together or not at all. A message retrieved again after its reservation expired has a higher
delivery_attempt, and an acknowledgement of the earlier attempt is rejected with 409, with nothing published.
A repeated request that was already committed returns 200 with the same msg_id values in published.

msg_ids.description: The msg_id values of the messages to acknowledge

consumed.description: The messages to acknowledge, each with the delivery_attempt with which it was retrieved

publish.description: Messages published in the same transaction as the acknowledgement, permitted only with consumed

with_publications.summary: One message acknowledged together with two publications

400.description:
Bad request (neither or both of msg_ids and consumed, publish without consumed, a list that is not a list
or has more than 1000 elements, an invalid msg_id or delivery_attempt, or a publication that is invalid
or names a topic not stored in the pub/sub database)

401.description: Authentication failed, no subscription found for user, or no permission to publish to a topic

403.description: A topic of a publication is inactive

409.description:
The acknowledgement names an attempt that is no longer current, the message was concluded with other
publications, or the msg_id of a publication is already stored with different content

500.description: Internal server error

info.description:
# Overview 

 Information and statistics about FIRST Robotics Competition teams and events. 

# Authentication 

All endpoints require an Auth Key to be passed in the header `X-TBA-Auth-Key`. If you do not have an auth key yet, you can obtain one from your [Account Page](/account).
info.title: The Blue Alliance API v3
info.x-version-info: Versions of the API follow the format X.Y.Z, with X being a major version, Y denoting the minor version, and Z the point release. Changes to the spec or API that result in a major version change will significantly impact implementations. Changes to the minor version indicate paths and/or fields in existing models may be added, and any breaking changes will be confined to paths or models listed as in-development in the prior minor version. Changes to the point release indicate no format or structure changes to the paths or models, but updated or clarified documentation. Note that changes to paths and models refer to the actual result from the API, not the documentation.
info.x-changes: 3.12.0: Add 2026 score breakdowns. 3.11.0: Deprecate Event.lat, Event.lng, Event.gmaps_place_id, Event.gmaps_url. Event models will no longer be geocoded. Moving forward, these fields will return null. Eventually these fields will be removed. Event.address will now return FRC-API address, and Event.location_name will return FRC-API venue. 3.10.1: Add remap_teams to event. 3.10.0: Upgrade to Openapi v3.1.1. 3.9.16: Marked Event.timezone as nullable, renamed District_List to District. 3.9.15: Add onshape to media type. 3.9.14: Adds max_team_page to Status. 3.9.13: Fixes missing 2023 endgame enum. 3.9.12: Updates 2025 match breakdown penalties to be correct for 2025. 3.9.11: Adds tba_botRowCount, tba_midRowCount, and tba_topRowCount to 2025 match breakdown autoReef and teleopReef. 3.9.10: Add 2025 score breakdowns. 3.9.9: Fix nullable fields within Team_Event_Status. 3.9.8: Add district awards endpoint. Add nullable to district rankings. 3.9.7: Add district history endpoint. 3.9.6: Added History endpoint; added NotablesInsight endpoint. 3.9.5: Properly documented that event.district may be null. 3.9.4: Properly documented that a Status may be null (future events). 3.9.3: Proper nullable event rankings/oprs/coprs 3.9.2: Add event/key/team_media endpoint; add team_keys to media objects. 3.9.1: Mark WLT_Record as nullable. 3.8.2-3.9.0: Fixed undefined vs nullable fields. Adds 2024 score breakdown. Links score breakdown types to score_breakdown field. Adds leaderboard insights endpoint and type. 3.8.1-3.8.2: Replace `If-Modified-Since` with `If-None-Match` and `Last-Modified` with `ETag`. 3.8.0-3.8.1: Added Webcast date field. 3.7.0-3.8.0: Added 2020 Match Breakdown. 3.6.0-3.7.0: Added Zebra MotionWorks endpoints and models. 3.5.2-3.6.0: Added `school_name` to the Team model. 3.5.1-3.5.2: Removed `key` from the Media object, set `foreign_key` as a required property. 3.5-3.5.1: Fixed api clients crashing when requesting simple matches resulting in ties. 3.04.1 - 3.5: Updated the spec to follow OpenAPI standards. 3.04.0 - 3.04.1: Team motto will now return null. 3.03.1 - 3.04.0: Add direct_url and view_url to the Media model. 3.03.0 - 3.03.1: Fix model of /team/{team_key}/robots to match API, add min and max for year and add min for page_num. 3.02.1 - 3.03.0: Added Timeseries models and endpoints. 3.02.0 - 3.02.1: Fixed the model for `/team/{team_key}/districts` to match return from API. 3.1.0 - 3.02.0: Added `tba_gameData` to score breakdown and a leading zero to the minor version number to allow for easier sorting later. 3.0.5 - 3.1.0: Version bump for 2018 added fields and endpoints. Models Updated: `Team_Event_Status`, `Media`, 2018 Score Breakdowns. Endpoints Added: `/team/{team_key}/events/{year}/statuses`, `/event/{event_key}/teams/statuses` 3.0.4 - 3.0.5: Minor spelling fixes. Remove 2016 fields from `Match_Score_Breakdown_2017_Alliance` model. Fix `first_event_id` in `Event` model to correct type. Update `Media`.`type` enum. --- 3.0.3 - 3.0.4: Correct syntax in `Team_Event_Status_playoff` object, include descriptions in `Event_District_Points` and fix the path in `Team_Event_Status_playoff.properties.record` in order to more closely match Swagger spec. Fix syntax of `Match.video` to be correct and accurately reflect what is returned by the API. --- 3.0.2 - 3.0.3: `extra_stats` and `extra_stats_info` added to `Event_Ranking` model. Corrected match video property claiming to use the `Media` model, which it doesn't. Added `first_event_code` to the `Event` model. Added `/team/{team_key}/media/tag/{media_tag}` and year endpoints. Added `dq_team_keys` to `Match_alliance` model.  --- 3.0.1 - 3.0.2: `Team_Event_Status` and `Event_Ranking` model documentation changed to reflect actual API return. Changes involved W-L-T and ranking properties. --- 3.0.0 - 3.0.1: Descriptions updated to clarify some terms and improve grammar. The `district` property on the `Event` object now points to the `District_List` model, which was identical. `Required` fields on fully documented models now represent fields that may not be `null`. `District_Ranking` model documented.

key.description: TBA event key with the format yyyy[EVENT_CODE], where yyyy is the year, and EVENT_CODE is the event code of the event.

name.description: Official name of event on record either provided by FIRST or organizers of offseason event.

event_code.description: Event short code, as provided by FIRST.

city.description: City, town, village, etc. the event is located in.

state_prov.description: State or Province the event is located in.

country.description: Country the event is located in.

year.description: Year the event data is for.

short_name.description: Same as `name` but doesn't include event specifiers, such as 'Regional' or 'District'. May be null.

event_type_string.description: Event Type, eg Regional, District, or Offseason.

week.description: Week of the event relative to the first official season event, zero-indexed. Only valid for Regionals, Districts, and District Championships. Null otherwise. (Eg. A season with a week 0 'preseason' event does not count, and week 1 events will show 0 here. Seasons with a week 0.5 regional event will show week 0 for those event(s) and week 1 for week 1 events and so on.)

address.description: Address of the event's venue, if available.

postal_code.description: Postal code from the event address.

lat.description: Latitude for the event address. Will be NULL, for future development.

lng.description: Longitude for the event address. Will be NULL, for future development.

location_name.description: Name of the location at the address for the event, eg. Blue Alliance High School.

playoff_type.description: Playoff Type, as defined under `PlayoffType`: https://github.com/the-blue-alliance/the-blue-alliance/blob/main/src/backend/common/consts/playoff_type.py#L37, or null.

additionalProperties.description: A key-value pair with team key (eg `frc254`) as key and CCWM as value.

get.description:
Serve a generated export file for an authenticated session.

Security:
- Token must map to a known session (any non-expired state).
- Filename is validated against a strict allowlist before any filesystem access.
- Path-traversal is prevented by both the regex and Path.resolve() confinement.
- Only .json and .csv files inside the exports directory are served.

info.title: Pistas API
info.summary: Asignación de slots de pista y administración de las pistas.
info.description:
API del servicio Pistas. Tiene dos partes:

- **El pedido de slot que hace Vuelos** (4.1), bajo `/internal`. Lo llama otro
  servicio, no una persona: el gateway la bloquea (15.7, 15.19), así que no lleva
  encabezados de identidad.
- **Las operaciones del operador** (F-09, F-10, F-11, F-20, F-21), fuera de
  `/internal` para que pasen por el gateway (15.19). Desde afuera se llaman con el
  prefijo `/api/pistas`, por ejemplo `/api/pistas/runways` (15.7). Llevan los
  encabezados de identidad que pone el gateway (15.6), y solo las acepta el rol
  `operator` (CA-19).

Además:

- **Pista y bloque:** la pista se identifica con un nombre sin barra, como `05-23`,
  y el bloque con su hora de inicio en UTC, en múltiplos de 15 minutos (4.11).
- **Errores:** formato Problem Details (RFC 9457) con un campo `code` propio, igual
  que Clima y Vuelos (6.14). Un error inesperado responde `500` con `INTERNAL_ERROR`,
  sin el detalle: lo que pasó queda en el log de Pistas (21.1).
- **Versionado:** la versión es la de este contrato (`info.version`), como en Clima
  (9.10).

servers.description: Las operaciones del operador en el arranque local, por el gateway (15.7). El servicio no expone su propio puerto (15.20).
Solo desde la red de Docker. El gateway no la expone (15.19).

post.summary: Pedir un slot para un vuelo (4.1, 4.15)
post.description:
Asigna el slot exacto que se pide (RN-07) o rechaza el pedido.

- Si el slot está libre, es del vuelo (RN-08).
- Si lo tiene un despegue y el que pide es un arribo, el arribo se lo queda
  (RN-11): la respuesta trae `displaced_flight_id` y Pistas publica
  `pistas.slot.cedido`.
- En cualquier otro caso ocupado, se rechaza con los 3 libres más cercanos
  (RN-09).

Cuando lo asigna, Pistas publica `pistas.slot.asignado` (4.12, 4.14).

**Se puede repetir.** Pedir de nuevo el mismo slot para el mismo vuelo devuelve
`200` con el mismo resultado y no ocupa otro (4.6, CA-06). Vuelos lo reintenta
ante una falla pasajera (4.5).

200.description: El slot es del vuelo, recién asignado o porque ya lo tenía con el mismo pedido.

get.summary: Ver las pistas y el estado del clima (F-21)
get.description:
Devuelve todas las pistas con su estado, y lo último que Pistas sabe del clima
(4.2): si se puede operar y si Clima tiene datos. Es lo que necesita la pantalla
del operador, incluido el aviso de "Clima sin datos" (RN-24, 6.19).

200.description: Las pistas y el estado del clima.

post.description:
La pista nace abierta, salvo que el último dato del clima diga que no se puede
operar: en ese caso nace cerrada por el clima, como las demás (RN-15).

201.description: La pista quedó dada de alta.

post.summary: Cerrar una pista a mano (F-10, RN-16)
post.description:
Cierra la pista con `closed_reason: operator`. Una pista cerrada a mano no se
reabre sola cuando el clima lo permite: la reabre el operador (RN-16, CA-24).

Al cerrarla, los vuelos con slot en ella de ahí en adelante lo pierden: los
despegues quedan demorados (RN-17) y los arribos, desviados (RN-18). Pistas
publica `pistas.pista.cerrada` y un `pistas.slot.liberado` por cada vuelo (4.12).

- Si la pista estaba cerrada por el clima, pasa a cerrada por el operador: así no
  se reabre sola cuando el clima mejore (RN-16).
- Si ya estaba cerrada por el operador, responde `200` sin cambiar nada.

200.description: La pista está cerrada por el operador.

post.description:
Reabre una pista cerrada por el operador. Una pista cerrada por el clima solo se
reabre a mano cuando Clima no tiene datos (RN-42, CA-40): mientras haya datos, la
reabre el clima, y se responde `409` con `RUNWAY_CLOSED_BY_WEATHER`. Una condición
forzada cuenta como dato: mientras esté puesta, manda sobre todo (RN-29) y tampoco
se reabre a mano. Mientras Clima tenga datos que no permiten operar, tampoco se
reabre una pista cerrada por el operador, y se responde el mismo `409` (23.6, CA-42). Para probar el cierre y la reapertura se usa el clima forzado (F-12). Pistas publica
`pistas.pista.reabierta`.

Los vuelos que perdieron su slot al cerrarse no lo recuperan: un despegue
demorado pide un slot nuevo (RN-19) y un arribo desviado ya no vuelve (RN-18).

Si la pista ya estaba abierta, responde `200` sin cambiar nada.

get.description:
La lista fija de alternativos, ordenada por distancia desde Córdoba (RN-25), con
si cada uno está disponible. Un arribo desviado va al primero disponible.

200.description: Los alternativos, del más cercano al más lejano.

post.summary: Marcar un alternativo como no disponible (RN-26, F-20)
post.description:
Los arribos que se desvíen de ahí en adelante lo saltean (RN-26, CA-22). No cambia
el destino de los que ya se desviaron. Si ya estaba no disponible, responde `200`
sin cambiar nada.
Si ya estaba disponible, responde `200` sin cambiar nada.

closed_reason.description:
Quién la cerró, con los mismos valores que el evento de pista cerrada (4.12):
`weather` si fue el clima, `operator` si fue el operador. `null` si está abierta.

Weather.description: Lo último que Pistas sabe del clima, por los eventos de Clima (4.2, 9.14).

data_available.description:
`false` después de un evento "Clima sin datos". Mientras dure, las pistas no
se cierran ni se reabren solas y la pantalla muestra el aviso (RN-24, 6.19).

operable.description: Si se puede operar según el último dato, o `null` si todavía no llegó ninguno.

nearest_free_slots.description: Solo en `SLOT_TAKEN`. Los 3 slots libres más cercanos al pedido, antes o después y en cualquier pista (RN-09).

Unavailable.description:
Falla pasajera de Pistas, por ejemplo su base no responde. Vuelos la reintenta (4.5):
repetir el pedido es seguro (4.6). Las operaciones del operador también se pueden
repetir sin riesgo.

InvalidRequest.description: Faltan datos o tienen mal formato, por ejemplo un bloque fuera de un múltiplo de 15 minutos.

example.detail: Solo el operador puede administrar las pistas.

RunwayAlreadyExists.description: Ya hay una pista con ese nombre.

ClosedByWeather.description:
Clima tiene datos y la pista la cerró el clima (23.4) o el clima no permite operar
(23.6): no se reabre a mano. Una cerrada por el clima la reabre el clima cuando vuelva
a permitir la operación. Para probar, se fuerza el clima (F-12).

example.title: El clima no permite reabrir la pista
example.detail: Mientras Clima tenga datos y no permita operar, la pista no se reabre a mano.

InternalError.description:
Falló algo que Pistas no esperaba, como un error de programación. La respuesta no
trae el detalle: queda en el log de Pistas. Vuelos no lo reintenta, porque
reintentar no lo arregla (21.1), pero cuenta como falla para el circuit breaker
(13.2).

All endpoints except /access-requests and /languages require a valid
Azure AD B2C Bearer token and allow-list membership.

**v2 changes** (feature 002-adaptive-learning-state):

- `EntryUpdate`: same field changes; `learningState` field removed.
