info.title: Treasures Finance B2B Public API
info.description:
Public B2B API for tokenized stock discovery, quoting and trade execution, USDC
bridging across Solana and Ethereum, and portfolio + trade history reads.

**Wire format.** All token amounts, USDC amounts, shares, prices and bps-derived
decimals are JSON **strings** to avoid float drift. Integer fields
(`expires_at`, `*_bps`, `quote_index`, timestamps in seconds) are JSON numbers.

**Auth.** Only `POST /quote/buy`, `POST /quote/sell`, `POST /bridge/quote` and the four
`/signals-orders` routes (`POST /signals-orders/exit/plan`, `POST /signals-orders/exit`,
`POST /signals-orders/rebalance/plan` and `POST /signals-orders/rebalance`) require
`ownership_proof` (wallet-key signature over a canonical challenge, see `OwnershipProof`).
`POST /trade/submit` is gated by the per-leg signed payload itself.

These routes **require** an integrator API key in `X-API-Key` (see `IntegratorApiKey`):

- `GET /settlements`
- the `/payouts` routes (your integrator fees and their payouts)
- `POST /quote/preview` (which binds no wallet, so the key is what identifies the caller)
- `GET /stocks/{ticker}` (whose profile, analyst, earnings and news blocks are served to
  contracted integrators only)
- the `/signals` routes (strategy target-weight books, served to contracted integrators)
- the `/signals-orders` routes (the orders that exit a book from your wallet, or rebalance it
  to the book)
- `POST /trade/submit/batch` (many signed submits in one request).

Every other route may be called anonymously.

**Integrator API keys are optional on every route but those, and never
ignored.** If you send `X-API-Key` on any route, a key beginning `tik_`/`trk_`
is verified and a bad one is rejected rather than silently downgraded to
anonymous:

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| Malformed or unknown key | `401 invalid_api_key` |
| Revoked key | `403 key_revoked` |
| Your organisation is suspended | `403 integrator_suspended` |
| Read-only (`trk_`) key on a non-reporting route | `403 insufficient_scope` |

A **`trk_` reporting key reaches the reporting routes and nothing else.**
Today that is exactly one route: `GET /settlements`. Everywhere else on this
API it answers `403 insufficient_scope`. That refusal is the point: it is what
makes the key safe to hand to a third party for reporting. Use your `tik_` key
for API access; it works on the reporting routes too. A credential for a
different Treasures plane (e.g. a `twk_` wallet key) is not addressed to this
API and is ignored, so those requests are served anonymously.

**Rate limits.** Per-IP and per-(IP, wallet) sliding windows.
Presenting a valid key adds a per-organisation bucket shared by all of your
keys, a cross-IP aggregate bound, additive to the per-IP limits rather than a
raised ceiling. Upstream 429s propagate as `502 provider_unavailable`.

get.summary: List active tradable stocks (catalog + live enrichment)
get.description:
Catalog with tradfi snapshot and onchain aggregate.
Cached server-side for 30 s.

Without query parameters this is the whole catalog in ticker order. `q`, `sort` and
`order` search and reorder it; `page` splits the result into pages of 25 and adds
`page`, `next_page` and `total` to the response. Search, sort and paging run over the
same cached snapshot, so they add no provider calls.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on `ticker`, `name` or a venue's `token_ticker` (e.g. `AAPLx`), 1 to 100 characters after trimming.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key. Omitted with `order` also omitted, the catalog's ticker order stands.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `asc` for `ticker` and `desc` for every metric. Sent without `sort`, it orders by `ticker`. Ticker order is always the catalog's own (`desc` reverses it), so it matches the unparameterised read row for row.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page of 25 rows. Omitted, the response carries every matching row and no paging fields.

get.description: Catalog rows only. Cached server-side for 5 min, so it is cheap to poll.

get.summary: Live per-protocol prices for requested tickers

parameters.name: tickers
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list, 1–50 tickers. Each item matches `^[A-Z0-9.-]{1,10}$`
**case-insensitively**; the server normalizes to uppercase before lookup.

get.description:
Everything the catalog knows about one ticker: profile (description, sector, industry,
website, logo), listings per (protocol, chain), the B2B tradfi block, pre/post-market
print, market session, analyst consensus and grades, next earnings, and the latest news.
Every block is best-effort and degrades to `null` on its own. Requires `X-API-Key`
(a general `tik_` key; reporting keys are refused). Cached 60 s.

There is deliberately **no `onchain` block** on this route; for per-protocol on-chain
prices call `GET /stocks/prices`.

This route takes no query parameters: any is a 400, as on the three sibling stocks routes.

aapl.summary: US large-cap during the regular session
aapl.description: Illustrative values. `exchange`, `exchange_country` and `data_delay` are present because the venue resolved; `display_ticker` is absent because a US row's bare `ticker` is already the display form. `extended_hours` is null during the regular session.

value.name: Apple Inc.
value.description: Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services.

news.title: Apple unveils new iPhone lineup
news.snippet: Apple introduced its next iPhone generation at its annual September event.

403.description: Reporting key presented (insufficient_scope)

post.summary: Quote USDC → stock token (one leg per chain the ticker lists, better first)
post.description:
Requires `ownership_proof` for each wallet provided. Returns one best leg per
chain the ticker lists (up to six: sol, eth, robinhood, base, arbitrum, bnb): the
signable quote legs (one per chain). On `bnb` (BNB Smart Chain, 56) three
protocols compete for that one leg, so a pinned bnb request should carry
`protocol` as well as `chain`. Cache the returned `quote_id`;
every signed leg is submitted together at `/trade/submit`.
Set `quote_only: true` for a non-executable price preview (the wallet need
not be funded; `quote_id`, `expires_at`, and `signable_payloads` are omitted).

`502 provider_unavailable` also fires when a `priority:"speed"` cross-chain leg's
sol-origin deposit fails to compile (an RPC blockhash read failure): the whole quote
is refused, not just that cell; retry.

default_routing.summary: Auto-route across every chain the ticker lists

speed_transaction.summary: Speed route on base, wallet pays gas (`execution` omitted = `"transaction"`)
speed_transaction.description: Returns one or two complete unsigned transactions (`evm_eip1559_tx` on base, `evm_legacy_tx` on robinhood) to sign whole and return as `evm_signed_tx`. The wallet needs native ETH on that chain. See the `speed_transaction_pair` response example.

speed_user_operation.summary: Speed route on base, your paymaster pays gas (`execution:"user_operation"`)
speed_user_operation.description: Returns one `evm_calls` payload to pack into a sponsored ERC-4337 v0.7 UserOperation from an EIP-7702-delegated Modular Account v2 wallet and return as `evm_user_operation`. Requires `priority:"speed"`. See the `speed_user_operation` response example.

speed_transaction_pair.summary: `priority:"speed"` on base: wallet not yet approved, so `approve` then `swap`
speed_transaction_pair.description: `tx_hex` / `tx_base64` are truncated here; each is a complete unsigned transaction with nonce, gas and fees already set. Sign both bytes-as-is and return one `evm_signed_tx` per payload, in this order. An already-approved wallet gets the `swap` payload only. `gasless:false` and `estimated_gas_usd` are the caller's own gas.

speed_user_operation.description: `calls[].data` is truncated here. Pack the calls, in order, into ONE ERC-4337 v0.7 UserOperation from `sender` (`execute` for one call, `executeBatch` for two), sponsor it with your paymaster, sign, and return it as `evm_user_operation`. The leg is `gasless:true` with `estimated_gas_usd:"0"` because the paymaster pays.

400.description: Invalid request body, slippage out of range, unknown ticker, zero amount, or (pinned `execution: "user_operation"`) a wallet not delegated to Modular Account v2.

410.description: Quote stale (upstream price moved past expiry mid-build).

422.description:
No fillable routes returned by the planner, or a basket listing whose
issuer-published price is unusable.

post.description:
The `quote_only` shape with **no wallet and no ownership proof**: prices every chain the
ticker lists (or those your `chain` / `protocol` filters allow) and returns the same legs
`POST /quote/buy` would, minus `quote_id`,
`expires_at`, every leg's `signable_payloads`, and `warnings_ack_token`. Nothing is
persisted, so there is no `/quote/{quote_id}/status` to poll and nothing to submit;
re-quote through `/quote/buy` for anything you intend to sign.

**A key is required here**, unlike every other quote route: this is the one quote that
binds no wallet at all. Send your general `tik_` key; a read-only `trk_` reporting key is
refused `403 insufficient_scope` like everywhere else off the reporting routes.

Identical requests inside a 10-second window are answered from one venue fan-out; a
refusal is never cached. Budgets are per-IP and per-organisation as elsewhere, **plus a
global ceiling shared by every caller of this route**, so a 429 here can be someone
else's traffic. Honour `Retry-After` rather than retrying immediately.

**Read `X-RateLimit-*` on this route as the shared bucket, not as yours.** The headers
report the **last** limiter applied, which here is that global ceiling, so
`X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` says the route is saturated across all callers, not that
*you* are out of budget. Back off for `Retry-After` seconds and retry; do not stand down
for a whole minute on the assumption you exhausted a per-caller window.

400.description: Invalid request body, slippage out of range, unknown ticker, zero amount, or an `amount_usdc` above the 1000000 preview cap.

401.description: No integrator key presented, or an unknown one.

403.description:
A read-only `trk_` reporting key was presented (`insufficient_scope`), the key was
retired (`key_revoked`), or your organisation is suspended (`integrator_suspended`).

422.description:
No fillable routes returned by the planner, or a basket listing whose
issuer-published price is unusable.

503.description:
Your configured fee schedule no longer fits a venue Treasures routes through
(`integrator_fee_misconfigured`). A Treasures-side configuration issue that retrying soon
won't clear; contact Treasures, or send `integrator_fee_bps: 0` to preview without your fee.

post.summary: Quote stock holdings → USDC (all legs needed; all-or-nothing submit)
post.description:
Plans the optimal sequence of swap legs across the user's current holdings.
Every returned leg must be signed and submitted together at `/trade/submit`.

400.description: Invalid request body, slippage out of range, unknown ticker, zero amount, a `payout_chain` the request cannot reach (its wallet missing, or nothing in scope can pay out there; see `payout_chain`), or (pinned `execution: "user_operation"`) a wallet not delegated to Modular Account v2.

value.message: payout_chain: no requested chain and protocol can pay out on "base"

410.description: Quote stale (upstream price moved past expiry mid-build).

422.description:
No fillable routes returned by the planner, or insufficient holdings
for the requested share amount. With `payout_chain`, holdings that
cover the amount but cannot pay out there are `no_routes` with
`reason: payout_route_unavailable`, never `holdings_insufficient`.
A sell refused for its size may carry `min_notional_usdc`, in USDC
of the shares it could not place (see `NoRoutesError`).

get.summary: Aggregate + per-leg status for a previously issued quote
get.description:
Public read-only; no `ownership_proof`. Ethereum in-flight rows are
lazy-flipped against the upstream venue on read; Solana `broadcast_unknown` rows stay
in-flight until operator action. In-progress aggregates are cached per venue class: 1 s while
a speed-route leg submitted in the last 5 min is still in flight, 3 s otherwise;
`poll_after_ms` sits just above that window and is `null` once the aggregate is terminal
(stop polling).

404.description: Unknown `quote_id` (expired cache, never issued, or no rows persisted).

post.description:
Idempotent on `(quote_id, quote_index)`. The per-leg signed payload IS the
authorization proof; no `ownership_proof` is required here. Re-quote (`410
quote_stale`) if the cached snapshot expired between issue and submit.

A quote that carries your integrator fee (`integrator_fee_bps > 0` on any leg) can
only be submitted with the same `X-API-Key` that quoted it; anything else is `403
quote_integrator_mismatch` and nothing is broadcast. Zero-fee quotes are unaffected.

speed_signed_pair.summary: Speed-route leg (`execution:"transaction"`): both transactions signed whole
speed_signed_pair.description: One `evm_signed_tx` per `SignableEvmTx` payload the quote issued, in the order issued (`approve` at nonce n, `swap` at n+1). Sign each `tx_hex` unchanged (never re-nonce, re-estimate or re-serialize) and do not broadcast; Treasures does. `signed_tx_hex` is truncated here.

user_operation.summary: Speed-route leg (`execution:"user_operation"`): one sponsored, signed UserOperation
user_operation.description: The v0.7 UserOperation you built from the quote's `evm_calls` payload, sponsored by your paymaster and signed by the delegated wallet. Do not send it to a bundler yourself; Treasures simulates, submits and returns `user_op_hash`. `callData`, `paymasterData` and `signature` are truncated here. Numerics may be decimal or 0x-hex strings.

200.description:
Partial-broadcast tolerated: legs that landed appear under `results`,
legs that hit an invariant break appear under `failed_legs` with a
generic `internal_error` code so the agent can reconcile on-chain.

speed_broadcast.summary: Speed-route leg accepted; `tx_hash` is the swap's from the start
speed_broadcast.description: On a pair the swap hash is known immediately (it is `keccak256` of the signed swap) but appears on chain only after the bundled `approve` mines. Poll `/quote/{quote_id}/status` until `completed`.

user_operation_broadcast.summary: UserOperation accepted by the bundler; `user_op_hash` set, `tx_hash` still null
user_operation_broadcast.description: `tx_hash` becomes the bundle transaction once mined; poll `/quote/{quote_id}/status`. A paymaster refusal would instead be `status: broadcast_failed` with `error_code: sponsorship_rejected`.

400.description: Malformed body, incomplete submit, or `quote_index` not in snapshot.

409.description: A leg under `(quote_id, quote_index)` was already submitted.

410.description: Snapshot expired between issue and submit; re-quote.

422.description:
You sent `acknowledged_warnings` and it does not match the warnings served with this
`quote_id`. Only reachable when the field is present; omitting it always proceeds.

example.message: echo warnings_ack_token from the quote as acknowledged_warnings to proceed

post.summary: Submit up to 25 signed quotes in one request
post.description:
Runs each submission exactly as `POST /trade/submit` would and answers every one, in
request order. `http_status` is the status that submit would have answered and `response`
its body; headers (`Retry-After`, the rate-limit counts) belong to the batch response
only. One submission's outcome never affects another's, so the batch's `200` says nothing
about any item: read each `http_status`.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

Refused as a whole, with nothing read or broadcast:

- The same `quote_id` in more than one submission: `400 invalid_request`. A buy's legs
  are alternatives, so splitting one quote across submissions would buy twice. Send each
  quote once, with all of the legs you sign for it in one submission.
- No submissions, more than 25, an unknown field, or any submission `POST /trade/submit`
  would refuse as malformed: `400 invalid_request`.
- A body over 100 KB (100,000 bytes): `413 { error: "Payload too large" }`, answered before
  the request reaches this operation. The limit of 25 assumes about one signed Solana leg
  per submission; submissions that sign several legs (a sell quoted with several legs)
  leave room for fewer, so size such batches smaller.
- The rate limit: `429`. Every submission counts once against a per-organisation budget
  (600 a minute) and a per-IP budget (300 a minute), on top of the per-request limits of
  every trade route. The batch is charged before any submission runs, and a batch refused
  with `429` still counts in full against the per-organisation budget, and against the
  per-IP budget too when that is the one that refused. A batch refused with `400` costs
  nothing against these two budgets.

  Size each batch to the budget you have left, and after a `429` wait for `Retry-After`.
  On a `200` the `X-RateLimit-*` headers describe the last of the two budgets charged (the
  per-IP one in production), counted in submissions.

Per submission, beside every answer `POST /trade/submit` can give:

- `422 batch_leg_unsupported` with that `quote_index`: a batch carries same-chain Solana
  legs only (`chain: sol`, quoted without `origin_chain` or `payout_chain`). Submit any
  other leg through `POST /trade/submit`. Nothing was sent. This check runs before the
  checks `POST /trade/submit` makes, so such a submission answers `422` even when it is
  also stale, bound to another organisation's fee or refused by screening; submitting it
  alone gives those answers.
- `503 batch_deadline_exceeded`: the batch ran long enough that this submission was not
  started, so nothing was sent and the batch could answer in time. Submit it again, alone
  or in a new batch, while its quote is live.
- `500 internal_error`: the submission failed unexpectedly. It may have been sent before
  it failed, so read `GET /quote/{quote_id}/status` before re-quoting. The single route's
  500 body reads `Internal server error`; inside a batch it is `internal_error`.

200.description: One result per submission, in request order.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.

post.description:
Returns a Treasures-issued `bridge_quote_id` plus a signable payload.

- By default (`delivery: self_broadcast`) you sign it and broadcast it yourself.
- With `delivery: submit` you sign it and hand it to `POST /bridge/{bridge_quote_id}/submit`
  instead; it can be executed no other way.

From an EVM origin that payload is typed data (`evm_permit_typed_data`): no transaction, no
nonce and no native gas on the origin.

Any two distinct chains in `BridgeChain` (with `delivery: submit`, the origin must be
`sol`, `eth`, `base` or `arbitrum` for now). `eth_wallet` and its proof are always
required; `sol_wallet` and its proof only when either side is `sol`.

400.description: Bad request, same-chain bridge, unsupported route, or slippage out of range.

422.description: Upstream reported insufficient liquidity for the route.

get.summary: Status of a previously issued bridge quote
get.description:
Required because the agent has no other way to discover the destination
tx hash; the upstream bridge's source tx hash alone cannot be used to
look up fill status.

post.summary: Submit a signed bridge for execution
post.description:
For a `delivery: submit` quote only (a `self_broadcast` quote answers
`400 quote_not_submittable`). Treasures checks the signatures recover to your wallet over
exactly the payload `/bridge/quote` issued, then runs it: an EVM origin's typed data is
executed by the upstream bridge (its gas taken from the amount); a Solana origin's signed
transaction is broadcast by Treasures.

One submission per quote: the same body may be resubmitted (idempotent) for up to an hour.
After a `502` it may have gone through, so resubmit the SAME body, never a new one; a
resubmission that still cannot tell answers `502` again, so poll status rather than
re-quote. Track the fill with `GET /bridge/{bridge_quote_id}/status`.

400.description:
Malformed body; signatures or a signed transaction that do not match the quote
(`signed_tx_mismatch`, `field` names the part); or a `self_broadcast` quote
(`quote_not_submittable`).

409.description:
`bridge_already_submitted`: this quote already holds a submission, or its retry
window has passed. Poll status; never sign a second deposit.

410.description: The quote expired (or its Solana blockhash did), or the bridge refused an EVM permit that can no longer run. Re-quote.

422.description: Refused before anything moved (for example, too little balance). Fix it, then re-quote. Solana origins only; a refused EVM permit answers 410.

502.description: The outcome is unknown. Resubmit the same body.

source_tx_hash.description: The Solana signature; null from an EVM origin.

get.summary: Reconciled holdings + USDC / USDG balances for the given wallets
get.description: At least one of `sol_wallet` / `eth_wallet` is required.

get.summary: Swap-only trade history for the given wallets
get.description:
Returns trades plus a `next_offset` cursor when more pages exist.
Synthesizes external rows on detected drift (source = `external`).

Every trade submitted through `POST /trade/submit` **with your API key
presented**, newest first. This is the one route a read-only `trk_` reporting
key may call; your `tik_` key works here too and returns the same rows.

**Settled fills only.** A trade appears once it reaches `completed`; on
Ethereum and Robinhood Chain that is when the resolver fills the order, which
can be minutes after you submitted it. Until then the amounts on record are
quote-time expectations, not what happened, so they are withheld rather than
reported as fact. Poll `GET /quote/{quote_id}/status` for in-flight legs.

**Attribution requires the header.** A submit sent without `X-API-Key` is not
attributed to anyone and will never appear here; there is no way to recover
it afterwards. Trades predating this endpoint are likewise absent.

Ordering and pagination key on settlement time. Pass the previous response's
`next_cursor` back as `cursor` to page; `has_more` tells you whether another
page exists. `data` may be shorter than `limit` while `has_more` is `true`.

**Re-scan a trailing window if you reconcile exactly.** A small number of Solana
trades are settled by a recovery job that records the on-chain block time, which
is earlier than when the record appeared, typically by minutes. Such a row lands
*behind* a cursor you have already paged past. If your totals must be exact,
re-scan roughly the last 2 hours on each pass rather than relying on the cursor
alone; `trade_id` is stable, so re-scanned rows deduplicate cleanly.

Note that 2 hours is a normal-operations figure, not a guaranteed bound: if that
recovery job is itself delayed, a row can be backdated by as long as the delay.
Treat a periodic wider re-scan as the backstop for balances that must tie out
exactly.

Each entry carries a LI.FI-style `sending` / `receiving` leg pair, each with its
own transaction hash, chain and explorer link. On a single-chain swap both legs
share one transaction hash, chain and timestamp; only the token and amount
differ.

A sell quoted with `payout_chain` is the exception: the stock leg (`sending`) is
the sale on the entry's `chain`, and the USDC leg (`receiving`) is the payout, its
own transaction on the chain the USDC landed on. That is `payout_chain`, or the
sale's own `chain` when the USDC was returned there instead, in which case the
entry is one chain with two transactions. Both legs carry the settlement time.

The top-level `token_out_address` and `amount` mirror the `receiving` leg; the
top-level `chain` and `tx_hash` are the trade's own, the same `tx_hash`
`GET /trades` reports, so on a cross-chain sell `tx_hash` is the sale
(`sending.tx_hash`) while `receiving.tx_hash` is the payout.

**Every amount is truncated, never rounded up.** Amounts, prices and fees are
reported at or below their true value, never above it, so a figure here is
always safe to reconcile, re-spend, or pay out against without a buffer. Treat
the last decimal place as a floor rather than a rounded value.

**Filtering.** All filter parameters are optional and combine with AND; omitting
one means "any". `chain`, `protocol` and `ticker` accept a comma-separated list
which is an OR *within* that parameter; `?chain=sol,eth&ticker=AAPL` means AAPL
on Solana or Ethereum. Repeating a parameter is **not** additive:
`?chain=sol&chain=eth` is read as `sol` alone, so use the comma form. A filter
that matches nothing returns an empty `data` with `200`, never an error.

**Casing follows the response.** Every filter value is matched in the casing this
endpoint reports it in: `chain`, `protocol` and `side` are lowercase and are
matched exactly (`?side=BUY` is rejected), while `ticker` is reported uppercase
and is the one filter accepted in any case. EVM `token_out_address` values are
case-insensitive; Solana addresses are base58 and case-sensitive.

**A cursor is bound to the filters that produced it.** Paging is a keyset over one
result set, so changing any filter mid-chain invalidates the cursor and returns
`400 cursor: filters_changed`; start that new query from the first page. Changing
`limit` is fine and does not invalidate the cursor.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`. Treat it as a blob, its encoding is not part of this contract and may change.

parameters.name: chain
parameters.description: Chains to include; omit for all. Values are lowercase, matched exactly. Matches each entry's `chain`, the chain of the stock traded: a sell paid out on another chain matches its stock's chain, not the payout's. To select sells by where their USDC landed, filter `token_out_address` on that chain's USDC.

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.description: Protocols to include; omit for all. Values are lowercase, matched exactly.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Tickers to include, case-insensitive. Matches the response's `ticker` field, not the venue-suffixed token symbol.

parameters.name: token_out_address
parameters.description: The contract address of the token **received**, matching the response's `token_out_address`. Because that field is side-dependent, so is this filter: a stock token address returns *buys* of that token, while a base-currency address (USDC, or USDG on Robinhood Chain) returns *sells* whose proceeds were received on that chain, including sells paid out there from a stock on another chain. An address we do not carry returns an empty page rather than an error.

parameters.name: settled_from
parameters.description: Earliest settlement time, inclusive, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Compares against the same `timestamp` each entry reports.

parameters.name: settled_to
parameters.description: Latest settlement time, **inclusive of the whole second**: an entry reporting `timestamp` equal to this value is always included. Must be greater than or equal to `settled_from`.

parameters.name: payout_id
parameters.description: Only the trades whose integrator fee went out in this payout, the entries a payout's `amount_usd` is summed from. Another organisation's payout id matches nothing.

parameters.name: payout_status
parameters.description: Where each trade's integrator fee stands. `unpaid`: no payout has claimed it yet; these entries sum exactly to `GET /payouts/accrued`. `processing` / `paid`: the status of the payout that claimed it. Only trades that carried an integrator fee match any value.

400.description: Invalid query. `cursor: malformed` means the cursor did not decode; restart from the first page rather than retrying it. `cursor: filters_changed` means the cursor came from a different set of filters; restart that query from the first page. `settled_from: must be <= settled_to` means the time range is inverted.

401.description: Missing, malformed or unknown `X-API-Key`. These are deliberately indistinguishable; the API never reveals whether a key exists.

403.description: A key you genuinely hold, but which may not be used here. `key_revoked`: the key was retired. `integrator_suspended`: your organisation is suspended, so every one of your keys is affected.

get.summary: What you are owed right now, and where it will be paid
get.description:
The sum of the `integrator_fee` entries on your settled trades that no payout has
claimed yet: exactly the entries `GET /settlements?payout_status=unpaid` lists, with
the same truncation. Fees earned on every chain are pooled into one USD figure
(USDC and USDG count 1:1).

`payout_address` / `payout_chain` are where payouts go. Only Treasures can set or
change them; ask your contact. `previous_payout_address` and
`payout_address_updated_at` show the last change, so an unexpected one is visible
to you.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`: a reporting key. `key_revoked` / `integrator_suspended` as on every route.

post.summary: Pay out everything you are owed, to your registered address
post.description:
Sends **all** of your accrued integrator fees (`GET /payouts/accrued`) to your registered
payout address, from Treasures' payout treasury. You choose nothing: the amount is what you are
owed, the destination is the address Treasures registered, and the body must be empty (or `{}`).

**`Idempotency-Key` is required.** A key is yours forever: repeating it returns the payout it
first created, whatever its status, including `failed`. To try again after a failure, send a
new key. Only one payout can be in progress at a time.

Limits: at least `minimum_usd`, at most `maximum_usd` (larger balances are paid out by
Treasures on request), one payout per cooldown window, and none for a while after your payout
address changes. `GET /payouts/accrued` reports all of them, including `next_eligible_at`.

`202` means the transfer was sent or is being sent. Poll `GET /payouts/{payoutId}` until
`status` is `paid` (or `failed`, in which case the fees are owed to you again).

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

202.description: Payout created and sent (or being sent).

200.description: The original payout, replayed for an `Idempotency-Key` you already used.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.

409.description:
- `payout_in_progress` (with `payout_id`)
- `payout_cooldown` / `address_hold` (with `retry_after`, Unix seconds, and a
  `Retry-After` header)
- `payout_address_missing` (ask Treasures to register one)
- `nothing_to_pay`.

422.description: `below_minimum` (with `amount_usd`, `minimum_usd`) or `requires_review` (with `amount_usd`, `maximum_usd`; Treasures pays balances this large on request).

503.description: `payouts_unavailable`: payouts are paused or cannot be made right now. Retry later.

get.description:
Every payout of your integrator fees, newest first. Pass the previous response's
`next_cursor` back as `cursor` to page. To see the trades a payout covered, call
`GET /settlements?payout_id=…`.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`.

400.description: Invalid query. `cursor: malformed` means restart from the first page.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.
`insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.

404.description: No such payout of yours. Another organisation's payout id answers the same, so the response never reveals whether an id exists.

get.summary: The strategies whose target-weight books you may read
get.description:
One page, newest first; `truncated` says whether the page cap of 100 cut it short (today
the catalog is a handful of rows). Only strategies published to integrators appear, so a
strategy visible in the Treasures app may be absent here. The catalog lists `active` and
`paused` strategies only; a `halted` strategy leaves the catalog but stays readable by id
or slug on the detail and history routes, with its last book.

`replication` is the honesty block for each book: a book is the source portfolio cut down
to the names Treasures can trade on chain and renormalised, so `names_replicated` of
`names_total` are in it and `skipped_source_weight` of the source's weight is not.

`strategy_id` is the stable key. `slug` is a convenience that may be renamed; the detail
and history routes accept either.

Each row carries its latest book's `book_hash`, `book_as_of` and `signal_id` (all `null`
when the strategy has no book yet), the same values `GET /signals/strategies/{id}` serves,
so one catalog read tells you which books changed since you last looked.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.

get.summary: One strategy and its current target-weight book
get.description:
`book` is the newest book the source produced that Treasures has finished acting on, or
`null` when there is none yet (or the newest one cannot be read; an older book is never
substituted). `as_of` is when Treasures ingested the book, not the date of the underlying
filing or disclosure.

`book_hash` identifies the book's contents (the set of `ticker: weight` pairs). Sources
that restate an unchanged portfolio daily produce a new `signal_id` with the same
`book_hash`, so compare hashes to know whether the weights moved.

Weights are decimal strings that sum to at most one; `cash_weight` is the remainder.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.

404.description: No such strategy for you. A strategy that exists but is not published to integrators answers the same, so the response never reveals whether an id exists.

get.summary: The strategy's past books, newest first
get.description:
Every book the source produced that Treasures finished acting on, as full weight vectors,
newest first. Treasures' own weekly restatements of an unchanged book are not rows here;
a source that re-publishes an unchanged portfolio daily is, so consecutive rows often share
a `book_hash`.

Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to page; `has_more` tells you whether another page
exists. `data` may be shorter than `limit` while `has_more` is `true`.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque; from a previous page's `next_cursor`.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.

404.description: No such strategy for you (see the detail route).

post.summary: The sells that exit a strategy book from your wallet, with no quotes
post.description:
Returns one full-share sell per name your Solana wallet holds in the strategy's current
book (plus any `tickers` you add). Nothing is quoted and nothing expires, so this is the
default flow: show the orders, then call `POST /quote/sell` per order when the signer is
ready, and submit each quote through `POST /trade/submit` unchanged. Human and
hardware-wallet flows should use this route; `POST /signals-orders/exit` is for
programmatic signers.

Solana only for now: a body carrying `eth_wallet` is refused with `400 invalid_request`.
`strategy_id` accepts the id or the slug; the response always carries the canonical id.
`as_of` is when Treasures ingested the book (unix seconds), not the filing date.

`nav_usdc` counts the priced names you hold in scope only; an unpriced holding is still
an order, with `notional_usdc: null`, ranked after the priced ones. Shares are floored to
18 decimal places, never rounded up. A holding worth under $0.01 reads as not held. A
holding that could not be read is skipped as `holdings_unknown`, never assumed absent,
with one exception: a token account found but not decodable into a balance reads as zero,
so that name is `not_held`.

At most 25 orders are returned and their upstream quote calls are capped at 30 (see
`POST /signals-orders/exit`); the overflow (the smallest by notional, unpriced first) is
skipped as `leg_cap`, so `POST /signals-orders/exit` answers the same split. With
`protocol` sent, only the pinned venues are read and sold: a name also held on another
venue gets no `skipped` entry, so repeat the call per venue.

**Quoting each order.** Send one `POST /quote/sell` per order, with the same wallet and a
fresh proof:
`{ "ticker": <ticker>, "amount_shares": <shares>, "chain": "sol", "protocol": <the protocol you sent here, if any>, "sol_wallet": <sol_wallet>, "ownership_proof": <proof>, "max_slippage_bps": <bps> }`.
To submit several quotes in one request, send them together through
`POST /trade/submit/batch`.

**One wallet per strategy.** Your holdings are not tracked per strategy: every name of the
book you hold in this wallet counts, whichever strategy (or none) you bought it for. Two
strategies sharing a name in one wallet will sell or resize each other's position, so give
each strategy its own wallet.

`expected_book_hash`, when sent, must equal the served book's `book_hash`, or the call is
refused with `409 book_changed` before the wallet is read or anything is quoted: re-read the
book and decide again.

`max_slippage_bps` is optional here (nothing is quoted) and range-checked when sent.
Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

400.description: Invalid request body (including `eth_wallet`, or a `protocol` with no Solana protocol), or slippage out of range.

example.message: eth_wallet is not supported on this route yet

422.description: `book_unavailable`: the strategy has no book yet.

post.summary: The sells that exit a strategy book, each with its signable quote
post.description:
The same orders as `POST /signals-orders/exit/plan`, each carrying `quote`: exactly the
`POST /quote/sell` answer for that order, signable payloads included. Sign and submit each
quote through `POST /trade/submit` unchanged.

**For programmatic signers only.** A Solana leg is signable for about 45 s after this
response. Each quote's own `expires_at` binds; the top-level `expires_at` is the earliest
of them and `signing_window_sec` is the seconds left until it. Human and hardware-wallet
flows should call `POST /signals-orders/exit/plan`, then `POST /quote/sell` per order when
ready.

A partial result is normal: an order whose quote is refused is moved to `skipped` with
the error code `POST /quote/sell` would have answered (for example `no_routes`, which on
a sub-minimum leg carries no minimum, or `holdings_insufficient`), and the response is
still `200`. An order whose quote expired before the response was sent is skipped as
`quote_stale`.

`max_slippage_bps` is required here and applies to every leg. To submit several quotes in
one request, send them together through `POST /trade/submit/batch`.

**One call at a time per wallet and strategy.** While a quote from an earlier `/exit` for
the same wallet and strategy is neither final (`GET /quote/{quote_id}/status`) nor five
minutes past its `expires_at`, a new call is refused with `409 orders_in_flight` naming
those `quote_ids` (an empty list while the earlier call is still quoting), with
`Retry-After` in seconds. A submitted quote counts as final once its status has been read
as final, so poll every quote you submit. The plan route is never refused this way.

Limits on this route count upstream quote calls, not requests: an order held on one
Solana venue costs 1 point, on two venues 3, on three 6 (each pass re-quotes the venues
not yet filled). Points come from a per-integrator bucket (30 a minute) and from a bucket
shared by every caller (90 a minute), charged only after the wallet is admitted and only
when there is something to quote.

The plan never costs more than 30 points: orders past that are skipped as `leg_cap`, so an
exit of more than ten names held on two venues each exits the rest on the next call. A
plan costing more than the points left is refused whole with `429` before any order is
quoted. A `429` from the shared bucket can be another integrator's traffic and does not
spend your own points. The `X-RateLimit-*` headers describe the shared bucket.

**One wallet per strategy.** Your holdings are not tracked per strategy: every name of the
book you hold in this wallet counts, whichever strategy (or none) you bought it for. Two
strategies sharing a name in one wallet will sell or resize each other's position, so give
each strategy its own wallet.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

400.description: Invalid request body (including `eth_wallet`, a missing `max_slippage_bps` or a `protocol` with no Solana protocol), or slippage out of range.

422.description: `book_unavailable`: the strategy has no book yet.

post.summary: The sells and buys that bring your strategy positions to its book, with no quotes
post.description:
Returns the orders that move your Solana wallet's positions in the strategy's names to the
strategy's current book. Nothing is quoted and nothing expires, so this is the default
flow: show the orders, then call `POST /quote/sell` (send `shares` as `amount_shares`) or
`POST /quote/buy` (send `notional_usdc` as `amount_usdc`) per order when the signer is
ready, and submit each quote through `POST /trade/submit` unchanged.

**Quoting each order.** With the same wallet and a fresh proof,

- a sell is `POST /quote/sell` with
  `{ "ticker": <ticker>, "amount_shares": <shares>, "chain": "sol", "sol_wallet": <sol_wallet>, "ownership_proof": <proof>, "max_slippage_bps": <bps> }`
- a buy is `POST /quote/buy` with
  `{ "ticker": <ticker>, "amount_usdc": <notional_usdc>, "chain": "sol", "sol_wallet": <sol_wallet>, "ownership_proof": <proof>, "max_slippage_bps": <bps> }`.

Send no `protocol`: the plan reads every Solana venue. To submit several quotes in one
request, send them together through `POST /trade/submit/batch`.

**Without `amount_usdc` the book's cash weight is sold on every call.** nav is then only
what you hold in scope, and the targets sum to the book's deployed weight of it, so a book
that is 10% cash sells about 10% of your held value each time it is called without
`amount_usdc`. Carry `funding.next_amount_usdc` into the next call to keep that cash in nav.

**Buy-in.** To buy into a strategy from cash, call with `amount_usdc` on a wallet that
holds none of its names: every order is a buy, sized by its book weight of `amount_usdc`.
One call orders at most 25 names and 30 upstream quote calls (a buy costs one per Solana
venue it can buy on), so a book of 20 names on two venues each takes more than one round:
submit the buys, wait for them to settle, and call again with `funding.next_amount_usdc`.

**Scoped nav.** The plan sizes every name against `nav_usdc`: the value of what you hold in
the book's names (plus any `tickers` you add), plus `amount_usdc`. Each name's target is its
book weight times that nav; the book's unweighted remainder stays as USDC and is never
ordered. A `tickers` name outside the book has weight zero and is sold in full. Holdings
outside the scope and the rest of your USDC are never touched. Every sol venue counts, so
`protocol` is not accepted here.

**Funding.** Buys spend only `amount_usdc`, never the rest of the wallet's USDC, and are
never larger than it: when the buys need more, each is scaled down pro rata and rounded
down (`funding.buys_scaled`). Scaling is pro rata and a scaled buy under $1 is skipped, so
a small `amount_usdc` spread over many buys (for example under $1 per buy when they are
equal) can deploy nothing that round; the whole shortfall stays in
`funding.buys_deferred_usdc`.

A buy that cannot be funded is skipped as `awaiting_sell_proceeds` when the plan also
sells, or `insufficient_balance` when it does not. A rebalance that only reshuffles what
you hold is therefore two rounds:

1. Call with `amount_usdc` omitted. Submit the sells.
2. Once they settle, call again with `amount_usdc` set to the smaller of
   `funding.next_amount_usdc` and `usdc_available` (proceeds land net of fees and
   slippage). Omit `amount_usdc` when that is zero: `"0"` is refused with `400`. Submit the
   buys.

Use `funding.next_amount_usdc`, not `funding.buys_deferred_usdc`: it is the strategy's cash
after this round (`amount_usdc` plus the sells, less the buys), so it keeps the book's
unweighted remainder and the weight of any `not_tradable` name in nav. Calling round 2
without `amount_usdc`, or with only the deferred buys, shrinks nav, and the plan sells
again.

**Wait for every order to finish before calling again.** Each order from the previous
round must have reached a final status (`GET /quote/{quote_id}/status`) before any new call.
The plan reads your holdings as they stand and this route never refuses an early or retried
call, so it returns the same sells again and both sets can execute.
(`POST /signals-orders/rebalance` refuses such a call with `409 orders_in_flight`.)

**One wallet per strategy.** Your holdings are not tracked per strategy: every name of the
book you hold in this wallet counts, whichever strategy (or none) you bought it for. Two
strategies sharing a name in one wallet will sell or resize each other's position, so give
each strategy its own wallet.

`expected_book_hash`, when sent, must equal the served book's `book_hash`, or the call is
refused with `409 book_changed` before the wallet is read or anything is quoted.

Sells are floored to 18 decimal places and buys to 6, never rounded up. A gap under $1 is
skipped as `below_min_notional`. A book name Treasures cannot buy on Solana is skipped as
`not_tradable` and its weight stays in USDC. At most 25 orders are returned and their
upstream quote calls are capped at 30 (see `POST /signals-orders/rebalance`): sells are
admitted first, then buys, each side largest first; the first order that does not fit and
every one after it is skipped as `leg_cap`.

Unlike `/exit`, which skips a name it cannot read, a rebalance refuses the whole request
when any name in scope cannot be read (`holdings_unknown`) or a held one cannot be priced
(`price_unavailable`), because one mis-sized name would mis-size every other order. The
refusal lists the `tickers` to retry or remove.

`max_slippage_bps` is optional here (nothing is quoted) and range-checked when sent.
Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

400.description: Invalid request body (including `eth_wallet`, `protocol` or `amount_usdc: "0"`), or slippage out of range.

422.description:
- `book_unavailable`: the strategy has no book yet.
- `holdings_unknown` or `price_unavailable` with `tickers`: those names could not be
  read or priced, so no plan is offered. A read or price failure is usually transient
  and can be retried, but a book name that is no longer tradable (an inactive listing)
  refuses every rebalance on this strategy until its next book, so do not retry
  blindly; `POST /signals-orders/exit` skips that name and serves the rest.
- `insufficient_balance`: `amount_usdc` is more than the wallet's Solana USDC.
- `strategy_halted`: the strategy is halted, so no rebalance is offered and nothing is
  read; `POST /signals-orders/exit/plan` still serves it.

post.summary: The sells and buys that bring your strategy positions to its book, each with its signable quote
post.description:
The same orders as `POST /signals-orders/rebalance/plan`, each carrying `quote`: exactly the
`POST /quote/sell` or `POST /quote/buy` answer for that order, signable payloads included.
Sign and submit each quote through `POST /trade/submit` unchanged. The two-round funding
flow is the plan route's: in round 1, submit the sells; once they settle, call again with
`amount_usdc` set to the smaller of `funding.next_amount_usdc` and `usdc_available`
(omitted when that is zero) for the buys.

Without `amount_usdc` the book's cash weight is sold on every call, and a buy-in from cash
is `amount_usdc` on a wallet holding none of the names; see
`POST /signals-orders/rebalance/plan`. To submit several quotes in one request, send them
together through `POST /trade/submit/batch`.

**One call at a time per wallet and strategy.** While a quote from an earlier `/rebalance`
for the same wallet and strategy is neither final (`GET /quote/{quote_id}/status`) nor
five minutes past its `expires_at`, a new call is refused with `409 orders_in_flight`
naming those `quote_ids` (an empty list while the earlier call is still quoting), with
`Retry-After` in seconds, so a retry never mints the same sells twice.

A submitted quote counts as final once its status has been read as final, so poll every
quote you submit. The plan route is never refused this way: wait for every order there
yourself.

**One wallet per strategy.** Your holdings are not tracked per strategy: every name of the
book you hold in this wallet counts, whichever strategy (or none) you bought it for. Two
strategies sharing a name in one wallet will sell or resize each other's position, so give
each strategy its own wallet.

**For programmatic signers only.** A Solana leg is signable for about 45 s after this
response. Each quote's own `expires_at` binds; the top-level `expires_at` is the earliest
of them and `signing_window_sec` is the seconds left until it. Human and hardware-wallet
flows should call `POST /signals-orders/rebalance/plan`, then quote each order when ready.

A partial result is normal: an order whose quote is refused is moved to `skipped` with the
error code its quote route would have answered (for example `no_routes`, also what a buy
the wallet cannot fund at quote time answers), and the response is still `200`. A buy
skipped here is counted in `funding.buys_deferred_usdc` and spends nothing from
`funding.next_amount_usdc`; a sell skipped here adds nothing to it, so the next call never
spends USDC that no sell freed.

When no sell is quoted, a buy the plan held as `awaiting_sell_proceeds` is skipped as
`insufficient_balance` instead, since no proceeds are coming. An order whose quote expired
before the response was sent is skipped as `quote_stale`.

`max_slippage_bps` is required here and applies to every leg.

Limits count upstream quote calls, from the same buckets as `POST /signals-orders/exit`: a
sell held on one Solana venue costs 1 point, on two 3, on three 6; a buy costs at most 1
point per Solana venue it can buy on. The plan never costs more than 30 points (orders past
that are skipped as `leg_cap`), so it always fits an empty per-integrator bucket; a plan
costing more than the points left this minute is refused whole with `429` before any order
is quoted. A `429` from the shared bucket does not spend your own points.

Requires your general (`tik_`) key; a reporting key is refused.

400.description: Invalid request body (including `eth_wallet`, `protocol`, `amount_usdc: "0"` or a missing `max_slippage_bps`), or slippage out of range.

422.description: As on `POST /signals-orders/rebalance/plan`, including `strategy_halted`; nothing is quoted.

IntegratorApiKey.name: X-API-Key
IntegratorApiKey.description:
Per-organisation key issued out of band. Two kinds:

- `tik_…` (general: API access)
- `trk_…` (reporting: read-only, intended to be handed to a third party, and accepted
  **only** on the reporting routes: today just `GET /settlements`. Every other route in
  this spec answers `insufficient_scope`).

Required by `GET /settlements`, by the `/payouts` routes, by `POST /quote/preview`, by
`GET /stocks/{ticker}`, by the `/signals` routes, by the `/signals-orders` routes and by
`POST /trade/submit/batch` (all but `/settlements` take a general `tik_` key only, being
non-reporting routes); accepted on every other route for attribution and a
per-organisation rate bucket. Send it on `POST /trade/submit` too; that is what makes a
trade appear in your `GET /settlements` reporting.

A missing or unknown key is `401 invalid_api_key`; a real but retired key is
`403 key_revoked`.

SourceQuery.name: source
SourceQuery.description: Column toggle (not a row filter). `all` (default) leaves the internal-lot P&L columns null; `internal` populates them from a replay of completed internal trades only. Realized P&L follows Hyperliquid `closedPnl` semantics.

SignalStrategyIdPath.name: id
SignalStrategyIdPath.description: The strategy's `strategy_id` (stable) or its `slug` (may be renamed).

InvalidRequest.description: Malformed query, body, or path parameter.

RateLimited.description: Sliding window exceeded: per-IP or per-(IP, wallet), plus a per-organisation bucket (shared across all of your keys) whenever a valid `X-API-Key` is presented. `Retry-After` header carries delta-seconds.

ProviderUnavailable.description: Upstream provider failed or rate-limited us.

AddressBlocked.description:
A wallet on the request was flagged by sanctions screening. Permanent;
do not retry with the same wallet.

ScreeningUnavailable.description:
Sanctions screening could not be completed and the request was rejected
(fail-closed). Transient; back off and retry.

SignalOrdersUnauthorized.description: Missing, malformed or unknown `X-API-Key`, or an ownership-proof failure.

SignalOrdersForbidden.description: `address_blocked` (sanctions screening flagged the wallet), or `insufficient_scope`, `key_revoked` or `integrator_suspended`.

SignalOrdersUnavailable.description:
Transient; retry.

- `screening_unavailable` or `integrator_fee_misconfigured` (see `POST /quote/sell`)
- `balance_unavailable`: the wallet's Solana USDC could not be read, and is never reported
  as zero
- `holdings_unavailable`: the wallet's holdings could not be read.

When the reads behind the plan (screening, the strategy and its book, holdings, prices and
USDC) did not answer within 15 seconds, the call answers `holdings_unavailable`, or
`screening_unavailable` when screening was the read still pending, with `Retry-After: 15`.

Retry-After.description: Delta-seconds, 15, sent when the reads passed their deadline. Wait that long before retrying.

SignalOrdersBookChanged.description: `book_changed`: `expected_book_hash` is not the book served now. The wallet was not read and nothing was quoted; re-read the book (`book_hash` is the served one) and decide again.

SignalOrdersConflict.description:
- `book_changed`: `expected_book_hash` is not the book served now; the wallet was not read
  and nothing was quoted.
- `orders_in_flight`: a quote from an earlier call for the same wallet and strategy is
  neither final nor five minutes past its `expires_at` (`quote_ids`; empty while that call
  is still quoting). Nothing was quoted; poll `GET /quote/{quote_id}/status` for the quotes
  you submitted, and call again after `Retry-After` seconds or once each is final.

  A quote you never submitted has no status to poll: `Retry-After` is how long until the
  earliest listed quote is five minutes past its `expires_at` (60 while the earlier call is
  still quoting). If an earlier call's response was lost, its quotes hold the wallet and
  strategy until the latest one's `expires_at` plus five minutes: wait out `Retry-After`,
  or submit the quotes you do hold.

Retry-After.description: Delta-seconds, sent with `orders_in_flight` only: until the earliest listed quote is five minutes past its `expires_at` (at least 1), or 60 while the earlier call is still quoting. Other listed quotes may still hold after it, and the next call says so.

SignalReadsRateLimited.description: A bucket of the `/signals` reads is spent: 1200 calls a minute per organisation (shared by all of your keys) and 600 a minute per key. There is no per-IP bucket on these routes. `Retry-After` carries delta-seconds.

PortfolioBusy.description:
The server is already computing as many fresh snapshots as it safely can
and yours was not cached. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds; cached
snapshots are never refused.

Retry-After.description: Delta-seconds to wait before retrying the same request.

QuoteServiceUnavailable.description:
`screening_unavailable`: sanctions screening could not be completed and the request was
rejected (fail-closed). Transient; back off and retry.
`integrator_fee_misconfigured` (with an `X-API-Key`): your configured fee schedule no longer
fits a venue Treasures routes through. A Treasures-side configuration issue that retrying
soon won't clear; contact Treasures, or send `integrator_fee_bps: 0` to quote without your fee.

Tradability.description: Probe warning for one cell. `thin`: the cell fills, but not at every size below its measured minimum. `untradable`: nothing filled at any size across a full measurement window, and no minimum accompanies it. **Neither value disables the cell**; quotes are still accepted for both. Absent means unmeasured or unwarned, never healthy-with-value-null.

WarnReason.description:
Why the cell is warned, strongest evidence first:

1. `settlement_failure` (a real order died)
2. `no_price_feed` (the venue holds no price for the pair)
3. `no_fill_window` (a full window of quiet auctions)
4. `no_settlements` (no value-bearing on-chain settlement in the census window)
5. `low_volume` (a volume proxy).

Absent when unwarned, or when the warn predates reason recording. Not stable over a cell's
lifetime: a `low_volume` warn that later kills a real order flips to `settlement_failure`.

SideNeutralWarnReason.description: The subset of `WarnReason` that bears on an exit as much as an entry, and the only values a sell surface publishes. The buy-sided reasons (`no_fill_window`, `settlement_failure`) are measured against buys, so a sell leg carrying one would warn about someone else's trade; a cell warned only for those publishes nothing here.

ThinSince.description: When the warning above was first raised. Present exactly when `tradability` is.

EvmAddress.description: Lowercased EVM address (server normalizes on parse).

DecimalString.description: Decimal number as a string to preserve full precision.

UsdcHumanAmount.description: USDC amount in human units, > 0, up to 6 fractional digits.

SharesHumanAmount.description: Share amount, > 0, up to 18 fractional digits.

Chain.description:
Settlement chain.

- `robinhood` = Robinhood Chain (4663, base currency USDG)
- `base` = Base (8453)
- `arbitrum` = Arbitrum One (42161)
- `bnb` = BNB Smart Chain (56).

`bnb` carries several protocols (`ondo`, `xstocks`, `bstocks`), as `sol` and `eth` do, so
`chain` alone does NOT identify a cell there: pin `protocol` too. `bnb` is always ACCEPTED
as an input (a quote `chain` pin, a `/settlements` filter), because historical rows must
stay queryable and a pin must not become a `400`; it appears on `/stocks*` RESPONSES only
while the venue is open.

With the venue closed, a `chain: "bnb"` buy answers `422 no_routes`, exactly as it would
for a ticker that never listed on 56, and a position you already hold on `bnb` still sells.

Protocol.description: Issuer/venue. `backpack` pairs only with `chain: sol` (Solana-only mints) and `bstocks` only with `chain: bnb`. `ondo` and `xstocks` list on `sol`, `eth` and `bnb`.

PayoutChain.description: A chain a sell can pay out on: USDC on that chain, paid to your own wallet there (`sol_wallet` on `sol`, `eth_wallet` on `eth` and `base`). `robinhood`, `arbitrum` and `bnb` are not payout chains.

SlippageBps.description:
Maximum tolerated slippage in basis points. Each route validates against
its own `[MIN, MAX]` window; out-of-range returns `400 invalid_slippage`
with the active bounds.

Execution.description:
How a **speed-route** leg is handed back.

- `"transaction"` (the default; absent and `null` mean the same) is the raw-transaction
  shape: one `SignableEvmTx` per transaction, signed whole, gas paid by the wallet.
- `"user_operation"` returns the same calls as ONE `evm_calls` payload (`SignableEvmCalls`)
  for you to pack into an ERC-4337 v0.7 UserOperation from the wallet (which must be
  **EIP-7702-delegated to Alchemy Modular Account v2** on that chain, or not delegated at
  all: a wallet with no code delegates in that first operation through `eip7702Auth`),
  sponsor with your own paymaster, sign, and return as `evm_user_operation`; Treasures
  submits it to a bundler and tracks it. The leg is then `gasless: true` with
  `estimated_gas_usd: "0"`.

Only meaningful with `priority: "speed"`; sending `"user_operation"` without it is
`400 invalid_request`.

Served on `base` and `robinhood` (a chain whose bundler is not configured answers
`422 no_routes` pinned, or drops that chain with `speed_route_unavailable` / `disabled`
unpinned). Not served on `bnb`: a bStocks leg there is always a `SignableEvmTx`, so under
`"user_operation"` it is dropped the same way. A wallet delegated to code other than
Modular Account v2 is `400 wallet_not_delegated` when pinned, or a `wallet_not_delegated`
drop reason.

Priority.description:
How to route, when there is a choice. `"speed"` asks for the **speed route** on the two L2
venues that have one (`robinhood`, `base`): a single on-chain swap that settles in one block
instead of a relayed order, quoted as a complete unsigned transaction you sign and Treasures
broadcasts. It costs you native gas on that chain; no pre-approval is needed: a wallet that
has not approved the router gets an `approve` payload bundled before the `swap` (see
`SignableEvmTx` `role`). Absent/`null` = today's routing, unchanged.

A **filter, not a preference**: under `"speed"` the same-chain candidates are

- `sol` (unchanged; its route is already fast)
- the `robinhood`/`base` speed routes
- the `bnb` + `bstocks` cell (a bStocks leg is a speed-route transaction at every priority,
  so `"speed"` changes nothing for it; `bnb` + `ondo` and `bnb` + `xstocks` have no speed
  route and are absent under `"speed"`).

A `robinhood`/`base` leg the speed route cannot serve is **absent** from the response (never
returned on its relayed route), with a `speed_route_unavailable` warning naming the chain
and the reason.

`eth` is never quoted on its own route under `"speed"`. On `/quote/buy` and `/quote/preview`
it can still come back as a cross-chain leg (`origin_chain` present) when you are not funded
on eth and another chain covers the amount, so a `chain: "eth"` pin yields that leg or
`422 no_routes`.

On `/quote/sell`, `chain: "eth"` (or `["eth"]`) together with `"speed"` is refused as
`400 invalid_request` (`priority: "speed" is not available on eth`), and a set that also
names other chains simply loses `eth`, unless the sell pays out on another chain
(`payout_chain`), where an `eth/ondo` position sells cross-chain whatever the `priority`. A
pin on any other chain with no speed route (for example `arbitrum`) is refused the same way
on every endpoint.

A `bnb` pin whose `protocol` names only `ondo` / `xstocks` is refused the same way on
`/quote/sell` (unless it pays out on another chain); on `/quote/buy` and `/quote/preview` it
passes the check, as an `eth` pin does, and answers `422 no_routes` because neither cell has
a speed or cross-chain route. The `bnb` + `bstocks` cell can also come back as a cross-chain
leg (`origin_chain` present) when you are not funded on `bnb` and another chain covers the
amount.

min_notional_usdc.description:
Present only when your order was below a known minimum for this
listing: the actionable answer to a refusal that would otherwise
carry no reason at all. Retry at or above this size. The number is
the venue's own floor when it states one or it is known in advance
(then `reason` is `amount_too_small`), a size a market maker quoted
your own wallet when asked again at refusal time, or otherwise a
minimum we measured for the listing.

Whenever `reason` is `amount_too_small`, it is present if any venue
that refused for size has a known floor above your order, even when
other venues refused for another reason. It then describes only the
venues that refused for size: a venue refused for another reason
(for example `insufficient_gas` on a Solana leg) still needs its own
remedy.

On `/quote/sell` it is a USDC value, not a share count: the shares
the quote could not place (the whole order, unless other legs could
take part of it), valued at the reference price, fell short of it.
Re-quote a share amount worth at least this much at the current
price. A position worth less may not be sellable on that chain until
it is topped up.

Read AFTER the venue refused, never before: this never causes a
refusal, it only explains one.

reason.description:
Present only when a strict majority of dropped cells share the same actionable reason;
otherwise omitted.

**This enum is deliberately smaller than the set of internal refusals.** A refusal with
no published counterpart yields a bare `no_routes` with no `reason` at all: notably an
unlisted cell, whether its venue is switched off or it is a supply-gated token (a
Coinbase B20 or bStocks token) that is deployed but not yet minted. The read side
already carries the remedy, since such a cell reports `address: null` (or no key at
all), omits its chain from `available_chains`, and publishes no `min_trade_size_usd`.
Re-read `/stocks/tickers` rather than retrying at another size.

- `price_off_reference` covers both non-caller-tunable price refusals: an outright
  refusal against the asset's reference market price (a route existed but priced too far
  from it to be safe to fill), and a dropped cell whose route price impact exceeded the
  absolute backstop. Unlike `slippage_exceeded`, neither cap is caller-tunable, so
  raising `max_slippage_bps` will not clear them; do not prompt for that.

  The cap tracks how live the reference is rather than the clock: outside the regular
  session the check may measure against a live market price instead of the previous
  close. The reference it used is internal and is NOT the `tradfi_reference` on a
  successful quote; do not reconstruct the check from that field. Treat the refusal as
  transient: neither a smaller size nor a higher `max_slippage_bps` clears it, but a
  re-quote 30–60s later may.

- `market_closed`: the listing's trading session is shut (weekend, overnight for a
  regular-hours-only listing, or a US market holiday). Refused **before** signing, so
  nothing was committed. Not size- or slippage-tunable: resubmit when the session
  reopens. Sessions are per-listing, and some listings close **per chain** rather than
  as a whole, so a `chain`-pinned request can be refused while another chain still
  serves the ticker. Retry unpinned, or on another chain from `available_chains`, before
  waiting out the session.

- `price_implausible`: the quote sits so far from the reference that we do not trust our
  own arithmetic, so we will not execute on it. No size, no `max_slippage_bps` and no
  acknowledgement clears it; a re-quote may.

- `reference_unavailable` is a **retained wire word with no current producer**. A
  missing reference used to refuse the quote; it is now served, with
  `tradfi_reference: null` and a `no_reference` entry in `warnings[]`. Keep parsing the
  value: it is still published, so a client that models it does not break, but do not
  build a flow around receiving it.

- `insufficient_balance` describes **your own wallet**, not the venue: it is short the
  spent token on that chain, so fund it and re-quote. On a Solana leg, the venue refused
  your wallet for the spent token (a buy whose wallet is short of USDC or has no USDC
  account, or a sell short of the shares it asks to sell; a Solana leg the venue still
  quotes is not checked against your balance again at submit, so a wallet short at
  submit fails that leg as `not_landed`).

  Under `priority: "speed"` a buy's Solana leg is refused before any venue is asked when
  your `sol_wallet` reads short the amount and none of your other wallets covers it
  either (when one does, see `cross_chain_route_unavailable`).

  A speed leg on any other chain refuses on the same condition: `chain`-pinned, the one
  shape where that leg is the only candidate, its refusal becomes the whole answer;
  unpinned, it drops that leg from the response (never a relayed fallback) and the
  response carries a `speed_route_unavailable` warning. (A missing router allowance is
  never a refusal on either shape; the quote bundles the approve.)

- `no_market_maker_fill`: no market maker or route answered for this size at this
  moment. Not slippage-tunable. A larger order may clear it (see `min_notional_usdc`
  when present), or a re-quote later.

- `insufficient_gas`: a Solana leg was refused and your `sol_wallet` holds under 0.002
  SOL, or under 0.01 SOL when the trade must create its output token account. Fund the
  wallet with SOL and re-quote; a larger order will not clear it.

  Never returned for `quote_only` or for `/quote/preview`, which spend none of your SOL,
  nor on a request carrying `sol_fee_payer`, which skips the SOL check. That request
  still sends a market-maker order bound to your `sol_wallet`, which can be refused when
  the wallet cannot cover the rent of a token account the trade opens; that refusal
  reads `no_market_maker_fill`.

- `cross_chain_wallet_missing`: under `priority: "speed"`, a buy could only be served
  cross-chain from a chain whose wallet the request did not include. Send both
  `sol_wallet` and `eth_wallet`.

- `payout_route_unavailable`: `/quote/sell` with `payout_chain` only. You hold enough in
  your `chain`/`protocol` scope, but not enough of it can pay out on `payout_chain` (see
  that field for which positions can), or the cross-chain route for a position that
  could pay out was refused or could not land. Not a holdings problem: pay out on
  another chain, send no `payout_chain` to sell each position on its own chain, or
  re-quote later.

- `cross_chain_route_unavailable`: a `priority: "speed"` buy only. Another of your
  wallets holds enough to fund the order (on `/quote/preview`, which reads no balance,
  the whole amount is assumed to sit on `origin_chain`, `sol` when absent), but no
  cross-chain route reached the leg: the route was refused or could not be completed, or
  the listing has none on that chain (on Solana, a leg your `sol_wallet` cannot fund is
  never served on its own chain instead; an `eth` leg never is under `"speed"`).

  `warnings[]` names each such leg with its own `reason`. Fund the named leg's own chain
  and re-quote; a refused route may also clear on a later re-quote.

warnings.description:
Present only on a `priority: "speed"` buy or preview refusal that dropped legs it would
otherwise have disclosed, or left out listings it never quotes. Two codes appear today,
each once per `chain`/`protocol`:

- `cross_chain_route_unavailable` (the same entry a served quote's `warnings[]` carries
  for that leg)
- `speed_route_unavailable` with `reason: no_speed_venue`, naming a listing whose
  own-chain venue `"speed"` never tries (an `eth` or `bnb` gasless order, or Reality on
  `arbitrum`).

An `eth` listing can carry both codes: its cross-chain route was tried and failed, and
its own-chain venue was not tried. A `no_speed_venue` entry means the same request
without `priority` would ask that venue: retry without it if a fill that can take
minutes is acceptable.

A listing whose session is closed is not named. Handle an unrecognised `code` as
described under `TradeWarning`. A refusal carries no `warnings_ack_token`: there is
nothing to submit.

BasketPriceUnavailableError.description:
Only reachable on **`/quote/buy`**, and only for a **basket** listing
(`MAG7X`, the Ondo Intelligent Portfolio). A basket has no single
underlying, so no reference market price exists for it and the usual
reference check cannot run; the one sanity check left is the issuer's
own published price. This refusal means that price was missing,
non-positive, or older than an hour.

`/quote/sell` never returns this: an exit is never gated on the issuer's
price feed, so a holder can always get out.

Distinct from `no_routes`: a route existed and the venue was fine, and
the refusal lands before any venue is asked for a price. Treat it as
transient and retry in a few minutes; no size or slippage change clears
it, and no other ticker is affected.

user_op_hash.description: Present only when the conflict is on a `user_operation` leg: the ERC-4337 op hash the earlier submit owns (its `tx_hash` is null until the bundle mines).

WalletNotDelegatedError.description: A `chain`-pinned `priority: "speed"` + `execution: "user_operation"` request whose `eth_wallet` carries code on that chain other than an EIP-7702 delegation to Alchemy Modular Account v2 (a wallet with no code is quoted: it delegates in its first operation through `eip7702Auth`). Only the caller can clear it (re-delegate to Modular Account v2, then re-quote), or re-quote with `execution: "transaction"` for the raw-transaction shape.

sol_signature.description:
Base64 raw Ed25519 signature over the canonical challenge. Required
when `sol_wallet` is present in the same request.

eth_signature.description:
`0x`-prefixed 65-byte EIP-191 `personal_sign` signature. Required when
`eth_wallet` is present in the same request.

issued_at.description:
Unix seconds. Server accepts up to **300 s past / 30 s future**;
outside that window → `401 ownership_proof_skewed`.

bnb_address.description: Token address on BNB Smart Chain (56), Ondo's and xStocks' third deployment. **Optional, and absent (not null) while the bnb venue is closed**: the key itself is withheld, so the block is byte-identical to its pre-bnb shape. `null` while the key IS present means the usual thing: this protocol does not list this ticker on 56. Treat "absent" and "null" identically; do not branch on the difference. Never present on the `backpack` block.

sol_min_trade_size_usd.description:
Per-cell measured minimum for this protocol on Solana, in whole USDC.
Same semantics as the ticker-level `min_trade_size_usd`: **absent means
no minimum is known**, never zero, and it is advisory rather than a gate.
Present only when the probe has measured this specific cell recently.

**Firm, taker-bound:** on a cell a market maker fills, each size is
asked as a quote bound to a funded wallet, so the minimum is a size a
market maker quoted to fill for a funded taker, not a price-only
preview (a pool-priced cell's quote is binding already). Until a cell
has been measured this way it may keep its earlier figure for a
transition period.

Market makers' own minimums move by day, so a smaller order may still be
refused; the refusal then names a size in `min_notional_usdc`. A position
worth less than this may not be sellable on Solana until it is topped up,
so avoid partial sells that leave less than it behind.

eth_min_trade_size_usd.description: Per-cell measured minimum for this protocol on Ethereum. Same presence and advisory semantics as `sol_min_trade_size_usd`, but measured from price quotes for an unfunded wallet, so it is an estimate rather than a firm one.

bnb_min_trade_size_usd.description: Per-cell minimum for this protocol on BNB Smart Chain (56): measured, or the venue's own floor where it is known before measurement, whichever is higher. Measured like `eth_min_trade_size_usd`. Rides the same conditional as `bnb_address`: always absent while the bnb venue is closed, and while this protocol has no 56 deployment for the ticker.

sol_tradability.description: Per-cell probe warning for this protocol on Solana. `thin`: the cell fills, but not at every size below `sol_min_trade_size_usd`. `untradable`: nothing filled at any size across a full measurement window, and no minimum accompanies it. **Neither value disables the cell**; quotes are still accepted for both. Absent means unmeasured or unwarned, never healthy-with-value-null. Chain-suffixed because this block spans a Solana and an Ethereum cell.

sol_warn_reason.description: Why the Solana cell is warned, strongest evidence first. Absent when unwarned, or when the warn predates reason recording. Not stable over a cell's lifetime: a `low_volume` warn that later kills a real order flips to `settlement_failure`.

sol_thin_since.description: When the Solana warning was first raised. Present exactly when `sol_tradability` is.

eth_tradability.description: Per-cell probe warning for this protocol on Ethereum. See `sol_tradability`.

eth_warn_reason.description: Why the Ethereum cell is warned, strongest evidence first. See `sol_warn_reason`.

eth_thin_since.description: When the Ethereum warning was first raised. Present exactly when `eth_tradability` is.

token_ticker.description: Issuer's wrapped-token symbol (`<TICKER>on` Ondo, `<TICKER>x` xStocks). Null when not listed.

RobinhoodListing.description: Robinhood Chain (4663) venue listing. Single-chain, so one `address` instead of the sol/eth pair; token decimals stay internal.

min_trade_size_usd.description: Measured minimum for this single-cell venue, in whole USDC. **Absent means no minimum is known**, never zero, and it is advisory rather than a gate.

tradability.description: Probe warning for this single-cell venue. `thin`: the cell fills, but not at every size below `min_trade_size_usd`. `untradable`: nothing filled at any size across a full measurement window, and no minimum accompanies it. **Neither value disables the cell**; quotes are still accepted for both. Absent means unmeasured or unwarned, never healthy-with-value-null. Bare rather than chain-suffixed: this block names exactly one cell.

warn_reason.description: Why the cell is warned, strongest evidence first. Absent when unwarned, or when the warn predates reason recording. Not stable over a cell's lifetime: a `low_volume` warn that later kills a real order flips to `settlement_failure`.

token_ticker.description: Bare stock symbol (Robinhood Stock Tokens carry no on/x suffix). Null when not listed.

currency.description: ISO-4217 quote currency of the underlying listing, "USD" for every US row. Every other price on this block is already converted to USD.

price_native.description: The price as the exchange quotes it, before conversion, so a client can render e.g. HK$446.20 without re-deriving it. Equal to current_price_usd when currency is "USD".

change_24h_pct.description: Percent change in the LISTING's own currency, not converted; a ratio does not convert, and doing it correctly would need yesterday's FX rate.

market_cap_usd.description: Null when the feed serves the line without a market cap (funds, newly listed board codes). Converted to USD like every other price here.

volume_shares.description: Shares traded in the current session, not a trailing average and not USD (contrast onchain volume_24h_usd). Null when the feed omits it.

volume_1d_usd.description: Session dollar volume, volume_shares × current_price_usd, rounded to whole dollars, so it is directly comparable to the onchain volume_24h_usd. Null exactly when volume_shares is null.

AnchorSource.description: Which reference a premium_vs_anchor_pct was measured against, the live regular-session print, the aftermarket print while it is still printing, or the frozen regular-session close. Never the on-chain mark - the premium measures an on-chain price, so anchoring it there would measure that price against itself.
