premium_vs_tradfi_pct.description: DEPRECATED - measured against tradfi.current_price_usd, which freezes at the regular-session close, so it overstates the premium overnight and at weekends. Use premium_vs_anchor_pct, which names the reference it used.

premium_vs_anchor_pct.description: Signed percent of avg_share_price_usd against the anchor named by anchor_source. Null when no tradfi reference resolves at all, in which case anchor_source is absent.
Signed percent of share_price_usd against the anchor named by anchor_source. Null when no tradfi reference resolves at all, in which case anchor_source is absent.

coinbase.description: Coinbase B20 on Base (8453). Carries the same supply gate as the listing: an unminted cell prices `null`.

bstocks.description:
bStocks on BNB Smart Chain (56). Carries the same supply gate as the listing: an unminted cell prices `null`.
**Optional, and absent (not null) while bStocks is not offered** (the bnb venue or bStocks switched off): the same key-dark contract as `bnb_address` on the listing blocks. When present it is emitted last.

min_trade_size_usd.description:
Smallest order size, in whole USDC, we have measured filling for this
ticker on any venue (the cheapest across cells, since a buy routes to
whichever cell can serve it).

**Absent means no minimum is known**, not that there is none: the
listing has not been measured recently enough to say. Fall back to the
$3 product floor. Never treat an absent field as `0`.

Advisory. A quote below this is still accepted and still goes to the
venue; it is simply likely to be refused. Measured in-session, and
published unchanged outside it as a valid lower bound; off-session
minimums are higher, never lower.

tradability.description:
Ticker-level roll-up of the per-cell warnings below. Present only when
**every** measured cell for this ticker is warned, not when any one is.
A ticker with one healthy measured cell is healthy somewhere and carries
nothing, so a single dead venue can never label a live listing.

The word follows the cheapest floor, exactly as it does per cell. `thin`:
every measured cell is warned and `min_trade_size_usd` is published
alongside. `untradable`: every measured cell is warned and none filled
at any size, so no minimum accompanies it. Cells the probe has not
measured are not counted either way, so `untradable` is a statement about
the measured surface, not proof that no venue can fill.

**Neither value means the listing is disabled.** Quotes are still
accepted for both; this is guidance to show a user before they try,
not a gate.

warn_reason.description:
Why the ticker is warned, strongest evidence first: a real order that
terminally expired, then the venue stating it holds no price for the
pair, then a full window of quiet auctions with no fill, then no
value-bearing on-chain settlement in the census window, then a
low-volume proxy.

Present only alongside `tradability`; absent when the warn predates
reason recording; that is "reason not recorded", never "no reason".
Rolled up as the **strongest** reason across the warned cells, not the
cheapest cell's, and not stable over a listing's lifetime: the value
changes when stronger evidence arrives. Read the per-cell
`sol_warn_reason` / `eth_warn_reason` / `warn_reason` on the venue
blocks below before committing to a cell.

There is no ticker-level `thin_since`: one stamp cannot date several
cells' warnings; take it per cell.

BstocksListing.description:
bStocks venue listing on BNB Smart Chain (56). Single-chain, so one `address` instead of
the sol/eth pair; token decimals stay internal.

**The whole block is OPTIONAL and is ABSENT while bStocks is not offered** (the bnb venue
or bStocks switched off), not present-with-nulls. bStocks lists on no other chain, so a
dark venue leaves nothing for the block to describe. This is the same key-dark rule as
`bnb_address` on the ondo/xstocks blocks and `onchain.bstocks` on `/stocks/prices`.

**Supply-gated**, exactly like `CoinbaseListing`: a cell stays hidden until real supply
exists. `address` and `token_ticker` are `null`, `bnb` is not added to `available_chains`
on its account, and a quote returns `422 no_routes`. `min_trade_size_usd` and the warn trio
(`tradability`, `warn_reason`, `thin_since`) are gated with them, so a hidden cell never
publishes a minimum or a warning for a venue the same response says does not exist.

**Listing is not tradeability here.** Many minted, priced bStocks cells carry no price
feed at the execution venue and refuse permanently (`422 no_routes`,
`reason: "no_price_feed"`). Read `tradability` / `min_trade_size_usd` before quoting.

share_multiplier.description: Shares per token, read live on chain each catalog refresh from the token's own scaled-UI-amount multiplier (ERC-8056 as adopted for BEP-20 by BEP-677). Not a static 1:1: it moves on splits and dividends.

min_trade_size_usd.description: Measured minimum for this single-cell venue, in whole USDC. **Absent means no minimum is known**, never zero, and it is advisory rather than a gate.

tradability.description: Probe warning for this cell. See `CoinbaseListing.tradability`.

warn_reason.description: Why the cell is warned. See `CoinbaseListing.warn_reason`.

token_ticker.description: Issuer's token symbol (`<TICKER>B`, e.g. `TSLAB`; a share class drops its dot, so `BRK.B` is `BRKBB`). Null when not listed.

BackpackListing.description:
Backpack Securities venue listing on Solana. Same shape as the `ondo` and `xstocks` blocks;
Backpack deploys on Solana only, so `eth_address` is always `null` and the `eth_*` fields
never appear.

**Optional, and absent while the venue is not offered.** When the key is present, a cell is
listed only once its token has real supply: until then `sol_address` and `token_ticker` are
`null`, `sol` is not added to `available_chains` on its account, and
`sol_min_trade_size_usd` and the `sol_` warn trio are gated with them. A ticker only this
venue carries is not served at all while its cell is unlisted. `token_ticker` is the bare
stock symbol (Backpack tokens carry no on/x suffix).

CoinbaseListing.description:
Coinbase B20 venue listing on Base (8453). Single-chain, so one `address`
instead of the sol/eth pair; token decimals stay internal.

**Supply-gated.** Coinbase deployed its B20 tokens unminted, and a cell stays
hidden until real supply exists: `address` and `token_ticker` are `null`, `base`
is omitted from `available_chains`, and a quote returns `422 no_routes`. The
listed set therefore grows over time; read this endpoint rather than hardcoding.
`min_trade_size_usd` and the warn trio (`tradability`, `warn_reason`,
`thin_since`) are gated with them, so a hidden cell never publishes a minimum
or a warning for a venue the same response says does not exist.

min_trade_size_usd.description: Measured minimum for this single-cell venue, in whole USDC. **Absent means no minimum is known**, never zero, and it is advisory rather than a gate.

tradability.description: Probe warning for this single-cell venue. `thin`: the cell fills, but not at every size below `min_trade_size_usd`. `untradable`: nothing filled at any size across a full measurement window, and no minimum accompanies it. **Neither value disables the cell**; quotes are still accepted for both. Absent means unmeasured or unwarned, never healthy-with-value-null. Bare rather than chain-suffixed: this block names exactly one cell.

warn_reason.description: Why the cell is warned, strongest evidence first. Absent when unwarned, or when the warn predates reason recording. Not stable over a cell's lifetime: a `low_volume` warn that later kills a real order flips to `settlement_failure`.

token_ticker.description: Bare stock symbol (B20 tokens carry no on/x suffix). Null when not listed.

RealityListing.description:
Reality rToken venue listing on Arbitrum One (42161). Single-chain, so one `address`
instead of the sol/eth pair; token decimals stay internal.

**Supply-gated, like `coinbase`, PLUS the venue kill switch.** A cell stays hidden while
either gate is closed: `address` and `token_ticker` are `null`, `arbitrum` is omitted from
`available_chains`, and a quote returns `422 no_routes`. The listed set therefore grows
over time; read this endpoint rather than hardcoding. `min_trade_size_usd` and the warn
trio (`tradability`, `warn_reason`, `thin_since`) are gated with them, so a hidden cell
never publishes a minimum or a warning for a venue the same response says does not exist.

min_trade_size_usd.description: Measured minimum for this single-cell venue, in whole USDC. **Absent means no minimum is known**, never zero, and it is advisory rather than a gate.

tradability.description: Probe warning for this single-cell venue. `thin`: the cell fills, but not at every size below `min_trade_size_usd`. `untradable`: nothing filled at any size across a full measurement window, and no minimum accompanies it. **Neither value disables the cell**; quotes are still accepted for both. Absent means unmeasured or unwarned, never healthy-with-value-null. Bare rather than chain-suffixed: this block names exactly one cell.

warn_reason.description: Why the cell is warned, strongest evidence first. Absent when unwarned, or when the warn predates reason recording. Not stable over a cell's lifetime: a `low_volume` warn that later kills a real order flips to `settlement_failure`.

token_ticker.description: Bare stock symbol (rTokens carry no on/x suffix). Null when not listed.

StockExchange.description: The listing venue a stock trades on, and the source of `exchange_country` and `data_delay`. Deliberately not the full exchange universe: it enumerates the venues this catalog serves, and grows without a breaking change; treat an unlisted value as a new venue, not an error.

StockDataDelay.description: How fresh the TradFi tape for this venue is. `realtime` is the live quote; `delayed_15m` means every price on the item, including `tradfi`, trails the market by about 15 minutes and must be labelled as delayed wherever it is shown.

StockDetailListing.description: One real (protocol, chain, address) token deployment for this ticker: the tuple you forward to the quote routes as `protocol` + `chain`. Combos the ticker does not list are simply absent, and a supply-gated `coinbase`, `reality` or `backpack` cell publishes no entry at all until its token is minted (`backpack` additionally stays absent while that venue is switched off). Token decimals stay internal; read them on-chain.

min_trade_size_usd.description: Smallest order size, in whole USDC, measured filling on THIS cell, or the venue's own floor where it is known before measurement, whichever is higher. **Absent means no minimum is known**, never zero, and it is advisory rather than a gate.

tradability.description: Probe warning for this one cell. `thin`: the cell fills, but not at every size below `min_trade_size_usd`. `untradable`: nothing filled at any size across a full measurement window, and no minimum accompanies it. **Neither value disables the cell**; quotes are still accepted for both. Absent means unmeasured or unwarned, never healthy-with-value-null.

warn_reason.description: Why the cell is warned, strongest evidence first. Absent when unwarned, or when the warn predates reason recording. Not stable over a cell's lifetime: a `low_volume` warn that later kills a real order flips to `settlement_failure`.

ExtendedHoursBlock.description: Last pre/post-market print: a sibling of `tradfi`, never a substitute for it, whose fields all stay anchored to the regular session. Null whenever no honest value exists: during the regular session (the feed is stale then), when the ticker has no extended print, when `tradfi` is null (no anchor for the change), or when the print is not newer than `tradfi.as_of`. The feed prints only inside 04:00–20:00 ET and then holds its last value, so overnight and at weekends this stays populated with the final post-market print; label staleness off `as_of` rather than assuming it is live.

change_pct.description: The same difference in percent, against the regular-session close. May be negative.

session.description: Which extended window this print came from, independent of `market_session`. Overnight `market_session` is `closed` while this stays `post`.

as_of.description: Timestamp of the extended print (unix seconds).

date.description: ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`.

NextEarnings.description: The ticker's nearest scheduled report inside a 30-day horizon. The block is null when no report falls in that window (or when the calendar read faulted), never a farther date.

eps_estimate.description: Consensus EPS estimate. Null when none is published for the report.

NewsItem.description: One stored headline for this ticker, newest first, at most 10 per response. There is no image field: the vendor's image host is not part of this plane's shape.

publisher.description: The news outlet that published the story.

type.description: Story class; `stock` for a symbol-scoped story, `press_release` for an issuer release. Open vocabulary: a value you do not recognise is a new class, not a schema violation.

StockDetailResponse.description:
Everything the catalog knows about one ticker.

Every block backed by I/O is fault-isolated and degrades to `null` on its own, so any block
can be null because its fetch failed. For `tradfi`, `extended_hours`, `analyst`,
`analyst_grades` and `earnings`, null **also** means "no such value exists for this ticker
right now", no coverage, no scheduled report, no extended print, no priced reference, and
the two causes are not distinguishable from the response; read each field's own
description for what its null covers.

`news` is the one block that separates them: `[]` means we hold no headlines, `null` means
the read failed, so it is the only one worth re-reading on an empty answer.

There is deliberately no `onchain` block: per-protocol on-chain prices live on
`GET /stocks/prices`.

description.description: Company/asset description. Null when none is stored for this ticker; it is refreshed on the catalog's own recheck cadence, not on your read.

logo_url.description: Absolute `https` URL of the company logo, served from Treasures' own object store rather than the upstream source. Null when no logo has been mirrored for this ticker.

exchange.description: The venue this stock lists on. **Absent** (never null) when we have not resolved one, so treat "no key" as unknown rather than as a US listing. Present together with `exchange_country` and `data_delay` or not at all.

exchange_country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country of the **exchange**, not of the issuer. Tencent lists in `HK` while its issuer country is CN; do not read this as domicile. Derived from `exchange`, so it is absent whenever `exchange` is.

data_delay.description: Freshness class of this row's TradFi prices, derived from `exchange`. Absent whenever `exchange` is; absent does **not** mean realtime.

display_ticker.description: The ticker as it should be rendered; `0700.HK` for the row keyed `700`. **Absent for a US row**, whose bare `ticker` is already the display form. Render `display_ticker ?? ticker`. Identity stays on `ticker`: every path segment and every other endpoint uses that, never this.

tradfi.description: Null when no reference price resolves for the ticker, a basket, or any row the tape does not cover, as well as on a fault.

extended_hours.description: Null for the ordinary reasons listed on `ExtendedHoursBlock` (the regular session, no extended print, no `tradfi` anchor, a print no newer than `tradfi.as_of`), as well as on a fault.

market_session.description: Current US-equity session: global, not per-ticker, and holiday/half-day aware. Picks which of `tradfi` / `extended_hours` to render. Null when the session read faulted.

is_holiday.description: True on a NASDAQ holiday **and on its eve** (an early-close day reports this too, not just the holiday's own date). Null when the session read faulted.

holiday_name.description: Name of the holiday when `is_holiday` is true; null otherwise, and null when the session read faulted.

analyst.description: Consensus rating and price target. Null when no analyst covers the ticker, and null on a fault; the two are not distinguishable here.

analyst_grades.description: Latest grade per firm, most recent first, at most 15 firms. Null when no firm covers the ticker, and null on a fault.

earnings.description: Null when no report falls inside the 30-day horizon, and null on a fault.

news.description: Up to 10 stored headlines, newest first. `[]` means we hold none for this ticker; `null` means the read faulted.

page.description: The page served. Present only when the request sent `page`.

next_page.description: The next page, or null on the last. Present only when the request sent `page`.

total.description: Rows matching `q` across all pages. Present only when the request sent `page`.

StockSortKey.description: List sort key. All but `ticker` read the `tradfi` block; a stock missing the metric sorts last in both directions, and ties break by ticker.

SignableSolanaTx.description:
On a `priority:"speed"` cross-chain leg whose origin is sol (`origin_chain: "sol"`), this
transaction's fee payer is your own sol wallet, which is also the deposit's signer: sign it
as issued, with one signature, and your wallet pays the network fee. To have a sponsor pay
instead, recompile the message with the sponsor's key as payer and have it co-sign; your
signature is still required. Every account key is static (no address-lookup tables), and
the submit-time bind accepts only the quoted deposit plus compute-budget,
token-account-creation and sponsor-paid rent-transfer instructions.

A cross-chain sell leg on `sol` (`payout_chain` present) is signed the same way, with your
sol wallet as fee payer, but its message uses address-lookup tables, and a sponsor's
recompile may reference only those quoted tables. The bind accepts every quoted instruction
unchanged and in its quoted order, plus at most four extra compute-budget,
token-account-creation and sponsor-paid rent-transfer instructions, and the signed
transaction must fit Solana's 1232-byte limit.

On a same-chain `sol` leg that carries `sol_fee_payer`, the transaction has two required
signers, the `sol_fee_payer` (the fee payer) and your sol wallet: both sign it **as
issued**, and it must never be recompiled.

Any other same-chain `sol` leg is signed by your sol wallet alone.

SignableEvmTypedData.description:
EIP-712 typed data for a gasless EVM order: the **default** payload on every EVM leg. eth
(Ethereum mainnet), robinhood (Robinhood Chain / 4663), base (Base / 8453), arbitrum
(Arbitrum One / 42161) and bnb (BNB Smart Chain / 56), which all share the same sign-only
model.

Exactly one payload per leg; sign it with `eth_signTypedData_v4` and return the signature
to `/trade/submit`. A resolver settles the signed order on-chain, so the caller broadcasts
nothing and pays no native gas for the trade. The one on-chain step is the wallet's own
one-time ERC-20 allowance of the spent token to that chain's settlement contract, sent with
that chain's native gas.

Two exceptions carry `SignableEvmTx` instead (a complete transaction, and not gasless):

- a robinhood or base leg under `priority: "speed"`
- a `bnb` + `bstocks` leg at **every** priority (bStocks has no gasless route; you pay BNB
  gas and Treasures broadcasts).

eth, arbitrum and the other bnb cells always carry this shape: eth is never quoted under
`priority: "speed"` at all, and arbitrum (Reality), bnb + `ondo` and bnb + `xstocks` have
no speed-route alternative to carry instead.

**On a gasless `bnb` leg the signing deadline is much shorter: about 17 seconds**, against
about 60 s on eth (the venue's auction starts sooner). The leg's own `expires_at` is that
deadline: read it per leg, not off the response's top-level value. Sign a bnb leg
immediately; do not batch it behind a human confirmation or a hardware-wallet round trip.
Past the deadline the order is not dead: the auction is live and still fillable along its
decay curve, at a worse price.

typed_data.description: EIP-712 typed-data object for the gasless EVM order; sign with `eth_signTypedData_v4`.

SignableEvmTx.description:
A **complete unsigned EVM transaction**. Three producers share this shape.

- **(1)** The speed-route payload, returned on a `priority: "speed"` leg (robinhood / base)
  and on every `bnb` + `bstocks` leg whatever the `priority` (`evm_legacy_tx`, BNB gas):
  `role` is `"approve"` then `"swap"`.
- **(2)** A `priority:"speed"` **cross-chain** leg's EVM origin under
  `execution:"transaction"` (`origin_chain` present on the leg): `role` is `"approve"` then
  `"deposit"`: the swap happens off-chain via the destination fill, this transaction only
  moves your stable off the origin chain, and the `approve` is **exact-amount**, not
  max-uint256 (a deliberate departure from the same-chain speed route's unlimited
  approval, since this arm targets a bridge depository, not a swap router).
- **(3)** A **cross-chain sell** leg on `eth`, `base` or `bnb` (`payout_chain` present on
  the leg): always both payloads, on the leg's own `chain`: an **exact-amount** `approve`
  of the tokens sold, served every time whatever allowance the wallet already has, then
  the `deposit`, which sells them on that chain and sends the USDC to `payout_chain`.

Every field the transaction needs is already in the bytes: `nonce`, `gas` and the fee pair
are server-completed, so sign `tx_hex` **as-is** with `signTransaction` and return
`{ type: "evm_signed_tx", signed_tx_hex }`; do not re-estimate, re-nonce or re-serialize
it, and do not broadcast it yourself. Treasures broadcasts the signed bytes; any edited
field fails the submit-time bind as `invalid_signature`.

`type` is `evm_eip1559_tx` when the chain reports EIP-1559 fees and `evm_legacy_tx` when it
reports a flat `gas_price`; the two carry the same fields apart from that pair. The fee
fields are **mirrors of what is already in `tx_hex`**, present only when the bytes carry
them: read them for display, never to rebuild the transaction, and treat an absent one as
"this transaction does not set it" rather than as zero. The wallet must hold native gas on
the leg's chain.

**No pre-approval is needed:** when the wallet has not approved the spender yet (and on
every cross-chain sell leg), the leg carries **two** payloads: `role: "approve"` (nonce n)
followed by `role: "swap"` or `role: "deposit"` (nonce n+1). Sign and return **both**, in
that order. An approved wallet gets the single second payload.

Treasures sends the approve, waits for its receipt, then sends the swap/deposit; the leg's
`tx_hash` is that second payload's from the start, but it becomes visible on chain only
after the approve mines (seconds). Sign each payload as-is: the nonces are consecutive and
a resigned or reordered one fails the bind as `invalid_signature`.

role.description:
Which transaction this is.

- `swap` is a same-chain speed-route trade.
- On a cross-chain buy leg (`origin_chain` present) `deposit` is the off-ramp to the
  bridge depository, never a swap in itself: the exchange happens on the destination
  chain.
- On a cross-chain sell leg (`payout_chain` present) `deposit` sells the stock on the
  leg's `chain` and sends the USDC to `payout_chain`.
- `approve` precedes a buy's `deposit` or a `swap` only on a wallet with no allowance to
  the relevant spender at quote time, and precedes a sell's `deposit` every time:
  **exact-amount** ahead of a `deposit`, max-uint256 ahead of a `swap`.

Branch on `role`, never on array position, and never sign only `signable_payloads[0]`
when there are two.

from.description: The signing wallet, i.e. the same EVM EOA the quote was bound to.

tx_hex.description: Unsigned RLP transaction, 0x-prefixed. Sign exactly these bytes.

tx_base64.description: The same unsigned transaction as base64, for callers whose signer takes bytes.

approval_spender.description: On the `swap` payload: the on-chain router the swap pulls the spent token through, **on this leg's chain**, informational; the bundled `approve` payload (when present) already targets it. On a `deposit` payload: the contract the `approve` payload grants, informational. `null` on the `approve` payload, which needs no allowance itself.

chain_id.description: EVM chain id these bytes are signed for.

nonce.description: Server-read pending nonce, already encoded in `tx_hex` (n on an `approve`, n+1 on the `swap` or `deposit` that follows it). One in-flight speed trade per wallet per chain; a second signed at the same nonce fails as `nonce_conflict`.

gas.description: Gas limit, already encoded in the bytes.

max_fee_per_gas.description: EIP-1559 only, never with `gas_price`. Optional: present exactly when `tx_hex` sets it.

max_priority_fee_per_gas.description: EIP-1559 only. Optional and independent of `max_fee_per_gas`: present exactly when `tx_hex` sets it, absent when the transaction carries no priority fee.

gas_price.description: Legacy only: sent instead of the 1559 pair, never alongside it. Present exactly when `tx_hex` sets it.

SignableEvmCalls.description:
The `execution: "user_operation"` speed-route leg (base or robinhood): the calls to pack
into ONE ERC-4337 v0.7 UserOperation from `sender` (your EIP-7702-delegated Modular
Account v2 wallet). Build it yourself (e.g. `@account-kit`):

- `execute(target, value, data)` for a single call, `executeBatch([...])` **in this order**
  for two
- sponsor it with your own paymaster (an unsponsored op is refused; the leg is ranked at
  $0 gas)
- sign it under `chain_id` and the v0.7 EntryPoint (`entry_point`; informational, the
  server pins it)
- return `{ type: "evm_user_operation", user_operation }`.

The server decodes `callData` and binds every call byte-for-byte to these, plus `sender` =
the quoted wallet, no `factory` / `factoryData`, zero `value` on every call, and a
non-empty `paymaster`; any mismatch is `invalid_signature`. A wallet with no code on the
chain delegates in this operation: send its signed EIP-7702 authorization as `eip7702Auth`
beside the op (see `SignedEvmUserOperation`). Exactly one per leg.

`approval_spender` is the router the `swap` call pulls through: what the `approve` call,
when present, grants (max-uint256).

**Cross-chain variant** (`priority:"speed"` with `origin_chain` present on the leg): the
SAME wire shape carries a `role:"deposit"` call in place of `role:"swap"`, `sender` is your
**origin**-chain wallet (not the destination-leg wallet), and `chain_id` may additionally
be `1` (Ethereum mainnet) for an eth-origin leg, a value the same-chain speed route never
returns.

**Cross-chain sell variant** (`payout_chain` present on a `/quote/sell` leg): the calls are
an `role:"approve"` of the stock for exactly the amount sold, then a `role:"deposit"`;
`sender` is your `eth_wallet`, `chain_id` the leg's own `chain` (`8453` or `1`), and
`approval_spender` what the deposit pulls the stock through.

chain_id.description:
The chain to sign and submit the op on:

- `8453` (base) or `4663` (robinhood) on a same-chain `priority:"speed"` leg
- on a cross-chain leg, the chain the deposit is made on, which may also be `1`
  (Ethereum): an eth-origin buy, or an `eth` sell paying out elsewhere.

CostBreakdownBps.description: Fee + slippage breakdown in basis points, informational. These fees are already deducted from `estimated_output_*` (the net deliverable) and reflected in `price_usdc_per_share`. The deduction is provider-dependent; do NOT reconstruct a gross amount as `estimated_output / (1 − fees)`; use `estimated_output_*` as-is.

dex_swap_fee_bps.description: Provider protocol + swap/execution fee. **Null on a cross-chain leg** (`origin_chain` present): the hop's cost is disclosed instead in `cross_chain_cost_bps`/`cross_chain_cost_usdc` on the leg, and a recorded `0` here would claim the venue charged nothing. Always a number on a same-chain leg.

integrator_fee_bps.description: Your own fee on this leg, net: your configured default, or the `integrator_fee_bps` you sent, stacked into the same on-wire fee as Treasures' and paid out to you. Always emitted; `0` on an anonymous quote or a leg whose venue could not collect it. Not yet in `required`, like `price_impact_bps`, so a strict validator built against an older copy of this spec keeps working.

estimated_slippage_bps.description: Execution tolerance: how far below the quote a fill may land. This is what `max_slippage_bps` bounds. On Solana it is 0 on a guaranteed-price or exact-orderbook fill; on EVM there is no separate tolerance signal, so it equals `price_impact_bps`.

price_impact_bps.description: Adverse route price impact: what this size costs against available depth; 0 when favorable or unreported. Informational: it is NOT charged against `max_slippage_bps` on Solana, so a quote may be returned with `price_impact_bps` above your cap. Display it alongside the price. A structurally broken market is still refused, by a separate non-tunable ceiling, as 422 `no_routes` with reason `price_off_reference`, never `slippage_exceeded`, since raising your cap cannot clear it.

slippage_vs_tradfi_bps.description: Signed; positive = unfavorable to you. Omitted when `tradfi_reference` is null; there was nothing to measure against.

LegGasless.description:
Who pays this leg's gas.

- `true`: a relayed order; you sign, a settlement network broadcasts, you spend no native
  gas.
- `false`: a speed-route leg (`priority: "speed"`), returned as a complete unsigned
  transaction you sign and Treasures broadcasts against **your** native balance on that
  chain. On a cross-chain leg (`origin_chain` present) that is the **origin** chain, not
  `chain`; a sol-origin cross-chain leg is `false` because your sol wallet pays the SOL
  network fee. A cross-chain sell leg (`payout_chain` present) is `false` whatever the
  `priority`: you pay the gas on the leg's own `chain`, where the sale is sent.

  The exception to both is the `execution: "user_operation"` lane, where your paymaster
  pays and any cross-chain leg is `true`. A same-chain `sol` leg carrying `sol_fee_payer`
  is `false`: no native gas leaves your user's wallet, but your `sol_fee_payer` pays it, so
  read `false` as "you or your `sol_fee_payer` pay".

Rides **every** kind of leg, not only speed ones; **absent** where the upstream never
reported it (some Solana legs), which is not the same claim as `false`; read the payload
`type` when it matters.

LegEstimatedGasUsd.description:
**Speed-route and cross-chain sell legs only** (absent on every relayed leg): the estimated
USD cost of the broadcast this leg asks you to fund, and the figure the route ranking
charged against this leg. `null` when no USD gas price was available; the leg still ranks,
just without its gas term, and a `speed_route_unpriced_gas` warning naming this leg's
`chain` says so.

That warning does **not** mean the leg fell back: this leg IS a speed-route leg and only its
gas figure is missing, so price the gas yourself before choosing it over a gasless leg.

On a cross-chain buy leg it prices the **origin** chain's transactions. A sol-origin or
user-operation cross-chain leg carries `null` with no warning: the SOL network fee is
neither estimated nor ranked, and a user operation's gas is your paymaster's.

A cross-chain sell leg (`payout_chain` present) carries it whatever the `priority`: on `eth`
or `base` it prices the `approve` and the sale on the leg's `chain` and is what the ranking
charges; it is `null`, with no warning, on `sol`, under `execution: "user_operation"` (your
paymaster pays), or when no USD gas price was available.

A same-chain `sol` leg carrying `sol_fee_payer` carries what that sponsor pays: the network
fees plus the rent of any token account the trade opens for your user's wallet, or `null`
when no USD price for SOL was available. It is not ranked.

An estimate over a live gas market: the signed transaction bounds what you can actually
spend, this string does not.

LegSolFeePayer.description: **Same-chain `sol` legs quoted with `sol_fee_payer` only.** Echoes the request's `sol_fee_payer` on a leg whose transaction it must co-sign and pay for: sign that leg's `solana_versioned_tx` with both the `sol_fee_payer` and your sol wallet, as issued. Absent on every other leg, including a `sol` leg filled by a market maker, which pays its own fee: sign that one with your sol wallet alone.

SolFeePayer.description:
A sol wallet you fund that pays the SOL network fees, and the rent of any token account the
trade opens, on every same-chain `sol` leg it can. Lets a wallet holding no SOL trade on
`sol`: without it, such a wallet is refused there with `422 no_routes`. Each `sol` leg is
then either a market-maker fill (no `sol_fee_payer` on the leg; the maker pays the fee) or a
leg carrying `sol_fee_payer`, which this wallet co-signs.

Every `ondo` leg is a market-maker fill, so this wallet never pays for one: a first buy of
an `ondo` token opens your user's token account at the user's own cost (about 0.01 SOL), and
a wallet short of it loses the `ondo` leg. Once sent, a `sol` leg that is not a market-maker
fill is only ever the sponsored one, so a sponsor that cannot pay fails the leg even when
your user's wallet holds SOL.

It must be **one fixed address** that signs from quote to submit: a fee payer whose address
changes between the two cannot sign the transaction it was quoted for. Requires `sol_wallet`
and must differ from it; refused with `quote_only: true`, which has nothing to sponsor.
Naming it proves nothing about it and grants nothing: the transaction does nothing until it
signs. It is screened like your wallets.

A first buy of a token opens your user's token account for roughly 0.0016 to 0.0021 SOL of
rent, paid by this wallet and kept by your user's wallet, so fund it for rent as well as
fees: when it cannot cover them, its `sol` legs are refused and the quote reads
`422 no_routes`. Cross-chain `sol` legs are unaffected. It covers only the quote it rides
on: send it on `/quote/sell` as well, because a sponsored buy does not sponsor the later
sell of the same position.

base_asset.description:
Base currency the caller spends; `usdc` on sol/eth/base/arbitrum/bnb legs, `usdg` on
robinhood legs. Disambiguates the `_usdc`-named fields (`price_usdc_per_share`,
`amount_usdc`) when the base is USDG, which shares USDC's 6-decimal scale.

**`usdc` is a wire enum, not a fungibility signal**: on `bnb` it is 18-decimal
Binance-Peg USDC, not a Circle deploy, and converting it to Circle USDC costs roughly 31
bps in and 7 to 9 bps out. Read `chain` alongside it before treating two legs as the
same money.

**On a cross-chain leg (`origin_chain` present) this names the ORIGIN's currency, not
the destination cell's**. For example, a robinhood-origin leg into an eth-priced cell
still carries `"usdg"`, because that is what actually left your wallet.

amount_base.description: Base amount spent, human-decimal, as the base-asset alias of `amount_usdc`.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds: **this leg's** signing deadline, and the one `/trade/submit` enforces when you sign this leg. Expiry is per leg because the venues' auction clocks differ: a `bnb` leg runs about 17 s where an `eth` leg runs about 60 s. The response's top-level `expires_at` is the EARLIEST leg's, safe for any leg but pessimistic for the longer-lived ones, so read this field once you have picked a leg. Omitted on `quote_only` previews and on `POST /quote/preview`.

origin_chain.description:
**Present only on a cross-chain leg, and its presence is what marks one**: a
`priority:"speed"` buy for a cell you are not funded on, reaching its destination
through a cross-chain hop. Names the chain your stable actually left (the request's
`origin_chain` whenever it sent one); `chain` above stays the destination cell (never
the origin), consistent with every other field on this leg.

- `eth` (including a `chain:["eth"]` pin), `sol/xstocks`, `sol/backpack`, `bnb/bstocks`,
  and `base` on an unpinned or multi-chain request are reachable cross-chain
- a single-chain `base`/`robinhood` pin always routes same-chain
- `robinhood`, `sol/ondo`, `eth/xstocks`, `bnb/ondo` and `bnb/xstocks` are never
  cross-chain destinations.
- `bnb` is a destination only: it is never an `origin_chain`.

`cross_chain_cost_bps` and `cross_chain_cost_usdc` disclose the hop's own cost. Absent on
every same-chain leg.

cross_chain_cost_bps.description: **Cross-chain legs only.** The hop's own cost in basis points (`swap_slippage_bps`, `gas_fee_bps`, `bridge_fee_bps`, `total_bps`), separate from `cost_breakdown_bps` above, whose `dex_swap_fee_bps` is `null` on this leg (the hop's swap cost lives here instead). `price_impact_bps` on `cost_breakdown_bps` equals this object's `swap_slippage_bps`.

cross_chain_cost_usdc.description: The same breakdown as `cross_chain_cost_bps`, in USDC.

signable_payloads.description: Omitted on `quote_only` previews and on every `POST /quote/preview` leg; the leg is non-executable.

tradability.description: Probe warning for **this leg's own cell**: an exact `(ticker, protocol, chain)` match, not a ticker roll-up. `thin`: the cell fills, but not at every size below its measured minimum. `untradable`: nothing filled at any size across a full measurement window. **Advisory, never a block**: the leg is still planned, priced and submittable, and there is no request param to exclude warned cells. Absent means unmeasured or unwarned, never healthy-with-value-null.

warn_reason.description: Why the cell is warned, strongest evidence first. Absent when unwarned, or when the warn predates reason recording. Not stable over a cell's lifetime: a `low_volume` warn that later kills a real order flips to `settlement_failure`.

base_asset.description: Base currency the caller receives; `usdc` on sol/eth/base/arbitrum/bnb legs, `usdg` on robinhood legs. Disambiguates the `_usdc`-named fields (`price_usdc_per_share`, `estimated_output_usdc`) when the base is USDG, which shares USDC's 6-decimal scale. On a cross-chain leg (`payout_chain` present) it names the payout chain's currency, always `usdc`. A same-chain `bnb` sell pays out **18-decimal Binance-Peg USDC**, a different token from Circle USDC; see `QuoteBuyLeg.base_asset`.

amount_base.description: Base amount received, human-decimal: the base-asset alias of `estimated_output_usdc` (equal value, base-denominated).

expires_at.description: Unix seconds: this leg's signing deadline. See `QuoteBuyLeg.expires_at` for why it is per leg. A **sell** submit must sign EVERY leg, so the deadline that actually binds a sell is the earliest of them, i.e. the top-level `expires_at`.

payout_chain.description:
**Present only on a cross-chain sell leg, and its presence is what marks one**: a
position sold on its own chain (`chain`/`protocol` above, unchanged) whose USDC is paid
out on this chain, to your wallet there, because you sent `payout_chain`. The sale and
the payout are one leg, with no separate payout step to submit.

`estimated_output_usdc` and `price_usdc_per_share` are what lands on this chain, net of
the route's fees; the network gas you pay to submit the sale is separate.
`cross_chain_cost_bps` and `cross_chain_cost_usdc` disclose the hop's own cost, and
`cost_breakdown_bps.dex_swap_fee_bps` is `null`. Absent on every same-chain leg.

origin_chain.description: Wire-shape parity with `/quote/buy`; never populated on a sell leg (a cross-chain sell carries `payout_chain` instead).

cross_chain_cost_bps.description: **Cross-chain legs only** (`payout_chain` present): the hop's own cost in basis points of the sale's USD value, as on a cross-chain buy leg. `price_impact_bps` on `cost_breakdown_bps` equals this object's `swap_slippage_bps`.

cross_chain_cost_usdc.description: The same breakdown as `cross_chain_cost_bps`, in USDC.

tradability.description: Probe warning for **this leg's own cell**, filtered to the sell side. Same two words as on a buy leg, but published only when `warn_reason` is side-neutral (see below), so a sell leg carries all three keys or none. **Advisory, never a block**: nothing here refuses an exit. No `min_trade_size_usd` accompanies a sell anywhere on the API: it is a USD buy floor while a sell is denominated in shares. A sell refused for its size names its own minimum instead, as `min_notional_usdc` on the `no_routes` refusal.

warn_reason.description:
Why the cell is warned. **Sell legs carry only the side-neutral reasons**:

- `low_volume` (a thin pool is a bad exit as surely as a bad entry)
- `no_price_feed` (no feed is no feed, either direction)
- `no_settlements` (nothing ever settling here is no less a dead end on exit).

The two buy-sided reasons, `no_fill_window` (the measurement ladder quotes buys) and
`settlement_failure` (recorded on buys only), say nothing about an exit and are
suppressed along with the whole trio, as is a warn whose reason was never recorded.

QuoteOriginChain.description:
Where the stable you will pay with sits (USDC; USDG on `robinhood`). Buy and preview only;
`/quote/sell` refuses it.

On the default route it changes the **ranking only**: a leg on any other chain ranks as if
it cost the measured transfer from this chain, so `quote_index: 0` is the cheapest leg for
money held here. That transfer cost is the route's measured fee only; it excludes the gas
you pay to send the transfer on this chain, which matters most on `eth`. No leg is added,
dropped or repriced, and a leg off this chain is still a same-chain leg: fund its chain
(for example through `/bridge/quote`) before you submit it.

Under `priority:"speed"` it is also the **only** chain a cross-chain leg may spend from
(`origin_chain` on such a leg is always this value); a cell already funded on its own chain
still trades there (`eth` aside: it has no `"speed"` route of its own, so an `eth`-funded
speed request returns no `eth` leg), and when this chain does not cover the amount no
cross-chain leg is offered at all. A single-chain `base` or `robinhood` pin is never
cross-chain, so there it is inert.

On `/quote/buy` the wallet for this chain must be in the request (`sol_wallet` for `sol`,
`eth_wallet` otherwise), else `400 invalid_request`. Absent or `null` = today's ranking and
origin choice.

chain.description: One chain pins routing to it. An array (one or more, unique) auto-routes within those chains only; `["x"]` is identical to `"x"`; a member the ticker has no cell on is dropped, and an empty intersection is 422 no_routes. null/omitted = every chain the ticker lists.

protocol.description: One protocol pins routing to it. An array (one or more, unique) auto-routes within those protocols only; `["x"]` is identical to `"x"`; a member the ticker has no cell on is dropped, and an empty intersection is 422 no_routes. Narrowing by protocol never relaxes admission: whatever survives still passes the same gates the unpinned route applies. null/omitted = every protocol the ticker lists. To exclude one, send the others.

preferred_chain.description: A preference, not a pin. The leg on this chain becomes `quote_index: 0` when the plan has one; the other legs keep their price order, and none is added or dropped. Must be one of the chains named in `chain` whenever `chain` is sent; a contradiction is `400 invalid_request`, never a silent fallback. Absent, or naming a chain the plan has no leg on, leaves the ordering exactly as it is today (cheapest first).

quote_only.description:
Price-only preview. When `true`, the quote is priced for a wallet that
need not hold the funds, but the result is non-executable: `quote_id`,
`expires_at`, and every leg's `signable_payloads` are omitted, nothing is
persisted, and there is no `/quote/{quote_id}/status` to poll or anything
to submit. `ownership_proof` is still required. Buy-only; sending it to
`/quote/sell` is rejected as an unknown field.

QuoteBuyRequest.description: At least one of `sol_wallet` / `eth_wallet` is required, with the matching signature in `ownership_proof`.

chain.description: One chain pins routing to it. An array (one or more, unique) auto-routes within those chains only; `["x"]` is identical to `"x"`; a member the ticker has no cell on is dropped, and an empty intersection is 422 no_routes. null/omitted = every chain the ticker lists.

protocol.description: One protocol pins routing to it. An array (one or more, unique) auto-routes within those protocols only; `["x"]` is identical to `"x"`; a member the ticker has no cell on is dropped, and an empty intersection is 422 no_routes. Narrowing by protocol never relaxes admission: whatever survives still passes the same gates the unpinned route applies. null/omitted = every protocol the ticker lists. To exclude one, send the others.

preferred_chain.description:
A preference, not a pin. The greedy fill runs over this chain's holdings first and over
everything still unfilled after, so it changes which cells fill, never which cells are
eligible, and never the all-or-nothing submit rule. A cell on this chain that cannot be
priced on the first pass rejoins the second pass alongside the other chains, so the
preference costs at most one extra quote attempt and can never leave a shortfall the
unpinned fill would have covered.

Must be one of the chains named in `chain` whenever `chain` is sent; a contradiction is
`400 invalid_request`. Absent = the plain greedy fill.

payout_chain.description:
Where the sale's USDC lands. Absent or `null` (the default) sells every position on its
own chain, exactly as a request without this field. Independent of `priority`.
Sell-only: sending it to `/quote/buy` or `/quote/preview` is `400 invalid_request`.

When set, every leg pays out USDC on this chain, to your own wallet there, and each
position you hold is planned on its own terms:
- a position on `payout_chain` sells on that chain as usual (under `priority: "speed"`
  it keeps the speed filter, so an `eth` position is left out when paying out on `eth`);
- a `sol/xstocks`, `sol/backpack`, `base/coinbase`, `eth/ondo` or `bnb/bstocks` position
  on another chain sells cross-chain as one leg, marked by `payout_chain` on that leg,
  whatever the `priority`;
- any other position (`sol/ondo`, `eth/xstocks`, `bnb/ondo`, `bnb/xstocks`, `robinhood`,
  `arbitrum`) is left out and named by a `cross_chain_route_unavailable` warning. It is
  never sold on its own chain instead, because that would pay out somewhere you did not
  ask for.

`400 invalid_request` (message prefixed `payout_chain: `) when the wallet for this chain
is missing (`sol_wallet` for `sol`, `eth_wallet` otherwise), or when nothing in your
`chain`/`protocol` scope can pay out here (for example a `robinhood` pin, or
`chain: ["eth"]` with `protocol: "xstocks"`).

Under `execution: "user_operation"` a `base` or `eth` position pays out cross-chain as
ONE `evm_calls` payload (an `approve` of the stock, then a `deposit`) that your
`eth_wallet` sends on the position's chain; a `sol` position keeps its
`solana_versioned_tx`; a `bnb/bstocks` position has no `user_operation` lane and is left
out with a `cross_chain_route_unavailable` warning (`disabled`). With a payout elsewhere,
`chain: ["eth"]` together with `priority: "speed"` is accepted: the `eth/ondo` position
sells cross-chain.

- `422 holdings_insufficient` when your holdings in scope fall short, wherever they sit.
- `422 no_routes` with `reason: payout_route_unavailable` when you hold enough, but not
  enough of it can pay out on this chain, or a cross-chain leg was refused or could not
  land. A leg that fails on our side does not count toward that reason; re-quote.

QuoteSellRequest.description: At least one of `sol_wallet` / `eth_wallet` is required, with the matching signature in `ownership_proof`.

QuotePreviewRequest.description: `QuoteBuyRequest` minus every wallet-bound field. `sol_wallet`, `eth_wallet`, `sol_fee_payer`, `ownership_proof` and `quote_only` are all rejected here as unknown keys; a preview binds no wallet, so there is nothing to prove ownership of and nothing that could be executed. `amount_usdc` is additionally capped at 1000000 on this route (unbounded on `/quote/buy`, which settles against a real balance): above it the request is a 400.

allOf.description: Preview-only bound; must be ≤ 1000000 USDC.

chain.description: One chain pins routing to it. An array (one or more, unique) auto-routes within those chains only; `["x"]` is identical to `"x"`; a member the ticker has no cell on is dropped, and an empty intersection is 422 no_routes. null/omitted = every chain the ticker lists.

protocol.description: One protocol pins routing to it. An array (one or more, unique) auto-routes within those protocols only; `["x"]` is identical to `"x"`; a member the ticker has no cell on is dropped, and an empty intersection is 422 no_routes. null/omitted = every protocol the ticker lists. To exclude one, send the others.

preferred_chain.description: A preference, not a pin: the leg on this chain becomes `quote_index: 0` when the preview has one, and the rest keep their price order. Must be one of the chains named in `chain` whenever `chain` is sent (`400 invalid_request` otherwise).

origin_chain.description: As on `/quote/buy`, except that the preview reads no balance: under `priority:"speed"` it prices as if the whole amount sits on this chain and nowhere else, so a leg on it is same-chain and a cross-chain-capable leg off it comes back cross-chain from it. `eth` is the exception on the first half: it has no `"speed"` route of its own, so a `"speed"` preview funded on `eth` returns no `eth` leg. Absent, a `"speed"` preview assumes `sol`, and the default route ranks exactly as it does today.

priority.description: Accepted here so a preview prices what an executable `speed` request would route. The preview binds no wallet, so the speed route is priced without one; its balance and allowance conditions surface only on `/quote/buy` or `/quote/sell`.

execution.description: Accepted so a preview prices the `user_operation` lane as it would execute (`gasless: true`, `estimated_gas_usd: "0"`). No wallet is bound, so the delegation check runs only on `/quote/buy` or `/quote/sell`.

IntegratorFeeBps.description: Your fee on this quote, net bps, overriding the default we configured for your key, up to your per-partner ceiling. Omit to use the default. Requires an `X-API-Key` (`tik_…`); a non-zero value without one is `400 integrator_fee_requires_api_key`. It is stacked into the same on-wire fee as Treasures' and already reflected in `estimated_output_*`; on Solana the venue keeps half of that fee, so it charges the trader twice this figure for you to net it. A quote that carries your fee can only be submitted with your key (`403 quote_integrator_mismatch`).

reason.description: Why a venue refused the requested fee, when that is the cause rather than your ceiling: `fee_above_maximum`, `fee_below_minimum` (raise it, or send 0), or `fee_unavailable` (no fee can be charged on some route right now). An open set; treat an unrecognised value as "this fee can't be charged".

TradeWarning.description: One disclosed risk on a quote. `code` shares the open vocabulary of `WarnReason` plus the two price-check codes below, so you learn one set rather than two; treat an unrecognised code as "warned, reason unknown" rather than an error. The other keys are the material values behind the code (a deviation in bps, the anchor used, the instant a warn was raised) and vary by code.

code.description:
- `no_reference`: no reference market price could be obtained for the asset, so nothing
  independent checked this quote's price. Permanent for an asset our market-data
  provider does not cover (the HK listings, the Ondo basket); transient during a
  provider outage.
- `off_reference`: a reference exists and the quote sits beyond its cap, in the
  direction that costs you. Beyond an implausibility bound the quote is refused
  outright instead (`no_routes` / `price_implausible`) and no acknowledgement can
  clear it.
- `speed_route_unavailable`: you sent `priority: "speed"` and the speed route could not
  serve the named chain, so **that chain's leg is absent** from this response (it is
  never returned on its relayed route instead). It carries `reason` and `chain` (the
  dropped leg's chain; absent only when the whole speed route is off, which is a
  response-level fact, not a per-leg one). Advisory: every leg that IS returned is
  fully executable; re-quote without `priority` to get the relayed route on that chain.

  The `reason` values this API emits today are exactly:

  - `disabled` (the speed route is switched off; this is the one reason with no `chain`)
  - `insufficient_balance` (the wallet is short the spent token)
  - `no_routes` (no reachable pool, or the built swap failed an integrity check)
  - `provider_error` (an upstream failure, caught and downgraded, including a delegation
    read that failed under `execution: "user_operation"`)
  - under `execution: "user_operation"` only, `wallet_not_delegated` (the wallet is
    delegated to code other than Modular Account v2 on the named chain), where
    `disabled` then also carries `chain` when it means "no bundler serves this chain
    yet".

  A missing router allowance is not a reason: the quote bundles the approve instead
  (`SignableEvmTx`).

  One more reason rides only a `no_routes` refusal (`NoRoutesError.warnings[]`), never a
  served quote: `no_speed_venue`, which also carries `protocol` and names a chain the
  speed route does not serve that listing on (`eth`, `bnb` or `arbitrum`). The named
  listing exists for this ticker but its own-chain venue is one `"speed"` never quotes
  (a gasless order that can take minutes to fill), so that venue was not tried.
  Re-quote without `priority` to reach it.

  The list is **open**: this object does not restrict its properties, and a future
  release may add a value. Branch on the ones you handle and treat anything else as
  "speed route unavailable, reason unknown" rather than an error.
- `speed_route_unpriced_gas`: the opposite outcome, and a separate code for exactly that
  reason: the leg on the named `chain` **was** served on the speed route, but no USD gas
  price was available, so its `estimated_gas_usd` is `null` and the route ranking
  ignored gas for it. Carries `chain`, and no `reason`. Advisory: price the gas yourself
  before choosing this leg over a gasless one.
- `cross_chain_route_unavailable`: a `priority:"speed"` cell you were not funded on, and
  that can be reached cross-chain (`eth/ondo`, `sol/xstocks`, `sol/backpack`,
  `base/coinbase`, `bnb/bstocks`), could not be served cross-chain and **fell back** to
  today's plan for that cell instead (a dropped same-chain speed leg on base or bnb, or
  no leg at all on sol and eth: a sol leg your `sol_wallet` cannot fund is never served,
  and eth is never served on its gasless route under `"speed"`).

  It also names a sol cell with no cross-chain route (such as `sol/ondo`) that your
  `sol_wallet` cannot fund while another of your wallets could: `reason: no_routes`, and
  no leg. When nothing is left to serve, the same entries ride the refusal's
  `NoRoutesError.warnings[]`.

  Carries `chain`, `protocol` and `reason`, a closed set today:

  - `no_routes`
  - `over_max` (above the cross-chain ceiling)
  - `fee_unavailable`
  - `disabled`
  - `provider_error`
  - `wallet_not_delegated`
  - `wallet_missing`, which this API has never yet emitted on this code (a missing
    origin wallet is dropped before a per-cell warning is composed); treat it as
    reserved.

  Not a `speed_route_unavailable` reason: that code means "your same-chain speed leg
  fell back", this one means "the cross-chain attempt for this cell fell back".

  On `/quote/sell` with `payout_chain` (any `priority`) the same code names a position
  you hold that is **left out** of the plan because it cannot pay out on that chain: a
  cell with no cross-chain route (`reason: no_routes`), or a cross-chain leg that was
  refused or could not land (its own `reason` from the set above). Such a position is
  never sold on its own chain instead, and one that a later part of the plan did sell
  is not named.
- `cross_chain_price_deviation`: the leg named by `chain`/`protocol` priced more than
  `threshold_bps` (500) away from the reference market price. Carries `deviation_bps`
  and `threshold_bps`. **Advisory only, never a refusal**: the leg is fully executable;
  a quote under this deviation, but still above what you would normally expect on that
  cell, may ship with no warning at all (the threshold is a bound, not a tight one).
- `exit_gas_unfunded`: a cross-chain buy leg (one carrying `origin_chain`) lands the
  asset on the named `chain`/`protocol` in a wallet whose native balance cannot pay the
  cheapest later exit: on an EVM chain, one token approval at the current gas price,
  doubled; on `sol`, two transaction fees, plus the rent for a USDC token account when
  the wallet has none. Carries `chain` and `protocol`.
  **Advisory only, never a refusal**: the leg is fully executable and you fund your own
  gas, so fund that wallet before you sell.

  A balance that could not be read is not warned. Also sent on `quote_only`; never sent
  by `POST /quote/preview`, which quotes no wallet of yours.

`cross_chain_route_unavailable` and `exit_gas_unfunded` appear once per affected
`chain`/`protocol` pair, `speed_route_unavailable` once per `chain` (once per
`chain`/`protocol` pair for `no_speed_venue`), and `speed_route_unpriced_gas` once per
`chain`; every other code appears at most once per response.

Every other `code` value is the routed cell's own `WarnReason`.

WarningsAckToken.description: A digest over this `quote_id` and the exact `warnings[]` served with it. Present only alongside a non-empty set, and never on a preview; `quote_only` and `POST /quote/preview` both omit it, having no `quote_id` to bind one to and nothing to submit it against. Echo it back as `acknowledged_warnings` on `POST /trade/submit` to record that you received these warnings before executing, see that field for what the record does and does not mean.

quote_id.description: Omitted on `quote_only` previews and on `POST /quote/preview` (no executable quote to submit).

expires_at.description: Unix seconds: the EARLIEST leg's deadline, so it is safe for any leg. Each leg also carries its own `expires_at`, which is what `/trade/submit` enforces for the leg you sign; on a multi-chain quote the longer-lived legs stay submittable past this value. A leg already past its own deadline when the response is built is dropped, so `quote_index` values can skip; always echo `quotes[].quote_index`, never the array position. Omitted on `quote_only` previews and on `POST /quote/preview`; neither has an executable quote to expire.

warnings.description:
Everything this quote discloses about the trade. **Always present**, `[]` when there is
nothing to disclose, so an empty list is never ambiguous with an older build. A warned
quote is still executable: this plane discloses and does not gate. Deciding what to show
an end user, and whether to proceed, is yours.

A leg reporting `tradability: "thin"` with no `warn_reason` emits NO
`warnings[]` entry: the reason column is newer than the verdict, so a cell warned before
it existed has nothing to name here and stays silent until the next probe pass records
one. The leg's own `tradability` is the disclosure in that window; do not read an empty
`warnings[]` beside a `thin` leg as "no risk".

expires_at.description: Unix seconds: the EARLIEST leg's deadline. A sell submit signs every leg, so this is the deadline that binds it; each leg's own `expires_at` is never later.

warnings.description: See `QuoteBuyResponse.warnings`; same contract on both sides.

tx_hash.description: The leg's transaction hash or signature. On a `failed` same-chain `sol` leg it is the signature the execution venue reported, which may not exist on chain.

user_op_hash.description: `user_operation` legs only: the ERC-4337 op hash, from `broadcast` on. On a same-chain leg `tx_hash` is null until the bundle mines, then carries the bundle transaction; on a cross-chain leg (`origin_chain` or `payout_chain` present) it stays null until the leg is terminal, then carries the destination fill (a completed buy) or the bundle (a sell, or a failed leg whose op was included); a leg whose op never landed keeps it null, so this hash is the leg's handle. Null on every other leg.

payout_chain.description:
**Cross-chain sell legs only** (quoted with `payout_chain`; absent on every other leg):
the chain the leg's USDC lands on: the `PayoutChain` you asked for, or the leg's own
`chain` after a return there (below), which can be `bnb`, not itself a payout chain.

`tx_hash` stays the sale on `chain` (under `execution: "user_operation"`, null until the
leg completes, then the bundle that sold it).

On `completed` it names where the USDC actually landed: if the cross-chain payout could
not be made, the USDC may be returned on the sale's own `chain` instead, and this field
then equals `chain`. `filled_usdc` is the USDC that landed.

payout_tx_hash.description: Present with `payout_chain`: the transaction on `payout_chain` that paid the USDC out. `null` unless the leg is `completed`.

is_cached.description: True when served from the in-progress cache; false on DB-fresh reads and all terminal aggregates.

poll_after_ms.description:
Minimum useful interval before the next poll, in milliseconds.

- `1250` while a speed-route leg submitted in the last 5 min is still in flight (it
  settles by receipt within a block or two)
- `3250` when only gasless or Solana legs remain (the upstream order status is synced
  at most every 3 s per leg regardless of poll rate) or a speed-route leg has sat
  unmined past 5 min.
- `null` once `aggregate_status` is terminal; stop polling.

The value sits just above the server-side cache window so a client polling at it never
reads a stale entry. On a cached response (`is_cached: true`) it is the time left on
that cached view, not the full window, so a client that arrives late is not asked to
wait another one; it is never below 1000. Advisory: polling faster returns the cached
view.

SignedEvmPayload.description: Signed gasless EVM order: the caller's EIP-712 signature over the quote leg's typed data. Used by **every** EVM leg: eth (mainnet), robinhood (Robinhood Chain / 4663), base (Base / 8453), arbitrum (Arbitrum One / 42161) and bnb (BNB Smart Chain / 56). The server relays the signed order to that chain's own resolver network; the caller never broadcasts an on-chain tx.

signature.description: 0x-prefixed EIP-712 EOA signature (132 chars).

SignedEvmTx.description:
A whole signed EVM transaction: the reply to a `SignableEvmTx` (speed-route) leg. Sign the
payload's `tx_hex` unchanged and send the serialized result back; **you do not broadcast
it**, Treasures does, after checking that the bytes are the ones it issued (signer, chain,
`to`, calldata, value, nonce, gas and fees all bind against the quote), that the wallet
still holds the token and the native gas (and the allowance, on a single-payload leg), and
that the transaction still simulates.

Any mismatch is a per-leg `invalid_signature`; a simulation revert is `swap_reverted` (or
`approve_failed` for a bundled approve) and nothing is sent. A leg that issued two
`SignableEvmTx` payloads needs **both** back, one `evm_signed_tx` each; the server matches
them by nonce.

SignedEvmUserOperation.description:
The reply to a `SignableEvmCalls` leg: the sponsored, signed ERC-4337 **v0.7**
UserOperation (unpacked fields, `factory`/`factoryData` absent). Numeric fields as decimal
or `0x` hex strings; hex fields `0x`-prefixed.

A wallet with no code on the chain adds `eip7702Auth`, its signed EIP-7702 authorization,
which the bundler applies in the same transaction; it must name a Modular Account v2
delegate as `address`, the leg's `chain_id` (never `0`, which would delegate the wallet on
every chain), and be signed by `sender`, else `invalid_signature`. It does not change the
op hash. An authorization the chain then skips (a stale `nonce`) leaves the wallet without
code, and the simulation refuses it as `swap_reverted`.

The server binds it to the quote (see `SignableEvmCalls`), dedupes on its hash, re-checks
balance (and allowance on a single-call leg), simulates it on the bundler
(`eth_estimateUserOperationGas`; a refusal never reached the mempool: `nonce_conflict`,
`sponsorship_rejected`, `swap_reverted`, `provider_error`), then submits it. The result is
`broadcast` with `user_op_hash` set and `tx_hash` null; `/status` flips it once the bundle
mines. Exactly one per leg; ≤ 16 KB.

eip7702Auth.description: A first-operation EIP-7702 delegation, as the bundler RPC spells it (viem's `authorization` on a UserOperation).

nonce.description: A uint64, decimal or `0x` hex; a larger value is `400 invalid_request`.

s.description: Exactly 32 bytes, low-s (at most half the curve order, as EIP-7702 requires); a high-s tuple is `invalid_signature`.

yParity.description: `0` or `1`, decimal or `0x` hex (`0x00` / `0x01` as viem sends it).

Uint256String.description: A uint256 as a decimal string, or as 0x-prefixed hex. The pattern admits up to 78 decimal digits, which overshoots 2^256-1; the server bounds the VALUE as well and answers `400 invalid_request` on an out-of-range one.

Uint128String.description: A uint128 as a decimal string, or as 0x-prefixed hex: the ERC-4337 v0.7 PACKING width of the gas-limit and fee fields (`accountGasLimits` and `gasFees` each pack two uint128s into one 32-byte slot). Bounded by value, not only by shape: an over-wide field is `400 invalid_request` rather than a hasher throw.

signed_payloads.description: One entry per payload the leg issued, IN THE ORDER THE QUOTE ISSUED THEM. A speed-route leg may issue two (`approve` then `swap`); sign and return both. Order is load-bearing for idempotency: a replay is recognised by a hash over this array, so a re-submit that reorders the entries is refused as a new submit (`leg_already_submitted`, 409). Fewer or more entries than the leg issued is `incomplete_submit` (400), before anything is sent.

acknowledged_warnings.description:
**Optional, and never required.** Echo the quote's `warnings_ack_token` to have the
acknowledgement recorded beside the trade; omit it and the trade proceeds exactly as
before, with the acknowledgement columns left empty.

We record the warnings we served on **every** trade whether or not you echo anything, so
omitting this loses you a record of your own acknowledgement, not ours of the disclosure.

Sending a value that does not match the warnings served with this `quote_id` is refused
with `warnings_not_acknowledged` (422) rather than recorded; clear it by omitting the
field or by re-quoting and echoing the fresh token. A clean quote (`warnings: []`)
ignores the field entirely.

**What this does not cover.** Disclosing risk to your own end users, and keeping evidence
that you did, is governed by your integrator agreement and your records, not by this
field. Echoing a token records what *you* were told, never what your user was.

tx_hash.description: The leg's transaction hash or signature. On a `failed` same-chain `sol` leg it is the signature the execution venue reported, which may not exist on chain.

user_op_hash.description: `user_operation` legs only: the ERC-4337 op hash the bundler took, set from `broadcast` on while `tx_hash` is still null (it becomes the bundle transaction once mined, poll `/status`). Null on every other leg.

error_code.description:
Per-leg failure reason: its own open vocabulary, never an HTTP `error` code:

- `invalid_signature`
- `quote_expired`
- `not_enough_balance_or_allowance`
- `provider_error`
- `status_check_exhausted`
- two that only a same-chain `sol` leg can carry, namely
  - `market_maker_rejected` (the market maker refused the fill: re-quote, possibly at
    another size)
  - `not_landed` (the transaction was reported as failing to land; whether it can still
    land later is not established, so when the leg carries a `tx_hash`, check it before
    trading the same size again; a wallet short of the token the leg spends also ends
    here, since its balance is not checked before sending)
- one that only a `user_operation` leg can carry, namely
  - `sponsorship_rejected` (your paymaster refused to sponsor the op: deposit, stake,
    rate limit, policy signature or a paymaster revert; nothing was submitted;
    re-sponsor and re-sign)
- five that a speed-route leg can carry, all but `swap_reverted` only there, namely
  - `nonce_conflict` (another transaction from this wallet took the nonce: wait for the
    earlier trade to go terminal, then re-quote)
  - `insufficient_native_gas` (the signed `gas × fee` exceeds the wallet's native
    balance: fund it, then re-quote)
  - `swap_reverted` (the swap reverted in simulation or on chain; nothing was spent on a
    simulation revert; re-quote; a same-chain `sol` leg carries it too, when the
    transaction was reported as failed by the execution venue with an on-chain program
    error; its signature is on `tx_hash`)
  - `tx_dropped` (accepted by the node, then evicted without mining: re-quote and
    re-sign)
  - `approve_failed` (a bundled `approve` reverted, or did not land within 10 minutes,
    so the swap was never sent: re-quote; if the approve did mine, the new quote is
    single-payload).

On any pair whose swap was never sent (`approve_failed`, and a `nonce_conflict` /
`provider_error` refused at the approve send), `tx_hash` is `null`, because the swap
hash the leg named never reached a node. `provider_error` now also covers a speed-route
pre-flight or transport failure; nothing was broadcast, so re-quoting is safe.

Five more that only a `priority:"speed"` **cross-chain** leg (`origin_chain` present on
the quote) can carry:

- `quote_stale` (the sol origin's deposit blockhash expired before broadcast; nothing
  left the wallet, so re-quote; distinct from the top-level `410 quote_stale` at submit,
  which fires before any leg's bytes leave at all)
- `deposit_reverted` (the EVM origin's deposit reverted past the retry window: re-quote)
- `refunded` (the cross-chain intent could not fill and the deposit was returned to your
  origin wallet, so no token was bought; re-quote)
- `delivered_other_currency` (terminal: you were delivered a stablecoin instead of the
  destination token; nothing to retry)
- `cross_chain_unsettled` (6 hours passed with no terminal outcome after the deposit
  left your wallet: **do not re-quote**; it may still fill or refund on the origin, and
  a late fill is healed automatically).

Treat an unrecognised value as "failed, reason unknown".

failed_legs.description: Empty on the full-success path; populated only when a partial broadcast hit an invariant break.

submissions.description: One `POST /trade/submit` body each. No `quote_id` may appear twice.

http_status.description: The status `POST /trade/submit` would have answered for this submission.

response.description:
- The body `POST /trade/submit` would have answered (body only, never headers)
- `TradeSubmitBatchUnsupportedLeg` (422)
- `TradeSubmitBatchNotStarted` (503)
- `{ "error": "internal_error" }` (500).

results.description: One per submission, in request order.

BridgeChain.description:
Any pair of distinct chains. `bnb` answers `400 unsupported_route` on a deployment
without a BNB Chain endpoint. `robinhood` settles in USDG, so a bridge to or from it
is a USDC↔USDG swap as well as a bridge.

allOf.description: Capped at the server-configured `BRIDGE_MAX_AMOUNT_USDC`.
Required when either side is `sol`; omit it on an EVM-to-EVM bridge.
The wallet on every EVM side (one address serves all EVM chains).

`eth_signature` is always required; `sol_signature` is required whenever
`sol_wallet` is sent.

delivery.description:
`self_broadcast`: you broadcast what you sign. `submit`: you hand it to
`POST /bridge/{bridge_quote_id}/submit`, the only way to execute it; from an EVM
origin the payload is `evm_permit_typed_data` and needs no native gas.

approval_spender.description:
ERC-20 spender to approve USDC to before broadcasting. Null when the
calldata needs no allowance.

BridgeSignablePermitPayload.description:
`delivery: submit` from an EVM origin. Sign each `typed_data` (as
`eth_signTypedData_v4` takes it) in order and send the signatures to
`POST /bridge/{bridge_quote_id}/submit`. Each authorizes moving `amount_in_usdc` of the
origin's base token once, to the bridge's settlement contract, for about ten minutes; sign
it as given (its domain or type names may name that contract).

approval_tx.description:
A one-time token approval your own wallet sends before signing, on tokens without a
built-in permit. Null on every origin offered today.

BridgeSubmitRequest.description: Exactly one of `signatures` (EVM origin) or `signed_tx` (Solana origin).

signatures.description:
One 65-byte signature (0x-hex) per `signable_payload.signatures[]` item, in the same
order, by `eth_wallet`.

signed_tx.description:
The `signable_payload` Solana transaction signed by `sol_wallet`, as base64, with its
message byte-for-byte unchanged (a wallet that adds instructions is refused).

source_tx_hash.description:
The Solana signature. Null from an EVM origin: the deposit is sent moments later and
appears in `GET /bridge/{bridge_quote_id}/status`.

shares_internal_only.description: Equity shares acquired via Treasures and still held (internal lot). Populated only with `source=internal`; null in `all` mode and when the cell has no share multiplier.

avg_entry_price_per_share.description: Weighted-average cost basis per share of the internal lot. Populated only with `source=internal`; null otherwise.

unrealized_pnl.description: internal_tokens × usd_per_token − internal cost. Populated only with `source=internal` and when a spot price exists; null otherwise.

tradability.description: Probe warning for the exact `(ticker, protocol, chain)` cell this position names, filtered to the sell side. Published only when `warn_reason` is side-neutral (see below), so a position carries all three keys or none. **Advisory, never a block**: it never marks a holding unsellable. `min_trade_size_usd` is never published on a position: it is a USD buy floor while a sell is denominated in shares. Absent means unmeasured, unwarned, or buy-sided, never healthy-with-value-null.

warn_reason.description: Why the held cell is warned. **Positions carry only the side-neutral reasons**: `low_volume`, `no_price_feed` and `no_settlements`. The buy-sided reasons (`no_fill_window`, `settlement_failure`) say nothing about an exit and suppress the whole trio, as does a warn whose reason was never recorded.

positions.description:
The sol/eth positions are read on-chain against the reconciler ledger. Positions on the
two single-cell venues, Robinhood Chain (4663) and Base (8453), are read for every
wallet Treasures knows on any chain, snapshotted for 30 s (invalidated the moment a
trade on that venue settles).

An `eth_wallet` that is not in Treasures's own custody, is not a B2C wallet, and has no
B2B ledger row anywhere gets an empty `positions` list here with no RPC, and is not
flagged `partial`. For a KNOWN wallet there is no trade-history gate on top of that: a
token transferred into your own EOA from outside shows exactly like one bought through
this API.

**Idle cash on these two venues (`usdc.base`, `usdg.robinhood`) is never gated**; it
still reads live even for an unknown wallet, so a wallet holding only cash still reports
it.

BNB Smart Chain (56) positions are read the same way, off the same EOA. On `bnb` a
position's `protocol` is one of `ondo`, `xstocks` or `bstocks`: like `sol` and `eth`, 56
carries more than one, so do not infer `protocol` from `chain`. Positions and `usdc.bnb`
are reported **even while the bnb venue is closed**: a portfolio reports what a wallet
holds.

usdc.description:
Idle USDC per chain.

- ⚠ **`base` is Base-native USDC on 8453, a DIFFERENT contract from mainnet USDC.** It is
  read from the caller's own 8453 EOA (keyed on `eth_wallet`) through its own 30 s
  snapshot that a settled trade invalidates (exactly like `usdg.robinhood`), not from
  the sol/eth reconciler. A failed read is never cached. `base` is `"0"` when no
  `eth_wallet` is supplied, no B20 cell is listed in the catalog, or the 8453 read
  fails.
- `arbitrum` is Arbitrum-native USDC on 42161, read the same way from the caller's own
  42161 EOA, and is `"0"` when no `eth_wallet` is supplied, no Arbitrum cell is listed,
  or the 42161 read fails.
- `bnb` is **Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Smart Chain (56): 18 decimals, and not a Circle
  deploy at all** (BSC has none). It is reported under the `usdc` name for wire
  compatibility; converting it to Circle USDC costs roughly 31 bps inbound and 7 to 9
  bps outbound, a cross-chain swap rather than a transfer. The value here is
  human-decimal, so the 18-dp scale does not leak into this field. It is read the same
  way from the caller's own 56 EOA, is `"0"` when no `eth_wallet` is supplied, no bnb
  cell is listed, or the 56 read fails, and is reported even while the bnb venue is
  closed.

The five keys are five different tokens: never pool them.

usdg.description: Base-currency cash on Robinhood Chain (4663): the venue's USDG, the 4663 analog of `usdc`. Read from the caller's own 4663 EOA (keyed on `eth_wallet`) through a 30 s snapshot that a settled trade invalidates, so a post-trade read reflects the new cash rather than waiting out the TTL. A failed read is never cached. `"0"` when no `eth_wallet` is supplied, the Robinhood venue is dormant, or the 4663 read fails.

partial.description:
`true` when a balance read failed on this pass, so `positions` omits cells the wallet
may hold and any sum over `usd_value` undercounts. Covers **every** position source: an
unreadable sol/eth cell, and an unreadable cell on any EOA-read venue chain (Robinhood
Chain 4663, Base 8453, Arbitrum One 42161, BNB Smart Chain 56).

Cash is not covered; `usdc`/`usdg` fault-isolate to `"0"` independently, since a failed
read there is indistinguishable from a real zero.

Retry for a complete answer; the response is otherwise a normal 200. May be `true`
alongside `is_cached: true`; the cells were unreadable when the snapshot was taken.

as_of.description: Unix seconds: when this snapshot was actually computed, so it is always the true age of the data. Reads are served from a snapshot that is refreshed in the background once it passes 30 s and recomputed inline past 5 minutes, so `as_of` can trail the request by **up to 5 minutes**. A settled trade invalidates the snapshot, so a post-trade read always recomputes rather than replaying a pre-trade view. Check `as_of` if your use case needs a tighter bound.

is_cached.description: `true` when the response was served from an existing snapshot rather than a fresh on-chain read. Says nothing about how old it is; use `as_of` for that.

payout_chain.description: **Cross-chain sells only** (quoted with `payout_chain`; absent on every other row): the chain this sale's USDC lands on, as on the `/quote/{quote_id}/status` leg (so `bnb` when a `bnb/bstocks` sale's USDC was returned on `bnb`). `tx_hash` stays the sale on `chain`, and `usdc_amount` is the USDC that landed.

payout_tx_hash.description: Present with `payout_chain`: the transaction on `payout_chain` that paid the USDC out. `null` unless the row is `completed`.
