usd_per_share.description: This row's settled execution price (usdc_amount / shares). Populated only with `source=internal` on completed rows; null in `all` mode, on non-completed (in-flight/failed/external) rows, and when usdc_amount is null.

avg_entry_price_per_share.description: Running internal weighted-average cost basis per share at this row. Populated only with `source=internal`; null on non-internal rows.

realized_pnl.description: Realized P&L for a closing internal sell: (px − avg_entry) × closed shares, gross of fees (Hyperliquid closedPnl parity). Populated only with `source=internal`; null on buys, oversell-uncovered, and non-internal rows.

next_offset.description: Pass back as `offset` to fetch the next page; `null` when there are no more rows.

address.description: Mint (Solana) or contract address (EVM) of this leg's token. `null` in the rare case where the catalog entry for the ticker is unavailable; the trade is still returned, since omitting a settled fill would understate your volume.

price_usd.description: Realized execution price for this leg, derived from the fill itself, not a market quote. Quoted per unit of THIS leg's token, matching `amount`/`tokens`; see `price_usd_per_share` for the equity-denominated figure. `1` on the stablecoin leg, which is the accounting unit. Truncated to 12 decimal places.

price_usd_per_share.description: The same realized fill priced per equity share rather than per token; `amount_usd ÷ shares`, truncated to 12 decimal places. Prefer this when comparing against a market or tradfi reference: on the rebase venues (xStocks on Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain) `price_usd` is a price per conserved internal unit and so matches no market quote, while this figure is comparable across venues and chains. The two coincide wherever the share multiplier is 1. `null` on the stablecoin leg, which has no share denomination, and on the rare fill whose `shares` floor to zero.

tx_hash.description: On-chain hash of this leg's transfer, on this leg's `chain`. Identical on both legs of a single-chain swap. On a sell paid out on another chain (or returned on the sale's own chain) the stock leg's hash is the sale and the USDC leg's is the payout.

tx_link.description: Block-explorer link, or `null` where no explorer is published for the chain (Robinhood Chain). The hash is still returned.

timestamp.description: Settlement time, unix seconds.

amount.description: Raw integer base units of this leg's token.

transfer_amount.description:
Raw integer base units as they appear in the on-chain transfer: the figure a block
explorer renders. Equal to `amount` on every venue except xStocks on Ethereum and
BNB Smart Chain, whose token rebases: there the contract emits BOTH a standard ERC-20
`Transfer` (carrying this value) and a shares-transfer event (carrying `amount`, the
conserved internal unit). Both are on-chain; they differ by the share multiplier, and
an explorer shows only the first. Reconcile explorer-visible movement on this field and
internal accounting on `amount`.

The byte-exact match to an explorer is an EVM property: on Solana Token-2022 ScaledUI
cells the transfer instruction carries the value reported here, but some explorers
render a display-scaled figure instead.

This is the raw movement on THIS leg, not a gross notional. Whether `fee_costs` has
already been netted out of the stablecoin leg is venue-dependent, so do not assume
either way:

- on a buy it is the full amount spent
- on an Ethereum/Robinhood sell the venue skims its fee from this leg, so the figure is
  already net and IS the wallet credit
- on a Solana sell the referral fee is collected in a separate transfer, so the figure
  sits above the credit by the disclosed bps
- on a sell paid out on another chain it is the payout transfer itself, so already net
  and IS the wallet credit.

Summing `transfer_amount + fee_costs` therefore does NOT give a consistent total across
chains.

`null` only for a rebasing trade settled before this field was recorded; no backfill is
possible, so treat `null` as unknown, never as zero.

tokens.description: `amount` in human-readable units. Provided because the token's decimal precision is not part of this contract; do not hardcode a scale.

amount_usd.description: Owed to you now, in USD at 6 dp, truncated.

payout_chain.description: The chain payouts are sent on. `null` until Treasures registers an address.

payout_address.description: The one address payouts go to. EVM addresses are EIP-55 checksummed.

previous_payout_address.description: The address the last change replaced; `null` if it has never changed.

payout_address_updated_at.description: Unix seconds of the last registration or change.

payouts_enabled.description: Whether `POST /payouts` is open on this environment.

maximum_usd.description: The largest payout `POST /payouts` makes; above it, Treasures pays on request.

next_eligible_at.description: Unix seconds before which `POST /payouts` will refuse (cooldown or address hold); `null` when nothing is waiting.

status.description:
- `processing`: created or sent, not yet final.
- `paid`: final (see `tx_hash`).
- `failed`: the transfer did not happen; its fees are owed to you again.
- `cancelled`: withdrawn before sending; its fees went back into what you are owed.

amount_usd.description: Sum of the `integrator_fee` entries it covers, exactly as `/settlements` reports each one (`GET /settlements?payout_id=…`).

chain.description: The chain it is paid on; `null` on a payout cut before an address was registered, until paid.

tx_hash.description: The transfer. On Solana it is known as soon as the payout is sent (while `processing`); on Base once it lands.

created_at.description: Unix seconds.

SignalSourceKind.description:
What the strategy's book is derived from.

- `congressional_disclosure`: a legislator's periodic transaction reports.
- `institutional_13f`: an institution's quarterly 13F holdings.
- `media_inverse`: the inverse of a broadcast pundit's calls.
- `social_account`: a public social-media account's posts.
- `manager_published`: a fund manager publishes the book to Treasures directly.

New values may be added; treat an unknown value as opaque.

SignalReplication.description: How much of the source portfolio the book carries. A book is the source cut down to the names Treasures can trade on chain and renormalised to them.

as_of.description: Unix seconds of the pass that produced these numbers.

skipped_source_weight.description: Decimal share of the source portfolio's weight that the book leaves out.

chains.description: The chains the book was cut against.

buyable_by_chain.description: How many of the source's names each chain could buy.

status.description: `active`: new books are expected. `paused` and `halted`: no new books for now; the last one stays readable.

weight.description: Decimal fraction of the book, at most 8 decimals.

as_of.description: Unix seconds. When Treasures ingested the book, not the filing or disclosure date.

book_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of the book's contents. Two books with the same weights have the same hash whatever their `signal_id`; compare hashes to detect a change.

as_of.description: Unix seconds. When Treasures ingested the book.

trading_day.description: The US trading day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) the book was acted on.

SignalCatalogStrategy.description: A catalog row, `SignalStrategy` plus its latest book's identity.

status.description: As on `SignalStrategy`.

book_hash.description: The latest book's `book_hash`; `null` when the strategy has no book yet.

book_as_of.description: The latest book's `as_of` (unix seconds); `null` with no book.

signal_id.description: The latest book's `signal_id`; `null` with no book.

truncated.description: `true` when the page cap of 100 cut the catalog short.

strategy_id.description: The strategy's `strategy_id` (stable) or its `slug` (may be renamed).

ownership_proof.description: The `sol_signature` over the canonical challenge is required.

tickers.description: Names to exit beside the book's own, for a position you hold that has since left the book. Each is sold only if held.

expected_book_hash.description: The `book_hash` you planned against. When sent and the served book differs, the call is refused with `409 book_changed` before the wallet is read or anything is quoted.

protocol.description: Narrows which holdings are read and sold, as on `POST /quote/sell`. null/omitted = every protocol. Must include a Solana protocol (`ondo`, `xstocks` or `backpack`), or the request is refused with `400 invalid_request`. A pinned exit covers the pinned venues only: a name also held on another venue is sold from the pinned one alone, with no `skipped` entry for the rest, so repeat the call per venue to exit fully.

SignalOrderSkipReason.description:
- `leg_cap`: more orders than fit: past 25 orders or 30 upstream quote calls. On `/exit` the
  smallest by notional, unpriced first, are skipped; on `/rebalance` sells are admitted
  first.
- `not_held`: no Solana position, or one worth under $0.01, or one that floors to zero
  shares, or a token account that cannot be decoded into a balance (read as zero).
- `holdings_unknown`: the holding could not be read, so it is never assumed absent (`/exit`
  only; a rebalance refuses the whole request instead).
- `below_min_notional`: a rebalance gap under $1.
- `awaiting_sell_proceeds`: a rebalance buy `amount_usdc` cannot fund while the plan also
  sells; call again with the proceeds once the sells settle.
- `not_tradable`: a book name Treasures cannot buy on Solana; its weight stays in USDC.
- `insufficient_balance`: a rebalance buy `amount_usdc` cannot fund, with no sell to wait
  on.

SignalOrderSide.description: Every `/exit` order is a sell; a rebalance order is either.

shares.description: A sell's share count, floored to 18 decimal places (the full position on `/exit`). Send as `amount_shares`. `null` on a buy, which is sized by `notional_usdc`.

notional_usdc.description: On a sell, its USD value, or `null` when it could not be priced (`/exit` only). On a buy, the USDC it spends, floored to 6 decimal places; send as `amount_usdc`.

quote.description: On `/exit` and `/rebalance` only. Exactly the `POST /quote/sell` (or, for a buy, `POST /quote/buy`) answer for this order.

reason.description: One of `SignalOrderSkipReason`, or, on `/exit` and `/rebalance`, the error code the order's quote route would have answered for that leg.

detail.description: The rest of that order's quote route error body, or `null` when there is none.

strategy_id.description: The canonical id, even when the request named the slug.

as_of.description: Unix seconds. When Treasures ingested the book, not the filing date.

nav_usdc.description: The USD value of the priced names you hold in scope. Unpriced names are excluded.

usdc_available.description: The wallet's Solana USDC, as a decimal string.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds. The earliest `orders[].quote.expires_at`; `null` when no order was quoted. Each quote's own `expires_at` is what `/trade/submit` enforces for it.

signing_window_sec.description: Seconds from this response until `expires_at`; `null` when no order was quoted.

strategy_id.description: The strategy's `strategy_id` (stable) or its `slug` (may be renamed).

ownership_proof.description: The `sol_signature` over the canonical challenge is required.

tickers.description: Names to bring into scope beside the book's own, for a position you hold that has since left the book. Each has weight zero, so it is sold in full if held.

expected_book_hash.description: The `book_hash` you planned against. When sent and the served book differs, the call is refused with `409 book_changed` before the wallet is read or anything is quoted.

amount_usdc.description: USDC from the wallet to deploy, counted into nav and the only USDC buys may spend. At most `usdc_available`. Omit it for none (`"0"` is refused); on the second round of a rebalance, send the smaller of `funding.next_amount_usdc` and `usdc_available`.

quote_ids.description: The earlier call's quotes that are neither final nor five minutes past their expiry; empty while that call is still quoting.

SignalOrderRefusalCode.description: `holdings_unknown`: a name in scope could not be read. `price_unavailable`: a held name in scope could not be priced. Either would mis-size every order, so nothing is planned.

tickers.description: The names that caused the refusal.

SignalOrderFunding.description: How `amount_usdc` funds the buys. Buys are scaled pro rata and a scaled buy under $1 is skipped, so a small pool spread over many buys can deploy nothing this round; the whole shortfall then stays in `buys_deferred_usdc`.

usdc_spendable.description: `amount_usdc`, or `"0"` when omitted: the only USDC this plan's buys spend. Differs from `usdc_available`, the wallet's whole Solana USDC.

buys_required_usdc.description: Every buy the book asks for, ordered or not, excluding buys under the $1 minimum (`below_min_notional`) and names that cannot be bought (`not_tradable`).

buys_scaled.description: True when buys were scaled down pro rata to fit `usdc_spendable`.

buys_deferred_usdc.description: `buys_required_usdc` less the buys in `orders` (on `/rebalance`, the buys quoted). Not the next round's `amount_usdc`: send `next_amount_usdc`.

buys_deferred_until_sells_settle.description: True when some buys are deferred and this plan sells: submit the sells, wait for them to settle, then call again.

next_amount_usdc.description:
The next call's `amount_usdc`. The server does not cap it at `usdc_available`, since
sell proceeds land net of fees and slippage: send the smaller of the two, and omit
`amount_usdc` when that is `"0"`.

It is `usdc_spendable` plus the sells in `orders`, less the buys in `orders` (on
`/rebalance`, only the orders quoted, so a refused sell adds nothing and a refused buy
spends nothing), rounded down to 6 decimal places and never below `"0"`. It is the
strategy's cash after this round, so the book's unweighted remainder and the weight of
any `not_tradable` name stay in nav and the next call does not sell again.

strategy_id.description: The canonical id, even when the request named the slug.

as_of.description: Unix seconds. When Treasures ingested the book, not the filing date.

nav_usdc.description: The USD value of what you hold in scope, plus `amount_usdc`.

usdc_available.description: The wallet's Solana USDC, as a decimal string.

orders.description: Sells first, then buys, each largest notional first.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds. The earliest `orders[].quote.expires_at`; `null` when no order was quoted. Each quote's own `expires_at` is what `/trade/submit` enforces for it.

signing_window_sec.description: Seconds from this response until `expires_at`; `null` when no order was quoted.

name.description:
- `integrator_fee` is your own fee on the trade, present only when the trade carried
  one; it is what payouts to you are summed from, entry by entry.
- `treasures_fee` is our own take and is always present.
- `dex_fee` is the venue's take, net of ours, and is present only when it was recorded;
  trades settled before it was captured omit the entry rather than reporting a
  fabricated zero, so read its absence as unknown. A recorded `0` IS emitted and means
  the venue charged no fee. On a speed-route leg that the server broadcast, it is
  measured from the settled transaction rather than taken from the quote.

`dex_fee` covers the venue's FEE, not execution spread. A resolver's auction margin on
an intent-based fill sits outside it, so `0.0000` means "no venue fee", not "no
execution cost". To measure all-in cost, compare `amount_usd` against a reference price
rather than summing this array.

percentage.description: Fee as a decimal fraction at 4 dp, e.g. `0.0025` for 25 bps.

amount_usd.description: The fee in the settlement currency, derived as `percentage` applied to the entry's `amount_usd`, not read back from the venue's own fee event. Treat it as a close estimate rather than a reconciled figure: the recorded settlement notional is already net of the fee on an Ethereum sell, on a sell paid out on another chain and on a Solana buy, and on other buys the fee is taken in the token received rather than in the settlement currency. Same caveat applies to reconstructing a gross notional from it. Both entries carry this caveat identically.

included.description: `true` when the fee was taken out of the swap rather than charged on top.

payout_id.description: `integrator_fee` only: the payout this fee went out in (see `GET /payouts/{payoutId}`), or `null` while it is still owed to you.

trade_id.description: Stable id for this leg. One user-facing sell can fan out across several venues, producing several entries with distinct hashes.

status.description: Only settled trades are returned, so this is currently always `DONE`.

from_address.description: The wallet that sent the input token. EVM addresses are EIP-55 checksummed.

to_address.description: The wallet that received the output token: the same wallet, for a swap; on a sell paid out on another chain, your wallet on that chain.

timestamp.description: Settlement time, unix seconds. Mirrors `receiving.timestamp`.

tx_hash.description: The trade's own transaction on `chain`, the same hash `GET /trades` reports. Equal to both legs' `tx_hash` on a single-chain swap; on a sell paid out on another chain it is the sale (`sending.tx_hash`), and the payout is `receiving.tx_hash`.

token_out_address.description: Address of the token received. Mirrors `receiving.token.address`: the stock token on a buy, the stablecoin on a sell. `null` when the catalog entry is unavailable.

amount.description: Raw base units received. Mirrors `receiving.amount`. For the rebase venues (xStocks on Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain) this is the conserved internal unit rather than the wallet-visible balance; reconcile on `shares`, which is the equity measure, or on `receiving.transfer_amount`, which is the raw figure the on-chain `Transfer` event carries and a block explorer renders.

amount_usd.description: USD value of the trade, as a decimal string at the settlement currency's scale, like every money field in this API. On Robinhood Chain the settlement currency is USDG rather than USDC.

shares.description: Equity shares this leg moved, floored: the same rounding `/trades` and `/portfolio` use. The denomination is the one recorded with the trade at submit, so if a token's on-chain denomination changes afterwards this value can differ in its trailing digits from the same trade on `/trades`, which reads the current one. Reconcile on `trade_id`.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

has_more.description: Whether another page exists. Authoritative; `data` can be shorter than `limit` while this is `true`, so do not treat a short page as the end.

info.title: CapellaQL GraphQL Service
info.description:
High-performance GraphQL service providing modern API interface for Couchbase Capella databases.

## Features
- **GraphQL API**: Full GraphQL query support with introspection
- **Response Caching**: Intelligent caching with per-field TTL configuration
- **OpenTelemetry**: Comprehensive distributed tracing, metrics, and logging
- **Health Monitoring**: Multiple health endpoints for Kubernetes probes
- **RFC 7807 Errors**: Standardized problem details for error responses

## GraphQL Endpoint
The primary API is exposed via GraphQL at `/graphql`. Use POST for queries/mutations
or GET for simple read operations. WebSocket connections are supported for subscriptions.

## Authentication
Authentication is handled via Kong API Gateway with JWT tokens.

info.title: DJZS Protocol — verify_pm_trade
info.summary: Deterministic pre-execution audit of a prediction-market trade thesis.
info.description: DJZS audits the thesis, not the transaction. Wallet-layer tooling checks whether a transfer is safe; nothing checks whether the reasoning behind it holds. verify_pm_trade extracts the claims from a free-text trade thesis and scores them against a frozen taxonomy (narrative/resolution gap, falsification absent, probability unsourced, consensus-as-edge), returning a verdict, the codes that fired, a risk score, and a hash anyone can recompute from the submitted text. Out-of-scope requests are refused free: no payment settles.
info.x-guidance: Submit the reasoning behind a prospective prediction-market position as free text in the `intent` field. A well-formed thesis states the claim and its outcome, a SOURCED probability with a citation, the falsification condition, and the edge versus the market price. A consensus-only thesis with no source returns FAIL (DJZS-M03 PROBABILITY_UNSOURCED) and no order should be placed. Abstention is a first-class outcome. The audit reads reasoning only: it does not read markets, verify quoted prices, or check whether an instrument has already settled. Informational only, not financial advice — see https://djzs.ai/legal.

info.title: AI Tender Evaluation Platform API
info.description:
REST API of the AI Tender Evaluation Platform. It serves the React single-page application and is the only way into the data.

**Authentication.** Every call carries a Keycloak access token (`Authorization: Bearer`). Tokens are issued to the `tender-spa` client by the `tender-eval` realm with the authorization code flow and PKCE. The API validates the signature, issuer, audience `tender-api` and expiry, and reads `sub`, `email` and the `roles` claim. The Chair designation is not in the token: it comes from the tender membership.

**Authorization.** Each operation lists the roles that may call it in `x-roles`. Who may see which rows is enforced again by the database (row-level security), so a role check alone never exposes another member's grades. An action that the caller can never take is hidden from `actions`; one that depends on state is returned with `allowed: false` and a one-line reason.

**Errors.** `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code`. 422 carries `errors` for fields and `failures` for pre-check lists. 403 for a tender the caller may not open carries `access_contacts`.

**Concurrency.** Editable resources return an `ETag` that is their `row_version`. `PATCH` and `PUT` on them need `If-Match`. A stale value returns 412 with the current row and who changed it.

**Notes.** Any action that overrides, deletes, rejects, reopens or reinstates takes a justification `note` or `reason`. Its minimum length is `client_config.min_note_length` from `GET /me`.

**Long-running work.** Starting extraction, evaluation, a pre-check, a retry or an export returns `202` with the job or export and a `Location` header. Progress arrives on `GET /events` and can always be read from `GET /jobs/{jobId}`.

**Lists.** `limit` (up to 500) and an opaque `cursor`. Responses are `{items, next_cursor, total}`.

**Times and language.** RFC 3339 UTC. English only.

**Traceability.** `x-ux` on each operation lists the requirement IDs and screens it serves, from the UX Requirements and UX Design documents.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A client-generated key. A repeat of the same request with the same key returns the first result instead of creating another job or export.

userId.name: userId
userId.description: userId.

notificationId.name: notificationId
notificationId.description: notificationId.

ReportVersionNo.name: version
ReportVersionNo.description: Report version number. Defaults to the version the caller may read.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be read.

Forbidden.description: The caller may not do this. When the caller has no access to the tender, access_contacts names who to ask (UX-ROL-04).

NotFound.description: No such object, or none the caller may know about.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state, for example job_overlap, duplicate_vendor or baseline_locked.

PreconditionFailed.description: If-Match named an old row_version. The body carries the current row and who changed it.

PreconditionRequired.description: If-Match is required on this request.

TooLarge.description: The file is larger than the upload limit.

UnsupportedType.description: Only PDF and DOCX files are accepted (UX-DOC-01).

Unprocessable.description: Validation failed. errors names the fields, and failures lists what must be fixed first (for example the pre-check list).

TooMany.description: Rate limit reached. Retry-After says when to try again.

UserRole.description: Platform role. Chair is not a role: it is a flag on a tender membership.

PrecheckFailure.description: One reason an action is not available yet, with a link to the objects to fix.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. code is a stable machine-readable value such as note_too_short.

ActionState.description: allowed false with a reason makes the control disabled with a one-line reason (UX-ROL-03). An action that is never available to the caller is omitted.

Actions.description: Map from action name to its state.

ConflictProblem.description: Returned on 412 when If-Match names an old row_version. current is the representation as it stands now.

NoteBody.description: A justification note. Its minimum length is in /me client_config.min_note_length.

ClientConfig.description: Values the SPA needs at start. The idle timeout is read from the Keycloak realm; the warning lead time is the setting session.warning_seconds (UX-AUTH-04).

DeactivateUser.description: What happens to work in progress: keep it as read-only history, or reassign it (UX-ROL-05).

file.description: PDF or DOCX, up to the upload limit.

parent_document_id.description: The RFP an addendum belongs to.

DocumentImpact.description: How many requirements were extracted from the superseded version (UX-DOC-04).

bbox.description: Rectangles on the page, each [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF points.

VendorStatus.description: An inactive vendor stays on the tenders it is already part of and cannot be added to another one.

confirm_duplicate.description: Set to true after the user saw the duplicate warning.

ProposalFile.description: A file of a proposal version. Until a member has declared no conflict for the vendor, the file's own record is closed to them (PG-13), so the row is listed with a generic name ("Main file", "Annex 2") and a null status. The declaration opens it.

status.description: Null while the file is closed to the caller because no declaration is on record.

file_roles.description: One role per file, in the same order. Exactly one main file in total.

reuse_document_version_ids.description: Unchanged annexes from the previous version.

change_reason.description: Required from version 2 when AI evaluation has run.

ProposalImpact.description: UX-VND-05: how many evaluations will be marked Outdated.

AddTenderVendor.description: Either an existing vendor_id or a new vendor created inline.

JobEvent.description: One line of a job's activity log. Messages come from a fixed vocabulary and never carry document text.

updated_at.description: When the job last changed (a status message, a step or the watchdog).

events.description: Activity log, oldest first. Filled by GET /jobs/{jobId} only, empty in lists.

detail.description: What the worker reported about the cause, for example the sizes that disagree. Fixed wording from the worker, never document text.

ExtractionCoverage.description: Which sections were extracted, by whom and when, and which extractions are running (UX-EXT-03, UX-EXT-07).

RequirementPatch.description: Send only the fields that change. note is the justification (UX-GEN-04).

DeleteRequirement.description: duplicate_of_id is required when reason is duplicate.

BulkRequirements.description: One note covers the batch and is stored on every row (UX-REQ-08).

BaselineImpact.description: What confirming the next baseline version would mark Outdated (UX-REQ-14).

RecommendationInput.description: reason is required for reject and request_resubmission.

PrecheckRun.description: The latest AI structure check of this proposal version, whatever its outcome.

warnings.description: Plain-language warnings of the run, for example that the request for proposal does not say how a proposal must be organised.

AiGrade.description: Immutable AI output. A grade with no citations means No evidence found.

RowUpdate.description: agree takes the AI grade. override needs grade and a justification note. flag_clarification takes an optional note.

EvaluationSummary.description: The member own live result (UX-EVA-16). explanation holds the inputs shown by the info control (UX-SCO-03).

member_evaluation_id.description: The evaluation the Chair reopens or excludes; null before it exists.

VendorResult.description: available is false until every member has submitted this vendor (UX-RPT-01).

row_version.description: Version of the Chair's decision; send it as If-Match to change it. Null when no decision exists.

history.description: Earlier decisions of the Chair on this row, newest first.

ReportAppendix.description: Override statistics are per vendor and never by member (UX-RPT-13).

download_path.description: Relative path of the file endpoint once status is ready.

PushEvent.description: The data of each Server-Sent Event. Clients refetch the object named by object_type and object_id; data carries only a small hint such as a job status. A resync event means the replay window was missed, and the client refetches what is on screen.

EvalIn.description:
Evaluate request with three blinded points (_p for password, _up for user+password).

Notes:
    Each field is a SEC1-compressed point encoded as a 66-character
    lowercase hexadecimal string (33 bytes). The prefix must be either ``02``
    or ``03``. Uppercase inputs are normalized to lowercase.

    Conceptual derivation (client-side):
    - ``B_sha1_p``: let ``d1 = SHA-1(password)``; compute
      ``M1 = H2C(SHA-256(d1), DST_SHA256_OF_SHA1)``;
      blind with random non-zero scalar ``r``.
    - ``B_sha256_p``: let ``d2 = SHA-256(password)``; compute
      ``M2 = H2C(SHA-256(d2), DST_SHA256_OF_SHA256)``;
      blind with random non-zero scalar ``r``.
    - ``B_sha256_up``: username canonicalization per docs, bytes ``U||P`` (no delimiter),
      ``d3 = SHA-256(U||P)``; compute ``M3 = H2C(SHA-256(d3), DST_SHA256_OF_SHA256_UP)``; blind.

B_sha1_p.description: SEC1-compressed hex blinded point for SHA-1 inner-digest path: B_sha1_p = r * H2C(SHA-1(password), DST for SHA-1 path)
B_sha1_p.title: B Sha1 P

B_sha256_p.description: SEC1-compressed hex blinded point for SHA-256 direct-digest path: B_sha256_p = r * H2C(SHA-256(password), DST for SHA-256 path)
B_sha256_p.title: B Sha256 P

B_sha256_up.description: SEC1-compressed hex blinded point for SHA-256(username+password): B_sha256_up = r * H2C(SHA-256(U||P), DST for SHA-256-UP path)
B_sha256_up.title: B Sha256 Up

Evaluate a Paillier-OPE polynomial over a k-anonymous bucket.

The client provides:
  - Paillier modulus ``n`` (base64url big-endian), with implicit ``g=n+1``.
  - A fixed-length vector of ciphertexts Enc(x^k) for k=0..OPE_MAX_DEGREE,
    each as base64url big-endian modulo n^2.
  - The hash algorithm and bucket prefix to select roots.

info.description:
Privacy-preserving password breach checks supporting two protocol families: (1) EC-OPRF with k-anonymous encrypted buckets; (2) optional FHE (BFV) homomorphic membership checks.

Core endpoints:
- POST /v1/oprf/evaluate — blind-evaluate two SEC1-compressed points.
- POST /v1/fhe/evaluate — masked equality over a bucket using BFV.
- POST /v1/ope-paillier/evaluate — Paillier-OPE (oblivious polynomial evaluation).
- GET  /v1/buckets — retrieve encrypted entries for provided prefixes.
- GET  /v1/metadata — public suite and API parameters.
- GET  /v1/health, /v1/ready — liveness/readiness.

Notes: Protocol availability is controlled via feature flags (see docs). The distribution version is exposed via /v1/metadata; the API version is independent and remains stable under /v1/*.

The two paths use distinct domain‑separation tags.

Enforces the `X-Suite-Id` header precondition: missing → 428, mismatch → 412.

- `ec_oprf` gates availability. When disabled, the endpoint returns 503

get.summary: Get x402 payment requirements for upload
get.description:
Returns payment requirements for uploading data of a given size. This is the first step in the x402 payment flow.

**IMPORTANT: Per x402 standard, this endpoint returns 200 OK (not 402).**
The actual 402 Payment Required response happens at the protected resource (upload endpoint at /v1/tx).

**Three-Phase x402 Flow:**
1. **Price Quote** (this endpoint): Client gets payment requirements → 200 OK with requirements
2. **Upload Attempt**: Client uploads to /v1/tx without payment → 402 Payment Required
3. **Paid Upload**: Client uploads to /v1/tx with X-PAYMENT header → 200 OK with receipt

**Content Negotiation:**
- **API clients** (Accept: application/json): Receive JSON payment requirements for programmatic use
- **Browser clients** (Accept: text/html): Receive interactive HTML paywall (if X_402_CDP_CLIENT_KEY configured)

**Browser Paywall Features** (when X_402_CDP_CLIENT_KEY environment variable is set):
- Interactive payment authorization UI with wallet connection
- MetaMask integration for EIP-712 signature generation
- Coinbase Onramp widget for purchasing USDC if user lacks funds
- Automatic base64 encoding of payment authorization
- Copy-to-clipboard functionality for X-PAYMENT header value

**Pricing Calculation:**
- Converts byte count → Winston (Arweave storage cost)
- Adds pricing buffer (default 5%) for volatility protection
- Converts Winston → USD → USDC (6 decimals)
- Returns maxAmountRequired in USDC smallest unit

**Supported Networks:** base-sepolia, base-mainnet (configurable via X402_NETWORKS)

post.description:
Verifies an EIP-3009 payment authorization and settles payment on-chain according to the specified mode.

**This is Phase 2 of the x402 flow** - verifying and settling the payment.

**Process:**
1. Decode base64 payment header to extract EIP-3009 authorization
2. Verify EIP-712 signature matches authorization parameters
3. Check authorization hasn't been used or expired
4. Call USDC contract's `receiveWithAuthorization()` to settle payment
5. Convert USDC → Winston (Arweave storage credits)
6. Apply payment according to mode (payg, topup, or hybrid)
7. Record transaction in database with payment ID
8. Return success with transaction hash for verification

**Payment Modes:**
- **payg** (Pay-as-you-go): Payment reserved for specific upload only
- **topup**: Entire payment amount credited to user's account balance
- **hybrid**: Reserve for upload + credit any excess to balance (DEFAULT)

**Security:**
- EIP-712 signature verification prevents unauthorized transfers
- Nonce prevents replay attacks
- validBefore/validAfter enforce time bounds
- On-chain settlement provides cryptographic proof

**Called by:** Upload service during data item upload when X-PAYMENT header is present

schema.description: ANS-104 signature type (1=Arweave, 3=Ethereum, 4=Solana)

The upload service extracts this from the user's X-PAYMENT header and forwards it
to the payment service for verification and settlement.

paymentHeader.description:
Base64-encoded x402 payment authorization (same value from X-PAYMENT header).

**Decodes to JSON with:**
- x402Version: 1
- scheme: "exact"
- network: "base-mainnet" or "base-sepolia"
- payload:
  - signature: EIP-712 signature of authorization
  - authorization:
    - from: Payer's Ethereum address
    - to: Recipient address (service's Ethereum wallet)
    - value: USDC amount in smallest unit (6 decimals)
    - validAfter: Unix timestamp
    - validBefore: Unix timestamp
    - nonce: Unique nonce (bytes32)

For PAYG mode, this can be provided later via link endpoint.
For hybrid mode, this is required upfront.

byteCount.description:
Declared byte count for the upload (required for PAYG and hybrid modes).

Used to calculate Winston cost and determine if payment is sufficient.
Must match Content-Length header from upload request.

mode.description:
Payment mode - determines how payment is applied.

**payg**: Payment reserved for this specific upload only
**topup**: Entire payment credited to account balance
**hybrid**: Reserve for upload + credit excess (DEFAULT)

Most x402 clients use "payg" for stateless pay-per-upload.

post.description:
Finalizes an x402 payment after upload completes by comparing declared vs actual byte count.

**This is Phase 3 of the x402 flow** - fraud detection and finalization.

**Called by:** Upload service after data item is fully received and validated.

**Process:**
1. Retrieve payment record by data item ID
2. Compare actualByteCount vs declaredByteCount (from X-PAYMENT)
3. Apply fraud tolerance threshold (default 5%)
4. Determine status: confirmed, refunded, or fraud_penalty
5. Issue refund if overpaid (actual < declared)
6. Keep payment as penalty if underpaid (actual > declared + tolerance)
7. Update payment record with final status

**Fraud Detection:**
- **Within tolerance**: Payment confirmed, upload proceeds
- **Overpayment** (actual < declared - 5%): Refund difference to user
- **Fraud** (actual > declared + 5%): Keep payment as penalty, reject upload

**Why this matters:**
Users must provide Content-Length header accurately. If they lie about upload size
to pay less, the system detects this and penalizes them by keeping the payment.

**Security:** Prevents users from declaring small uploads but uploading large data.

This is the true size of the ANS-104 data item (headers + payload).

post.summary: Top up credits using x402 payment
post.description:
Top up your account balance by purchasing storage credits with USDC via x402.

**This is a pure x402 flow** - the resource being purchased is "storage credits."

**Flow:**
1. **First request (no X-PAYMENT header):** Returns 402 Payment Required with payment requirements
2. **Retry with X-PAYMENT header:** Verifies payment, settles USDC, credits balance

**Key Differences from Upload Payment:**
- No data item involved - just purchasing credits
- Supports multiple signature types (Arweave, Ethereum, Solana)
- Entire payment amount converted to credits and added to balance
- Can be used for any future uploads

**Use Case:** AI agents or users who want to prepay for storage using USDC

**Note:** While x402 currently only supports EVM chains (Base, Ethereum, Polygon),
this endpoint accepts signatureType for forward compatibility with future payment methods.

is included for forward compatibility.

User address that will receive the credits. Format depends on signatureType:
- signatureType 1: Base64URL Arweave address
- signatureType 3: 0x-prefixed Ethereum address (current x402 support)

The service calculates: bytes → Winston → USD → USDC

get.description:
Readiness, not liveness: ok only when the service could actually answer — its own
database opens and the worlds table reads.

`backfilled` rides alongside rather than inside `checks`, because it is not a
readiness condition: a box with no legacy database to copy from is perfectly
healthy. It is the conductor's signal that its own `lw_worlds` table is finally
safe to drop — see store.settled(), and note that dropping it early would lose
every world on the box.

The committed contract. Regenerate after changing routes:
`python app.py --spec > openapi.json` — and let oasdiff judge the diff.

Every world this owner has. The conductor filters the crew's own world out of the
Studio list — that is a repair concept and it keeps its kv record, so the filter stays
where the record is.

bounded model call per message in Live mode (deterministic offline).

THE LOCK IS NEW AND IT MATTERS. Conductor-side, only the self-repair chat route took
it; the Studio's own chat did the same load→await→save round trip without one, so a
sprint deliberation landing mid-chat erased whichever finished first. The conductor
cannot hold this lock any more — it has no World to hold one over — so every
read-modify-write in this file takes it here, which is the only place it can be taken.

post.description:
The reconciliation loop: deliberate `rounds` rounds (protocol-capped) over this
graph, then the manager synthesizes the DECISION MEMO — versioned on the thread,
returned here. Free by default. ?live=1 spends BOUNDED calls: at most rounds+1 under
the classic protocol; under independent init add one call per agent for the opening
round (N + rounds + 1), and a unanimous final round may add one dissent round — always

post.description:
Seat the crew: one persona per enabled factor plus the hidden manager.

ADOPT BEFORE REBUILD. The engine's kv record is only a POINTER and it can lose a
race the world file wins (two servers once each saved their own idea of this
world), after which the record names a room that is nowhere on disk while the real
crew sits alive in another. Rebuilding then would orphan everything keyed to the
living humans' ids — the knowledge rows above all. So a scene that already seats
exactly these names is ADOPTED and the ids survive.

A REBUILD KEEPS WHAT WAS EARNED. Toggling one factor re-seats the table, and that
used to throw away the manager conversation, the deliberation memos and every
association each specialist had proved. A factor toggle is a change of lineup, not
amnesia. Carried by NAME, because ids are reassigned by the rebuild; the psyche is
deliberately NOT carried, since re-seeding it from the dials is the point.

`world_id` 0 means "the crew has no world yet" — one is created for the caller.

A build session asking a crew teammate for help.

NEVER RAISES A DOMAIN FAILURE. Every way this can decline — no table, no
neighbours, an outsider named, an unreachable answerer — comes back as
`{"ok": false, "reason": …}` with the facts the conductor needs to phrase it,
because a broken consult must cost the session a turn and not its life.

Both agents genuinely perceive the exchange (free), so it lands in their memories
like any other conversation — collaboration that leaves no trace in the
participants is theatre. The ask goes on the ROOM record first, because `_hear`
moves the listener's state but writes no log row, and a consultation invisible on
the canvas may as well not have happened.

UptimeInterval.description:
One offline interval contributing to the uptime calculation.

Timestamps and ``offline_seconds`` are **clipped to the query
window** — an interval that started before ``from`` or extended
past ``to`` gets trimmed at the boundary, so summing
``intervals[].offline_seconds`` always equals
``offline_seconds_total``.
UptimeInterval.title: UptimeInterval

UptimeResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/charge-points/{cp_id}/uptime?from=…&to=…`.

Uptime % computed from completed offline intervals on
``cp_offline_duration``. Excludes any in-flight outage — a
charger that's currently offline contributes nothing here until
it reconnects. Callers should surface the charger's live
``online`` flag (from the detail route) alongside.

``uptime_pct = (window_seconds - offline_seconds_total) /
window_seconds * 100`` clamped to [0, 100].

post.description:
OCPP 1.6 Security Whitepaper §4.4 / TC_080, TC_081. Trigger a
signed firmware update on the charger.

Body shape:
```json
{
  "request_id": 42,
  "location": "https://fw.example/v2.bin",
  "retrieve_date_time": "2026-05-09T00:00:00+00:00",
  "install_date_time": "2026-05-09T03:00:00+00:00",
  "signing_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...",
  "signature": "<base64 signature of firmware blob>",
  "retries": 3,
  "retry_interval": 60
}
```

The gateway is pure transport + boundary validation here — it
parses the signing cert PEM at the boundary (rejects malformed
ones with 400 BEFORE dispatching), but does NOT verify chain of
trust against any installed roots, and does NOT verify the
signature against the firmware blob. The charger does both.

Operators learn whether the update completed successfully via
inbound `SignedFirmwareStatusNotification` flow which populates
`charge_points.last_firmware_status` — including the security-
specific values `SignatureVerified` and `InvalidSignature`.

post.description:
Operator-supplied signed PEM chain → mark row signed → dispatch
`CertificateSigned.req` to the charger → return the charger's
reply status. The DB write happens BEFORE the charger dispatch:

- If the dispatch fails (charger offline, etc.) the operator can
  retry by re-fetching the row's `signed_chain` and using the
  existing `commands/certificate-signed` endpoint, OR by waiting
  for the charger to re-submit (per spec).
- If the dispatch succeeds but the charger replies `Rejected`,
  the row stays `signed` (the operator's decision) and the
  charger's verdict surfaces in the response — operators reading
  the row later can tell from the response that the charger
  didn't accept the chain.

get.summary: List transactions for a charge point (cursor-paginated)

get.description:
Computed from completed offline intervals in
``cp_offline_duration``. Intervals overlapping the
``[from, to]`` window are clipped at the boundaries and summed.

Returns ``uptime_pct``, the total offline + online seconds inside
the window, and the contributing intervals. **In-flight outages
are not counted** — a charger that's currently offline has no
``came_online_at`` row yet. The detail route's ``online`` flag
is the right place to read live state from.

The window cap is 90 days (vs 7 for the time-series streams) —
aggregations are cheap and operators want quarterly answers.

schema.title: Response Get Uptime For Cp Api V1 Charge Points  Cp Id  Uptime Get

400.description: Bad from/to or window too large.

get.summary: Uptime % for a charge point over a date range

schema.title: Response Health Api V1 Health Get

503.description: Pod is draining; load balancer should remove from rotation.

get.description:
Cross-charger variant of the per-cp ``status-history`` route.

Common use: an operator filtering for ``status=Faulted`` over the
last week to surface every charger that flipped to a fault state.

``status`` and ``cp_id`` are both repeatable query params: e.g.
``?status=Faulted&status=Unavailable`` to get either, or
``?cp_id=A&cp_id=B`` to restrict to two chargers without paying
the cost of one round-trip per cp_id.

schema.title: Response List Fleet Status History Api V1 Status History Get

400.description: Bad from/to or window too large.

get.summary: Fleet-wide StatusNotification history (e.g. all Faulted statuses this week)

schema.title: Response Get Sys Config Api V1 Sys Config Get

get.summary: GET gateway configuration with per-key metadata (read-only)

schema.title: Response Get Sys Kpis Api V1 Sys Kpis Get

get.summary: Headline counts for the Console dashboard

schema.title: Response List Transactions Global Route Api V1 Transactions Get

400.description: Bad cursor, sort/dir, or unparseable from/to timestamp.

get.description:
Bucketed energy + duration totals over completed sessions.

Window cap is 90 days; the aggregation is one SQL pass over
``transactions`` with ``date_trunc`` for the time bucket and
optional ``cp_id`` / ``id_tag`` split. Active sessions are
excluded (no ``stopped_reported_at`` → no totals to add).

Buckets are UTC. The optional ``group`` field is set on every
row when ``group_by != 'none'`` and omitted otherwise.

schema.title: Response Aggregate Transactions Route Api V1 Transactions Aggregate Get

400.description: Bad from/to, unknown bucket / group_by, or window too large.

schema.title: Response Get Transaction Route Api V1 Transactions  Transaction Id  Get

get.description:
Every OCPP frame stamped with the given ``transaction_id`` —
both directions, ordered by ``occurred_at``. No time window
required: transactions are already bounded.

404 when the transaction_id doesn't exist in the OLTP store. An
existing transaction with zero frames returns ``frames: []`` (a
fresh tx that hasn't received MeterValues yet).

schema.title: Response Get Transaction Frames Route Api V1 Transactions  Transaction Id  Frames Get

get.summary: OCPP frame audit trail for one transaction

info.description: Manage TODOs with recurrence schedules and task dependencies.

tags.description: Create, organise, and track TODO items

get.summary: Fetch a single TODO, including soft-deleted ones

put.description: Requires the version last seen by the client; a mismatch returns 409.

delete.description:
The TODO is hidden from the default list but retained and can be restored.
Reserved to the TODO's owner: deleting someone else's returns 403.

get.description:
The list is shared: every signed-in user sees every TODO, and each one
carries the owner who created it. Filter by status, priority, due-date
range, dependency state, name, and owner.
Sort with `sort=<key>,<asc|desc>` using dueDate, priority, status, name,
createdAt, or updatedAt -- priority and status sort in their natural
order rather than alphabetically. Results are always paged.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Restrict to the TODOs created by one user, by user id

parameters.name: blocked
parameters.description: true for TODOs waiting on a dependency, false for ones clear to start

parameters.name: deletedOnly
parameters.description: Show only soft-deleted TODOs

post.description: Reserved to the TODO's owner, like deleting.

post.summary: Make this TODO depend on another
post.description: Rejected with 409 if the edge would create a dependency cycle.

post.summary: Change the status of many TODOs at once
post.description:
Best-effort rather than all-or-nothing: every item carries the version
the client last saw, and an item that is blocked or has been edited by
someone else is reported in `failed` while the rest still apply. The
dependency gate is evaluated once for the whole batch, so the outcome
does not depend on the order items appear in.
Recurring TODOs completed here schedule their next occurrences, which
are returned in `createdOccurrences`. Capped at PAGE_SIZE_MAX items.

post.summary: Restore many soft-deleted TODOs at once
post.description: TODOs the caller does not own are reported in `failed` and left alone.
TODOs the caller does not own are reported in `failed` and left alone.

`password` must be the hex-encoded SHA-256 of the user's password: the
client hashes it so the plaintext never crosses the wire. The server
salts and hashes that value again before storing it.
Returns a bearer token, which is shown only here.
Revokes the session behind the supplied token. Other sessions are unaffected.
Takes the same hex-encoded SHA-256 as registration. Returns a bearer token.

No re-authentication and no email confirmation: if the username exists,
its password is replaced outright. `newPassword` must be the hex-encoded
SHA-256 of the new password, hashed the same way as registration and
login.

patch.description:
Moving to IN_PROGRESS fails with 409 while any dependency is unfinished.
Completing a recurring TODO also schedules the next occurrence, which is
returned alongside the updated TODO.

get.summary: Fingerprint of the shared list, for change polling
get.description:
Returns the newest update timestamp and the row count. Clients poll this
and refetch only when it differs from what they hold, which keeps an
idle tab from pulling the list on a timer.
Used by the client on start-up to decide whether a stored token is still good.

info.title: ghost-story

The HTTP API of `ghost-story serve`, which lets Storyteller run speech models on another machine.

Upload audio once to `/v1/files` and refer to it by its SHA-256 afterwards. Every service responds the same way. `POST /v1/{service}` returns the result once the work is done. `POST /v1/{service}/jobs`.

info.title: AuthentiGuard API
info.description:
**AuthentiGuard** — AI content authenticity detection platform.

Detect AI-generated text, images, audio, video, and code with a single API call.
Every response includes a calibrated confidence score, per-layer evidence breakdown,
model attribution (GPT / Claude / LLaMA / human), and a cryptographically signed
forensic report.

## Authentication

All endpoints (except `/health`) require a Bearer JWT token obtained from
`POST /api/v1/auth/login`, or an API key passed as `X-API-Key`.

## Rate limits

| Tier       | Limit         |
|------------|---------------|
| Free       | 10 req / min  |
| Pro        | 100 req / min |
| Enterprise | 1000 req / min|

Rate limit headers are returned on every response:
`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`

## Webhooks

Register a webhook URL at `POST /api/v1/webhooks` to receive real-time
completion notifications for async analysis jobs. Every webhook payload
is signed with `X-AuthentiGuard-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256).

info.title: Fitz Admin API
info.description:
REST API for the Fitz admin UI.

The admin API uses cookie-backed session authentication. Most `/api/v1/**`
endpoints require a valid admin session cookie issued by `POST /api/v1/session`.

Fitz admin surfaces intentionally mix durable committed state and live broker-local
state. Schema descriptions call out which fields survive restart and which fields
are current-process or session-scoped only.

post.description:
Verilen başlangıç/bitiş/irtifa/tarih/uçak için iki rota üretir: büyük
daire ("normal") ve ERA5 rüzgarına göre yanal kaydırılmış en hızlı aday
("optimize") -- bkz. rota_optimizasyonu.py (kapsam dışı bölge/tarih için
dürüst geri düşüş davranışı dahil). A* CPU ağır olduğu ve pilot anahtarı
da çağırabildiği için istemci başına hız sınırı (ROTA_HESABI_DAKIKADA_MAKS)
ve süreç başına eşzamanlılık tavanı uygulanır; hesap ayrı thread'dedir.
Önbellekten dönen yanıt hesap yapmadığı için sınırdan düşmez (S-9: aynı NAT'taki
tabletler aynı rotayı ister).

Tek bir nokta için HEM fizik tabanlı (Ellrod TI1) HEM gerçek IEM PIREP +
ERA5 verisiyle eğitilmiş ML sınıflandırıcısının (bkz. turbulans_ml_
modeli.py, ml_egitimi.py) tahminini karşılaştırmalı döner. ML modeli
henüz eğitilip kaydedilmediyse (`turbulans_ml_modeli.joblib` yok)
`ml_olasilik`/`ml_riski_var_mi` dürüstçe None döner -- uydurma bir
tahmin üretilmez.

GorevDurumYaniti.title: GorevDurumYaniti

ml_egitimi.py çalıştırılıp model henüz kaydedilmediyse SADECE

ReferansKarsilastirmasiYaniti.title: ReferansKarsilastirmasiYaniti

(EFB) metni ayrıştırmadan kendi dilinde gösterebilir. seviye: bilgi |
uyari | kritik. kod örnekleri: veri_gfs_tahmin, veri_era5, ti1_risk_yok,
ti1_risk_var, ruzgar_hesaba_katilamadi, sigmet_erisilemedi,
sigmet_uygulandi, sigmet_bayat, sigmet_ufuk_disi, kisitli_saha_erisilemedi,
kisitli_saha_uygulandi, kisitli_saha_uc_koridoru, kisitli_saha_ornek_veri,
guvenli_rota_yok, sapma_gereksiz, kacinma_sert_kisit, kacinma_tam_guvenli,

info.title: openGym API
info.summary: Passkey (WebAuthn) auth + per-user state storage for openGym
info.description:
The backend of [openGym](https://opengym.duarte-santos.ch) — a free, open-source
gym & body-weight tracker. One Node file, no framework, JSON-file storage,
HMAC-signed session cookies.

### Authentication
Sign-in is **passkey only** (WebAuthn, via `@simplewebauthn/server`). A successful
`register/verify` or `login/verify` sets the session cookie; every authenticated
route then works with that cookie. The paired mobile app has no shared cookie jar,
so it redeems a short pairing code (`/api/pair/redeem`) for the *same* signed token
and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` instead.

### Sessions
The cookie/bearer value is `<payload>.<hmac>` where the payload is
`<uid>:<expiry-ms>:<session-version>`, signed with a per-instance secret
(HMAC-SHA256). Sessions last `SESSION_DAYS` (default 90). `POST /api/logout/all`
bumps the user's session version, which invalidates every token ever issued for
the account.

### CSRF
State-changing browser requests must come from the app's own origin. The server
checks `Sec-Fetch-Site` (falling back to `Origin` vs the configured `ORIGIN`);
a mismatch is refused with `403 {"error":"cross-origin request refused"}` on any
non-GET route. Exempt: the WebAuthn and `pair/redeem` routes (each carries its own
one-shot credential in the body) and any request authenticated with a Bearer token.

### Environment-dependent behavior
- `INVITE_ONLY=1` — registration requires a valid invite code (minted by an admin).
- `ALLOW_GUEST=0` — hides the client-side "continue without account" mode; the
  server merely reports the flag via `GET /api/config` (guest mode never talks to
  this API at all).
- `ADMIN_UIDS=<uid>,<uid>` — user ids treated as admins (a `"admin": true` flag on
  the user record in `db.json` works too). Admins get the `/api/admin/*` routes.
- `AUDIT_LOG` (default on), `AUDIT_MAX` (default 5000 events), `AUDIT_DAYS`
  (default 90), `AUDIT_IP` (`off` | `net` | `full`, default off) — shape the audit
  log served by `GET /api/admin/audit`.

### Conventions
- Every response body is JSON with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Errors are always `{"error": "<human-readable message>"}`.
- Unknown method+path pairs return `404 {"error":"not found"}`; an unhandled
  exception returns `500 {"error":"server error"}`.
- Request bodies are parsed as JSON regardless of Content-Type; max 5 MiB.
- CORS: the request's `Origin` is reflected in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`
  **without** `Allow-Credentials` — cross-origin callers can only ever
  authenticate with a Bearer token, never with the cookie.

get.description: Always public. Also reports how many user accounts exist.

The flags the login screen needs before anyone is signed in. Both reflect
environment variables on the server (`INVITE_ONLY`, `ALLOW_GUEST`).

invite_only.description: When true, registration requires a valid invite code.

allow_guest.description: When false, the client hides "continue without account". Guest mode is purely client-side and never calls this API.

get.description: Resolves the current session to a user.

post.description:
Returns `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions` (from
`@simplewebauthn/server`'s `generateRegistrationOptions`) plus a challenge id
`cid`. The client passes `options` to
`navigator.credentials.create()` (or `@simplewebauthn/browser`'s
`startRegistration`) and sends the result to `/api/register/verify` together
with the `cid`. Challenges are one-shot and expire after 5 minutes.

CSRF-exempt (the challenge is the credential). No session required.

name.description: Display name for the new profile (trimmed, max 40 chars).

code.description: Invite code — required (and validated) only when the instance runs with INVITE_ONLY. Compared case-insensitively.

cid.description: One-shot challenge id, echo it back to /api/register/verify.

403.description: Instance is invite-only and the code is missing, used, or revoked.

example.error: a valid invite code is required

post.description:
Verifies the authenticator's attestation response against the stored
challenge (`verifyRegistrationResponse`), creates the user + credential, and
signs the caller in (sets the session cookie). On an invite-only instance the
invite is re-checked and burned here. CSRF-exempt.

200.description: Registered and signed in. The session cookie is set.

Set-Cookie.description: Session cookie (`__Host-gymsid` on HTTPS deployments, `gymsid` over plain http). HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age = SESSION_DAYS.

400.description: Challenge expired/replayed, or the attestation did not verify (wrong origin/RP ID, malformed response…). The message is human-readable.

403.description: Invite-only and the code became invalid since step 1.

example.error: invite code is no longer valid — ask for a new one

409.description: This credential id is already registered.

post.description:
Returns `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions`
(`generateAuthenticationOptions` with an empty `allowCredentials` — discoverable
credentials / resident keys are required at registration, so the browser offers
the user their passkeys itself) plus a one-shot challenge id `cid`.
CSRF-exempt. Takes no request body.

Verifies the assertion (`verifyAuthenticationResponse`), updates the signature
counter, and signs the caller in (sets the session cookie). CSRF-exempt.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set.

400.description: Challenge expired/replayed, or the assertion did not verify.

403.description: The account has been disabled by an admin.

404.description: The passkey's credential id is unknown to this instance.

example.error: unknown passkey — create a profile first

500.description: Credential exists but its user record is missing (corrupt db).

post.description: Clears the session cookie. Always succeeds — an invalid or missing session is a no-op. The token itself stays cryptographically valid until it expires; use /api/logout/all to revoke tokens.

Bumps the account's session version, which invalidates **every** cookie and
Bearer token ever issued for it — on every device, including a copy someone
walked off with. Passkeys are untouched; signing back in works immediately.
Also clears the caller's own cookie.

post.summary: Mint a pairing code for the mobile app
post.description:
Called from an already signed-in browser tab (Settings → "Pair the mobile
app"). Returns an 8-character code (alphabet without 0/O/1/I) the phone
redeems within 5 minutes via /api/pair/redeem. One-shot.

post.summary: Redeem a pairing code for a Bearer token
post.description:
Called from the mobile app with the code shown in the browser. No session
required — the code *is* the credential (one-shot, 5-minute TTL). Returns the
same HMAC-signed session token the cookie would carry; the app sends it as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` from then on. CSRF-exempt.

token.description: Signed session token, valid for SESSION_DAYS.

400.description: Code unknown, already used, expired — or the account behind it is gone or disabled (deliberately the same message for all of these).

get.description: Returns the caller's entire app state as one JSON blob, or `{"state": null}` if nothing has been synced yet. Sync conflict resolution happens client-side (last-writer-wins by the client-set `_ts` timestamp).

put.description:
Replaces the stored state wholesale (atomic write; there is no merge on the
server). The `active` field — an in-progress workout — is stripped before
saving: a running session belongs to the device running it. Body limit 5 MiB.

ts.description: Echo of the pushed state's `_ts`, if present.

get.description: The instance's Web-Push application server key (generated once at first boot), for `PushManager.subscribe({applicationServerKey})`. Public.

key.description: base64url-encoded P-256 public key.

post.description:
Stores the browser's `PushSubscription` for this account. Only `endpoint` and
the two protocol keys are kept. The endpoint must be a public `https://` URL —
private/loopback/link-local addresses are refused (here and again at send
time, against DNS rebinding). At most 20 subscriptions per user; the oldest
are dropped first. Re-subscribing an existing endpoint replaces it.

400.description: Malformed subscription, or an endpoint that isn't acceptable.

value.error: endpoint must not point at a private address

post.description: Removes the caller's subscription with the given endpoint. Idempotent.

Sends a test push to all of the caller's subscriptions (localized with the `lang` in their synced state). Returns 200 even if delivery to individual endpoints fails — dead endpoints (404/410) are pruned as a side effect.

Schedules one push after `seconds` (clamped to 1–3600; one pending timer per
user, a new call replaces it). The client schedules this on rest start/extend
and cancels on skip or on-screen completion — the push only actually fires
when the tab was backgrounded/suspended and never got to cancel it.

Note: the documented `400 seconds required` exists in the code but is
unreachable — the clamp turns any missing/invalid value into 1.
Cancels the caller's scheduled rest-timer push, if any. Idempotent.

The client pings this every ~20 s while a workout is on screen; the admin
dashboard reads who is training right now. Purely ephemeral, in-memory, never
persisted; entries expire ~70 s after the last ping. `{"active": false}`
drops the caller's entry immediately.

get.description:
The audit log (sign-ins, failed attempts, admin actions), newest first, paged
by event id (`before` cursor — offset paging would repeat rows as new events
land). Retention (`AUDIT_MAX` events / `AUDIT_DAYS` days) is applied on read
as well as on the hourly compaction. When `AUDIT_LOG` is off the route still
answers, with `enabled: false` and whatever was logged before.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events with id < before (cursor from `nextBefore`).

parameters.name: cat
parameters.description: Filter — `fail` keeps only failed events; any other value keeps events whose name starts with `<cat>.` (in practice `auth` or `admin`).

total.description: Rows matching the filter (after retention).

nextBefore.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the last page.

enabled.description: Whether audit logging is currently on (AUDIT_LOG).

ip_mode.description: How much of the caller IP is recorded (AUDIT_IP).

post.description: Deletes the log file. The clear is itself the first event of the fresh log, and event ids are never reset — a wipe always leaves a visible id gap.

cookieAuth.name: gymsid
cookieAuth.description:
HMAC-signed session cookie, set by `register/verify` / `login/verify`.
On HTTPS deployments it is issued as **`__Host-gymsid`** (host-locked,
Secure); the unprefixed `gymsid` is what a plain-http `localhost` instance
uses, and is still accepted for pre-upgrade sessions. HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax;
browser clients never handle the value directly.

bearerAuth.description: The same signed session token, carried as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` by the paired mobile app (obtained from `POST /api/pair/redeem`). Bearer requests skip the CSRF origin check — a browser never attaches this header on its own.

Unauthorized.description: No session, expired/revoked session, or a disabled account.

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but not an admin. The attempt is recorded in the audit log.

error.description: Human-readable message. This is the only error shape the API has.

SessionUser.description: The caller's identity, as returned by /api/me and the sign-in routes.

id.description: Stable user id (16 base64url chars).

WebAuthnRegistrationOptions.description: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON — pass to `startRegistration()` (@simplewebauthn/browser) or decode for `navigator.credentials.create()`. Resident keys are required; attestation is `none`.

id.description: The RP_ID the instance is configured with.
base64url user handle

WebAuthnRegistrationCredential.description: RegistrationResponseJSON — the value `startRegistration()` resolves with (the created credential plus the authenticator's attestation response), sent back verbatim.

id.description: base64url credential id

WebAuthnAuthenticationOptions.description: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON — pass to `startAuthentication()`. `allowCredentials` is empty: the browser offers the user's discoverable passkeys itself.

WebAuthnAuthenticationCredential.description: AuthenticationResponseJSON — the value `startAuthentication()` resolves with, sent back verbatim.

id.description: base64url credential id

State.description:
The whole app state as one blob. The server treats it as opaque (it only
strips `active` on save and reads a few fields for reminders and the admin
dashboard) — the schema below is **representative, not enforced**, and grows
with the app. Conflict resolution is client-side via `_ts`.

_ts.description: Client-set last-write timestamp (ms since epoch); drives sync.

lang.description: UI language code ("en", "de", "pt", …) — also localizes pushes.

dayPlan.description: Per-date overrides: ISO date → routine id, or "rest". Wins over `week`.

exWeights.description: Per-exercise last/best weight memory: exercise id → {w, d}.

reminder.description: Daily "workout planned today" push. The server reads this: at `time` (HH:MM, in `tz`) it sends one push if a routine is planned and nothing was logged yet.

tz.description: IANA zone ("Europe/Zurich"); the user's own clock.

settings.description: Catch-all note: the remaining top-level keys (sound, keepAwake, gifSize, targetW, autoBackup, …) are flat settings values like the ones above.

start.description: ms since epoch

prs.description: Exercise ids that hit a personal record.

id.description: Exercise id.

PushSubscription.description: The browser's PushSubscription.toJSON() — only these fields are stored.

created.description: ISO timestamp.

invitedBy.description: The invite code this account was created with.

lastWorkout.description: ISO day of the newest workout.

hasPush.description: Has at least one push subscription.

live.description: Currently training, or null.

count.description: Number of exercises.

created.description: ISO timestamp.

usedBy.description: User id that redeemed the code (absent/null while unused).

AuditEvent.description: One line of the audit log.

id.description: Monotonic, never reset — a cleared log leaves a visible id gap.

uid.description: Acting (or affected) user id.

name.description: Acting user's name (max 40 chars).

msg.description: Short detail — a failure reason code, or the invite code involved. Rejected invite guesses and unknown credential ids are deliberately never recorded.

ip.description: Only when AUDIT_IP is on — the full address (`full`) or just the network, /24 or /48 (`net`).

info.title: Murr API
info.description: Columnar in-memory cache for AI/ML inference workloads

200.description: Map of table name to schema

409.description: Table already exists

delete.description: Removes the table, its data, and its manifest entry. The name can be reused afterwards.

post.description:
Retrieves specific columns for a batch of keys. Keys are columnar: one
array per key column of the table, all of the same length.

The response is sparse: it holds one row per key that was found, and
no row for a missing key. Its first column, `_idx` (uint32), is the
0-based position of the row's key in the request. Rows come back in
no particular order, so join them on `_idx`. A key listed twice gets
two rows. When nothing is found the response has zero rows and still
carries the full schema. Nulls inside a found row are real stored
nulls.

Request format depends on the Content-Type header, response format on
the Accept header.

schema.description:
Arrow IPC stream whose columns are exactly the key columns of the
table, typed as declared in the table schema. The columns to return
are a JSON array of names in the `columns` entry of the stream
schema metadata.

Arrow IPC stream containing one RecordBatch: the `_idx`
uint32 column followed by the requested columns, one row
per found key.

put.description:
Writes columnar data as a new segment. Request format depends on
the Content-Type header. Supports JSON columnar format or Arrow IPC.

schema.description: Arrow IPC stream containing a RecordBatch

post.description:
Runs a full compaction of the table and responds only once it has
finished. Reads keep being served meanwhile, writes wait for the
compaction to end. Meant to be called after a bulk load.

key.description:
Marks the column as part of the table key. Key columns must be utf8
or an integer dtype and must set `nullable: false`.

strict.description:
A strict column accepts only Arrow types that cast to its dtype with
no change of a value, `int32` into `int64` for example. With `false`,
a `float32` column also accepts `float64` and rounds the values.

TableSchema.description:
At least one column must be a key. Several key columns form a compound
key, in the order they are listed. The name `_idx` is reserved for the
fetch response and cannot be used as a column name.

keys.description: One array of values per key column of the table.

columns.description:
`_idx` plus one array per requested column, all of the same
length: the number of keys that were found. `_idx[i]` is the
position in the request keys that row i answers.

tags.name: event
tags.description: Asynchronous Event API. This API is used to post events to the system. Data recipients can request footprints and will receive notifications when these requests are fulfilled or rejected. Data owners can post updated and newly published footprints to data recipients.

get.description:
Retrieve a list of Product Carbon Footprints (PCFs) from the [=data owner=].
The [=data recipient=] can specify various criteria to filter the
list, and the [=data owner=] can paginate the result set, if necessary.

Host systems SHOULD implement an access management system and only 
return the product footprints for which the data owner granted access 
to the requesting data recipient.

The host system SHOULD include footprints which have been deprecated in the 
resulting list of footprints, except if the `status` query parameter 
explicity requests only active footprints.

### Pagination

 1. The host system MUST NOT return more product footprints than requested in 
    case a `limit` parameter was specified by a [=data recipient=]
 2. The host system MUST return an HTTP `Link` header if there are additional 
    ProductFootprints ready to be retrieved, such that
      - The `Link` header conforms to [[!RFC8288]]
      - The value of the `rel` parameter is equal to `next`
      - the target URI of the `Link` header is absolute
      - The value of `host` of the target URI is equal to the value of the `host` 
        request header from the original `ListFootprints` HTTP request
 3. The target URI from the `Link` header is called a pagination link.
 4. A pagination link MUST be valid for at least 180 seconds after creation
 5. The data recipient CAN call the pagination link more than once
 6. Upon each call, the host system
      - MUST NOT return more product footprints than requested in case 
        `limit` was defined by a [=data recipient=]
      - MUST return a `Link` header conforming with the previous description in case 
        there are additional ProductFootprints available
        ```http
        link: <https://api.example.com/3/footprints?geography=FR&limit=10&offset=10>; rel="next"
        ```
 7. If a response contains a second pagination link and the data recipient has called 
    that second pagination link, the previous pagination link MAY no longer work: data 
    recipients MUST NOT assume that previous pagination links continue to return results 
    after advancing in the pagination process.

### Filtering

The [=host system=] MUST support filtering of the list of footprints by 
criteria described under Parameters. Note that these are the same filters 
used by the [[#request-created-event]] Event.

Most criteria (like `productId`, `geography`, etc.) can contain multiple 
values. Each footprint in the resulting list MUST match for EACH single 
criterion at least ONE value.

So, the filtering logic is as follows:
- For each filter criterion (e.g., `productId`, `geography`, `classification`), if multiple values are provided, the filter matches if the footprint matches at least one of the values for that criterion (logical OR within a criterion).
- Across different criteria, a footprint must match all specified criteria (logical AND between criteria).

In other words:
- Within a single criterion: values are combined with OR.
- Between different criteria: criteria are combined with AND.

For example, the query string for `ListFootprints` 

```http
?productId=x&productid=y&productid=z&geography=DE&geography=FR&validon=2025-04-01T00:00Z 
```

translates to the following logic:

```
(productId='x' OR productId='y' OR productId='z') AND
(geography='DE' OR geography='FR') AND
(validOn='2025-04-01T00:00Z')
``` 

Additionally, a host system MAY provide additional filter criteria for the data 
recipient to use. These parameters MUST be prefixed with `x-<identifier>-`.  

For example, to add functionality to search for product 
footprints based on an invoice number, a software solution could choose 
to support a parameter `x-atq-invoice-id`. 

```http
/3/footprints/?geography=FR&x-atq-invoice-id=12345&limit=100
```

Advisement: the ODataV4 `$filter` syntax present in v2.x has been deprecated in v3.0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
The maximum number of footprints to return. The [=host system=] MAY return fewer 
footprints, but MUST return a Link header conforming to [[!RFC8288]] if there are 
additional ProductFootprints ready to be retrieved.

200.description:
The host system succesfully returns a list of product footprints. This list 
MAY be incomplete, in which case the host system MUST return a Link header
conforming to [[!RFC8288]], also see [[#pagination]]. The list MUST NOT be 
larger than the `limit`, if specified. 

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
link: <https://api.example.com/3/footprints?geography=FR&limit=10&offset=10>; rel="next"
content-type: application/json
```
```json
{
  "data": [ 
    {"id": "079e425a-464f-528d-341d-4a944a1dfd70", ... },
    {"id": "f4b1225a-bd44-4c8e-861d-079e4e1dfd69", ... }
    ...
  ]
}
```

The list MAY also be empty. If the list is empty, the host system MUST return an empty 
JSON array. The list MUST NOT be NULL.

```json
{
  "data": [] // MUST NOT be null
}
```
