info.title: Archipelago Stats API
info.description:
## Overview

The Archipelago Stats API provides real-time visibility into the Decentraland communication system by aggregating peer heartbeats and the cluster topology published by Pulse. This API enables monitoring, debugging, and analytics of user distribution, island clustering, and system health across the metaverse.

### Purpose

This service acts as an observability layer for the Archipelago protocol, transforming internal system state into queryable metrics and snapshots. It is designed for:

- **Monitoring**: Track system health, user activity, and island distribution in real-time
- **Analytics**: Analyze crowd patterns, popular areas, and user movement across parcels
- **Debugging**: Inspect individual peer states, island configurations, and service availability
- **Visualization**: Power dashboards and tools that display live metaverse activity

### Key Concepts

**Parcels** represent geographic coordinates in Decentraland's 2D grid system. Each parcel has an X/Y coordinate, and the API provides peer density information per parcel, enabling identification of crowded areas and popular destinations.

**Peers** are individual users/avatars currently active in the Archipelago system. Each peer entry includes their unique identifier, Ethereum address, real-time position coordinates (X, Y, Z), assigned island, and last heartbeat timestamp. This enables tracking of individual users and their current state in the system.

**Islands** are dynamic clusters of peers that are continuously recalculated based on user positions. They group nearby users together to optimize message routing and rendering performance. Each island has center coordinates, a radius, and a list of all peers currently assigned to it. Island IDs read `C{n}` and `maxPeers` reads `0`: clusters are uncapped.

### How It Works

Clustering is performed by **Pulse**, which publishes the topology this API serves. Clusters have no size limit; comms-gatekeeper maps each one to a single LiveKit room named `island-C{n}`, so room size follows cluster size. Note the ID mismatch: clients receive the room name (`island-C{n}`) as their `islandId`, while this API reports the bare cluster ID (`C{n}`).

The Stats API continuously aggregates the published topology and provides it through REST endpoints with low latency, enabling real-time monitoring and analysis. Peer positions still come from client heartbeats.

### Data Freshness

All data is provided in real-time and reflects the current state of the Archipelago system at the time of the API call. Island assignments, peer positions, and parcel densities are continuously updated as users move through the metaverse. The API does not provide historical data—each request returns the current snapshot of the system.

### Use Cases

- **Live Dashboards**: Display real-time user distribution and popular areas
- **System Monitoring**: Track service health, island counts, and user capacity
- **Analytics Tools**: Analyze crowd patterns and identify trending scenes
- **Developer Tools**: Debug communication issues and inspect peer connections
- **Administrative Interfaces**: Monitor system load and user activity

For detailed information about the Archipelago protocol architecture, see [ADR-204](https://adr.decentraland.org/adr/ADR-204).

get.description: Returns a list of parcels with their current peer density information. Parcels represent geographic coordinates in Decentraland, and this endpoint helps identify areas with high user concentration. The peer count for each parcel indicates how many users are currently present in that geographic area, enabling crowd visualization and hotspot detection.

200.description: List of parcels with peer counts

500.description: Internal server error

get.description: Returns a list of all peers (users) currently active in the archipelago system. Each peer includes their unique identifier, Ethereum address, current position coordinates, assigned island, and last heartbeat timestamp. This endpoint provides a comprehensive view of all active users in the system at any given moment.

500.description: Internal server error

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Peer ID

get.description: Returns a list of all active islands in the archipelago system. Islands are dynamic clusters of peers, recalculated by Pulse as users move. Each entry includes the island identifier (`C{n}`), `maxPeers` (always 0 — clusters are uncapped), center coordinates (x, y, z), radius, and the list of peers assigned to it. The peer list is a join against heartbeat data, so a peer Pulse has assigned but which has not sent a heartbeat is omitted.

get.description: Returns data about popular scenes (hot scenes) in Decentraland based on current user activity. Hot scenes help identify trending areas and popular destinations in the metaverse.

info.title: Quotacore
info.summary: Quota and metering enforcement for AI SaaS.
info.description:
Quotacore is a quota service. It holds a balance per tenant, per feature, and answers
whether a call is allowed before the call is made, or applies it after.

This document is the source of truth for the wire format. It is generated from
`docs/architecture/api-conventions.md` and `docs/product/error-catalog.md`, not from the
code, and the types and request validation in the service are generated from this file
(ADR-0010). A disagreement between this file and those documents is a defect in whichever
one was edited last.

**Conventions that hold on every route in this document.**

- Every response carries `X-Request-Id`, and the `request_id` in an error body equals it
  (NFR-S10). Quote it in a bug report.
- Every error body is the same envelope, and `code` is the only field to branch on. The HTTP
  status is a class hint; `429` in particular means two different things, which is
  `quota_exceeded` and `rate_limited` (DR-040).
- `Idempotency-Key` is required on `POST /v1/consume` and `POST /v1/refund` and on nothing
  else. There is no server-generated fallback, because a generated key silently defeats the
  purpose.
- Amounts are JSON integers, never floats. A float is `400 validation_failed` naming the
  field.
- Timestamps are RFC 3339 **with an explicit offset**, always, including `Z`. A client never
  has to branch on whether the zone is UTC.
- `cycle_start` and `cycle_end` are `null` together, for a `never` entitlement. That is the
  documented shape, not an omission (DR-008, INV-C6).
- A request with an undeclared field is `400 validation_failed`. Every object in this
  document sets `additionalProperties: false`, which is what makes a typo a clear error
  instead of a silently ignored key.
- Validation errors aggregate. Three bad fields produce one `validation_failed` naming all
  three, in `details.errors`.

**Two guarantees worth reading before integrating.**

A `500` on `consume` or `refund` always means the balance is unchanged. The mutation is a
single atomic script execution, so there is no state in which a deduction was partially
applied, and a client-side retry after a `500` is safe.

A retry with the *same* `Idempotency-Key` is charged once, within 24 hours of the first
application. A retry with a *new* key is a second operation and is charged twice. No
server-side scheme detects that (FS-03).

servers.description: Local development, the default in `docker compose up`

tags.name: data-plane
tags.description:
The four routes a customer's application calls on the request path. These are the ones
with a latency budget, and the ones that open no database connection.

tags.name: admin-features
tags.description: The catalogue of metered features. A feature is a key, a unit and a name.

tags.name: admin-plans
tags.description: Plans and their entitlements. A plan is an offer; a tenant override is a contract term.

tags.name: admin-tenants
tags.description: Tenants, their plan assignment, grants, overrides and usage history.

tags.name: admin-keys
tags.description: API key issuance and revocation. A key is never readable after issue.

tags.name: admin-observe
tags.description: Status and audit. The two routes an operator reads when something is wrong.

tags.name: operational
tags.description:
Probes, metrics and this document. No error envelope, and the probes need no
credential.

post.summary: Deduct an amount from the current cycle's balance
post.description:
The call a customer's application makes instead of decrementing a counter itself.

`Idempotency-Key` is required. The same key replayed with the same
`operation | tenant | feature | amount` returns the original response's state values
unchanged, with `replayed: true` where the original said `false`, and the same key with a different fingerprint is
`409 idempotency_key_reuse` with no state change at all (DR-028, INV-I2).

The window is 24 hours from the first application. A key first seen after that is a new
operation, not a replay (DR-029). The window is fixed and is not configurable, because it
is a documented customer guarantee.

post.summary: Return an amount to the current cycle's balance
post.description:
A refund is its own operation, not a negative consume. The direction is the endpoint and
never a sign (DR-023, ADR-0005), so a refund can never be confused with a malformed
amount.

`Idempotency-Key` is required, on the same 24-hour window as `consume`.

A refund never returns `quota_exceeded`. A refund cannot exceed a balance; the bound it
can break is `balance <= limit + bonus`, which is `refund_exceeds_grant` (DR-019). If the
intent is a permanent increase, use an admin `grant` instead.

post.summary: Ask whether an amount would be allowed
post.description:
Advisory. Returns `200` with `allowed: false` when the answer is no; a denial here is
**not** a `429` (DR-024). A `429` from this route means the *service* is rate-limiting
you, which is a different problem with a different remedy (DR-040).

No `Idempotency-Key`, because nothing is mutated, so a duplicate is harmless
(DR-024). This route never returns `idempotency_key_reuse`.

It is `POST` rather than `GET` because the question is in a body, and a `GET` with a body
is not portable. The verb is `check` and not `quote` because it reserves nothing.

The limitation is stated here as well as in the reference, because ignoring it looks like
a bug the first time a customer hits it: two requests can both pass `check` and one can
then be denied at `consume`. `check` reduces denials, it does not eliminate the race.

get.summary: Read the balances of a tenant
get.description:
With `feature_key`, one entry. Without it, the tenant's full set, which is bounded by the
plan's entitlement count (NFR-T5), so the unbounded case does not exist. `feature_key` is
optional.

`cycle_start` and `cycle_end` are always present and are `null` together for a `never`
entitlement.

An unknown feature key on this route is `404 feature_not_found`. This is the admin-plane
behaviour and it is the one documented exception to the data plane's non-disclosure rule:
the caller already knows a key it is asking about, and `feature_not_in_plan` would be
indistinguishable from an exhausted allowance, which is the distinction the caller most
needs (FS-17).

A page of the catalogue, newest first, with the same opaque cursor as every other list. A
feature is a key, a unit and a name, and the unit is what an `amount` counts.

post.description:
`key` is immutable always and `unit` once the feature is referenced, because reinterpreting a
historical amount is not allowed (INV-F2, INV-F3). `kind: boolean` is a v0.2 surface and is
`501 not_implemented` on a v0.1 build (F-5).

value.name: LLM output tokens
value.description: Completion tokens billed to the customer

patch.summary: Rename a feature, or correct an unreferenced unit
patch.description:
`version` is required and is the optimistic-concurrency token. A mismatch is
`409 resource_version_conflict` with the current version in `details`, so a client can
re-read and retry deliberately. Last-write-wins on a resource that governs a customer's
money is not acceptable, and an operator with two open browser tabs is exactly the case
(FS-12).

`unit` may change only while nothing references the feature: no plan entitlement, no
override and no usage event. Once anything does, a unit change is
`409 feature_unit_immutable`, because it would reinterpret every historical amount
(INV-F2).

delete.description:
A hard delete, permitted only while no plan entitlement, override or usage event
references the feature (F-6). Otherwise `409 feature_in_use`, and archiving is the remedy,
because the history must never dangle (DR-016). The delete is audited with its reason.

delete.summary: Remove a feature created by mistake

post.description:
Archiving, not deleting. A feature referenced by a plan, a tenant or a historical event
may be archived but not deleted, so the audit and event history never dangles (DR-016).

Archiving denies new consumption with `403 feature_archived` and leaves existing balances
intact until their natural cycle end. A zeroed balance would be a lie about money the
customer has already paid for.

A plan is bounded at 100 entitlements, and the bound is a documented validation limit
rather than a struct size (NFR-T5), so a larger plan is a validation error rather than a
slow request.

patch.description:
The edit changes what applies to **new assignments immediately** and to **existing
tenants at their next boundary**. It does not touch an open cycle's balance, and it does
not move a boundary. `POST /v1/admin/plans/{id}/apply` is the route that changes that, and
it is guarded by blast radius (DR-014).

What reaches an existing tenant, and when:

- A **limit** change binds at the tenant's own next boundary.
- An **interval** change, and a **feature added** to the plan, reach the tenant at its next
  re-anchor (a plan change or an apply-now), because a live interval would renumber the
  open cycle and an added feature has no balance yet (E-3, DR-045). Until then the tenant
  keeps the cadence and the feature set it was anchored on.
- A **feature removed** stays the tenant's, at the limit it had, until the end of the
  window the edit landed in; a removed `never` feature stays until the next re-anchor
  (E-4, INV-E1). Adding it back before then keeps it.

`entitlements` replaces the whole set, because a partial update of a bounded set is an
ambiguity, and a plan that is an offer should be edited as one. An archived plan cannot
be edited: `400 validation_failed`.

delete.description:
A hard delete, permitted only while no tenant, including a soft-deleted one, is assigned to
the plan (P-6, DR-035). Otherwise `409 plan_in_use`, and archiving is the remedy. The
plan's own entitlements go with it. The delete is audited with its reason.

delete.summary: Remove a plan that was never sold

post.summary: Re-anchor and re-limit every assigned tenant, now
post.description:
This re-anchors every tenant assigned to the plan, so it is guarded by **blast radius**
rather than by operator intent (DR-046).

At or below `QUOTACORE_PLAN_APPLY_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD` (default 50) it is one call and a
`200`. Above it, the service counts first, writes nothing, and returns
`409 confirmation_required` carrying a single-use token. Re-issue the identical request
with `confirmation_token` and it applies.

The token is honoured once, and only for the plan, the `resource_version` and the
`reason` it was issued for, and only while the plan's count has not grown past the one it
was issued against. Anything else, a plan edited in between included, is counted afresh:
above the threshold that is a new `409` with a new token, because the count the operator
approved is no longer the count. A `409` writes nothing and records no audit row; an
apply bumps the plan's version, so no token survives it. There is no `Idempotency-Key` on
this route, deliberately. The handshake is already exactly-once
by construction, and adding a second exactly-once mechanism to one operation is a way to
have two opinions about whether it happened.

Every tenant on the plan, suspended ones included, is re-anchored at the request's
instant in one transaction, and its balances are rewritten after it: inline while the
request has time, and by a background drain for any it did not reach. Until a tenant's
balances are rewritten it is served its previous state, never a fresh allowance. An
archived plan cannot be applied: `400 validation_failed`.

To preview the numbers without provoking the error, call
`GET /v1/admin/plans/{id}/impact` first.

Archiving a plan does not reassign its tenants and does not change any balance. It stops
new assignments, and a tenant already on the plan keeps working until it is moved
(DR-016).

archive.summary: Retire a plan no longer sold

get.summary: Preview how many tenants an apply would affect
get.description:
Read-only. Nothing is re-anchored, no audit row records a mutation and no token is
issued. The route exists so that the common case is a quiet read rather than a `409`
(UC-19).

It describes an apply-now of the plan **as saved**: every non-deleted tenant on it, and
the earliest end of their current cycles over their features that reset, in the zone of
the tenant it belongs to. It is computed by the same function the `409` uses, so the two
agree.

Newest first, with an opaque signed cursor. Totals are not returned: a count over a large
tenant table is a slow query pretending to be metadata.

post.description:
Balances are materialised here, at provisioning, and at cycle transitions. They are
**not** materialised on first read, because a balance created on demand would hand a full
allowance to whoever triggered it (DR-045).

`timezone` is an IANA name such as `Europe/Berlin`. Abbreviations are rejected: a
timezone is a set of rules, and an abbreviation is not one. The tenant's zone is what its
cycle boundaries are computed in, so a wrong zone is a wrong bill.

`external_id` cannot contain `@`, which makes it structurally impossible to store an
email address as a tenant identifier (DR-034, NFR-S2).

patch.summary: Change a tenant's plan, name or zone
patch.description:
**Changing `plan_key` is a hard reset.** The new plan's limits apply immediately and the
tenant's anchor is set to the current instant, starting a fresh cycle. The previous
balance is discarded, not prorated, and the discard is recorded as a `plan_changed` event
so it is visible in history (DR-013).

Proration is deferred, and it is deferred on purpose: prorating a limit is a claim about
time that the customer did not buy. The balance was for the cycle that just ended.

delete.description:
A soft delete, and it is **not retroactive**. Existing usage events and audit rows stay
queryable, which is what makes a billing dispute answerable after a churn event (T-15).

Soft deletion is terminal: there is no undelete. A soft-deleted tenant is treated exactly
as absent by every endpoint that takes an identifier, so `tenant_not_found` is the usual
answer and `tenant_deleted` appears only where the caller has already been authorised to
see that the tenant exists.

post.description:
Consumption becomes `403 tenant_suspended`. **The balance is preserved, not zeroed**, and
resuming restores it exactly, because a suspension is a billing decision by the operator
and not a change in what the customer bought (DR-032).

post.summary: Add bonus quota for the current cycle
post.description:
Adds `amount` to both `balance` and `bonus` in the current cycle, after any rollover that
is due, and applies immediately. Because both rise together, `balance <= limit + bonus`
holds by construction and a grant to a full balance succeeds. A grant is
**cycle-scoped**: it does not survive the boundary, because a bonus is a gesture and a
limit is a contract (DR-019, DR-020).

A grant on a `never` entitlement increases the balance with no cycle to end it.

`409 grant_exceeds_ceiling` is a grant that would take the balance or the bonus past
`2^53 - 1`, the largest amount the service represents exactly (DR-022). To raise a limit
durably, use an override, which is the correct remedy for a lasting increase.

A grant has no `version` and no `Idempotency-Key`, so a grant retried after a timeout is a
second grant; each is in the audit log with its reason.

value.reason: incident INC-2211, 30 minutes of failed responses

post.summary: Set a balance to an exact value
post.description:
Overwrites the current cycle's balance outright, after any rollover that is due. It is the
blunt instrument, and it is the right one when a migration produced a number that is
known to be wrong.

`value` is `0` to `limit + bonus`. Above that is `409 grant_exceeds_ceiling`: grant first.
Setting `0`, or suspending the tenant, is how to stop a tenant until its boundary; a
negative balance is not representable in v0.1 (Q-23).

post.summary: Roll one feature's cycle over now
post.description:
Refills one feature now: the balance becomes the effective limit and the bonus `0`, in
the cycle the tenant's anchor puts this instant in, whatever cycle the stored balance
was on. That also repairs a balance stuck on a cycle index that is ahead. It does not move
the anchor. A second call refills again. It is audited with a mandatory `reason`, and a
refill that changed the balance is a `force_rolled_over` event in the ledger.

A `never` entitlement cannot be rolled, because there is no cycle to roll:
`409 reset_not_supported`. Grant explicitly instead (DR-008).

rollover.summary: Customer asked for a fresh month

post.summary: Set or replace a per-feature override
post.description:
An override is a **contract term** and it outranks the plan (DR-011). It survives later
plan edits, because a plan is an offer and an override is what this one customer signed
for.

At least one of `limit_value` or `interval` must be present. An override that set neither
would inherit everything from the plan and would therefore be indistinguishable from not
existing, so it is `400 validation_failed` (UC-13).

`apply_at` is `immediate` by default. It is a **mode, not a timestamp**. For the limit,
`immediate` re-limits the open cycle and keeps what was spent: the balance moves by the
same difference as the limit, floored at zero. `next_boundary` writes the override only,
and the tenant's next boundary grants the new limit. An `interval` reaches the tenant at
its next re-anchor in either mode, because a live interval would renumber the open cycle.

An override can raise a limit above the plan's. That is the mechanism for "custom limits
for an enterprise customer". It cannot add a feature the plan does not include, which is
`400 validation_failed` (DR-012, DR-015).

Clearing an override is `DELETE` on the per-feature sub-path, not this route. See that
route for why.

limit.summary: Ten times the plan limit, from the next boundary

interval.summary: Custom reset cadence, limit inherited from the plan

delete.description:
Removes the override, so the plan value applies again (UC-13). `immediate` re-limits the
open cycle to the plan's limit as an override's `immediate` does; `next_boundary` lets the
next boundary grant it. Clearing an override that does not exist changes nothing and is
still `204`.

`apply_at` is in the body rather than a query parameter because it changes *when* money is
owed, and a `DELETE` that silently means "now" would be a surprise in a billing system.
`next_boundary` restores the plan value at the tenant's next boundary; `immediate` applies
it at once.

This is a `DELETE` on a per-feature sub-path rather than another `POST` on the collection
because the storage cannot represent "an override that sets nothing":
`tenant_overrides_not_empty` rejects a row with both `limit_value` and `interval` null, so
clearing is the **absence of the row** rather than a row of nulls. Expressing it as a
`clear: true` field on the `POST` would mean one route with two mutually exclusive body
modes, which is exactly the shape that generated SDKs handle worst.

This is one of the two routes in the contract where a `DELETE` takes a body: the body
holds `apply_at`, and the rule that a body is capped applies here like any other, so
`413 payload_too_large` is on this route (NFR-T6).

clear.summary: Restore the plan value from the next boundary

get.description:
The route that decides whether a team keeps the product, because the first time a
customer disputes a deduction is the first time anyone evaluates it (UC-16).

Each event shows the instant, the signed `delta`, the `balance_after`, the cycle window,
the `source` and the `request_id`. Summing the deltas for a cycle and comparing with the
reported balance is the reconciliation an operator performs by hand, and it is why
`balance_after` is stored rather than recomputed (DR-042).

For a specific disputed charge, filter by the customer's `Idempotency-Key` to see the
recorded outcome, which is how you prove whether a call was applied once or twice. If a
lost data store let the same key be applied twice, the filter returns the first
deduction, the second, and the `system` refund that reconciliation issued to reverse the
second, all three under the customer's key (DR-049, amended 2026-10-20).

A known limitation, stated here because a silently incomplete history is worse than a
documented one: events are appended to the ledger **best effort and at-least-once**, and a
consumer deduplicates on `id`. Where an event could not be appended, nothing is written in
its place; the gap is recorded by `ledger_dropped_total` in `GET /v1/admin/status` and by
`quotacore_event_sink_dropped_total` (ADR-0016).

Metadata only. The secret is returned exactly once, by the create route, and there is no
route that returns it again and none ever will be added (INV-K3). A lost key is replaced,
not recovered.

`prefix` is the public, unique part of a key. It appears in this list and in the audit
log so a key leaked in a support ticket can be traced to the key that leaked, which is the
entire operational purpose of a credential identifier (DR-043, K-1).

post.description:
The plaintext key is in this response and nowhere else. Only a SHA-256 digest of the secret
and the public prefix are stored, and the digest is deliberately not indexed, because
indexing a verifier invites a timing-oracle design (ADR-0018).

Scope is visible in the token itself, so a scope mismatch is not a 400-line debugging
session: `qc_runtime_<prefix>.<secret>` and `qc_admin_<prefix>.<secret>`.

key.summary: A runtime key for one customer's app

delete.description:
Revocation takes effect on the next request to the instance that served it, and within the
propagation bound (NFR-D3) on every other, because each instance's key cache re-reads its
keys on every invalidation and refresh tick (UC-15, K-2). Revoking a key that is already
revoked is `204` and changes nothing. An id that names no key is `404 api_key_not_found`,
so a mistyped id in an incident is never mistaken for a revoked key.

get.description:
The contractual record, kept separately from usage history because they answer different
questions and merging them would answer neither (UC-16). Every administrative mutation
writes an audit row **in the same transaction as the mutation** (NFR-D4). An audit log
written best effort is a log, not an audit trail.

get.summary: Dependency health, version and queue state
get.description:
The one call an operator makes when something is wrong, so it is **not** allowed to fail
with an error envelope: an endpoint that returned `unauthorized` when a dependency was
down could not report that the dependency was down, which is the one thing it exists to
do. It reports dependency failure as data, at `200`.

It does still require the `admin` scope (NFR-O5). A missing or invalid credential is a bare
`401`, a key of the wrong scope a bare `403`, and a caller over the admin rate limit a bare
`429` with `Retry-After`, each with no body, because those are answers about the caller
rather than about a dependency. Reports the build, the `tzdata` version the binary was built
with, the current time and the snapshot size.

Answers `200` while the process is running. It checks no dependency, deliberately: a
liveness probe that fails when Postgres is unreachable restarts a process that was not
the problem.

Amended 2026-10-21 (`IP-13`): it answers `200` with its body from start to exit,
including while the process drains after `SIGTERM`, because a liveness probe that fails
during a graceful drain gets the process killed before its requests have answered.

Answers `200` only when the service can actually serve: the required dependencies are
reachable and the bootstrap key has been acknowledged (NFR-S9). This is the probe that
gates traffic, and unlike `/healthz` it does look at dependencies.

Amended 2026-10-21 (`IP-13`): the terms are those of observability.md section 4. The
data store answered the last probe within `QUOTACORE_DATASCRIPT_TIMEOUT`; the snapshot
has read the configuration once, however many tenants exist; migrations are current;
the process is not draining; and it is in normal mode, so read-only or a rebuild holding
the fence is not ready. Postgres is not a term: during a control-plane outage cached
tenants still enforce (NFR-A2), and an instance that went unready would take them with
it. The bootstrap acknowledgement is not a term either, because the process refuses to
start without it. Any other state is a `503` with no body.

Prometheus text exposition format, not JSON and not an error envelope.

`quotacore_errors_total` is labelled by `code`, and the label set is
[error-catalog.md](../../docs/product/error-catalog.md) by reference: a contract test
asserts the two match, so a code cannot be raised in the service without being in the
catalogue.

Amended 2026-10-21 (`IP-13`): this operation is served on the metrics listener at
`QUOTACORE_METRICS_ADDR` (`127.0.0.1:9090` by default, deployment.md section 4.1), not
on the API's address, which answers it `404`. It takes no credential; the loopback bind
is the control (security-model.md section 7). The series are observability.md
section 1.

get.summary: This document, as served by the running service
get.description:
The contract the running binary was built from, rendered as JSON.

The source of truth is `api/openapi.yaml`, which is embedded in the binary at build time,
so a contract cannot drift from the binary in a way nothing would notice (ADR-0010, DoD
item 5). The bytes served are a JSON rendering of that embedded document rather than the
YAML text: `application/json` is what a client and a tool expect here, and a YAML body
labelled as JSON is the kind of small lie that costs someone an afternoon. A test asserts
that the served document is a faithful, order-preserving conversion of the embedded YAML,
so the rendering cannot quietly drop or reorder anything either.

A single self-contained HTML page generated from this document at build time, with no
third-party JavaScript and no call to a CDN. It works on a host with no egress, which is
the same constraint as everything else in this product.

The page is generated by `make docs` and CI fails if the committed page differs from the
generated one, so it cannot rot silently.

bearerAuth.description:
An API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

A key is either `qc_runtime_<prefix>.<secret>` or `qc_admin_<prefix>.<secret>`. The scope
is visible in the token itself, so a scope mismatch is not a debugging session: a
`runtime` key on `/v1/admin/*` is `403 insufficient_scope`, and an `admin` key works on
both planes.

An HTTP bearer scheme has no scopes, so the scope array in every requirement above is
empty, as OpenAPI requires. The scope a route needs is recorded instead in
`x-required-scope`, which is `runtime` on the four data-plane routes, `admin` on
`/v1/admin/*`, and absent on the operational routes that take no credential at all. The
rule itself is stated once, in
[api-conventions.md](../../docs/architecture/api-conventions.md) (DR-043, NFR-O5).

Possession of a runtime key gives access to **every** tenant on the instance. A key is a
credential for the whole instance, and `external_id` in the request selects the tenant.
This is a single-tenant-per-instance product (ADR-0013), and the key issuance is an
audited, per-customer decision for that reason.

There is no recovery path. A key that leaks is rotated, not recovered.

XRequestId.description:
Identifies this request, and is the join key across logs, events and a customer report
(NFR-S10). Adopted from the inbound request when it is a valid ULID or UUID, otherwise
minted. Present on **every** response, including the error responses and the probes.

IdempotentReplay.description:
`true` when this response is a replay of a stored one rather than a new application. A
proxy or a client can tell without parsing the body. `replayed` in the body says the same
thing, and it is the only field in which a replay differs from the original (DR-027).

RetryAfter.description:
Seconds to wait. Present on `429 rate_limited`, which is the service protecting itself and
is deliberately distinguishable from `429 quota_exceeded` (DR-040). It is **not** present
on `quota_exceeded`: that one is retryable at `cycle_end`, which is in `details`, and a
`Retry-After` of a few seconds would invite a hammering loop.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
One key per **logical operation**, reused across every attempt including retries. Derive
it from your own durable operation identifier where one exists.

A repeat with a matching fingerprint replays the stored response. A repeat with a
different fingerprint is `409 idempotency_key_reuse` and changes nothing. The window is 24
hours from application, per tenant, and is not configurable.

**The one case no server can protect against:** a retry with a *new* key is a second
operation and is charged twice. No scheme detects that (FS-03).

IdempotencyKeyQuery.name: idempotency_key
IdempotencyKeyQuery.description:
Filter the ledger to one logical operation, by the key the customer sent. This is how a
disputed charge is resolved: the recorded outcome shows whether it was applied once or
twice (UC-16). The filter also returns a duplicate that reconciliation reversed and the
reversal itself, which carry the key they reconcile (DR-049, amended 2026-10-20).

TenantExternalIdRequired.name: tenant_external_id
TenantExternalIdRequired.description:
Your identifier for the tenant whose balances you are reading. Required here, because the
route cannot answer without a tenant; absent is `400 validation_failed`.

TenantExternalIdQuery.name: tenant_external_id
TenantExternalIdQuery.description: Your identifier for the tenant. The customer never handles an internal `tenant_id`.

FeatureKeyQuery.name: feature_key
FeatureKeyQuery.description:
Restrict to one feature. On `GET /v1/balance` it is optional, and omitting it returns the
tenant's full set, which is bounded by the plan's entitlement count (NFR-T5).

PlanKeyQuery.name: plan_key
PlanKeyQuery.description: Restrict the tenant list to one plan.

FeatureKeyPath.name: feature_key
FeatureKeyPath.description: The feature key, as in the catalogue.

PlanIdPath.name: id
PlanIdPath.description:
A plan identifier. Either the UUID or the plan key; both address a plan. A UUID-shaped value
is looked up as an id first and as a plan key second. An identifier that names no plan is
`404 plan_not_found`, never `400`.

TenantIdPath.name: id
TenantIdPath.description:
A tenant identifier. Either the UUID or the `external_id`; both address a tenant. A
UUID-shaped value is looked up as an id first and as an `external_id` second. An identifier
that names no tenant is `404 tenant_not_found`, never `400`, and is never echoed.

KeyIdPath.name: id
KeyIdPath.description: A key identifier (the UUID, not the secret).

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
Opaque and signed. A tampered cursor is `400 validation_failed`, never a silent full
scan. Newest first, always, with a stable tiebreaker so a cursor is never ambiguous.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. An empty page returns an empty array, never `null`.

FromQuery.name: from
FromQuery.description: Start of the time range, RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. Same format as responses.

ToQuery.name: to
ToQuery.description: End of the time range, RFC 3339 with an explicit offset.

EventTypeQuery.name: event_type
EventTypeQuery.description:
One of the seven ledger event types. Any other value is `400 validation_failed`, never an
empty result: a filter that silently matches nothing is worse than one that says no.

SourceQuery.name: source
SourceQuery.description: Who caused the event. Any other value is `400 validation_failed`.

ValidationFailed.summary: One entry per offending field, in one response
ValidationFailed.description:
Aggregated on purpose. Three bad fields produce one `validation_failed` naming all three,
not three responses, because a client fixing a request should not have to make three
round trips to learn three things.

InvalidAmount.description:
The direction is the endpoint, never a sign. Use `POST /v1/refund`, not a negative
`consume` (DR-023, ADR-0005).

InvalidWindow.summary: A window that disagrees with the cadence
InvalidWindow.description:
Either the window is not valid for the feature's cadence, or it is a v0.2 feature called
on a v0.1 build. The two cadences are never silently mixed, because a silent mix makes
the balance a lie.

error.message: window: rolling_1h is not available in v0.1

InvalidTimezone.summary: An abbreviation where an IANA name is required
InvalidTimezone.description:
A timezone is a set of historical and future rules. `CET` is not that. Rejecting
abbreviations is what stops a boundary being computed from the wrong rules forever.

error.message: timezone: 'CET' is not an IANA time zone name

MissingIdempotencyKey.summary: No Idempotency-Key on a route that requires one
MissingIdempotencyKey.description:
There is no server-generated fallback. A generated key silently defeats the purpose of
the header, which is to make one logical operation one charge (DR-026).

error.message: the Idempotency-Key header is required on this route

ApiKeyInvalid.summary: A key that is unknown, revoked, expired or malformed
ApiKeyInvalid.description: There is no recovery path. Rotate the key; the old one cannot be made to work again.

error.message: the presented API key is not valid

InsufficientScope.summary: A valid key with the wrong scope
InsufficientScope.description:
`403`, not `404`. Hiding the endpoint from an authenticated caller helps nobody, and a
`runtime` key discovering it exists is not a disclosure worth preventing (FS-18).

error.message: this key does not carry the admin scope

FeatureNotInPlan.description:
A limit of `0` and an absent entitlement are different states, and the difference has to
be visible: "you get none of this because you are on Free" and "your Free plan includes
zero of this" are different product messages (DR-012).

An unknown feature key on the data plane produces this same code, so feature existence is
not leaked (FS-17).

error.message: feature llm.tokens.output is not in the tenant's plan

FeatureArchived.summary: The feature exists but is archived
FeatureArchived.description:
Balances are preserved, not zeroed. Archiving a feature does not take money the customer
has already bought (DR-016).

error.message: feature llm.tokens.output is archived and no longer accepts consumption

TenantSuspended.description:
The balance is preserved and resuming restores it exactly. A suspension is a billing
decision, not a change in what the customer bought (DR-032).

TenantNotFound.description:
A soft-deleted tenant is treated exactly as absent, so this is also the answer after a
soft delete. A recently provisioned tenant may not be visible yet (DR-031).

FeatureNotFound.summary: Unknown feature key on the admin API

PlanNotFound.summary: Unknown plan on the admin API

ApiKeyNotFound.summary: Revoking a key id that names no key

error.message: no API key has that id

PayloadTooLarge.description:
The whole body is capped at 64 KiB before it is parsed, and `metadata` at 4 KiB once it is
decoded (NFR-T6). Either is this code, never `validation_failed`. `metadata` is correlation, not a data store.

IdempotencyKeyReuse.summary: The same key, a different operation
IdempotencyKeyReuse.description:
The fingerprint is a hash of `operation | tenant | feature | amount`. A mismatch is
refused and **no state changes**; the original record is preserved (DR-028, INV-I2).

error.message: this Idempotency-Key was first used for a different operation

PlanInUse.summary: Delete attempted on a referenced plan
PlanInUse.description: Archive it instead. The reference is enforced in the database too, by `ON DELETE RESTRICT` (DR-016).

error.message: plan pro is assigned to 1840 tenants

FeatureInUse.summary: Delete attempted on a referenced feature

error.message: feature llm.tokens.output is referenced by 3 plans

TenantExists.description:
Deliberately **not** idempotent, so the data error surfaces. Returning the existing tenant
as if it had been created would hide a provisioning bug.

TenantDeleted.summary: An operation on a soft-deleted tenant
TenantDeleted.description:
Soft deletion is terminal. Create a new tenant, or restore from a backup. This code
appears only where the caller is already authorised to know the tenant exists; elsewhere
the answer is `tenant_not_found`.

error.message: tenant acme-prod-01 was deleted on 2026-09-30 and cannot be modified

RefundExceedsGrant.summary: A refund that would break the ceiling
RefundExceedsGrant.description:
A refund may not take `balance` above `limit + bonus`. A refund never returns
`quota_exceeded`: the bound a refund can break is this one (DR-019). If the intent is a
permanent increase, use an admin `grant`.

error.message: refund of 90000 would take the balance above limit plus bonus

GrantExceedsCeiling.summary: A grant that would break the ceiling
GrantExceedsCeiling.description:
A `set` above `limit + bonus`. Grant first, or raise the limit with an override: a grant
is cycle-scoped and a limit is a contract, and a lasting increase is a limit change
(DR-019, DR-020). A grant itself raises the bonus with the balance, so it is refused only
past `2^53 - 1`, with that number as `ceiling`.

error.message: the balance would pass limit plus bonus; raise the limit with an override first

ResetNotSupported.description:
There is no cycle to roll. `never` is a lifetime allowance with no boundary and no
expiry, so a rollover request against it is a category error, not a missing feature
(DR-008). Grant explicitly.

error.message: feature api.requests has interval never, which has no cycle to roll over

FeatureUnitImmutable.summary: A unit change on an assigned feature
FeatureUnitImmutable.description:
Reinterpreting historical amounts is not allowed, so a unit that has been used to
account for anything can never change. Create a new feature (INV-F2).

error.message: unit of feature llm.tokens.output cannot change from token to request

ResourceVersionConflict.summary: A stale version on a control-plane mutation
ResourceVersionConflict.description:
Retryable **after a re-read**, not by retrying the same body. The current version is in
`details` so a client can re-read and retry deliberately (FS-12).

error.message: the resource was modified by someone else

ConfirmationRequired.summary: apply-now above the threshold, and nothing was applied
ConfirmationRequired.description:
The service counted first, wrote nothing, and issued a single-use token bound to the plan
`resource_version` it was counted against (DR-046). Re-issue the identical request with
`confirmation_token`.

Retryable by re-issuing **with** the token. A retried confirmation cannot re-apply an
operation that already applied.

QuotaExceeded.description:
Retryable at `cycle_end`, which is in `details` and is authoritative. This is **not** the
service rate-limiting you: there is no `Retry-After` on this code, on purpose, because a
few seconds is not what fixes it and the header would invite a hammering loop (DR-040).

error.message: balance 50 is below the requested amount 100

RateLimited.description:
Deliberately distinguishable from `quota_exceeded` by code, because the remedy is
completely different: back off, rather than wait for a reset (DR-040).

error.message: too many requests for this key

InternalError.summary: A defect, and nothing was applied
InternalError.description:
A `500` on `consume` or `refund` **always** means the balance is unchanged, because the
mutation is one atomic script execution. A client-side retry after a `500` is safe.

Quote the `request_id`.

ServiceUnavailable.summary: A data-store problem, or the atomic script could not be evaluated
ServiceUnavailable.description:
Retryable with backoff and jitter. Whether to fail **open** or **closed** is a
deliberate decision in your application, not one this service makes for you (DR-037).

Note that `consume` is not safe to retry blindly here unless you also send the same
`Idempotency-Key`; a new key on retry is a second charge (FS-03).

ControlPlaneUnavailable.summary: Postgres is unreachable and this tenant is not in the snapshot
ControlPlaneUnavailable.description:
Distinct from `service_unavailable` on purpose. Tenants already in the snapshot are
unaffected, which is the whole reason the snapshot exists, and a code that conflated the
two would make an incident impossible to diagnose (DR-036).

error.message: tenant configuration is not available in the snapshot

NotImplemented.summary: A later-release surface called on an MVP build
NotImplemented.description:
The remedy is to upgrade, or to use the MVP equivalent. This is not a transient failure
and retrying does not help.

error.message: this endpoint is not available in v0.1

NoContent.description:
Done, and there is nothing to return. `X-Request-Id` is still on the response: NFR-S10 says
every response carries it, and a `204` is a response.

MeteredOK.description:
The deduction was applied, or the stored response was replayed. `balance` is **after** the
deduction, `consumed` is the amount the *original* call applied, and the two together
reconstruct the balance before it.

`consumed` is returned unchanged on a replay, because a replay reads the recorded state
rather than recomputing it (DR-027). The replay differs from the original only in
`replayed`. To tell whether this particular call moved
anything, read `replayed` or the `Idempotent-Replay` header; it is a one-field test rather
than an inference from arithmetic.

replayed.summary: The same key replayed, with the identical body and replayed: true

CheckOK.description:
The answer, which is a `200` whenever the question could be answered. A denial is
`allowed: false`, **not** a `429` (DR-024).

denied.summary: It would not, and this is still a 200

BalanceOK.description:
The balances. With `feature_key`, one entry; without it, the tenant's full set, bounded by
the plan's entitlement count (NFR-T5). `cycle_start` and `cycle_end` are `null` together
for a `never` entitlement.

full.summary: A tenant on a two-feature plan

BalanceEntryOK.description:
The single affected balance, after the administrative change. Returning it is what lets
an operator see the effect of a `grant`, a `set` or a `force-rollover` without a second
round trip, and it is the same shape `GET /v1/balance` returns for one feature.

value.name: LLM output tokens
value.description: Completion tokens billed to the customer

features.name: LLM output tokens
features.description: Completion tokens billed to the customer

PlanAppliedOK.description:
Every assigned tenant has been re-anchored and re-limited. The count is returned so the
operator can record what happened, and it matches the `affected_tenants` they were shown
in the confirmation.

PlanImpactOK.description:
What an edit **would** affect. Nothing changed, no audit row was written and no token was
issued (UC-19).

impact.summary: 12 tenants, the earliest ending in three months

TenantListOK.description:
A page of tenants, newest first. Totals are deliberately absent: a count over a large
tenant table is a slow query pretending to be metadata.

TenantCreated.description:
Provisioned, with balances materialised now rather than on first read. A balance created
on demand would hand a full allowance to whoever triggered it (DR-045).

OverrideOK.description: The override as stored, including which aspects it inherits from the plan.

UsageEventListOK.description:
A page of ledger events, newest first. `delta` is signed and never zero, so summing the
deltas for a cycle and comparing with `balance_after` is the reconciliation an operator
performs by hand (DR-042).

KeyListOK.description: Key metadata. No secret is present, and no route will ever return one (INV-K3).

KeyCreated.description:
The only response that ever contains the plaintext key. It is not recoverable afterwards:
only a SHA-256 digest of the secret and the public prefix are stored (ADR-0018, INV-K3).

issued.summary: The one time this secret is visible

AuditEntryListOK.description:
A page of audit records, newest first. Kept separate from usage history because they
answer different questions (UC-16).

entries.summary: One override, set by the acme-prod-deploy key

StatusOK.description:
The one call an operator makes when something is wrong, so it reports dependency failure
as data rather than failing with an error envelope. It does still require the `admin`
scope (NFR-O5).

HealthzOK.description: The process is running. No dependency is checked, deliberately.

ReadyzOK.description:
The service can serve: required dependencies are reachable and the bootstrap key has been
acknowledged (NFR-S9).

ReadyzNotReady.description:
The service cannot serve, so traffic should not reach it. No body and no error envelope:
the probe is for an orchestrator, which reads the status. Added 2026-10-21 (`IP-13`).

MetricsOK.description: Prometheus text exposition format. Not JSON, and not an error envelope.

sample.summary: A few series, elided (amended 2026-10-21, `IP-13`, to series that exist)
sample.value:
# HELP quotacore_http_requests_total Every HTTP request, by contract operation, method and status.
# TYPE quotacore_http_requests_total counter
quotacore_http_requests_total{endpoint="POST /v1/consume",method="POST",status="200"} 18402
# HELP quotacore_errors_total Error envelopes written, by code and by the contract operation that wrote them.
# TYPE quotacore_errors_total counter
quotacore_errors_total{code="quota_exceeded",endpoint="POST /v1/consume"} 91

OpenAPIOK.description:
This document, as the running binary was built from it. A test asserts the bytes served
equal the bytes of `api/openapi.yaml` in the repository (DoD item 5).

schema.description: An OpenAPI 3.1 document, identical to `api/openapi.yaml`.

DocsOK.description: A single self-contained HTML page, with no third-party JavaScript.

schema.description: A generated HTML reference for this document.

ErrorBadRequestMetered.description:
The request was not applied. Nothing is charged and nothing is reserved.

`missing_idempotency_key` and `invalid_window` are in the same `400` as
`validation_failed` because they are the same class of mistake, but they are distinct
codes: a client that retries with a key fixes one and not the others.

ErrorBadRequestWindow.description:
The question could not be asked. `check` takes no `Idempotency-Key` and never returns
`quota_exceeded` or `idempotency_key_reuse`, because it mutates nothing (DR-024).

ErrorBadRequestPlain.description:
The request was rejected and nothing changed. Validation errors aggregate, so one response
names every offending field.

ErrorBadRequestTimezone.description:
A rejected request. `invalid_timezone` is separate from `validation_failed` because the
remedy is different and a wrong timezone is a wrong bill, not a typo.

ErrorUnauthorized.description:
No usable credential. `api_key_invalid` covers unknown, revoked, expired and malformed
keys, and there is no recovery path for any of them: rotate.

ErrorForbiddenEntitlement.description:
A refusal that is about the caller or the entitlement, not the request's shape. Nothing
was charged.

All four are `403` and they are told apart by `code`, never by status: this is the case
the catalogue's "no code carries meaning in its HTTP status" rule exists for.

ErrorForbiddenScope.description:
A valid key with the wrong scope. `403` and not `404`, because the caller is already
authenticated and hiding the endpoint helps nobody (FS-18).

ErrorFeatureNotFound.description: No such feature key on the admin API.

ErrorTenantNotFound.description:
Unknown or soft-deleted tenant. A soft-deleted tenant is treated exactly as absent, which
is why this is also the answer after a soft delete (T-15).

ErrorNotFoundResource.description:
Neither the tenant nor the named feature exists. On the admin API existence is not
hidden, because the operator is already authorised for the whole instance.

ErrorIdempotencyKeyReuse.description:
The key was first used for a different operation. No state changed and the original record
is preserved (DR-028, INV-I2). Retry with a **new** key only if the new operation is
genuinely a new one.

ErrorRefundConflict.description:
A refund conflict. It never returns `quota_exceeded`: a refund cannot exceed a balance,
and the bound it can break is `balance <= limit + bonus` (DR-019).

ErrorConflictFeature.description:
A feature conflict, and nothing changed. `feature_unit_immutable` and
`resource_version_conflict` are the two ways a feature mutation is refused; the other two
are duplicate-key and still-referenced.

ErrorConflictPlan.description:
A plan conflict, and **nothing changed**. `confirmation_required` is the same status
because it also applied nothing: it is a refusal that hands back a token, not a partial
application (DR-046).

ErrorConfirmationRequired.description:
The edit would affect more tenants than
`QUOTACORE_PLAN_APPLY_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD` (default 50), so it applied **nothing** and
returned a single-use token instead.

Re-issue the identical request with `confirmation_token`. The token is bound to the plan
`resource_version` it was issued against, so a plan edited in between is refused.

ErrorConflictTenant.description:
A tenant conflict, and nothing changed. `tenant_exists` is deliberately not idempotent, so
a provisioning bug surfaces instead of being hidden.

ErrorConflictTenantDeleted.description: The tenant is deleted, which is terminal, so nothing about it can change (T-7).

ErrorConflictQuota.description:
A refused administrative change to a balance. Nothing was applied in any of the four
cases. `tenant_deleted` is a tenant whose deletion is terminal (T-7).

ErrorKeyNotFound.description:
No API key has that id. Distinct from a successful revocation, so a mistyped id is never
mistaken for a revoked key. List the keys and check the id.

ErrorPayloadTooLarge.description:
The body was refused **before it was parsed** (NFR-T6). Absent from every read route, and
from `DELETE .../overrides/{feature_key}`, which takes no body.

ErrorQuotaAndRate.description:
Two entirely different problems that share a status, which is why the catalogue says no
code may carry meaning in its status alone (DR-040).

`quota_exceeded` is the tenant's money for this cycle and is retryable at
`details.cycle_end`, with no `Retry-After`. `rate_limited` is this service protecting
itself and is retryable in seconds, with a `Retry-After`.

ErrorRateLimited.description:
This service is rate-limiting the key. Distinct from `quota_exceeded`, which is the
tenant's allowance rather than the service's protection (DR-040).

ErrorInternal.description:
A defect, and **nothing was applied**. On `consume` or `refund` a `500` always means the
balance is unchanged, because the mutation is a single atomic script execution, so a
client-side retry is safe.

Quote the `request_id`.

ErrorNotImplemented.description:
A later-release surface called on an MVP build. Not transient: retrying does not help.
Upgrade, or use the MVP equivalent.

ErrorControlPlaneUnavailable.description:
Postgres did not answer. A route that reads only the control plane cannot answer
`service_unavailable`, because it never touches the data store. Retryable with backoff and
jitter.

ErrorUnavailable.description:
A dependency is unavailable. Both are retryable with backoff and jitter, and whether to
fail **open** or **closed** is a decision your application makes deliberately
(DR-037).

The two codes are separate because cached tenants are unaffected when Postgres is
unreachable, and conflating them would make an incident impossible to diagnose
(DR-036).

RequestId.description:
A ULID or a UUID. Adopted from the inbound `X-Request-Id` when it is one of those,
otherwise minted. It is the join key across logs, ledger events and a customer's bug
report (NFR-S10).

IdempotencyKey.description:
One key per logical operation, reused across every attempt including retries. The window
is 24 hours from application and is **not** configurable, because it is a documented
customer guarantee (DR-029).

derived.summary: Derived from the customer's own durable operation identifier

Timestamp.description:
RFC 3339 with an **explicit offset**, always, including `Z`. The offset is present even
when it is `Z` unless `Z` is the whole value, so no client branches on whether a zone is
UTC.

The difference this prevents is not academic: the gap between a UTC assumption and
`Europe/Berlin` across a DST change is 31 days minus one hour, and a customer notices.

ExternalId.description:
Your identifier for a tenant, as in `tenant_external_id`.

The character class **excludes `@`**, which makes it structurally impossible to store an
email address as a tenant identifier. That is a schema-level guarantee about the absence
of PII rather than a convention (DR-034, NFR-S2).

FeatureKey.description:
A metered feature's key, matching the `features_key_format` constraint. The key is
immutable once created (INV-F3).

PlanKey.description: A plan key, matching the `plans_key_format` constraint.

Unit.description:
What one `amount` counts: `token`, `request`, `image`, and so on. The unit is documented on
the feature and is **never inferred**, which is why it is immutable once the feature is
used for anything (INV-F2).

Amount.description:
A count of the feature's unit. JSON **integers only**: `4200.0` is
`400 validation_failed` naming the field, because accepting a float and rounding it
silently is how a customer loses money without noticing (DR-022).

The maximum is `2^53 - 1`, not `2^63 - 1`, and that is a scripting-language limit rather
than a storage one: the atomic script's numbers are doubles, so a balance above `2^53 - 1`
cannot be represented exactly by the code that enforces the ceiling. The database, the API
and the script all reject the same values, so a metering system that silently rounds is
avoided in favour of one that refuses the value.

Limit.description: A cycle allowance. Same integer rules and same `2^53 - 1` ceiling as `Amount`.

Version.description:
Optimistic-concurrency token. Read it, send it back, and on a mismatch re-read before
retrying. Last-write-wins on a resource that governs a customer's money is not acceptable
(FS-12).

ResetInterval.description:
The cadence of an entitlement. A `never` entitlement is a lifetime allowance: no boundary,
no expiry, no rollover, and `cycle_start` and `cycle_end` are `null` (DR-008, INV-C6).

OverrideApplyAt.description:
A **mode, not a timestamp**. `immediate` applies a limit now, re-limiting the open cycle
and keeping what was spent; `next_boundary` applies it at the tenant's next boundary. An
interval reaches the tenant at its next re-anchor in either mode, because that is the
only moment a cadence change is meaningful.

It is a mode because the actual instant an override takes effect is always the tenant's
next boundary, computed by the cycle engine and never stored. The name is a deliberate
wart kept for the API's benefit, and it is why the enum type exists in the schema: a
`timestamptz DEFAULT 'immediate'` would not be a slightly awkward value, it would not
parse.

KeyScope.description:
`runtime` for `/v1/*`, `admin` for `/v1/admin/*`. An `admin` key also works on the data
plane.

KeyState.description:
A key's lifecycle. Revocation is effective on the next request to the instance that served
it, and within the propagation bound (NFR-D3) on every other.

TenantState.description:
`suspended` preserves the balance exactly; resuming restores it (DR-032). `deleted` is a
soft delete and is terminal.

ArchiveState.description:
A resource is archived rather than deleted, so audit and event history never dangles
(DR-016).

FeatureKind.description:
`metered` in v0.1. `boolean` exists in the schema with no v0.1 use, because adding an enum
value later is a schema change and v0.2's design is already known.

EventType.description:
The seven ledger event types. `delta` is signed and never zero, so an `amount: 0` consume
records no event at all (DR-023).

Metadata.description:
Correlation only: at most 4 KiB, never indexed, never logged, and **never returned by any
endpoint** (DR-043, NFR-T6). It is not a data store and it is not a place for PII.

ErrorCode.description:
The only field to branch on. Stable, permanent, lower snake case. A code may be retired
only in a major version, and only if no client could reasonably depend on it.

The enum is the catalogue by reference, and a contract test asserts the two match, so the
service cannot raise a code that is not in
[error-catalog.md](../../docs/product/error-catalog.md).

ErrorResponse.description:
The one error shape, everywhere, and it is non-negotiable. No endpoint returns a bare
`400` or a bare `500` without it.

`additionalProperties: false` here is what makes a typo in an error field a visible
defect rather than a silently dropped key.

error.description:
The error itself, nested under `error` so the envelope is extensible. `code` is the
contract; `message` is not.

message.description:
Human-readable and may improve between releases. **Never parse it.** Branch on
`code` and on `details`.

retry_after_ms.description:
Present only when retrying is correct. On `quota_exceeded` it is **absent**,
because the wait is a calendar duration in `details.cycle_end` and a small number
here would invite a hammering loop.

ErrorDetails.description:
Code-specific and additive across versions. Every code-specific field lives **here**, not
beside `code`, which is what keeps the envelope one shape everywhere.

Additive means a field may be added without a version bump. It does not mean a field's
type or meaning may change, and a client must tolerate a field it does not know.

MeteredRequest.description:
The body of `consume`, `refund` and `check`. It is the same body on all three, because the
three differ in what they do with it rather than in what they need.

feature_key.description:
A **single** key, never an array. One feature per call, by design: a bundle would have
to attribute its cost across features, which breaks the per-feature event model and
the idempotency fingerprint, and a partial bundle failure is a state the caller cannot
reason about. A bundle is two calls ([Q-05](../../docs/product/assumptions-and-open-questions.md#2-open-questions)).

tenant_external_id.description: The customer never handles an internal `tenant_id`.

window.description:
v0.2. Omitted means the anchored cycle, which is the only cadence in v0.1
(ADR-0008). A window that disagrees with the feature's cadence is
`400 invalid_window`, and supplying any window on a v0.1 build is also
`invalid_window`, because the two cadences are never silently mixed.

MeteredResponse.description:
One feature's numbers after a metered call, describing the cycle the call fell in. A replay
returns the same body with `replayed: true`, because a retrying client must not be able to
tell a replay from a second charge by its shape alone (DR-049).

balance.description: The remaining balance **after** the deduction.

bonus.description: Cycle-scoped granted quota. It does not survive the boundary (DR-020).

consumed.description:
The amount the **original** call applied, returned unchanged on a replay because a
replay reads the recorded state (DR-027). On `consume`, `balance` minus `consumed` is
the balance before the original deduction. On `refund` the schema is shared, so
`consumed` is the amount refunded and `balance` minus `consumed` is the balance before
the refund.

replayed.description:
Whether this response is a replay of a stored one. A client that needs to know
whether **this call** moved anything reads this, rather than inferring it from
arithmetic, and it can also read the `Idempotent-Replay` header.

CheckResponse.description: The answer to "would this be allowed", which is always a `200` when answerable.

allowed.description:
A denial is `allowed: false` at `200`, **not** a `429` (DR-024). A `429` from this
route means the service is rate-limiting you.

cycle_end.description: When a currently-denied amount would become available.

BalanceEntry.description:
One feature's balance for the current cycle. A feature the tenant's plan does not include is
absent rather than zero, so a caller can tell an omission from an exhausted allowance.

consumed.description:
Net consumption in the stored cycle, derived as `limit + bonus - balance`. A refund
lowers it and an administrative `set` shows through it. It is computed from the balance
hash rather than read from the ledger, because this route never reads the control
plane (DR-039).

BalanceResponse.description:
Every feature's balance for one tenant, in one call. Paged by feature rather than by tenant,
because the question is never about a tenant on its own.

entries.description:
One entry, or the tenant's full set. The set is bounded by the plan's entitlement
count (NFR-T5), so the unbounded case does not exist. An empty page is `[]`, never
`null`.

Feature.description:
One feature in Quotacore's catalogue. A feature is the thing that is metered; a plan says how
much of it a tenant gets, and a tenant is assigned to exactly one plan (UC-05).

id.description:
Internal. The admin routes address a feature by `feature_key`, never by this id, which
exists for the audit log's `subject_id`.

name.description: The operator's display name. Cosmetic, and the only mutable field but `description`.

unit.description:
Immutable once the feature is referenced by an assignment or an event. Reinterpreting
historical amounts is not allowed, and that is what `feature_unit_immutable` is for
(INV-F2).

description.description: Free text for an operator reading a plan. Empty when there is nothing to say.

FeatureCreate.description:
Create a feature. The catalogue is small and edited deliberately, because a feature key whose
meaning later changes is a change to history (INV-F2, INV-F3).

name.description: The operator's display name for the new feature.

unit.description: Immutable once referenced, and documented on the feature rather than inferred.

description.description: Optional free text. Absent and `''` are the same thing, which is why it defaults to `''`.

kind.description:
Optional, `metered` by default. `boolean` is a v0.2 surface and is `501 not_implemented`
on a v0.1 build (F-5).

FeatureUpdate.description:
A rename, or a unit correction. `feature_key` is absent by design: it is immutable always, and
offering an immutable field and then refusing it is a worse API than not offering it. `unit`
is offered because it is mutable until the feature is referenced (INV-F2).

version.description:
Required. The optimistic-concurrency token from the `GET` that preceded this call. A
mismatch is `409 resource_version_conflict` with the current version in `details`.

name.description: The new display name, replacing the current one.

description.description: Replaces the current free text. `''` clears it, so clearing is an explicit act.

unit.description:
A new unit, accepted only while no plan entitlement, override or usage event references
the feature. Otherwise `409 feature_unit_immutable` (INV-F2).

FeatureList.description:
A page of the feature catalogue, for a picker or a review. Features are created and archived,
never deleted, so a historical event always resolves to something (UC-05).

features.description: The page of features. An empty page is `[]`, never `null`.

next_cursor.description: Null on the last page. An empty page is an empty array, never `null`.

PlanEntitlement.description: One feature's allowance in a plan.

Plan.description:
One plan: the offer a tenant is assigned to. A plan is a bounded set of entitlements and
nothing else â€” no tenant, no key and no balance (DR-011).

id.description: Internal, and what `/v1/admin/plans/{id}` and `/v1/admin/plans/{id}/impact` take.

name.description: The operator's display name for the plan.

description.description: Free text for an operator reading the plan. Empty when there is nothing to say.

entitlements.description:
At most 100. The bound is a documented validation limit rather than a struct size, so
a larger plan is a `400 validation_failed` rather than a slow request (NFR-T5).

PlanCreate.description:
Create a plan, entitlements included. A plan is created whole, because a plan with no
entitlements is not a plan (UC-11).

name.description: The operator's display name for the new plan.

description.description: Optional free text. Absent and `''` are the same thing, which is why it defaults to `''`.

entitlements.description:
The whole offer, 1 to 100 features. The upper bound is a documented validation limit
rather than a struct size, so a larger plan is a `400 validation_failed` rather than a
slow request (NFR-T5).

PlanUpdate.description:
An edit to a plan's entitlements. It applies to new assignments immediately; an existing
tenant takes a new limit at its next boundary and a new interval or an added feature at its
next re-anchor, and keeps a removed feature until the end of the window the edit landed
in. It does not touch an open balance and it does not move a boundary (DR-014).

version.description:
Required. The plan is an offer that governs a customer's money, so last-write-wins is
not acceptable: a mismatch is `409 resource_version_conflict` (FS-12).

name.description: The new display name, replacing the current one.

description.description: Replaces the current free text. `''` clears it, so clearing is an explicit act.

entitlements.description:
**Replaces the whole set.** A partial update of a bounded set is an ambiguity, and a
plan is edited as one offer.

PlanApplyRequest.description:
Re-anchor every tenant assigned to a plan. It is the only control-plane write that touches
tenants it was not addressed to, and the reason a reason is required is that a decision with a
blast radius is a decision worth reading later (DR-014).

reason.description:
Required and audited. Re-anchoring every assigned tenant is a decision with a blast
radius, and a decision with a blast radius is one whose reason is worth having later.

confirmation_token.description:
Present only when re-issuing after `409 confirmation_required`. Single-use, bound to
the plan, the `resource_version` and the `reason` it was issued against, and expiring on
`QUOTACORE_CONFIRMATION_TTL`, because an abandoned token must not accumulate in a
store that cannot evict (DR-048).

PlanApplied.description:
The outcome of a completed apply, so a caller can record what happened without re-reading the
plan and hoping it has not been edited since (UC-18).

affected_tenants.description:
How many tenants were re-anchored, as committed. It is at most the `affected_tenants`
the operator was shown in the confirmation: a token is not honoured once the plan's
count has grown past it.

version.description: The plan's version after the apply.

PlanImpact.description:
What an apply-now of the plan as saved would affect, read-only. Nothing is re-anchored, no
audit row records a mutation and no token is issued (UC-19).

affected_tenants.description:
How many non-deleted tenants are on the plan, suspended ones included, which is the
number `exceeds_confirmation_threshold` compares against the configured threshold.

earliest_cycle_end.description:
The earliest `cycle_end` among affected tenants' features that reset, in that tenant's
zone, or null when there is none. It is the same value `confirmation_required`
reports, so the common case is a quiet read rather than a `409`.

exceeds_confirmation_threshold.description:
Whether `affected_tenants` is above `QUOTACORE_PLAN_APPLY_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD`. The
operator can tell whether to expect a confirmation without provoking one.

PlanList.description: A page of plans, for a picker or a review.

plans.description: The page of plans. An empty page is `[]`, never `null`.

TenantMetadata.description:
A small JSON object on the tenant, explicitly not PII, not indexed by content and excluded
from logs (DR-043, NFR-O6). Distinct from a request body's `metadata`, which is never
returned.

Tenant.description:
One tenant: the customer Quotacore meters. `external_id` is the customer's identifier, and
every other field is either derived from it or operational bookkeeping (DR-001).

id.description:
Internal.             The customer uses `external_id`; this exists for the audit log's
`subject_id`.

display_name.description:
A label for an operator reading a tenant list. Not an identity and not a lookup key:
two tenants may share one, so the uniqueness rule is on `external_id` alone.

timezone.description:
An IANA name. The tenant's cycle boundaries are computed in this zone, so a wrong zone
is a wrong bill. Abbreviations are `400 invalid_timezone`; a timezone is a set of rules
and an abbreviation is not one (ADR-0007).

anchor_at.description:
The tenant's **only** per-tenant cycle state (DR-002). There is deliberately no stored
current window: a stored window that could disagree with the anchor is exactly the
defect the pure-function design removes, and boundaries are computed from the anchor
in the application, in UTC, with the zone applied to the arithmetic (ADR-0003).

deleted_at.description:
Set by a soft delete, which is **not retroactive**: events and audit rows stay
queryable, which is what makes a dispute answerable after a churn event (T-15). There
is no undelete.

TenantCreate.description:
Provision a tenant on a plan. The cycle starts now, at the anchor, and the allowance is
materialised immediately rather than on first use, so a missing balance is a defect and not a
lazy read (DR-002, DR-045).

external_id.description:
Your identifier for this tenant. A duplicate is `409 tenant_exists`, deliberately not
idempotent, so a provisioning bug surfaces instead of being hidden.

display_name.description: An operator-facing label. Not unique, and never a lookup key.

timezone.description:
An IANA name; defaults to `UTC`. The zone the tenant's cycle boundaries are computed
in.

TenantUpdate.description:
A change to a tenant. **Changing `plan_key` is a hard reset**: the new limits apply
immediately, the anchor is set to now, and the previous balance is discarded rather than
prorated, recorded as a `plan_changed` event so the discard is visible (DR-013).

Proration is deferred deliberately. Prorating a limit is a claim about time the customer
did not buy; the balance was for the cycle that just ended.

version.description:
Required. The optimistic-concurrency token. A mismatch is
`409 resource_version_conflict`.

display_name.description: The new operator-facing label, replacing the current one.

plan_key.description: A change here starts a fresh cycle and discards the open balance.

timezone.description:
An IANA name, as on `Tenant.timezone`, and an abbreviation is `400
invalid_timezone` for the same reason. The zone boundaries are recomputed from the
unchanged anchor, so this moves future boundaries and leaves past ones alone.

TenantList.description: A page of tenants, for an operator. Admin-scoped, because it enumerates other customers.

tenants.description: The page of tenants. An empty page is `[]`, never `null`.

next_cursor.description:
Null on the last page. Totals are deliberately not returned: a count over a large
tenant table is a slow query pretending to be metadata.

Cursor.description:
An opaque, signed pagination cursor. Never parse it and never construct one. A tampered
cursor is `400 validation_failed`, not a silent full scan.

ReasonRequest.description: A state-changing admin call with a mandatory reason, audited with before and after.

version.description: The optimistic-concurrency token. A mismatch is `409 resource_version_conflict`.

reason.description:
Required. Every administrative mutation writes an audit row in the same transaction as
the mutation (NFR-D4), and a reason is the part of that row a human reads later.

ArchiveRequest.description:
Archive a plan or a feature. Archiving is not deletion: the record keeps its history and stops
being assignable (UC-13). v0.1 has no unarchive route, so archiving is one-way here, and
archiving a record that is already archived is a `200` that changes nothing and writes no
audit row.

version.description: The optimistic-concurrency token.

reason.description:
Required and audited. Archiving hides a plan or feature from new assignments, so the
reason is what an operator reads to know whether it was deliberate.

DeleteRequest.description:
Delete a tenant, a plan or a feature, with the reason the audit row records. A tenant is
soft-deleted: deletion is terminal for the tenant, so the open balance is not re-granted and
the ledger is kept, because a deleted tenant still has events (UC-14). A plan or a feature is
hard-deleted, and only while nothing references it (P-6, F-6); otherwise the answer is
`409 plan_in_use` or `409 feature_in_use`, and archiving is the remedy.

reason.description:
Required and audited. Deletion is terminal, so the reason is the only record of why it
happened.

GrantRequest.description:
Add cycle-scoped bonus quota. A grant does not survive the boundary: a bonus is a gesture
and a limit is a contract (DR-019, DR-020).

amount.description:
A grant only adds, so it is never negative. A grant on a `never` entitlement
increases the balance with no ceiling tied to a cycle and no expiry.

reason.description: Required, and audited. Goodwill is a decision, not a correction.

SetRequest.description:
Set a balance to an exact value. The blunt instrument, and the right one when a migration
produced a number that is known to be wrong.

value.description: The balance after this call.

reason.description:
Required and audited. Overwriting a balance destroys the previous figure, so the reason
is the only record of what it was replaced by.

ForceRolloverRequest.description:
Roll one feature's cycle over now, applying the next cycle's allowance immediately. It is
audited and recorded as a `force_rolled_over` event.

reason.description:
Required and audited. Rolling a cycle over early gives the tenant its next allowance
now, so the reason is the record of who decided to and why.

OverrideUpsert.description:
Set or replace a per-feature override. An override is a **contract term** and outranks the
plan: it survives later plan edits, because a plan is an offer and an override is what one
customer signed for (DR-011).

Clearing an override is `DELETE /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/overrides/{feature_key}`, not this
route, because the storage cannot represent an override that sets nothing.

**`limit_value` and `interval` are both required and both nullable.** UC-13 says "a limit,
