a reset interval, or both", and a required-but-nullable field is how "this aspect is not
overridden" is stated without ambiguity. Requiring the key is deliberate: absence would
mean two things, that the aspect is inherited and that the operator forgot it, and a
quota system should not have a wire format with those two readings.

**At least one of the two must be non-null, and this schema does not enforce that.** It is
the one constraint in the contract that lives in the data store, as
`tenant_overrides_not_empty`, and a request that sends both null is
`400 validation_failed`. The reason is recorded here rather than papered over: expressing
it in JSON Schema needs an `anyOf` over object branches, and the generator
(ogen 1.24.0) cannot generate that, failing with "complex anyOf is not implemented yet".
Silently dropping the constraint from the document to make the generator happy would
leave a reader believing the wire format guarantees something it does not.

The rule is normative in api-conventions.md section 7.4, which states the
presence-and-null convention and the division of labour between the schema and the store.

limit_value.description:
Null means "inherit the limit from the plan for this aspect". A non-null value may
exceed the plan's limit: that is the mechanism for custom limits for an enterprise
customer (DR-015).

interval.description: Null means "inherit the cadence from the plan".

apply_at.description:
`immediate` by default. A mode, not a timestamp; the instant an override takes effect
is always the tenant's next boundary, computed rather than stored.

version.description:
Optional expected version for the existing override. Omitted means "create or replace
without a concurrency check", which is appropriate when a single operator is the only
writer.

limit.summary: Ten times the plan limit, from the next boundary

interval.summary: Custom cadence, limit inherited from the plan

both.summary: A limit and a cadence, neither inherited

OverrideClearRequest.description:
The body of the override-clearing `DELETE`.

`apply_at` is in the body rather than a query parameter because it changes **when** money
is owed, and a `DELETE` that silently meant "now" would be a surprise in a billing system.

clear.summary: Restore the plan value from the next boundary

Override.description:
One per-feature override on one tenant. An override is a contract term and outranks the plan,
which is why it is modelled separately rather than expressed as a plan edit (DR-011).

id.description:
Internal. An override is addressed by tenant and `feature_key` rather than by this id,
so there is at most one per pair.

limit_value.description: Null when the limit is inherited from the plan.

interval.description: Null when the cadence is inherited from the plan.

UsageEvent.description:
One ledger row. The ledger is append-only (INV-U2), reconstructed rather than trusted, and
delivered downstream best effort and at-least-once, so `event_id` deduplication at the
consumer is part of the contract rather than an oversight (ADR-0016).

id.description: The `event_id` a downstream consumer deduplicates on.

cycle_index.description:
Which cycle this was, monotonically increasing. A memo for reconciliation and
pagination, **not** a second authority: the window itself is recomputed from the
tenant's anchor, and a disagreement here is a reconciliation finding rather than a
truth.

delta.description:
Signed and **never zero** (a database constraint), so an `amount: 0` consume records no
event at all. Negative consumes, positive refunds, grants, sets and rollovers.

balance_after.description:
Stored so history is readable without replaying, and so the reconciliation identity of
DR-042 is directly checkable: the opening allowance plus the sum of the deltas equals
this.

request_id.description:
The request that caused the event. A `system` event, such as a rollover by the reset
worker, carries the request id the job minted for its run, so every event joins to a log
line (NFR-S10). The column is `NOT NULL` (data-model.md §2.7); `null` is allowed by the
schema and is not produced.

idempotency_key.description:
The customer's key, on `consumed` and `refunded`. Filtering by it is how a disputed
charge is resolved: the recorded outcome shows whether it was applied once or twice
(UC-16). On a duplicate that reconciliation reversed, and on the `system` refund that
reversed it, this is the customer's key the pair reconciles (DR-049, amended
2026-10-20).

cycle_start.description:
The start of the event's cycle, recomputed from the tenant's current anchor, zone and
interval. Null for an event older than the current anchor, because a window from before
a re-anchor cannot be recomputed from the anchor that replaced it.

cycle_end.description:
The end of the event's cycle, on the same terms as `cycle_start`, and also null for a
`never` entitlement (INV-C6).

UsageEventList.description:
A page of the ledger, newest first, for reconciliation and for settling a disputed charge
(UC-16).

events.description: Newest first, with a stable tiebreaker. An empty page is `[]`, never `null`.

AuditEntry.description:
One administrative mutation, written in the same transaction as the mutation (NFR-D4). An
audit log written best effort is a log, not an audit trail.

id.description: The audit row's own identifier, for citing a row rather than for looking one up by resource.

actor.description:
`bootstrap`, `cli:<host>`, or a key's name. A key's name rather than its secret, so an
audit record can be shown to someone without handing them a credential (DR-043).

actor_key_id.description: Null for the bootstrap actor and for CLI calls, which have no key.

action.description: A dotted action name.

subject_type.description:
Which kind of resource changed, so a log reader can filter by it. `system` is a note
about the installation itself, such as the truncation an operator records after a
Postgres restore with `quotacore audit note`; its `subject_id` is null.

subject_id.description:
The resource's internal id, or null when the mutation has no single subject — a plan
`apply-now` touches every assigned tenant, so the tenants are not recorded here one by
one.

before.description: The resource before the change, or null when it was created.

after.description: The resource after the change, or null when it was deleted.

reason.description:
The reason the caller gave, for the mutations that require one (archive, delete, suspend,
resume), and null for the rest.

AuditEntryList.description:
A page of the audit log, newest first. Append-only, and the reason a mutation cannot be
quietly undone after the fact (NFR-D4).

entries.description: The page of entries, newest first. An empty page is `[]`, never `null`.

Key.description: Key metadata. The secret is never present here and no route will return it (INV-K3).

id.description: Internal, and what `/v1/admin/keys/{id}` takes.

name.description: Unique. A duplicate name is `400 validation_failed` naming the field.

prefix.description:
The public, unique part of the key. It appears in this list, in the audit log and in
logs **in place of the key**, which is how a key leaked in a support ticket is traced
to the key that leaked (DR-043, K-1).

expires_at.description:
Optional at issue time, enforced on every request. A key past this is
`401 api_key_invalid`.

revoked_at.description:
Revocation takes effect on the next request to the instance that served it, and within
the propagation bound (NFR-D3) on every other instance (UC-15, K-2).

KeyCreate.description:
Issue an API key. The plaintext is returned once, on this route and nowhere else
(ADR-0012).

name.description:
Unique and operator-chosen. It is the `actor` on every audit row this key produces, so
it should say what the key is for rather than who typed it.

scope.description:
Visible in the token itself, so a scope mismatch is not a debugging session. Issuance
is an admin action and is audited, and it is a per-customer decision: a runtime key is
a credential for the whole instance.

expires_at.description: Optional. An expiry is a limit on a credential's blast radius.

KeyCreated.description:
The **only** response that ever contains the plaintext key. It is not recoverable
afterwards; only a SHA-256 digest of the secret and the public prefix are stored, and the
digest is deliberately not indexed because indexing a verifier invites a timing-oracle
design (ADR-0018).

A lost key is replaced, not recovered (UC-15).

id.description: The new key's id, as it appears in every later `Key` response.

name.description: The name chosen at creation, echoed back.

prefix.description: The public prefix, so it can be recorded where the key cannot.

key.description: The plaintext credential, in the form `qc_<scope>_<prefix>.<secret>`. Shown once.

KeyList.description: A page of key metadata. The secret is never present, and no route will return it (INV-K3).

keys.description: The page of keys. An empty page is `[]`, never `null`.

DependencyHealth.description:
One dependency's health, reported as data. A failure here is a `200` with
`healthy: false`, never an error envelope, because a status endpoint that fails when a
dependency is down cannot report that it is down.

name.description: Which dependency this row is about.

healthy.description:
Whether a probe succeeded. `false` is reported here rather than as an error envelope,
so the status endpoint can still answer the question that was asked of it.

latency_ms.description: The probe's round-trip time, or null when the probe did not complete.

error.description: The failure reason, and safe to show: it is a connection error, not data.

CacheStats.description:
The configuration snapshot's size. An empty key space after a restart is a normal state and
it is reported as such rather than inferred from a failing request.

entries.description: Configuration entries held in the snapshot, across all tenants and features.

tenants.description: Tenants the snapshot currently covers. Zero right after a restart is normal.

size_bytes.description:
Approximate memory held by the snapshot. Sizing the store needs this number, which is
why it is reported rather than estimated by a reader.

Status.description:
Everything an operator needs when something is wrong, in one call: dependency health, the
build, the `tzdata` version the binary was built with, the current time and the snapshot
size (NFR-O5).

The `tzdata` version is reported because a boundary disagreement between a node and the
reference tables is diagnosable if you know which tables the node used, and is not
diagnosable otherwise (ADR-0007).

status.description:
A single word for a dashboard. Read `dependencies` for the detail: one word cannot say
which dependency is down, and a status that cannot is the status that gets ignored.

mode.description:
`readonly` while this instance was started with `QUOTACORE_STARTUP_MODE=readonly` for a
rebuild, or has lost its hold on the rebuild fence; it then refuses every write to a
tenant's balances and idempotency records with `503 service_unavailable`, and
`/readyz` is not ready. `normal` otherwise (consistency-and-recovery.md section 4.1,
added 2026-10-20).

version.description: The build version.

commit.description: The build commit, so a running binary is traceable to a source tree.

zone_data_version.description: The `tzdata` version the binary was built with.

server_time.description:
The service's own time, so a client that disagrees can see the discrepancy instead of
computing a silent one.

uptime_s.description:
Seconds since this process started, which is not the same as seconds since the
service was last healthy. A restart is visible here and not in `status`.

dependencies.description:
One row per dependency, and the reason to read this endpoint at all: the detail behind
the one word in `status`.

queue_depth.description:
The ledger queue's current depth on the instance that answered: events accepted and
not yet written. Growth toward `QUOTACORE_EVENT_QUEUE_SIZE` means the writer is behind,
and drops follow (ADR-0016).

worker.description:
The ledger writer's state on the instance that answered: `running`, `draining` while a
shutdown writes what is queued, and `stopped` before it starts or after it has drained.

ledger_dropped_total.description:
Ledger events this instance dropped since it started, over every reason. **Non-zero
means the history is incomplete**, and that is reported rather than hidden, because a
silently incomplete history is worse than a documented one (ADR-0016). An event the
ledger refused is kept as a dead letter, not counted here.

HealthResponse.description:
The probe response. Deliberately minimal: a liveness probe that inspects dependencies
restarts a process that was not the problem.

status.description:
`ok` from the liveness probe, `ready` from the readiness probe. The two differ
deliberately: a process that is alive but not ready is still the right process to keep
running.

ActivityItem.description: string ActivityItem.Action is one of the audit actions (e.g. `version.ready`, `pin.changed`); JsonElement ActivityItem.Data its details.

AuthResponse.description:
string? AuthResponse.RefreshToken is only returned to native clients. With the `X-Client: web` header the
refresh token is set as an HttpOnly cookie on `/v1/auth` instead.

BillingDetailsRequest.description:
Who Brazilian invoices (NFS-e) are made out to. string BillingDetailsRequest.TaxId is a CPF or CNPJ (numeric or alphanumeric),
punctuation allowed; string BillingDetailsRequest.PostalCode is the CEP; string BillingDetailsRequest.AddressNumber may be "S/N".

BillingResponse.description:
bool BillingResponse.LowCredits: 2 or fewer left after buying some ("Buy 10 and save 15%"). PaymentProvider BillingResponse.Provider takes
the organization's payments; bool BillingResponse.BillingDetailsRequired: Asaas needs the invoice details first.

BuildingAnalyticsResponse.description:
Non-internal activity over int BuildingAnalyticsResponse.Days days (rolled up hourly). double BuildingAnalyticsResponse.ObjectOpenedShare is the
share of visits that opened at least one element card: "87% of service visits used the digital twin".

converterVersionBelow.description: Reprocess versions built by a converter older than this (e.g. `1.1.0`); versions with no recorded converter count as older.

currentOnly.description: Only the versions buildings show (default). Older ready versions are rebuilt when they're made current again.

dryRun.description: List what would be reprocessed without enqueuing anything (default).

limit.description: At most this many versions per call (default 200, max 1000); call again for the rest.

matched.description: Versions matching the filter, including those over the limit.

enqueued.description: Versions queued now (0 on a dry run).

versionIds.description: The versions this call selected (at most the limit), oldest first.

CheckoutPix.description: The Pix "copia e cola" code (the app draws the QR from it) and until when the QR code works.

CheckoutResponse.description:
Uri? CheckoutResponse.Url: Stripe's checkout page, or Asaas's invoice page (boleto and card). CheckoutPix? CheckoutResponse.Pix is set for
open Asaas checkouts when Pix is available. Unpaid after DateTimeOffset CheckoutResponse.ExpiresAt, it becomes Expired.

CreateCheckoutRequest.description: IReadOnlyList<Guid>? CreateCheckoutRequest.BuildingIds for `Activation`; int? CreateCheckoutRequest.Pack (10 or 50) for `Pack`.

CreatedLinkResponse.description: The token only appears here, once: share Uri CreatedLinkResponse.Url or its QR.

CreateLinkRequest.description: IReadOnlyList<string>? CreateLinkRequest.Systems: system keys from the catalog; null or omitted means every system.

CreateVisitRequest.description:
The device ID goes in the `X-Device-Id` header (a random UUID the app or browser keeps);
string? CreateVisitRequest.DeviceId in the body is accepted when the header can't be set.

Discipline.description: What the uploader says a file contains; the converter uses it as a classification hint.

DocumentRef.description: A document linked to an element; Uri DocumentRef.Url is a presigned download valid for 15 minutes.

DocumentResponse.description: Uri? DocumentResponse.Url is a presigned download link valid for 15 minutes (null until the upload is confirmed).

DocumentUploadResponse.description: PUT the file to Uri DocumentUploadResponse.UploadUrl with `Content-Type: {ContentType}`, then call `/complete`.

props.description: Property sets by name, then properties by name.

ElementResponse.description:
An element's details. string? ElementResponse.GlobalId, string? ElementResponse.IfcClass and IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, JsonElement>> ElementResponse.Props are technical
details for members: null and empty for guests, link and grant visitors (PLAN §9).

EventInput.description: JsonElement? EventInput.Props is a small JSON object; the fields per type are listed in PLAN §12.

EventsRequest.description: Guid? EventsRequest.BuildingId is required with a user token and ignored with a visit token.

ExportResponse.description: Links are presigned for DateTimeOffset ExportResponse.UrlsExpireAt; ask again for fresh ones.

FunnelWeek.description:
One signup week (ISO week of the organization's creation) and how many of its organizations reached each
A-09 step. "Live" is the go-live action; "Visited" is the first non-internal visit (the activation metric).

GrantRole.description: Labels for the company; every grant role sees the building read-only, limited to its systems.

ManifestResponse.description:
The manifest clients load a building from (PLAN §9): chunk files as presigned URLs, only the
chunks the caller's scope allows. URLs expire at DateTimeOffset ManifestResponse.UrlsExpireAt; fetch it again then.

ManifestRoomCorrection.description:
A room's correction in this version's model coordinates: turn by double ManifestRoomCorrection.Yaw radians about +Y through
IReadOnlyList<double> ManifestRoomCorrection.Pivot, then move by IReadOnlyList<double> ManifestRoomCorrection.Offset (horizontal, y = 0). A model point p of the room is
really at Rot(yaw)·(p − pivot) + pivot + offset.

ManifestSpaceResponse.description:
A room; element meta refers to it by string ManifestSpaceResponse.Id (`r`). `floorY` is its floor height and
`outline` its floor outline as model [x, z] pairs seen from above, the room on the left of every edge
(inward normal = up × (next − this)); both are null when the file has no room geometry. `correction` is
where the room really is compared with the model, when an admin saved it or visitors agree on it.

MyBuildingResponse.description:
One building the caller can open. string MyBuildingResponse.Role is the organization role (Owner, Admin, Member) or the
grant role (Owner, Viewer, Contractor); IReadOnlyList<string>? MyBuildingResponse.Systems null means every system.

OrganizationRole.description: Ordered from least to most privileged, so roles compare with `>=`.

PlatePlacementRequest.description:
A placement in the model coordinates (metres, Y-up) of Guid PlatePlacementRequest.VersionId, as the viewer shows it.
IReadOnlyList<double> PlatePlacementRequest.Normal points out of the wall; IReadOnlyList<double> PlatePlacementRequest.Up is the plate's up direction.

int PlateResponse.SizeMm is the printed width of the plate image, quiet zone included. Uri PlateResponse.ImageUrl
is the AR reference image (about 1024 px).

errors.description: Field errors for `validation`.

PublicBuilder.description: Builder branding; both are null when the company turned branding off. The logo arrives with M3 branding.

PublicBuildingResponse.description: What a guest landing shows before anything else (PLAN §5, "QR scan → AR").

RefreshRequest.description: From the iOS app; the web sends the refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie instead.

RoomAdjustment.description: How far a room is moved (metres) and turned (degrees) from the model.

RoomCorrectionResponse.description:
A room's corrections. RoomCorrectionSource? RoomCorrectionResponse.Source is the one in use (null: none yet). RoomAdjustment? RoomCorrectionResponse.Visitors is set once
int RoomCorrectionResponse.DevicesNeeded devices agree, even under an admin's correction, so the two can be compared.

RoomObservationRequest.description:
A "Fix here" in AR, in the visited version's model coordinates. string? RoomObservationRequest.BaseSpaceId is the room the
alignment that was placing the building was made in (null: a plate on no room's wall), and
double RoomObservationRequest.BaseDistance its distance to the fix (metres). IReadOnlyList<double> RoomObservationRequest.Anchor is the model corner fixed;
IReadOnlyList<double> RoomObservationRequest.MarkInBase is where it really is, in the base room's model frame (the mark brought in by that
room's alignment). double? RoomObservationRequest.Turn is the room's turn relative to the base room (radians about +Y), only
when the fix measured it. bool RoomObservationRequest.HasTranslation is false for a fix against a wall (it gives the turn,
not where the room is along the wall).

SearchHit.description:
One result. string SearchHit.Id is the element or space id (`e{hex}`) to select in the viewer.
string SearchHit.Title is the element's name, or its kind in the caller's language when it has none.

SetPinRequest.description: string? SetPinRequest.Pin is required when enabling a PIN for the first time or changing it.

SetRoomCorrectionRequest.description: A room's correction in Guid SetRoomCorrectionRequest.VersionId's model coordinates, as in the manifest's `correction`.

SystemGroupResponse.description:
One group in the systems review: elements that share a source IFC system name and IFC class, with the
Insite View system they were assigned and why (string? SystemGroupResponse.ClassifiedBy).

OrganizationRole UpdateMemberRequest.Role Owner by an owner makes the member an owner too; with bool UpdateMemberRequest.TransferOwnership the

UpdatePlateRequest.description: Every field is optional; bool? UpdatePlateRequest.ClearPlacement removes the placement.

IReadOnlyList<string>? VisitResponse.Systems null means every system. bool VisitResponse.PinLocked: the building has a PIN the guest
hasn't entered, so only architecture is visible until `POST /v1/visit/unlock`.
bool VisitResponse.ReadOnly: an expired building, shown as an archive.

info.title: Kannon REST API
info.description: Versioned REST contract of Kannon. Authenticate with the configured Admin Token or a Domain API Key as a Bearer token. Decisions are recorded in docs/rest-api-design.md.

implementation_follow_up: Go generator selection and enforcement of domain/transport import separation.
Application operations, storage support and contract tests; preserve existing api_keys rows and secrets.
x-design-review.acceptance: User confirmed Q46 and subsequently approved the five-role simplification and lean implementation constraints. Implementation remains a separate task.

get.description: Ordering: Domain name ascending.
Ordering: Template ID ascending.

delete.summary: Delete a Template without affecting accepted Batches

post.description: Requires admin authority on the path Domain. Issue only supported roles anchored to that Domain. Existing API Keys remain in api_keys; no limited-role credential issuance or generic delegation engine is introduced.

get.description: Ordering: created_at descending, then ID descending.

patch.description: Idempotent revocation; roles cannot change and revoked credentials cannot be reactivated. Maps to domain delete authority even though the HTTP method is PATCH.

post.summary: Create an immutable Batch and accepted Deliveries atomically

200.description: Idempotent replay. No second Batch or Delivery is created. Original inline rejection details are unavailable.

post.description: At least one Recipient must be accepted. Persists accepted Deliveries atomically before 201. Submission success does not imply SMTP delivery. Rejected rows appear with original indexes. Max 2000 Recipients, 10 MiB HTTP body.

get.description: Ordering: created_at descending, then ID descending.

get.summary: Read a Batch and its immutable content

get.description: Ordering: Delivery ID ascending.
Ordering: timestamp descending, then ID descending.
Ordering: Bucket start ascending.

bearerAuth.description: Configured Admin Token or Domain API Key. Authentication resolves a Principal; role checks happen in application operations.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: Opaque cursor bound to Domain, collection and filters. Using it with a different query or an invalid token produces 400. No snapshot guarantee while data changes; do not edit the cursor.

from.name: from
from.description: Inclusive start.

group_by.name: group_by
group_by.description: Go duration syntax. Whole-hour multiples >= 1h. Buckets start at from; from aligns to a UTC hour and to-from is a multiple of group_by. Examples: 1h, 6h, 24h, 168h. Runtime validation required. Maximum 1000 buckets per query; empty buckets are returned with zeros.

idempotency.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotency.description: Domain-scoped creation key. Successful creation prevents duplicate Batch creation for at least 24 hours and retains the same Batch identity and original intake counts. Inline rejection details are never persisted or replayed. Changed input conflicts. Rejection before creation leaves the key reusable; an in-progress creation returns 409; every replay is reauthorized. After expiry, key reuse may create a new Batch.

attribution.name: X-Kannon-Attribution

schema.description: Application validation additionally enforces 256 UTF-8 bytes, not just characters.

attribution.description: Optional audit claim, not authority. Requires attribute on the target resource; admin holds it, other accepted roles do not. Valid UTF-8, at most 256 bytes, no control characters, trimmed non-empty value; an empty header means absent. Authenticated credential identity is always retained.

delivery_status.name: status
delivery_status.description: Filter persisted Deliveries by current state. rejected means post-intake validation rejection; inline rejections are never persisted.

ID.description: Opaque identifier. Clients must not parse its structure.

Fields.description: String personalization values interpreted literally. Global values are defaults overridden by per-recipient fields. email is reserved for the actual recipient address and cannot be supplied as an override.

TrackingOverride.description: Omitted axes impose no additional restriction. A Batch request above the Domain ceiling fails.

RecipientTracking.description: Values use TrackingMode names. Unsupported modes or modes above the Domain ceiling reject this Recipient, not the entire Batch.

email.description: A bare address, without a display name; use name for that. Not restricted to the Domain.

ReplyTo.description: Where replies should go, emitted as the Reply-To header. Literal, not personalized. When omitted, no Reply-To header is emitted and replies go to from.

Unsubscribe.description: Sender-owned HTTPS endpoint template, personalized with recipient fields. Not a Kannon endpoint.

Headers.description: Display headers only; recipients defines actual delivery targets.

AttachmentInput.description: Filenames must be unique within the request. An exact duplicate fails the whole request with 422 duplicate_attachment_filename; no attachment is silently overwritten.

RecipientInput.description: Input only. Missing/invalid address, unsupported policy, reserved-field override or unresolved personalization reject this Recipient inline. No rejected recipient data is persisted. Trim outer whitespace and lowercase only the email domain for duplicate comparison; preserve local-part case, dots and plus-tags. Later duplicate rows are rejected by original index.

scheduled_at.description: Omit for immediate sending. If supplied, must be in the future at first creation; otherwise 422. A valid replay does not revalidate the timestamp against the current clock.

global_fields.description: Defaults merged with each recipient fields, which take precedence. Applied to both subject and HTML. email is reserved. Missing placeholders reject the affected Recipient inline. A Recipient may carry at most 1000 fields, global fields included, or the whole request fails with 422 too_many_fields. Keys and values of all Recipients' fields plus 64 bytes for each field, global fields counted once per Recipient, may total at most 10 MiB, or the whole request fails with 422 fields_too_large.

BatchCreate.description: Maximum HTTP body 10 MiB including base64. Scheduling, tracking and personalization follow the documented domain rules.

type.description: Stable identifier: urn:kannon:problem:<code>. Does not require a hosted documentation endpoint.

Problem.description: RFC 9457. Stable type identifier urn:kannon:problem:<code>. Codes are stable; title/detail are human-readable. Extension fields may be added.

RecipientRejection.description: Zero-based input index. Initial response only: no Delivery or rejection record is persisted for this row.

Domain.description: The Domain name is its identifier; there is no separate generated Domain ID.

DomainPatch.description: Replaces the full policy; the Domain name is immutable.

TemplatePatch.description: Omitted fields stay unchanged. Null is not an instruction to delete a field.

APIKey.description: Metadata from the existing api_keys table. Secret is never returned on reads. Legacy rows without role metadata expose sender. expires_at null means no automatic expiry.

APIKeyCreated.description: Secret is returned once on creation only.

expires_at.description: Optional. Omit for no automatic expiration. If present, must be in the future.

APIKeyCreate.description: Issue in the existing api_keys table. Roles are immutable and anchored to the path Domain; requested authority cannot exceed issuer authority. Legacy keys without role metadata remain sender-only and retain their secrets and identifiers.

BatchSummary.description: Completed means no remaining attempts, not all delivered. History expires 30 days after processing completion. Later bounces do not restart that clock.

content.description: Immutable content snapshot. Source reference is provenance, not a live Template dependency.

Batch.description: History expires 30 days after Batch processing completion. GET then returns 404; Stats may still retain events referencing this ID.

BatchCreated.description: Initial creation receipt. Rejected recipient details are response-only and are never persisted. Intake counts and state here reflect creation; GET reads current state.

Delivery.description: Public history persists beyond removal of the worker pool row. Rejected here means validation rejected an existing Delivery, not intake rejection. History expires 30 days after Batch processing completion. GET then returns 404; Stats may still retain events referencing this ID.

permanent.description: Permanent SMTP refusal versus retry exhaustion after transient refusals; both are terminal bounced outcomes.

StatsEvent.description: Engagement identity fields follow Tracking Policy. Anonymous events exist only as counters. Pseudonymous events must not expose email or original delivery_id. Transient worker errors are not public outcome events. Original identifiers may outlive Batch/Delivery history; these historical references do not guarantee the resource remains retrievable.

AggregateSeries.description: Domain-level event occurrence counters, not unique-recipient counts; no batch_id filter. Includes zero-filled empty buckets. Maximum 1000 complete buckets; split the range or increase group_by. A zero does not prove collection was operational.

BatchReplay.description: Same Batch and original intake counts. Inline rejected recipient details are deliberately absent, never reconstructed or persisted. This is a creation receipt, not current Delivery state.

Error400.description: Malformed request or invalid/unknown query parameter.

Retry-After.description: When retry is appropriate, delay in seconds. Not present for a permanent conflict.

Error422.description: Invalid content; all recipients rejected creates no Batch.

Retry-After.description: When retry is appropriate, delay in seconds. Not present for a permanent conflict.
When retry is appropriate, delay in seconds. Not present for a permanent conflict.

x-credential-storage: Retain the existing api_keys table and rows. No key replacement, reissuance, copying or backfill. Add role metadata in place; absent legacy metadata means sender on the existing Domain.
x-compatibility: Compatible evolution within v1. Breaking changes require a new version. Legacy gRPC receives necessary fixes with no removal date fixed.
x-time-format: RFC 3339 input with explicit timezone; UTC output. Fractional-second precision is not fixed.
x-implementation-constraints: Reuse existing application modules; add Batch creation where missing. REST adapter -> application operation -> persistence.
Generated OpenAPI types stay out of domain/application interfaces. No command bus, per-endpoint factories or redundant pass-through layers.
Simple persistent Delivery history with query-based Batch state counts initially; no event sourcing or generic projection framework. Preserve existing Stats pipeline.
Batch-specific transactional idempotency with unique constraint and minimal receipt; no generic response cache.
Fixed-order keyset cursors; no persisted pagination sessions or distributed snapshots.

info.title: Dashy REST API
info.summary: Read and write your Dashy config over HTTP.
info.description:
The Dashy API is a simple opt-in REST API for CRUD actions over your config.
For full usage guide, examples and architecture, see the [API Docs](https://dashy.to/docs/api).

<details>
<summary>Enabling the API</summary>

The API is off by default. To enable it, set the `ENABLE_API` env var to true,
and restart Dashy.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Authenticating</summary>

By default, the API will use the same auth system as the rest of your Dashy instance.
If you don't have auth configured, or would prefer to use bearer token for the API instead,
then you can do so, by setting an `API_TOKEN` environmental variable,
and then passing that as a bearer token in the authorization header when making requests,
like `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-long-random-secret>' http://dashy.local/api/config`

</details>

> [!IMPORTANT]
> There is no warranty. It is your responsibility to correctly configure and protect your instance.
> The API is experimental.

Pool.description: effectivePricingUsdlReserveRaw=virtualUsdlReserveRaw+realUsdlBalanceRaw. Virtual reserve participates only in pricing and is not withdrawable funds. Current quote asset is verified deployed USDL6. Creation protocol fee1000000rawUSDL excludes PAX gas.

PoolStats.description: realUsdlBalanceRaw is booked real USDL backing, not virtual reserve or guaranteed per-wallet entitlement. Optional indicative TVL excludes virtual USDL and declares token mark. Rolling window end is source watermark chainSecond+1 with events constrained<=sourceUpperPosition; [end-window,end) event-time membership. Interface 2.2.0 additive fields (optional on the wire so frames committed before 2.2.0 stay valid; the producer always emits them): priceChangeBps5m/1h/6h with changeBaselineQuality5m/1h/6h use the priceChangeBps24h/changeBaselineQuality rule over [windowEnd-300s|3600s|21600s, windowEnd) at the same anchor. spotPriceWad is the pool getPrice() at the latest canonical price event (EventEmitter Swap or PoolStateUpdated) at or below sourceUpperPosition: floor(effectiveUsdlReserveRaw*10^18/tokenReserveRaw) with effectiveUsdlReserveRaw=virtualUsdlReserve+realUsdlBalance, both raw integers; null when no price event exists. spotPriceUsdlRaw is the price of one whole token (10^tokenDecimals raw) in USDL raw units (USDL has 6 decimals): floor(spotPriceWad*10^tokenDecimals/10^18), which equals floor(effectiveUsdlReserveRaw*10^tokenDecimals/tokenReserveRaw) exactly; null when spotPriceWad is null or tokenDecimals>18. uniqueTraders24h counts distinct committed fill actors and txCount24h counts committed fills (buys24h+sells24h) in [windowStart,windowEnd). totalSupplyRaw is the Transfer-authoritative indexed supply at sourceUpperPosition (complete holdings coverage only, else null); circulatingSupplyRaw=totalSupplyRaw minus the pool contract own token balance under circulationModel supply_minus_pool_reserve_v1. top10HolderShareBps and creatorHoldingShareBps are floor(10000*balance/circulatingSupplyRaw) at sourceUpperPosition over non-pool holders; the creator is the canonical pool creation creator; null when circulating supply is zero or unknown.

PortfolioPosition.description: Apply req.D06_001,D06_002,D06_005 proportional_floor_v1 exactly. For total T=K+U and disposal q, k=floor(q*K/T),u=q-k,pK=floor(P*k/q),pU=P-pK,c=floor(C*k/K) when K>0; c=C when k=K. Remaining K-k,U-u,C-c; known realized increases pK-c. Unknown proceeds never imply zero-cost gain. Outgoing transfer invents no sale proceeds. Verified linked-wallet basis carry requires explicit policy/consent.

PortfolioSummary.description: pricedSubtotal sums only known marked positions and is explicitly partial if anyunpriced. completeValue isnull until all valuations known. Summary covers allpositions,not currentpage. Unknown profitability remainsnull; PAX gas never subtracted asUSDL without conversion provenance.

Price.description: Gross execution uses actual paid input/output; post-swap spot uses pinned effective reserves and is not executable liquidation proceeds; external display never gates core launch/trade.

Reward.description: Claimability derives verified contract state or funded authorized program ledger; display cannot invent balances or settlement.

Stream.description: Public shape never includes ingest key; live status comes from authenticated provider evidence; viewer count distinct TTL heartbeats.

Token.description: Unavailable decimals/supply staynull with independent quality. Token identity remains readable but human normalization/valuation requiring unknown metadata unavailable. No assumed one-billion supply or default18decimals.

info.title: VYSEL API
info.summary: AI-powered personal styling — Style DNA from a single selfie.
info.description:
Initial public contract for the VYSEL platform (Phase 1.1).

## Conventions
- **Base path** — all routes are versioned under `/v1`. The web app reaches the API
  through a same-origin proxy (`/api/v1/*` → `/v1/*`), so browsers never make
  cross-origin calls.
- **Auth** — short-lived JWT access token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
  The refresh token lives only in an `HttpOnly` cookie scoped to `/v1/auth`.
- **IDs** — prefixed, opaque strings (`usr_`, `img_`, `anl_`). Do not parse them.
- **Timestamps** — RFC 3339, UTC.
- **Errors** — every non-2xx response is `application/problem+json`
  ([RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457)) with a stable,
  machine-readable `code`. Clients branch on `code`, never on `detail`.
- **Async work** — analysis is asynchronous. `POST /analyses` returns `202` with a
  `Location` and `Retry-After`; poll `GET /analyses/{analysis_id}` until the status
  is terminal (`succeeded` or `failed`).
- **Idempotency** — `POST /analyses` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header so retries
  never start duplicate jobs.
- **Estimates, not truths** — every inferred feature carries a `confidence` and the
  literal label `estimate`, matching the product's explainability principle.

placement.description: Where the branch landed (epic qits-1580, the soft feature freeze). Once the repository's active request holds as many counted sources as the threshold in force, it is frozen. Counted are branches naming a work item (epics, tasks, tickets of any type); main, maintenance/* and release/* never count. The threshold is the repository's own feature_freeze in .config/qits/release-requests.yml, else the project's release_requests.feature_freeze, else 3, and 0 turns it off. While it is frozen, every branch new to the repository's requests (a feature, a bug fix or a maintenance bump) lands in the one request queued behind it, minted if absent, which folds nothing and runs no gate until the active request has released or been withdrawn. A branch already a source of an unreleased request answers PRESENT where it is. outcome is CREATED, JOINED or PRESENT, queued says the answering request is queued, and detail is one sentence saying where the branch went.

Where the branch landed (epic qits-1580). An explicit join overrides the soft feature freeze: a request frozen at its threshold admits any branch named onto it here (a feature, a bug fix or a maintenance branch), and the new source carries explicitJoin true, with a detail saying it joined a frozen request explicitly. From RELEASED on no join is accepted: the 409 says the request is released and names the repository's next unreleased request by qualified id, if there is one.

assignee.description: An epic's or a ticket's assignee; null clears it.

repositoryId.description: A task's repository, in the task's project. Cannot be cleared.

implementedAt.description: A feature's or task's implemented marker (ISO-8601 instant); null clears it. Moves only while the owning epic is READY_FOR_DEV or IMPLEMENTING. Setting it moves the item's status to IMPLEMENTED; clearing it takes an IMPLEMENTED item back to IMPLEMENTING (or READY_FOR_DEV when it was never marked implementing).

implementingAt.description: A feature's or task's implementing marker (ISO-8601 instant): when its implementation was started. Cannot be cleared. Moves only while the owning epic is READY_FOR_DEV or IMPLEMENTING, and moves the item's status to IMPLEMENTING when it is not already there or further. On a task it also stamps the task's feature the first time, and moves an epic still READY_FOR_DEV to IMPLEMENTING.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An epic's or ticket's acceptance criteria, the whole list in order; null or an empty list clears them. Each item is one line of Markdown: not blank, no line break, at most one '.', and fewer than 20 whitespace characters. Editable at REFINED (outside an epic's scope freeze); from READY_FOR_DEV on a changed list is a 409, and restating the same list passes.

inspiredBy.description: The work's inspiration, on every archetype: the id of an idea of the same project; null clears it. Editable at every status. Setting, changing or clearing it re-derives the ideas' status.

priority.description: The ranking among siblings, on every archetype: higher sorts first, null after every number, then by number. Editable at every status but DONE and DROPPED (409), outside every scope freeze; null clears it. PUT /projects/api/work/{qualifiedId}/priority ranks by drop instead.

tags.description: The work's tags, on every archetype, the whole set: RESERVED_FOR_HUMAN marks work an agent cannot complete — a person does it and moves its status by hand, and no agent is dispatched onto it (say why in the description). CONDITION marks a condition other work waits for, not work of its own (say what closes it in the description); no agent is dispatched onto it. Editable at every status, outside every scope freeze; an empty array or null clears them. An unknown tag is a 400 naming the legal ones. A transition never changes them.

needs.description: What an epic, a ticket, a feature or a task waits for (qits-1903), the whole list: each entry a work item of the same project and the status it must reach. Editable at every status, outside every scope freeze; an empty array or null clears them. A transition never changes them.

WorkPriorities.description: The siblings a drop renumbered — the moved item and every one above it — in their new order, highest first.

WorkPriority.description: One sibling and the priority it now holds.

WorkRefinementAnswer.description: A work entity's refinement room; null on a read that found none.

WorkReprioritize.description: Where a dropped work item now sits among its siblings: directly above or directly below one of them. Exactly one of above and below.

above.description: The sibling the item now sits directly above, by qualified id or UUID.

below.description: The sibling the item now sits directly below, by qualified id or UUID.

WorkStatusMove.description: A lifecycle move: the status to move to, and — for a move into DROPPED — why the work is closed and what answers for it.

target.description: REPORTED, REFINED, READY_FOR_DEV, IMPLEMENTING, IMPLEMENTED, VERIFYING, VERIFIED, DONE or DROPPED — one the entity's current status may move to: a neighbour on the walk (IMPLEMENTING has no move back, and READY_FOR_DEV none to REPORTED), or IMPLEMENTED from READY_FOR_DEV or VERIFIED from IMPLEMENTED (the skips).

outcome.description: Why the work is closed: required with a move into DROPPED and refused with any other move. DUPLICATE — another item asks for the same thing; RESOLVED_ELSEWHERE — another item's change resolved it; SUPERSEDED — replaced by a successor; OBSOLETE — the subject went away by itself; INVALID — it never was a problem; WONT_DO — a decision was taken not to do it (scratch and probe items too). Reopening (DROPPED to REPORTED) clears it.

supersededBy.description: The item that answers for the drop, by qualified id (<projectSlug>-<n>) or UUID: required with outcome DUPLICATE, RESOLVED_ELSEWHERE or SUPERSEDED, refused with OBSOLETE, INVALID or WONT_DO and with any move not into DROPPED. It must name an item of the same project, never the item itself. Reopening clears it.

reason.description: An issue's move only, written on its thread: required and one line with OBSOLETE, and with RESOLVED from the desk; optional with RESOLVED from a person (the answer). Refused on every other archetype.

WorkWorkspaces.description: The workspaces a dispatch stood on a work entity's branch.

WrapperClosing.description: One VERIFIED ticket's wrapper branch, its ledger row and request, and the verdict the platform's close rules hold of it now.

verdict.description: NO_REQUEST (no wrapper, no ledger row, or a PUSHED row naming no request), IN_FLIGHT (the row names a request whose delivery has not ended), CLOSING (LIVE, or withdrawn as the empty wrapper: the platform moves the ticket to DONE) or UNPROVEN (the row ended without the ledger proving an ending: only the git host can still close it)

step.description: The wrapper ledger row's step; null when there is no row

requestId.description: The request the row names; null when none

approval.description: That request's approval state as the release-request read derives it: NOT_REQUIRED, WAITING, APPROVED or DECLINED; null when no request

version.description: The row's version (RELEASED, LIVE)

WrapperClosings.description: Every VERIFIED ticket of a project, with where its wrapper closing stands.

closings.description: One per VERIFIED ticket, ordered by ticket number

It also re-asserts the project's announced configuration: the wrapper's project.yml is read again and ProjectChanged restates supportsEnvironments and frontDeskLifecycle as stored, best effort and absent from the answer.

Never a push to main: the edit is committed onto a branch and released through the repository's release request. Reads .config/qits/repository.yml at main; when it already says what was asked the answer is 200 with outcome unchanged and nothing is opened. Otherwise the file is edited as text, comments and every other key kept, and the edit is refused with 422 (error ARCHIVE_EDIT_REFUSED, nothing written) when the result would change anything but repository.archived or the file cannot be edited safely (a flow-style repository: {...}, a document that does not parse). The branch is created at main (or an existing one brought up to date with it), the edit committed onto it as chore(platform): <verb> <repository name>, and the branch asked for exactly as POST .../release-requests asks: it creates or JOINS the repository's open request. 202 with outcome requested, the branch, the commit and the release request's id and qualifiedId. post.summary: Reset this repository's backup twin whose main holds unrelated history
post.description: Probes the backup twin's main branch (the repository's url) and pushes ours onto it, under the repository's backup lock. A twin with no main, at ours, or behind ours is fast-forwarded with the backup's own push (kind FAST_FORWARD, no force). A twin whose main shares no commit with ours (a forge's seed commit) has its main force-updated with a lease on the sha probed, tags pushed without force (kind UNRELATED_RESET); only main is ever forced. A twin ahead of ours or diverged from a common base is refused with 409 naming both shas, and nothing is pushed. On success the backup outcome reads SUCCEEDED and the reset is recorded with who decided and why (GET .../backup-resets). Only a person — qits:admin, verified by this service from a browser session or a person's qits CLI token — or the project's delivery desk (its own delivery token, in its own project; recorded under its token subject). Asserted identity headers, agents, CI, service clients and another project's desk answer 403.
