schema.description: Information about a Source for which the metadata has been modified.

event_timestamp.description: Timestamp at which the Source was modified

schema.title: Source Deleted Notification
schema.description: Notification that a Source has been deleted.

event_timestamp.description: Timestamp at which the Source was modified

trait_resource_info_head_400.description: Bad request. Query parameters are invalid.

trait_paged_limit.name: limit
trait_paged_limit.description: Restrict the response to the specified number of results. Service implementations may specify their own default and maximum for the limit

trait_resource_paged_key.name: page
trait_resource_paged_key.description: Opaque string used by backend to access a specific page of results. Clients should read the next URL from the `Link` header returned with responses, or use value of the returned X-Paging-NextKey header. If not supplied, the first page is accessed. Service implementations should ensure a consistent sort order is applied to pages of results.

basic_auth.description:
HTTP basic authentication using a username and password.

This option should only be used in constrained cases where Bearer tokens are impractical, since the password is intrinsically long-lived, and managing user credentials across systems is difficult compared to using centralised auth (e.g. via OAuth2) with Bearer tokens

bearer_token_auth.description:
HTTP bearer token authentication.

The method through which a client should acquire a bearer token is assumed to be an OAuth2 grant (either the Authorization Code or Client Credentials grant), however the OpenAPI `OAuth Flow` object cannot be used because it requires that the relevant URLs are known in advance.

Clients should provide options to allow one (or both) grant types to be configured, as appropriate.

Where tokens are not JWTs, or are acquired through some other mechanism, the API key method should be used instead.

url_token_auth.name: access_token
url_token_auth.description:
URL token authentication.

The method through which a client should acquire the token is not specified: it is assumed this takes place in another way, and a TAMS client may well be passed a URL to a TAMS service instance including the token.

Clients should retain the token in the `access_token` query string parameter, and use it for subsequent requests to the TAMS service instance in the same session.

collectionitem.title: Collection Item
collectionitem.description: Describes how an entity (Source or Flow) is collected into another entity of the same type

id.description: Source or Flow Identifier of the member of this collection. Sources MUST only collect Sources, and Flows MUST only collect Flows. Must already be registered in this service instance

role.description: The purpose of this element in the collection, primarily intended to be human-readable.

containermapping.title: Container Mapping
containermapping.description: Defines the location of Flow essence data in a container track

track_index.description: A zero-based and sequential track index in the container. This assumes a reliable ordering of tracks

format_track_index.description: A zero-based and sequential track index in the container for a particular Flow format. A container with a video and 2 audio tracks would have a format_track_index 0 for the video Flow and format_track_index 0 and 1 for the audio Flows. This assumes a reliable ordering of tracks for each Flow format

audio_track.description: Mapping for channels in audio tracks to the Flow channels

channel_numbers.description: Array of (zero-based) container channel numbers in Flow order

channel_range.description: Inclusive range of (zero-based) container channel numbers

mp2ts_container.description: Mapping to MPEG-2 Transport Stream containers, ISO/IEC 13818-1 or ITU-T Recommendation H.222.0

pid.description: The packet ID for the elementary stream packets

mxf_container.description: Mapping to Material Exchange Format containers, SMPTE ST 377-1

package_uid.description: The package UID. Either a SMPTE UMID URN or UUID URN

track_id.description: The track ID in the package

isobmff_container.description: Mapping to ISO Base Media File Format (e.g. MP4 and MOV) containers, ISO/IEC 14496-12

contentformat.title: Content Format
contentformat.description: Identifies the content format for a Flow or Source using a URN string

id.description: Deletion Request ID

flow_id.description: ID of the Flow to which the deletion request relates

timerange_to_delete.description: The timerange of Flow Segments to be deleted in this request, as described by the [TimeRange](#/schemas/timerange) type

timerange_remaining.description: The timerange of Flow Segments not yet deleted by this request, as described by the [TimeRange](#/schemas/timerange) type

delete_flow.description: Whether the Flow should be deleted once the timerange has been

created.description: Date/Time when this deletion request was created

created_by.description: A string identifier for the entity that created the deletion request. Service implementations SHOULD set suitable default values for `created_by` based on the principal accessing the system.

updated.description: Date/Time when this deletion request was updated

expiry.description: Date/Time when this deletion request will be deleted

status.description: Status of the delete request

error.description: Provides more information for the error status, as described by the [Error](#/schemas/error) type

error.title: Error status metadata
error.description: Provides more information for an error status.

summary.description: Summary description of the error and causes.

traceback.description: Stack trace leading to error (as a list of strings)

time.description: Time at which the error ocurred, to aid in log correlation

eventstreamcommon.title: Event Stream Mechanism
eventstreamcommon.description: Describes an event stream mechanism available in this service instance

name.description: Name of this type of event stream mechanism. Must be unique. Any name defined in this specification is reserved

docs.description: Location (e.g. a URL) at which documentation for this event stream mechanism may be found

config.description: Configuration options required to make use of this mechanism

format.description: The primary content type URN for the Flow.

essence_parameters.title: Audio Flow Essence Parameters
essence_parameters.description: Describes the parameters of the essence inside this audio Flow

sample_rate.description: The fixed number of samples per second.

bit_depth.description: The number of significant bits used to represent the audio sample. The minumum number of bytes then equals `round_up(bit_depth / 8)`. If codec is `audio/x-raw-int` bit_depth must be set. If codec is `audio/x-raw-float` bit_depth must be set to 32 or 64

coded_frame_size.description: The fixed number of samples per coded audio frame.

mp4_oti.description: The MPEG-4 Object Type Identification. For more information on the use of this property in codec strings, see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Formats/codecs_parameter#mpeg-4_audio

unc_type.description: The uncompressed audio multi-channel representation type. If codec is `audio/x-raw-int` or `audio/x-raw-float`, unc_type must be set.

init_segments.description: Whether the Flow makes use of initialisation segments. This parameter MUST be set to `true` if Media Objects have `init_object` populated. If set to `true`, all Media Objects MUST have `init_object` populated. Assume `false` if omitted.

flowcollection.title: Flow Collection
flowcollection.description: Describes how Flows are collected into another Flow. Note that this is an ordered list.

container_mapping.description: Describes the mapping of the Flow essence from this Flow collection's container

flowcommon.description: Describes the core fields of a Flow (common properties to all Flows, imported by flow-get and flow-put specifications)
flowcommon.title: Flow Common

id.description: Flow identifier

label.description: Freeform string label for the Flow. This should be a very short, human-readable label that may be displayed in listings of Flows.

description.description: Freeform text describing the Flow. This should be a human-readable description that may be showed in detailed views of Flows. The description should be longer and more detailed than `label`.

created_by.description: A string identifier for the entity that created the Flow. Service implementations SHOULD set suitable default values for `created_by` based on the principal accessing the system, and MAY permit clients to edit the value, subject to suitable permissions-based limitations.

updated_by.description: A string identifier for the entity that updated the Flow metadata most recently. Service implementations SHOULD set suitable default values for `updated_by` based on the principal accessing the system, and MAY permit clients to edit the value, subject to suitable permissions-based limitations.

tags.description: Key value is a freeform string. WARNING: When updating a Flow with `tags` set, `tags` will be replaced with the provided dictionary. `tags` WILL NOT be merged with the provided values. When `tags` is not set in the request, `tags` will be unset (i.e. set to `{}`). To update individual tags, clients should use the [Create or Update Flow Tag](#/operations/PUT_flows-flowId-tags-name) endpoint.

metadata_version.description: A change to the Flow metadata, not including metadata_version, metadata_updated, segments_updated or Segments, results in a new version. If the metadata_version for Flow instances is identical then the metadata is identical. Service implementations SHOULD set suitable default values for `metadata_version` whenever Flow metadata is changed and `metadata_version` is either not set by the client, or set to it's existing value. Service implementations MAY permit clients to edit the value, subject to suitable permissions-based limitations. Where media is transfered between TAMS service instances without changing the Flow metadata, clients SHOULD maintain the `metadata_version`. To support this, service implementations SHOULD always accept the setting of `metadata_version` by the client on initial Flow creation. Service implementations SHOULD update this field where metadata is updated via child endpoints. Note that this specification places no requirements on incremental versioning. Service implementations may, for example, choose to use hashes or date-time version identifiers.

generation.description: An indication of how many lossy encodings the Flow content has been through. This parameter provides a hint to clients as to which is the "highest qualty" Flow available to them. A Flow with a higher generation may contain less of the original information than a flow with a lower generation. Where a Flow is captured straight from the orginating device (e.g. camera/microphone) in its highest quality, and there is no possibility of the content becoming available in a higher quality (e.g. via capture from ST2110 or SDI), it SHOULD have a `generation` of `0`. Where the originating device outputs multiple qualities of the Source, `generation` should represent the encoding processes each has been through as accurately as possible.

created.description: The date-time the Flow was created in a given context, e.g. in the service instance. Service implementations SHOULD ignore this if given in a PUT request, and instead manage it internally

metadata_updated.description: The date-time the Flow metadata was updated in a given context, e.g. in the service instance. Service implementations SHOULD ignore this if given in a PUT request, and instead manage it internally

segments_updated.description: The date-time the Flow Segments were updated in a given context, e.g. in the service instance. Service implementations SHOULD ignore this if given in a PUT request, and instead manage it internally

read_only.description: If set to 'true', service implementations SHOULD reject client requests to update Flow metadata (other than the read_only property), and Flow Segments. Service implementations should also reject requests to the [`/flows/{flowId}/storage`](#/operations/POST_flows-flowId-storage) endpoint for the Flow, and requests to delete the Flow.

max_bit_rate.description: The maximum bit rate of the Flow Segments in 1000 bits/second. A precise definition can be found in the [Setting Flow Bit Rate Properties](https://github.com/bbc/tams/blob/main/docs/appnotes/0013-setting-flow-bit-rate-properties.md) AppNote.

timerange.description: The timerange of samples available in the Flow, as described by the [TimeRange](../schemas/timerange#top) type. Service implementations MUST ignore this if given in a PUT request, and instead manage it internally.

flow_collection.description: List of Flows that are collected together by this Flow.

collected_by.description: Flows that reference this Flow to include it in a collection. This attribute is intended to be read-only. Service implementations SHOULD ignore this if given in a PUT request, and instead manage it internally

format.description: The primary content type URN for the Flow.

essence_parameters.title: Data Flow Essence Parameters
essence_parameters.description: Describes the parameters of the essence inside this data Flow

data_type.description: The type of information encoded in the Flow, identified using a URN. e.g. The data_type may be urn:x-tams:data:bounding-box, and the codec `application/json`.

init_segments.description: Whether the Flow makes use of initialisation segments. This parameter MUST be set to `true` if Media Objects have `init_object` populated. If set to `true`, all Media Objects MUST have `init_object` populated. Assume `false` if omitted.

profile_id.description: Profile identifier that was used to create the flow.

flowimage.title: Image Flow
flowimage.description: Describes a still image Flow, for use by thumbnail tracks etc

format.description: The primary content type URN for the Flow.

essence_parameters.title: Image Flow Essence Parameters
essence_parameters.description: Describes the parameters of the essence inside this image Flow

frame_width.description: The width of the picture in pixels.

frame_height.description: The height of the picture in pixels.

aspect_ratio.description: The display aspect ratio. i.e. display_width / display_height

format.description: The primary content type URN for the flow.

essence_parameters.title: Multi Flow Essence Parameters
essence_parameters.description: Describes the parameters of the essence inside this multi Flow

init_segments.description: Whether the Flow makes use of initialisation segments. This parameter MUST be set to `true` if Media Objects have `init_object` populated. If set to `true`, all Media Objects MUST have `init_object` populated. Assume `false` if omitted.

profile_id.description: Profile identifier that was used to create the flow.  When supplying a profile_id no metadata which can be contained in a Profile should also be provided, doing so will result in a 400 validation error.  Trying to create a Flow using a Profile ID that does not exist should also provide a 400 validation error

flowsegment.description: Provides the location and metadata of the media files corresponding to timerange segments of a Flow.
flowsegment.title: Flow Segment

object_id.description: The object store identifier for the Media Object.

ts_offset.description: The timestamp offset between the sample timestamps stored in the media file and the corresponding timestamp in the Segment, ie. ts_offset = segment ts - media object ts. Assumed to be 0:0 if not set. Format as described by the [Timestamp](#/schemas/timestamp) type

timerange.description: The timerange for the samples contained in the Segment. The timerange start is always inclusive. If samples have a duration then the timerange end is exclusive and covers at least the duration of the last sample. The exclusive timerange end will typically be set to the timestamp of the next sample. If the samples don't have a duration then the timerange end is inclusive. Format is described by the [TimeRange](#/schemas/timerange) type. Note that where temporal re-ordering is used, the timerange and samples refers to the presentation timeline.

last_duration.description: The difference between the exclusive end of the `timerange` and the last sample timestamp. Format as described by the [Timestamp](#/schemas/timestamp) type, but cannot be negative

object_timerange.description: The timerange covering the sample timestamps embedded in or derived from the Media Object itself, on the Media Object's timeline.

sample_offset.description: The start of the Segment represented as a count of samples from the start of the Media Object. Note that a sample is a video frame or audio sample. A (coded) audio frame has multiple audio samples. Assumed to be 0 if not set. DEPRECATED: Use object_timerange instead - see AppNote 0036. Service implementations SHOULD continue to store and return it if set.

sample_count.description: The count of samples in the Segment (which may be fewer than in the Media Object). The count could be less than expected given the Segment duration and rate if there are gaps. If not set, every sample from sample_offset onwards is used. Note that a sample is a video frame or audio sample. A (coded) audio frame has multiple audio samples. DEPRECATED: Use object_timerange instead - see AppNote 0036. Service implementations SHOULD continue to store and return it if set.

init_object.title: Initialisation Object
init_object.description: The Object containing the initialisation segment required to decode the parent Media Object.

object_id.description: The identifier of the initialisation Object.

flowsegmentbulkfailure.title: Failed Segments
flowsegmentbulkfailure.description: List of Segments that have failed to register

failed_segments.description: The list of Segments which have failed to register with the service instance

items.description: Failed Segment details

object_id.description: The Object ID of the Segment which has failed to register with the service instance

timerange.description: The timerange of Segment that has failed, as described by the [TimeRange](#/schemas/timerange) type

error.description: Provides more information for the error status, as described by the [Error](#/schemas/error) type

flowsegmentpost.title: Flow Segment Post
flowsegmentpost.description: Provides the location and metadata of the media files corresponding to timerange Segments of a Flow.

object_id.description: The Object identifier for the Media Object. The `content-type` of the Media Object MUST match the `container` mime-type of the Flow. Service implementations SHOULD reject Objects IDs which have previously been registered as an `init_object_id` on other Flow Segments. i.e. init segments may not be used as media segments.

init_object_id.description: The Object identifier for the initialisation segment Object required to decode the Media Object. The `content-type` of the initialisation segment Object MAY differ from the `container` mime-type of the Flow. This parameter MUST only be set where the media format makes use of initialisation segments. Initialisation Objects SHOULD be re-used where possible. This parameter SHOULD be omitted where the Object `object_id` already exists and is being re-used. Service implementations SHOULD reject Objects IDs which have previously been registered as an `id` on other Flow Segments. i.e. media segments may not be used as init segments.

ts_offset.description: The timestamp offset between the sample timestamps stored in, or inferred from, the media file and the corresponding timestamp in the Segment, ie. ts_offset = segment ts - media object ts. Assumed to be 0:0 if not set. Format as described by the [Timestamp](#/schemas/timestamp) type

timerange.description: The timerange for the samples contained in the Segment. The timerange start is always inclusive. If samples have a duration then the timerange end is exclusive and covers at least the duration of the last sample. The exclusive timerange end will typically be set to the timestamp of the next sample. If the samples don't have a duration then the timerange end is inclusive. Format is described by the [TimeRange](#/schemas/timerange) type. Note that where temporal re-ordering is used, the timerange and samples refers to the presentation timeline.

object_timerange.description: The timerange covering the sample timestamps embedded in or derived from the Media Object itself, on the Media Object's timeline. If not given at first registration of an Object, defaults to `timerange - ts_offset` on the assumption that the Flow Segment uses the entire Media Object. Clients should not set this when Media Objects are re-used. Service implementations should reject requests where `object_timerange` is set to a value that conflicts with the existing Media Object metadata.

last_duration.description: The difference between the exclusive end of the `timerange` and the last sample timestamp. Format as described by the [Timestamp](#/schemas/timestamp) type, but cannot be negative

sample_offset.description: The start of the Segment represented as a count of samples from the start of the Object. Note that a sample is a video frame or audio sample. A (coded) audio frame has multiple audio samples. Assumed to be 0 if not set. Must be set if the Flow Segment doesn't start at the beginning of the Media Object. DEPRECATED: Use object_timerange instead - see AppNote 0036. Service implementations SHOULD continue to store and return it if set.

sample_count.description: The count of samples in the Segment (which may be fewer than in the Object). The count could be less than expected given the Segment duration and rate if there are gaps. If not set, every sample from sample_offset onwards is used. Must be set if the Flow Segment doesn't use the entire Media Object. Note that a sample is a video frame or audio sample. A (coded) audio frame has multiple audio samples. DEPRECATED: Use object_timerange instead - see AppNote 0036. Service implementations SHOULD continue to store and return it if set.

get_urls.description: A list of URLs to which a GET request can be made to directly retrieve the contents of the Media Object. This is required by the `http_object_store` Storage Backend type, which is the only one currently described. Clients may choose any URL in the list and treat them as identical, however service instances may sort the list such that the preferred URL is first. `get_urls` should only be used to add uncontrolled URLs. URLs for the provided object_id controlled by the service instance will be populated automatically by the service instance.

url.description: A URL to which a GET request can be made to directly retrieve the contents of the Media Object. Clients should include credentials if the provide URL is on the same origin as the API endpoint

label.description: Label identifying this URL. Service implementations should reject any requests using labels that are already associated with Storage Backends. Service implementations should reject any requests containing multiple `get_urls` with the same `label`.

key_frame_count.description: The number of key frames in the Media Object. This should be set greater than zero when the Media Object contains key frames that serve as a stream access point

flowstatus.title: Flow Status
flowstatus.description: The current ingest status of a Flow. Available values are as follows. `awaiting_content` - Flow is expecting, but not currently receiving content. `ingesting` - Content is currently being ingested. `replication_in_progress` - Content is currently being ingested to this Flow from another Service Instance via a replication process. `closed_complete` - Flow is complete and will not receive any more content. NOTE: Because this parameter is maintained/updated by a Client, the value of this parameter is only indicative and not authoritative. If the Client ingesting the content becomes unavailable, it may leave this parameter in an incorrect state. Clients should aim to tidy up this state appropriately once they recover. Service Implementers MAY consider adding more active management of the `status` of Flows to mitigate Clients failing to tidy up on completion/failure, as part of more general lifecycle management capability, in line with the approach described for [retention management](https://github.com/bbc/tams/blob/main/docs/appnotes/0019-implementing-retention-management.md). But Clients should not assume such capability.

flowstorage.title: Media Bucket Object Store
flowstorage.description: Gives information on storage for Objects. This schema is for the `http_object_store` Storage Backend type which provides URLs for storing Objects in object store buckets, and is the only Storage Backend type currently implemented.  URLs SHOULD support the inclusion of checksums in headers as supported by advertised Storage Backend product. See AppNote 0048 for more details. Where included in the response, `content-type` MUST match the corresponding value in the request.

media_objects.description: List of information for identifying and uploading Objects

items.description: Information for a Object

object_id.description: The object store identifier for the Object.

presigned.description: If `true`, this URL is pre-signed. If this parameter is unset, the URL is NOT pre-signed. The presigned URL SHALL remain valid for the timeframe advertised in [`min_presigned_url_timeout` at the `/service`](#/operations/GET_service) endpoint, which is subject to a specified minimum (see service endpoint schema).

flowstoragepost.title: Flow Storage Post
flowstoragepost.description: Post data for the Flow storage endpoint

limit.description: Limit the number of Objects in each response page. Service implementations may specify their own default and maximum for the limit

object_ids.description: Array of object_ids to use. The supplied object_ids must be new and not already in use in this TAMS service instance. A 400 response will be returned if any supplied object_id already exists.

storage_id.description: The Storage Backend to allocate storage in. A Storage Backend identifier as advertised at the [/service/storage-backends](#/operations/GET_storage-backends) endpoint. If not set the default, as advertised at the [/service/storage-backends](#/operations/GET_storage-backends) endpoint, will be used if available. An invalid Storage Backend identifier will result in a 400 error.

content_type.description: The `content_type` to use for the Objects. This parameter MUST only be set where requesting storage for initialisation segments in media formats which require them, and where the mime-type of those initialisation segments differs to that of the media segments. Assumed to be the `container` type of the Flow if not set.

presigned.description: If set to `true`, the `put_url`s in the response will be presigned. If set to `false`, the `put_url`s in the response will not be presigned. If `presigned` is set to `false`, the response from the service could be substantially faster if it is not required to generate a large number of pre-signed URLs. Services may choose their own default. If Clients only support one mode of operation, they SHOULD specify this parameter.

flowtechnical.title: Flow Technical
flowtechnical.description: Describes the technical characteristics of a Flow (imported by type-specific specifications or as part of a profile)

codec.description: A MIME type identification of the (lossy or lossless) coding used for the Flow content. Note that the `type` component of the container MIME type (i.e. the component before the `/`) may be different to the `type` component of the codec MIME type. e.g. An audio Flow may have `audio/aac` coded content may be wrapped in a `video/mp2t` container. Mime types from the [IANA registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml) should be preferred. Where multiple MIME types are possible, the most common should be preferred. Where this is insufficient, the maintainers of the TAMS repository may create an application note advising which MIME type to use.

container.description: The container MIME type for Flow Segments. Note that the `type` component of the container MIME type (i.e. the component before the `/`) may be different to the `type` component of the codec MIME type. e.g. An audio Flow may have `audio/aac` coded content may be wrapped in a `video/mp2t` container. Where multiple types exist for a subtype (e.g. `video/mp4`, `audio/mp4`, `application/mp4`), the closest MIME type to the Flow `format` should be used (e.g. `audio/mp4` for a Flow `format` of `urn:x-nmos:format:audio`). Mime types from the [IANA registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml) should be preferred. Where multiple MIME types are possible, the most common should be preferred. Where this is insufficient, the maintainers of the TAMS repository may create an application note advising which MIME type to use.

avg_bit_rate.description: The average bit rate of the Flow Segments in 1000 bits/second. A precise definition can be found in the [Setting Flow Bit Rate Properties](https://github.com/bbc/tams/blob/main/docs/appnotes/0013-setting-flow-bit-rate-properties.md) AppNote.

segment_duration.description: The target Flow Segment duration in seconds. The duration for each Segment may vary around this target value. See also the [Setting Flow Bit Rate Properties](https://github.com/bbc/tams/blob/main/docs/appnotes/0013-setting-flow-bit-rate-properties.md) AppNote for how this property can be used to calculate buffer sizes.

container_mapping.description: Describes the mapping of the Flow essence from the this Flow's container

format.description: The primary content type URN for the Flow.

essence_parameters.title: Video Flow Essence Parameters
essence_parameters.description: Describes the parameters of the essence inside this video Flow

frame_width.description: The width of the picture in pixels.

frame_height.description: The height of the picture in pixels.

bit_depth.description: The number of significant bits used to represent the video component sample. If codec is `video/raw`, bit_depth must be set.

interlace_mode.description: Interlaced video mode for frames in this Flow

aspect_ratio.description: The display aspect ratio. i.e. display_width / display_height

pixel_aspect_ratio.description: The pixel aspect ratio. This is usually 1:1 (i.e. square pixels) for modern video. Some, usually older, video formats use non-square pixels e.g. some Standard Definition video. This is where that may be indicated.

horiz_chroma_subs.description: Horizontal chroma component sub-sampling. When unc_type is set to a YUV type, horiz_chroma_subs must be set.

vert_chroma_subs.description: Vertical chroma component sub-sampling. When unc_type is set to a YUV type, vert_chroma_subs must be set.

unc_type.description: Uncompressed picture packing type. If codec is `video/raw`, unc_type must be set.

profile.description: AVC / H.264 profile byte. For more information on the use of this property in codec strings, see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Formats/codecs_parameter#using_the_codecs_parameter

level.description: AVC / H.264 level byte. For more information on the use of this property in codec strings, see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Formats/codecs_parameter#using_the_codecs_parameter

flags.description: AVC / H.264 flags byte. For more information on the use of this property in codec strings, see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Formats/codecs_parameter#using_the_codecs_parameter

frame_rate.title: Fixed Frame Rate
frame_rate.description: The fixed number of frames per second. MUST be set if `vfr` is `false` or omitted. MUST NOT be set if `vfr` is `true`.

vfr.description: If `true`, the frame rate of the Flow is variable and `frame_rate` MUST NOT be set. If `false` or omitted, the frame rate of the Flow is fixed and `frame_rate` MUST be set.

init_segments.description: Whether the Flow makes use of initialisation segments. This parameter MUST be set to `true` if Media Objects have `init_object` populated. If set to `true`, all Media Objects MUST have `init_object` populated. Assume `false` if omitted.

httprequest.title: HTTP Request
httprequest.description: Gives information on a particular http request a client should perform

url.description: The URL to make the request to. Where this URL is pre-signed, it SHALL remain valid for the timeframe advertised in [`min_presigned_url_timeout` at the `/service`](#/operations/GET_service) endpoint, which is subject to a specified minimum (see service endpoint schema).

body.description: The text of the body which needs to be included in the request

content-type.description: The content type which must be used

headers.description: Additional headers that should be included

mimetype.title: MIME Type
mimetype.description: A Mime Type without parameters as defined in [RFC2045](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2045#section-5.1) and [RFC7231](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-3.1.1.1)

id.description: The Object identifier.

referenced_by_flows.description: List of Flows that reference this Object via Flow Segments in this store instance. For init Objects, this reference is indirect via Media Objects.

This Flow is also present in 'referenced_by_flows' if it is still referenced by the Flow. timerange.title: TimeRange
timerange.description:
A timerange of timestamps. It is represented using one or two timestamps with inclusivity and exclusivity markers.

E.g.
* `[0:0_10:0)` represents 10 seconds of media starting at timestamp `0:0` and ending before `10:0`.
* `(5:0_` represents a timerange starting after `5:0` and to eternity.
* `_` without timestamps or inclusivity markers represents "eternity" (i.e. the entire timeline).
* `()` without timestamps represents "never" (i.e. a range of zero length in no particular position).
* `[1694429247:0_1694429248:0)` is a 1 second TAI timerange starting at 2023-09-11T10:46:50.0Z UTC.
* `[1694429247:0]` is an instantaneous TAI timerange at 2023-09-11T10:46:50.0Z UTC.
  This is equivalent to `[1694429247:0_1694429247:0]`.
  The short syntax is preferred due to ease of identification as instantaneous.
  Instantaneous TimeRanges cannot use exclusive markers (i.e. `(` or `)`).
* A `[` or `]` indicates that bound is inclusive, and a `(` or `)` indicates that bound is exclusive.

Details of the format can be found in the [Timestamps in TAMS](https://github.com/bbc/tams/blob/main/docs/appnotes/0008-timestamps-in-TAMS.md) application note.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description:
A signed nanosecond resolution timestamp represented as "{sign?}{seconds}:{nanoseconds}". The intended
interpretation of the value is assumed to be defined elsewhere.

E.g.
* "1:40000000" is the timestamp of the 27th video frame for 25 Hz video with origin at "0:0".
* "1694429247:40000000" is the TAI timestamp for a video frame at 2023-09-11T10:46:50.04Z UTC.

Details of the format can be found in the [Timestamps in TAMS](https://github.com/bbc/tams/blob/main/docs/appnotes/0008-timestamps-in-TAMS.md) application note.

A webhook in the `error` or `disabled` state may be re-enabled by a client by setting the status to `created`. info.description: API used by panels/addons to create, manage, monitor, back up, and restore hosted database instances.

get.summary: Inspect live import/export scheduling capacity and estimate representative concurrency.
get.description: The recommendation is a conservative resource model, not a measured throughput guarantee. A result of zero means the live memory budget cannot safely fit one modelled job and must not be coerced to one. CPU and I/O are concurrency weights; a memory-safe job that exceeds either whole weight budget may run only as one isolated job. A compressed logical import is charged at the configured prepared-data ceiling because its expansion ratio is not trusted before bounded extraction; compressed Redis, Valkey, and Qdrant physical imports are charged at the target disk allocation, capped by the physical archive limit. MongoDB, Redis, Valkey, and Qdrant are always modelled as natively compressed. action=export with mode=wipe is invalid.

200.description: Live scheduler snapshot and model-based recommendation.

patch.summary: Merge a validated config patch into the daemon config file.
patch.description: Writes config.yml and returns restart_required=true. Refuses identity/token, managed-path, container-image, S3-endpoint, executable-helper, and Fuse helper edits, including replacement or removal of their ancestors. The allocation.prevent_cpu_overallocation, allocation.prevent_memory_overallocation, and allocation.prevent_disk_overallocation booleans may be changed independently; all default to true.

get.description: Returns success when the authenticated management API is reachable, independently of database instance and gateway readiness.

get.summary: Get Prometheus metrics for the daemon.
List database instances with route-safe live status classification.

202.description: Instance creation accepted and continuing in the background.

400.description: Invalid create request, including a disabled protocol or a shared deployment requested for Redis, Valkey, or Qdrant.

409.description: Instance ID already exists.

422.description: Request JSON does not match the create schema, for example an unknown deployment_mode value or a missing required field.

503.description: Creation admission is closed or the bounded creation queue is full.

get.summary: Get one instance with route-safe live status classification.

delete.summary: Irreversibly delete one instance, its jobs, artifacts, backups, recovery data, and database contents.
delete.description: Dedicated deletion removes the owned engine runtime. Shared deletion removes only the logical tenant and removes the pool runtime only when its final tenant is gone.

patch.summary: Update CPU, memory, and disk limits for an instance.
patch.description: Dedicated limits apply to the owned runtime. Shared requests accept disk_mib only and update the tenant's disk reservation within the existing fixed pool budget. They never resize pool CPU/RAM/disk. A shared disk decrease briefly fences and drains the tenant, measures its physical usage, and returns 409 without changing the limit when existing data does not fit.

409.description: A shared tenant disk decrease is below its current physical usage, or the tenant could not be fenced and drained safely for the shrink check. The existing limit remains unchanged.

503.description: An enabled CPU, memory, or disk allocation guard rejected a limit increase. Capacity guards do not reject decreases; shared disk decreases can separately return 409 when current data does not fit.

patch.summary: Reset an instance tenant password or API key.
patch.description: Atomically rotates and validates the tenant credential and attempts to restore the previous credential if any step fails. Shared mode changes only the selected tenant and never recreates or restarts the pool. Dedicated mode normally rotates in place but may recreate its owned runtime when the engine stores immutable startup credentials. The instance must be running and experiences a brief connection interruption.

200.description: Credential reset result. The password is never included.

get.summary: List durable deployment-migration attempts for an instance.

post.description: Migrations in both directions, dedicated-to-shared and shared-to-dedicated, run asynchronously through a tenant-scoped logical export/import, target validation, atomic placement cutover, and source cleanup. A successful start returns 202 immediately; poll the returned Location for durable progress. The source remains authoritative until cutover, and crash recovery records a safe rollback, cleanup, or manual-intervention stage.

202.description: Migration accepted and durably queued.

400.description: A valid shared target was requested for an unsupported protocol.

409.description: Source is not ready, already uses the target mode, lacks a current encrypted tenant credential, has active data work, or already has an active migration.

422.description: Request JSON does not match the migration schema, for example target_mode is missing or is not dedicated/shared.

429.description: The import/export scheduler has no global capacity for the migration.

503.description: Daemon shutdown or mutation draining has started; no migration was accepted.

post.summary: Reconcile stored instance status with its engine runtime.
post.description: Dedicated mode inspects its owned runtime. Shared mode also verifies the pool placement while preserving tenant-only route and lifecycle state.

post.summary: Unified power API for start, stop, restart, and kill.
post.description: Dedicated actions control the owned engine runtime. Shared actions fence or restore only this tenant's login, routes, and sessions; they never stop or kill the shared pool for another tenant.

patch.summary: Pull and switch an instance to a new database image.
patch.description: Dedicated instances only. Same-major updates recreate the owned runtime on its existing volume. Major version changes require major_upgrade=true and run the safer export/import migration workflow where supported. Shared tenants return 409 because pool images are selected through placement and deployment migration.

get.summary: List resource usage for all instances.
Get node capacity, allocation, and whole-host resource pressure.
get.description: Allocation includes all managed instances, including stopped instances that may be restarted. Host usage covers the entire Linux node. Managed usage is null when any running or booting instance could not be sampled. Disk totals describe the filesystem backing paths.volumes.

200.description: Node-wide resource summary for scheduling and capacity decisions.

get.description: Pool CPU and memory are whole-engine cgroup measurements, not individual tenant usage. Null means unavailable, not zero. Panel backends must filter inventory to the authorized server before exposing it.

post.description: Creates an empty, persistent server-owned pool. Only PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB and ClickHouse. One per authenticated panel namespace, server_id and engine; duplicates fail asynchronously. Poll status_url after 202.

202.description: Operation result.

get.description: Pool CPU and memory are whole-engine cgroup measurements, not individual tenant usage. Null means unavailable, not zero. Panel backends must filter inventory to the authorized server before exposing it.

delete.description: Requires confirm=true and a nonempty reason. Only an empty pool without active work can be deleted. Deleting its last child never deletes the pool automatically.

patch.description: Requires pools:write. Fixed capacity; memory and disk may grow but cannot shrink online. max_tenants cannot fall below reservations. No automatic growth or overflow pool.

get.description: Lists published child databases. In-flight creations and provisional migration targets are omitted until published; use the creation status_url for progress. Unexplained orphan reservations and ownership mismatches still fail rather than being silently adopted.

post.description: Creates a child in this explicit pool using the existing instance provisioning path. Protocol, owner and image come from the pool. Returns the child instance_id/status_url, not another pool.

202.description: Operation result.

get.summary: Get pool state and retained operation progress.
get.description: Get pool state and retained operation progress.

post.description: Start, stop, restart or kill the physical engine, affecting all its databases. Active data jobs/migrations and pending image recovery reject the action. Stop intent survives daemon restart.

patch.summary: Update a pool image within its release line.
patch.description: Requires pools:write and images:admin, confirm=true and a reason. Take backups first. Uses a disposable no-data-mount version probe, then preserves volumes and verifies the replacement before routing. Rejects downgrades and different release lines. Interrupted updates are quarantined; retry only the same immutable image.

202.description: Operation result.

get.description: Read recent redacted pool logs.

get.summary: List backups of the pool's databases.
get.description: Lists existing per-database backups for this pool. Requires pools:read and backups:read. These remain independent backups, not a simultaneous whole-engine snapshot.

Requires an owner-and-generation-bound pools:monitor JWT minted with pools plus server_id. No instance token grants this access. Sends one unbatched pool_stats snapshot per second; progress is change-only. Merge reset/removals/updates and reconnect with a fresh one-use JWT after a sequence gap. Values are already percentage points/bytes; keep null and sample freshness.

Requires an owner-and-generation-bound pools:logs JWT, not logs:read. Pool-wide logs can contain data from every child database. Same reset/append/end protocol as dedicated logs, with runtime_id instead of instance_id. Reconnect with a fresh one-use JWT. No query-token authentication.

get.summary: Get resource usage for one instance.
Get current tenant-attributed gateway and query activity.
get.description: Returns cumulative gateway counters plus explicitly source-labelled engine observations. For gateway sources, accepted means forwarded by DBEV rather than successfully executed, and rejected includes only DBEV pre-backend rejections. It never returns SQL text, bind values, client addresses, errors, or whole-pool CPU/RAM as tenant usage.

Returns at most 1440 aggregate buckets in chronological order on a target 60-second cadence. If sampling is delayed, one bucket covers the complete elapsed interval and duration_seconds is authoritative. before is an exclusive Unix timestamp for backwards pagination. DBEV persists only aggregate counters in SQLite and never exposes SQL text, bind values, client addresses, or engine errors through this API. get.summary: WebSocket stream of instance resource snapshots.
get.description: Requires monitor:read on a short-lived generation-bound WebSocket JWT. Browser authentication uses Sec-WebSocket-Protocol ["dbe.jwt", "<jwt>"]; query tokens are rejected. One full authorized instance snapshot is produced per second, split into bounded messages with sequence, sampled_at_unix, batch_index and batch_count. Assemble every batch before applying a sequence. Reconnect with a fresh JWT on a missing/incomplete sequence; skipping progress deltas loses updates. API 0.16 instance identity lives only on the outer item: instance_id, runtime_id, deployment_mode, resource_scope, protocol, status, runtime. resources contains only cpu, memory and disk (or null with resource_error); REST resource responses remain self-contained. activity omits instance_id and is the only WebSocket location for rx_bytes and tx_bytes. install_progress contains changed records only. After assembling a sequence, clear the progress cache if progress_reset is true, remove install_progress_removed IDs, and upsert install_progress by instance_id. Missing progress is not deletion or a creating state. New connections receive a complete retained progress snapshot with progress_reset=true. Reset sequence/batch state on reconnect; keep explicit null values, source labels, timestamps and stats_epoch discontinuities. CPU remains percentage points (11.0 means 11%). Shared tenant CPU/RAM remains null, never whole-pool consumption. Sampling, generation checks, authorization and 16-KiB batch limits are unchanged.

get.summary: WebSocket stream of container logs for one instance.
get.description: Requires logs:read on a generation-bound WebSocket JWT. Dedicated instances only; shared logs return 409. API 0.16 sends type=logs with event=reset and sequence=0, then event=append with stream=stdout|stderr and data containing new text only. One Docker follow request delivers the requested tail followed by live output. Append to a bounded client buffer; never replace it for append events. event=end terminates the stream, optionally with a public error. Sequence numbers are per connection. Reconnect clears local sequence state and receives a new reset/tail, not guaranteed lossless history. Complete records are redacted across runtime chunks, then split into UTF-8-safe messages below 16 KiB. An incomplete final secret value is omitted. Records exceeding the 128-KiB redaction budget end the stream with log_record_limit; do not retry that error in a tight loop. Heartbeats use Ping/Pong every 30 seconds and never resend log text. Expiry, shutdown and generation fencing remain enforced.

get.summary: WebSocket stream of import/export jobs for one instance.
get.description: Requires a short-lived WebSocket JWT with import-export:read and access to the instance in the path. Messages and frames are limited to 16 KiB.

info.title: Proofestra local API
info.summary: Proposed extensible personal API; no runtime, tool executor or endpoint is implemented.
info.description: Draft same-origin personal UI contract. Provider IDs/catalogs are extensible through validated adapter manifests; the initial three targets are not a fixed enum. Profiles identify execution backends and versioned capability/control metadata. No provider SDK, CLI, API or tool execution is implemented. Validate Host/session/CSRF/Origin, disable CORS, enforce a 128 KiB body maximum, and use no-store plus X-Request-ID. Live work requires explicit authorized submission. Personal numerical defaults are not product ceilings; finite runtime-policy ceilings govern admission. Observable harness invocations are not opaque internal model/tool counts. No universal compatibility, guaranteed cancellation, billing or accuracy claims. Confirmed design scope includes provider API tools, local agent applications, SDKs/CLIs, MCP tools and hosted agent services. Compatibility/implementation are staged per adapter; none is implied live by inclusion in scope.

get.description: Validate Host even here. Refresh may replace the session without losing saved conversations.

Set-Cookie.description: HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1; Secure under HTTPS. Never export or log.

get.description: Extensible validated adapter registry, initially targeting OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini. Provider IDs are open registered strings; multiple profiles/backends per provider. No credentials, model discovery, CLI launch or provider calls.

delete.summary: Delete a conversation and its associated local records
delete.description: Returns 204 even for an absent valid UUID. Any active run in this conversation blocks deletion. Logical deletion is not forensic erasure of backups, SQLite pages, exports, or provider data.

get.summary: Page messages in stable chronological sequence

200.description: User prompts and final presentations; drafts remain run artifacts.

post.summary: Atomically save prompt and configuration and enqueue one run
post.description: Resolve durable idempotency before the single global active-run guard, including waiting/approval states. Freeze profile/backend/capability/runtime-policy/grant versions and safe context atomically with prompt/run/key/event. Reject unique-ID, membership, readiness, control, scope, context and finite deployment-policy violations before dispatch. Repeated provider/profile roots and larger teams within deployment policy are valid. All-peers base plan is not dynamic internal work; no blind global 32 internal-call promise. No new destinations/grants or silent synthesizer replacement. Returns queued, not a completed answer.

get.summary: Read a run snapshot without starting or resuming work
get.description: Read current lineage, observable accounting, external status and first-page tool records/cursor. Tool/provider denials are run data, not HTTP 500. Does not execute/resume work; no raw credentials/vendor/private reasoning traces.

put.summary: Request cancellation and return the current snapshot
put.description: Idempotent local workflow cancellation across descendants/tools/continuations/native jobs. Completion may win. Stop new scheduling; request remote stop, never undo completed side effects. If remote completion is unknown retain unknown/orphaned external status; do not claim cancellation/refund. Workflow terminal state remains immutable while separate external status/usage reconciliation can append records. Never auto-resubmit after restart.

get.summary: Replay durable bounded stage events using SSE
get.description: Read-only persisted run-scoped SSE replay; disconnect does not cancel/duplicate work. Last-Event-ID absent replays after zero; malformed/negative/future IDs return 400. Event name equals EventEnvelope.type. Includes lineage, routes, approvals, tool results and scoped usage; no raw token stream/private reasoning. Close after workflow terminal event; later external reconciliation is available by snapshot/tool pages and a fresh explicit replay. Return 204 when cursor is already at the latest terminal sequence. Never auto-resume or fake remote cancellation. If a terminal run has newer reconciliation records after the cursor, replay them and close when caught up; 204 only when terminal and already at the latest stored sequence.

200.description: SSE frames with durable numeric IDs and JSON event data.

get.summary: Export portable version-1 JSON after all conversation runs terminate
get.description: Full logical version-1 export includes every terminal run tree, route/tool/approval/source record and scoped usage, not first-page previews. Contains user/task text; disclose before download. Exclude credentials/cookies/CSRF/raw vendor/hidden reasoning data. Any active/waiting/approval run returns 409. Unknown/orphaned external work may remain after local cancellation/deletion.

200.description: Full logical conversation export, not a paginated list.

get.summary: Page compatible tool/profile/backend metadata without executing tools
get.description: Filter by registered metadata. Compatibility evidence/readiness/auth/grants/egress/observability are separate; no claim of universal tool/model/mode support. Cursors bind catalog version and filters.

get.summary: Read versioned personal defaults and finite deployment ceilings
get.description: No mutation or provider calls. Requests cannot raise server ceilings; snapshot the effective version and reject stale/incompatible admission.

get.summary: Page all tool executions and their route/approval records

200.description: Current execution records in stable sequence.

post.summary: Record human approval or denial of one pending exact action
post.description: Verify session/CSRF/Origin, pending record/run/caller/tool/profile/backend/task/policy bindings, exact argument digest, expiry and current run state. Same key/payload replays; changed decision/payload or stale/mismatched action returns 409. Approval never expands frozen allowlists or bypasses compatibility/budget. Consent is not execution. Models cannot invoke this browser-authorized operation or mint grants. Approval control surfaces and credentials are isolated from agent tools. Freeze initial scope; recheck current grant validity/revocation before execution. An action-scoped approval cannot widen tools/backends/profiles/destinations; broader changes need a new run.

200.description: Stable exact-action decision, including idempotent replay.

Provider.description: Open registered provider ID, not an enum. Initial targets are openai, anthropic and gemini; custom IDs require a validated operator-installed adapter manifest.

ProviderConfig.description: Operator-registered adapter with configured profiles. Profile IDs are globally unique; profile counts are bounded by deployment policy, not a product-wide constant.

ProviderList.description: Paginated extensible provider registry. Core targets are not a promise that exactly three entries exist or every listed tool is implemented.

execution_controls.notes: Illustrative deterministic mock control mapping, not a tested live backend.

RunCreate.description: Quick requires one root and no synthesizer; Team at least two roots and a root synthesizer_agent_id. Repeated providers/profiles are valid; unique IDs/membership/profile/control/grant checks are application invariants. Provider IDs/catalog are extensible. Freeze profiles, backend/capability/policy versions, context and authorized scopes; reject before dispatch if base work cannot fit. all_peers plans 2n+1 base harness calls, not fixed dynamic work. Other review topologies remain future designs. Personal default root count 6 may be raised only within advertised deployment ceilings. Client input cannot contain raw model IDs, credentials, lineage, new grants or arbitrary adapter definitions. Live submissions bind the displayed expected_catalog_version and expected_runtime_policy_version; changed registry/policy returns 409 before dispatch. Recheck current grant validity/revocation before every action, without broadening frozen scope.

RunLimitsInput.description: Personal defaults, not hard-coded product ceilings. Default max_harness_invocations=32/retries=1 except Quick with delegation disabled AND tool mode off uses 1/0. All omitted fields normalize under the versioned runtime policy. Requests can exceed personal defaults only within finite deployment ceilings. Validate root/base-stage/output/time/concurrency relationships before dispatch. Harness counts cover only coordinator-scheduled calls, not opaque native internals. Observable operation/job limits govern local admission; remote observations can arrive after execution. Strict routes must enforce requested controls, otherwise decline. Never promise a global internal-call or billing hard cap.

AgentSnapshot.description: Run-scoped runtime identity. Roots have parent null, root_agent_id=self, depth=0 and task=null; children have an existing parent, inherited root ID, depth=parent+1 and bounded assigned task. Validate acyclic same-run links, unique IDs, reciprocal child lists and lifetime quotas in application logic. Identical provider/profile does not merge agents.

ContextSnapshot.description: Frozen all visible history plus current prompt; records the exact included message IDs. Fit is a conservative local estimate, not guaranteed vendor counting. No hidden per-provider trimming. Children reuse this history plus scoped task/authorized branch artifacts; drafting branches cannot see current peer-root drafts. Recheck child/continuation capacity before dispatch.

Usage.description: Scope-aware ledger. Harness invocations count calls the coordinator dispatches, including initial/child/continuation/retry calls and one outer native-job launch; do not infer internal calls from that count. Observed tool operations/native jobs are distinct counters. Nullable internal counts/cost remain unknown, never zero by assumption. Whole-tree totals require actual complete reporting; opaque SDK/server-tool work may remain incomplete. Remote observations can arrive after local admission/cancellation; keep them separately reconcilable without resuming the workflow. Cost is an estimate, never a billing guarantee. Simulation is labeled explicitly.

NormalizedFailure.description: Safe concise message, never raw vendor response, secrets, or stack trace.

Source.description: Retrieval and claim support are separate: retrieved is never automatically verified. Preserve exact source origin/location/time and checking method. A model opinion is not ground truth. Model-supplied URLs start not_retrieved/unassessed.

Finding.description: Concise model finding with identity/provenance, never private reasoning. IDs refer to the containing run/step.

StepSnapshot.description: Unique stage/task identity. attempts counts coordinator-dispatched harness invocations for this step, including resumes/retries, not opaque internal model calls. Waiting for children/tools/approval releases local execution permits; deadline/reservations remain. Sum actual harness calls within effective policy; helper work is not a root vote. No raw vendor/private reasoning traces.

spawn_decisions.description: Complete accepted/denied decisions under the run deadline and bounded model output; do not truncate away denials in exports.

RunSnapshot.description: Snapshot of frozen identities/profiles/backends/context/policy/grants plus effective personal/deployment limits. Agent/step/spawn counts obey dynamic runtime policy, not fixed product ceilings. base_planned_calls counts all_peers root harness work only; usage distinguishes observed harness/tool/job counts from nullable internal usage. Tool history is a first-page preview with a cursor; paginated tool records and full export preserve all routes/approvals/results. Completed means authorized required workflow completion, never factual correctness. Accepted-child failure/missing Team work/fallback is partial; zero successful root drafts fails. No silent synthesizer swap. Terminal workflow outcome is immutable; external unknown/orphaned status and usage may be reconciled separately without auto-resume. Keys/private reasoning/raw vendor debug payloads never appear.

execution_controls.notes: Illustrative deterministic mock control mapping, not a tested live backend.

steps.output: Simulated answer; no live model was called.

examples.final_answer: Simulated answer; no live model was called.
limitations: Unreviewed simulated response; mock cost is zero because no provider requests occur.

data.description: Lineage and step/run harness counts only; completed helper output/usage is scoped. Opaque internals may be unknown. Waiting tools/approval release permits; no private reasoning.
Read-only external status/metering reconciliation, not auto-resume. Exactly one target ID is nonnull; validate it belongs to this run.

EventEnvelope.description: Run-scoped durable numeric sequence. Lineage, routes, exact-action approvals and bounded tool results are typed events. Scope counters to observable harness/operations/jobs; never infer hidden internal work. Terminal state stays immutable; separately labeled external reconciliation can append records without restarting work.

ConversationExport.description: Complete logical terminal-run export, including all tool execution pages, routes, human decisions, source retrieval/support provenance, descendants and scoped usage. No credentials/raw vendor/private reasoning traces. Does not imply remote work was canceled or external data erased.

ProfileId.description: Stable server-configured model-profile slug; no client-supplied model IDs or keys.

DelegationCapability.description: supported means the adapter/profile internal delegation round trip was compatibility checked. Configuration alone is not support; no vendor-native agent service is implied.

ModelProfile.description: Server-configured profile and backend/capacity/control metadata. Repeated provider/model/profile agents remain distinct. Readiness is configuration only; keys and raw auth state never appear. Missing capacities/control mappings make a demanding route ineligible.

AgentDefinition.description: Root identity is independent of provider/profile. Agent IDs must be unique within a run; repeated profile/provider is allowed. Role text cannot expand permissions.

DelegationInput.description: Defaults: Team enabled, Quick disabled; allowed_profile_ids empty. The allowlist grants alternate child profiles only; inheritance uses the parent profile. Resolve and freeze permission at run admission. Model text cannot expand it.

InvocationSnapshot.description: One reserved/dispatched adapter call. A tool-request response can complete an invocation while the step waits; a continuation is a new counted call. Schedule one logical continuation per parent invocation response batch, never per duplicate callback; resumes_after_invocation_id identifies it. A bounded safe retry may be a separate retry invocation of that continuation. At most one retry per logical step across its entire initial/continuation sequence, only a known pre-generation rejection. Initial calls have null retry/resume IDs; retries name the rejected invocation. Queued records do not count as dispatched. Cross-record references stay in the same parent step/run. One observable harness invocation can wrap many server-tool/SDK internal operations; usage declares scope rather than treating that whole job as one internal call. Capture native job ID/control/deadline/external status when relevant; unconfirmed remote stop remains unknown/orphaned.

SpawnRequest.description: Adapter-neutral internal spawn_subagent tool arguments, not a browser endpoint. Parent/run/step/tool-call IDs come from trusted coordinator context, not model arguments. Omitted profile inherits parent; an alternate must be preapproved in delegation.allowed_profile_ids. Model text cannot grant itself permissions.

SpawnDenialCode.description: Safe visible policy/quota reason. Invalid/unready/incompatible profile, conflicting tool-call payload or malformed arguments use invalid_request; no child is created.

SpawnDecision.description: Durable bounded decision. Idempotency tuple is run,parent,step,parent_invocation_id,provider_tool_call_id plus normalized request digest. Server derives ancestry/invocation IDs. Matching replays return the original decision/child; changed payload is invalid_request without replacing the original or creating another child. The same provider tool-call ID from another invocation is a new request subject to lifetime quotas. A malformed request records request=null and a safe notice rather than raw arguments. Acceptance atomically reserves child initial work, one logical parent continuation per response batch and remaining required root work. Denial itself dispatches no call; a normal continuation still needs budget. Denial alone is not partial; accepted-child failure is. All lifetime/depth/call/output checks use the snapshotted runtime policy. A native opaque backend cannot bypass caller/grant/context restrictions or masquerade its hidden subagents as fully observed harness nodes.

request.task: Check the arithmetic in the supplied figures.
request.name: Arithmetic helper

examples.notice: Accepted within the run limits; one child call and a parent continuation are reserved.

ExecutionBackend.description: Versioned configured execution route, not a universal provider capability. No credentials or automatic login/discovery calls.

CompatibilityEvidence.description: Documentation evidence is distinct from tested compatibility and current availability. Record exact backend/tool/model/mode versions before marking tested.

AuthRequirements.description: Auth method labels and scope/readiness only. No keys, OAuth/session tokens, raw headers or subscription credentials. API-key and user-authorized unmodified CLI flows remain separate routes.

PermissionRequirements.description: A matching existing task/session grant can authorize suitable actions without another prompt. Some exact actions require action approval. Model text cannot issue grants.

EgressMetadata.description: Known permitted destination patterns and context flow. Runtime enforces scope, including redirects; self-hosting does not keep remote provider/MCP data local.

ExecutionControls.description: Finite configured/enforceable backend execution caps, or null when unavailable. Strict admission requires every requested control to map to enforcement. Bounded-job use of opaque internals requires explicit opt-in and an enforced job/launch deadline. No monetary guarantee. Enforce delegation_disabled when helpers are off; inability to prevent native helper spawning cannot be excused by opaque-usage opt-in. Direct request/job-launch acknowledgement deadlines are distinct from the supervised native-job lifetime; each job is bounded by remaining run time and its snapshotted execution cap.

arguments_schema.description: Validated tool JSON Schema supplied by the registered manifest; data, never executable client code.

CapabilityMetadata.description: Versioned tool/profile/backend metadata; not universal support for a provider or model. Catalog reads never call tools or verify credentials.

ToolPolicyInput.description: Team mode defaults auto, Quick off. Allowlist/grant fields default to the user's existing authorized selection (empty if none), resolved and frozen at admission; never implicitly all catalog entries. Models cannot mint grants or add destinations. Auto selects only compatible authorized direct/helper routes. Alternate helper profiles must satisfy relevant delegation/tool permissions. A matching task/session grant avoids needless reapproval. Missing grants pause an exact action or block it; incompatible/forbidden routes cannot be approved into existence. Strict requires enforceable requested bounds; bounded_job plus allow_unknown_internal_usage=true explicitly permits opaque internals under a finite job deadline. Tool-created managed helpers require delegation.enabled. Helpers-off must disable native/runtime helper spawning too; a backend unable to enforce that permission boundary is ineligible even for bounded-job mode. Initial selection/grant references stay frozen; recheck expiration/revocation and required scope before each dispatch. A broader configuration change requires a new run. required_controls is combined with mandatory deployment controls, not a way to remove them. Deadline enforcement scope and remote-cancellation limitations must be disclosed by backend metadata; a local supervisor timeout does not prove remote work stopped.

RunLimitCeilings.description: Finite operator-enforced ceilings for each request bound. Values are deployment configuration, not user/model authority; defaults and effective limits must not exceed them. All counts/deadlines are finite integers.

RuntimePolicy.description: Read-only effective server policy. Future topology/ceiling changes need implementation validation; clients cannot increase ceilings by sending a policy object. One global active run remains the personal-deployment default. Effective requested controls include the union of mandatory server controls and user-requested controls; a client cannot remove mandatory grant/context/security controls.

ExternalWorkStatus.description: External truth/status is distinct from immutable local workflow state. An unconfirmed stop is unknown/orphaned, never assumed canceled or reversed.

arguments.description: Validate against the selected registered tool schema and configured byte/depth limits (initial safe default 16 KiB). No auth headers, raw credentials, policy or caller identity fields. Never execute before policy resolution.

ToolInvocationRequest.description: Internal model request, not browser authentication or permission. Coordinator supplies caller/run/step/parent invocation/tool-call IDs; optional specific tool does not bypass the frozen capability/profile/backend/grant scope.

RouteDecision.description: Durable exact routing decision under frozen policy. Direct chooses a compatible permitted native route; delegated chooses an already approved helper profile/backend. No eligible route is unavailable/blocked, never a new destination or changed root synthesizer. Awaiting approval cannot repair an incompatible/out-of-scope route. Match request identity/digest for replay; distinct decisions may record approval-driven transitions of one execution. Delegated routes require delegation.enabled; auto tool mode cannot override helpers-off or create a hidden managed child.

PendingToolApproval.description: One pending exact action bound server-side to run, execution, caller, tool/profile/backend, task and policy version. Preview contains all nonsecret normalized arguments and credential-scope references, never secret values. Changed action requires another pending record; no broad grant.

ToolApprovalInput.description: Human UI response for a pending exact action. CSRF/Origin/session plus Idempotency-Key required. Server verifies all bindings/scope/run state; models cannot approve or mint grants. Approval records consent, not completed execution. The approval UI and its session/CSRF credentials must be inaccessible to agent-controlled browsers, shells and MCP environments; Origin/CSRF alone does not prove a human action.

ToolApprovalResult.description: Stable decision replay; same idempotency key/payload returns original. Conflicting payload/decision or stale action returns 409. An action-scoped server grant may be created only for a valid human approval; never widen run allowlists. Persist one decision per pending approval; duplicate approval requests/callbacks do not issue another grant, execute again or resume the parent twice.

ToolExecution.description: Bounded normalized action/result ledger, not unrestricted vendor traces. Every execution has stable sequence, caller/invocation identity and exact digest; duplicate callbacks cannot execute twice. Grants/routes and pending approval remain bound to the exact action. Unknown/orphaned external status is not fake cancellation. Results are inert content. Denials alone need not make a run partial; an unfinished required action/stage does. Later external status/metering reconciliation can update this separate record after run terminal state, without changing workflow outcome or launching work.

info.title: PACT API Specification
info.summary: Technical Specifications for PCF Data Exchange
info.description:
This document describes the technical specifications for the exchange of 
Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) data between systems. The specification is 
maintained by the WBCSD PACT project and intended to be used by organizations 
that wish to exchange PCF data with other organizations. The specifications 
are designed to be technology-agnostic.
info.x-rule:
SHALL = Required to report on
BIO = Required if biogenic and land sector related emissions are applicable, 0 if not applicable, blank if unknown or unavailable
BIO-2027 = Required by 31/12/2027 if biogenic and land sector related emissions are applicable , 0 if not applicable, blank if unknown or unavalaible
CCU = Required if CCU applicable and data known and available, blank otherwise
CCS = Required if CCS applicable and data known and available, blank otherwise
SHOULD = Recommended to report on in, exceptions possible
MAY = Optional
